## About this document

This document collects the 60 standalone analyses written alongside the main
analysis (`analysis/analysis_v17.Rmd`) and the figure code
(`figures/figures_v2.Rmd`). Each was written and run as an independent script,
addressing one question: a robustness check, a reviewer's objection, a control,
or a replication in the second cohort or an external one.

**They are not a pipeline and do not knit in sequence.** Each needs its own
inputs, and several are alternatives to one another rather than successive
steps. Every chunk is therefore `eval=FALSE`. The chunks are named after their
source scripts, so `knitr::purl()` on this file regenerates each brief as a
runnable `.R` exactly as it was run.

**Input-file discipline.** Pittsburgh quantities come from
`final_run/figure_inputs.rds` (14 October 2026, 302 MB, md5 prefix `80100a3a`),
which carries the `MG_DB` field. An earlier `Results_v8/figure_inputs.rds`
(23 September, 53 MB, 47 patients) exists and silently yields different
numbers -- it is **not** the input for anything here. Where a brief reads
`figure_inputs.rds`, it means the 14 October file. That file is not in this
repository; see `data/README.md`.

## Vintage

These briefs were written over several months, and each records the numbers its
run produced at the time. Two things moved underneath them.

The Pittsburgh paired set went from **47 to 48 patients** on 13 October 2026,
when a mislabelled channel was traced to its correct patient; briefs written
before that date state n = 47. The analysis input was replaced on 14 October
for the same reason, which moved the Bacillota/Bacteroidota clade gap from
+0.310 to **+0.3291** -- one patient, not a change of method. Some briefs
already assume the later values: `B33_external_clade`'s own harness check
asserts it must return +0.35 / +0.02, which is the 48-patient result.

So a number in a brief may be the value as computed then rather than the value
reported now. **The manuscript and the deposited Supplementary Tables are
authoritative.** Where a brief disagrees with them, the brief is a historical
record, not a correction.

The manuscript is the authoritative statement of results. These briefs are the
working record of how each question was answered, written as the work
proceeded.


## B1 — full space prep

build the null input for a correction over the ENTIRE examined search space.

Source: `B1_full_space_prep.R`

```{r B1_full_space_prep, eval=FALSE}
## B1 — build the null input for a correction over the ENTIRE examined search space.
##
## q = 0.045 corrects among the 30 sets carried into the null, not across the
## five-layer scan that identified them. The existing draws cannot answer this:
## each stores only pathway/size/NES for those 30 sets, not the per-draw
## statistic vector, so nothing can be re-scored without refitting. This writes a
## new input whose set list is every set actually examined, plus the 30 reported.
##
## What the space is, stated so it can be argued with: the five layers exactly as
## §6a examined them (initial annotation, the state in which the hypothesis was
## formed), plus the 30 completed-annotation sets that were reported. §6a's
## universe was settled on 23 Sep 2026 as the R1+R2+R3 discovery tiers — 538
## sets, the space searched when the hypothesis was selected, not the tighter
## R1+R2 universe adopted later for new work. This script reads `sets` as §6a
## built it, so it inherits that definition automatically; if §6a is ever
## changed, check that this still corrects over the space actually searched. Sets are
## name-prefixed by layer so the two annotations cannot collide.
##
## Run in the analysis session after §6b, then run the server driver against the
## input it writes. Wall cost is close to the original: the msqrob refit per draw
## dominates and is shared; only the fgsea call grows.

need <- c("sets", "SETS_P", "SETS_S", "stat", "qf", "SAMP_PRIMARY", "PARAMS",
          "RESP_LEVELS", "KEEP_P", "KEEP_S", "fit_arm", "pick_denom", "arm_mix_v13")
miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss)) stop("run analysis_v17.Rmd through §7b first; missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(purrr) })
OUT <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "full_space"); dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
MIN_N <- 10L

flat <- function(lst, tag) {
  if (!length(lst)) return(list())
  s <- lapply(lst, function(x) intersect(x, names(stat)))
  s <- s[lengths(s) >= MIN_N]
  if (!length(s)) return(list())
  setNames(s, paste0(tag, ":", names(s)))
}
LAYERS <- list(KO = "KO", COG = "COG", Pfam = "Pfam", KEGGmod = "KEGGmod", KEGGpath = "KEGGpath")
examined <- do.call(c, lapply(names(LAYERS), function(L)
  if (!is.null(sets[[L]])) flat(sets[[L]], L) else list()))
reported <- setNames(SETS_P, paste0("reported:", names(SETS_P)))
SETS_FULL <- c(examined, reported)
SETS_FULL <- SETS_FULL[!duplicated(names(SETS_FULL))]

cat("sets per layer (>= ", MIN_N, " members, in the analysis universe):\n", sep = "")
print(c(vapply(names(LAYERS), function(L) sum(startsWith(names(SETS_FULL), paste0(L, ":"))), 0L),
        reported = sum(startsWith(names(SETS_FULL), "reported:")), TOTAL = length(SETS_FULL)))
stopifnot(length(SETS_FULL) > length(SETS_P),
          all(c("reported:O", "reported:chaperones") %in% names(SETS_FULL)))

## run_null.R reads SETS_P by name, so the full space is handed over under it.
SETS_P_ORIGINAL <- SETS_P
SETS_P <- SETS_FULL
save(qf, SAMP_PRIMARY, PARAMS, RESP_LEVELS, SETS_P, SETS_S, KEEP_P, KEEP_S,
     fit_arm, pick_denom, arm_mix_v13,
     file = file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData"), compress = "xz")
SETS_P <- SETS_P_ORIGINAL
saveRDS(vapply(SETS_FULL, length, 0L), file.path(OUT, "set_sizes.rds"))
cat(sprintf("\nwritten: %s (%.1f MB)\nrun:  label=pitt_full cohort=pitt input=%s\n",
            file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData"),
            file.size(file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData")) / 1e6, file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData")))
```

## B1b — full space score

score the full-space run: Westfall-Young max-T (FWER) and BH (FDR)

Source: `B1b_full_space_score.R`

```{r B1b_full_space_score, eval=FALSE}
## B1b — score the full-space run: Westfall-Young max-T (FWER) and BH (FDR)
## across every set examined, with the reading FIXED BEFORE THE RESULT IS SEEN.
##
## The expected outcome should be stated plainly: with a null SD near 1.15 and
## perhaps 100-200 effectively independent sets, the per-draw max |NES| lands
## near 3.5 while COG O is 2.24. BH over ~570 sets is no kinder at rank 1.
## Survival would be a genuine surprise. The rule below is written for the
## likely outcome as much as the hoped-for one.
##
## Rscript B1b_full_space_score.R /path/to/nulls_pitt_full

d <- commandArgs(TRUE)[1]; if (is.na(d)) stop("usage: B1b_full_space_score.R <null dir>")
obs <- as.data.frame(readRDS(file.path(d, "observed_pitt.rds")))
fs  <- list.files(d, "^null_pitt_[0-9]+\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("%d sets, %d draws\n", nrow(obs), length(fs)))
nl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fs, function(f) as.data.frame(readRDS(f))))

## per-draw maximum |NES| across the whole space -> the Westfall-Young null
mx <- vapply(split(abs(nl$NES), nl$draw), max, 0, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
p_wy <- vapply(abs(obs$NES), function(o) (1 + sum(mx >= o)) / (1 + length(mx)), 0)
p_set <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(obs)), function(i) {
  x <- nl$NES[nl$pathway == obs$pathway[i]]
  (1 + sum(abs(x) >= abs(obs$NES[i]), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(!is.na(x)))
}, 0)
res <- data.frame(pathway = obs$pathway, size = obs$size, NES = obs$NES,
                  p_set = p_set, q_bh_full = p.adjust(p_set, "BH"), p_wy = p_wy)
res <- res[order(res$p_set), ]
cat(sprintf("\nnull max|NES| per draw: median %.2f, 95th pct %.2f, max %.2f\n",
            median(mx), quantile(mx, .95), max(mx)))
key <- c("reported:O", "reported:O_chap", "reported:chaperones", "reported:O_chap_noGD")
print(res[res$pathway %in% key, ], row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
cat(sprintf("\nrank of reported:O by |NES| among %d sets: %d\n", nrow(res),
            which(order(-abs(res$NES)) == which(res$pathway == "reported:O"))))
cat(sprintf("sets at BH q<0.10 over the full space: %d; at Westfall-Young p<0.05: %d\n",
            sum(res$q_bh_full < 0.10), sum(res$p_wy < 0.05)))

o <- res[res$pathway == "reported:O", ]
verdict <- if (o$p_wy < 0.05) "fwer" else if (o$q_bh_full < 0.10) "fdr" else "neither"
READ <- list(
fwer = "
COG O survives family-wise correction over the ENTIRE examined space. This is the
strongest available statement and it should lead: the association is not an
artefact of the search. Report p_WY beside q = 0.045 and drop the hedging about
incomplete correction in §2.1. The paper can be sold on the chaperone result as
well as the paired-layer one.",
fdr = "
COG O survives FDR but not FWER across the full space. Report both: q over the
full space is the honest headline number, and the failure to meet FWER is stated
rather than omitted. §2.1's sentence about correcting within 30 sets is replaced
by the full-space q. The chaperone result stays a result; it does not become the
paper's sole support.",
neither = "
COG O does not survive correction over the full examined space. This is the
expected outcome and it is not a retraction — it is the honest multiplicity
statement for a discovery cohort. Act on it: stop using significance as the basis
of the chaperone claim, describe it as the worked example identified in an
exploratory scan and quantified thereafter, keep every effect size and the
per-sample share, and move the paper's weight onto the paired-layer result and
the decomposition, neither of which depends on this correction. §2.1 reports
q = 0.045 among the 30, the full-space q, and says plainly that the latter does
not clear. Sheba's negative then costs nothing further, because nothing rests on
the discovery p-value.")
cat("\n---- the reading, fixed before the result was seen ----\n", READ[[verdict]], "\n")
write.csv(res, file.path(d, "full_space_scored.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## B1d — distinct fdr

the FDR column on DISTINCT sets

Source: `B1d_distinct_fdr.R`

```{r B1d_distinct_fdr, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B1d — the FDR column on DISTINCT sets
## ============================================================================
##
## Why. 63 of the 565 sets in the correction family carry a member list
## identical to another set's under a different name. Two sets with the same
## members are ONE test, so the family is 502 and the Benjamini-Hochberg
## calculation should run over that.
##
## THE DIRECTION IS NOT PREDICTABLE, and an earlier note in this project claimed
## it was. Duplicating a test duplicates its p-value, which raises BOTH the
## denominator m AND the rank of that p, and BH is p * m / rank. For a duplicated
## SMALL p the rank effect dominates and the as-counted q is too SMALL; for
## duplicates at large p the denominator dominates and it is too large. Simulated
## at this table's scale the correction spans 0.95x to 1.78x depending only on
## where the duplicates sit. So this is run to get the right number, not to make
## it smaller, and the result is reported whichever way it moves.
##
## The family-wise value is NOT affected and is not recomputed here. A min-P
## Westfall-Young maximum cannot be inflated by perfectly correlated tests, which
## is part of why that procedure was chosen over Bonferroni.
##
## Nothing here changes a conclusion: nothing in this family approaches 0.05 by
## either route. A q reported larger than it should be is still worth fixing.
##
## Duplicates are identified WITHOUT the member lists. Two sets with the same
## members produce the same NES and the same per-set p by construction, so an
## identical (size, NES, p_set) triple identifies them. The count is checked
## against the 63 the archive's MANIFEST records; if it disagrees, the script
## stops rather than guess.
##
## Run against the scored table from the 10,000-draw run. No session objects
## needed beyond `paths`.

local({

  ## Find the scored table wherever the archive was unpacked. Unzipping creates
  ## nulls_pitt_full/nulls_pitt_full/, so a fixed path list misses it; search
  ## instead. BOTH scored files live side by side and they are NOT
  ## interchangeable: full_space_scored.csv is the 1,000-draw run and
  ## full_space_scored_10k.csv the 10,000-draw one. The manuscript quotes the
  ## 10,000-draw values throughout, so this refuses to use the smaller run
  ## silently.
  f <- Sys.getenv("ICB_SCORED_10K")
  if (!nzchar(f) || !file.exists(f)) {
    found <- list.files(paths$out_dir, pattern = "^full_space_scored(_10k)?\\.csv$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
    if (length(found)) {
      cat("scored tables found:\n"); for (x in found) cat("  ", x, "\n", sep = "")
      tenk <- found[grepl("_10k\\.csv$", found)]
      if (length(tenk)) f <- tenk[1] else {
        cat("\nB1d STOPPED: only the 1,000-draw table is present.\n",
            "  full_space_scored_10k.csv is the run the manuscript reports, and the\n",
            "  two give different p-values (O_chap 0.0030 against 0.0078). Point\n",
            "  ICB_SCORED_10K at the 10,000-draw table, or re-score it.\n", sep = "")
        return(invisible())
      }
    } else f <- NA_character_
  }
  if (is.na(f) || !file.exists(f)) {
    cat("B1d SKIPPED: no scored table under ", paths$out_dir, ".\n",
        "  Set ICB_SCORED_10K to full_space_scored_10k.csv.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  cat("using: ", f, "\n", sep = "")
  d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  need <- c("pathway", "size", "NES", "p_set")
  if (!all(need %in% names(d)))
    stop("scored table lacks: ", paste(setdiff(need, names(d)), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  cat("scored table: ", basename(f), " (", nrow(d), " sets)\n", sep = "")

  key <- paste(d$size, round(d$NES, 10), round(d$p_set, 10))
  dup <- sum(duplicated(key))
  cat(sprintf("distinct member lists: %d; redundant rows: %d\n", length(unique(key)), dup))
  if (dup != 63)
    cat(sprintf("  NOTE: the archive MANIFEST records 63 duplicate member lists, not %d.\n", dup),
        "  Proceeding, but reconcile this before quoting the corrected q.\n", sep = "")

  ## BH over one row per distinct member list, then written back to every row
  ## that shares it, so each named set still reports a q.
  ## The BH values come back in the order of the FIRST-OCCURRENCE rows, so they
  ## must be indexed as their own vector. Writing them into a 565-length vector
  ## and then indexing that by match() reads positions 1..502 of the long vector,
  ## which are not the first-occurrence positions: every set receives some other
  ## set's q. That produced a table where a set at P = 0.090 carried a smaller q
  ## than one at P = 0.0078, which BH can never do.
  first  <- !duplicated(key)
  q_head <- p.adjust(d$p_set[first], "BH")        # length = number of distinct sets
  q_dist <- q_head[match(key, key[first])]        # broadcast back to every row
  d$q_distinct <- q_dist

  ## BH is monotone in p by construction. If this fails the mapping is wrong.
  o <- order(d$p_set)
  if (any(diff(q_dist[o]) < -1e-9))
    stop("q_distinct is not monotone in p_set — the duplicate mapping is wrong.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (any(is.na(q_dist)))
    stop(sum(is.na(q_dist)), " sets received no q.", call. = FALSE)

  old <- if ("q_bh" %in% names(d)) d$q_bh else p.adjust(d$p_set, "BH")
  cat(sprintf("\nminimum q: %.4f as counted (%d sets) -> %.4f on distinct sets (%d)\n",
              min(old, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(d), min(q_dist, na.rm = TRUE), sum(first)))

  ## RANK MUST BE ON DISTINCT SETS TOO. "8th of 565" counts a set twice whenever
  ## two names share a member list — the GrpE KO and its Pfam domain are one such
  ## pair, both at NES -2.22 and p 0.0046, sitting above the reported sets. A
  ## duplicate is not independent evidence that a set is extreme, so the rank a
  ## reader should see is the one among distinct member lists.
  d$rank_counted  <- rank(d$p_set, ties.method = "min")
  rd <- rank(d$p_set[first], ties.method = "min")
  d$rank_distinct <- rd[match(key, key[first])]
  cat(sprintf("\nrank of the most extreme set: %d of %d as counted -> %d of %d distinct\n",
              min(d$rank_counted), nrow(d), min(d$rank_distinct), sum(first)))

  key_sets <- c("reported:O_chap", "reported:chaperones", "reported:O", "reported:ribosomal")
  i <- match(key_sets, d$pathway); i <- i[!is.na(i)]
  if (length(i)) {
    cat("\nthe reported sets:\n")
    print(data.frame(set = d$pathway[i], NES = round(d$NES[i], 2),
                     P = signif(d$p_set[i], 3),
                     rank_counted = d$rank_counted[i],
                     rank_distinct = d$rank_distinct[i],
                     q_as_counted = round(old[i], 4),
                     q_distinct = round(q_dist[i], 4), row.names = NULL))
    cat(sprintf("\n  the manuscript should quote rank %d of %d (distinct member lists),\n",
                d$rank_distinct[i][1], sum(first)),
        sprintf("  not %d of %d, which counts duplicate sets as separate evidence.\n",
                d$rank_counted[i][1], nrow(d)), sep = "")
  }
  cat("\nThe family-wise value is unchanged and is not recomputed here.\n")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B1d_distinct_fdr"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  write.csv(d, file.path(od, "full_space_scored_10k_distinct.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("written to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b1d_distinct <<- d
})
```

## B12 — sheba coupling

own versus stranger, and the clade test, in Sheba.

Source: `B12_sheba_coupling.R`

```{r B12_sheba_coupling, eval=FALSE}
## B12 — own versus stranger, and the clade test, in Sheba.
##
## WHY THIS IS THE ONE CROSS-COHORT TEST THE CONFOUNDING DOES NOT REACH.
## The cohorts share nothing upstream of the FASTQ and mzML files: preservation
## (RNAlater against frozen), extraction laboratory and protocol, and instrument
## all differ, and every cross-cohort composition comparison in this project is
## constrained by that. This design is not. It compares patient i's metagenome
## against patient i's proteome, versus patient j's metagenome against patient
## i's proteome, with i and j BOTH IN SHEBA. Any cohort-level bias — preservation,
## extraction, platform, database scale, annotation depth — enters both pairings
## identically and cancels. What crosses cohorts is the QUESTION, not the
## measurement. If the coupling reproduces here, Pillar 1 stops being a
## Pittsburgh observation and becomes the only replicated finding in the paper.
##
## Both tests are response-free,
## so the cohorts' different timepoints and outcome definitions do not matter,
## and nothing is compared against Pittsburgh, so no shared database is needed.
## Two claims are on offer, not one — generic weak coupling (§2.3) and the
## Bacteroidota clade specificity — and Sheba tests them at a different site,
## against a different search database, at a different acquisition.
##
## Requires S10_sheba_ko_regroup.sh to have run. Point SHEBA_KO at its joined
## table. §2.9 reports 24 Sheba metagenome-proteome pairs in mixtures 3-5, which
## is the expected n; anything much larger means the pairing is wrong.
##
## Run after §10 and §12 of analysis_v17.Rmd.

need <- c("OS", "annot_new", "sh_set5", "mp")   # sh_id no longer used: the link is BioReplicate
miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss)) stop("run analysis_v17.Rmd §12 first; missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
## WHICH TABLE, and why. Pittsburgh's ko_cpm is built from the RAW regrouped
## merge (merged_genefamilies_ko.tsv): §10c filters stratified rows and
## UNMAPPED/UNGROUPED, and only THEN computes CPM in R, so the denominator is the
## sum over retained KO rows. HUMAnN's own renormalisation never enters it. The
## matching Sheba table is therefore the un-renormalised join, and the same
## transform is applied below.
##
## It would be easy to think the choice does not matter: the coupling statistic
## is Spearman, which is invariant to any per-sample scaling, so arms [1] and [2]
## give identical correlations from either table. But the variable-core selection
## uses each KO's SD ACROSS patients, which is not invariant — a different
## normalisation selects a different 200 KOs, and that is the powered arm. Use
## the un-renormalised table.
if (!exists("SHEBA_KO")) {
  cand <- file.path(paths$out_dir,
    c("sheba_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv",             # dropped straight into final_run
      "sheba_ko/sheba_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv",    # S10's own layout
      "sheba_ko_cpm_joined.tsv",                      # the renormalised one — wrong, see above
      "sheba_ko/sheba_ko_cpm_joined.tsv"))
  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (!length(hit))
    stop("no Sheba KO table found. Looked for:\n  ", paste(cand, collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nRun S10_sheba_ko_regroup.sh, or set SHEBA_KO / ICB_SHEBA_KO.", call. = FALSE)
  SHEBA_KO <- hit[1]
  if (grepl("cpm_joined", basename(SHEBA_KO)))
    warning("using the RENORMALISED table (", basename(SHEBA_KO), "). Pittsburgh's ",
            "ko_cpm is built from the un-renormalised merge, so the variable-core ",
            "selection in arm [2] will not match. Prefer ",
            "sheba_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv.", call. = FALSE)
}
cat("KO table:", SHEBA_KO, "\n")
if (!file.exists(SHEBA_KO)) stop("no KO table at ", SHEBA_KO, " — run S10_sheba_ko_regroup.sh first")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(stringr) })
OUT <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else ".", "B12_sheba_coupling")
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
set.seed(1201); EPS <- 1e-9; MIN_KO <- 30L

## ---- the metagenome side ----------------------------------------------------
raw <- read.delim(SHEBA_KO, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(raw)[1] <- "feature"
raw <- raw |>
  filter(!grepl("^(UNMAPPED|UNGROUPED)", feature),   # exactly as §10c drops them
         !grepl("\\|", feature))                      # unstratified rows only
KO <- as.matrix(raw[, -1, drop = FALSE]); rownames(KO) <- sub(":.*$", "", raw$feature)
colnames(KO) <- sub("_Abundance.*$", "", sub("_genefamilies.*$", "", colnames(KO)))
## ONE KEY EVERYWHERE. The three tables name the same library three ways:
## KO columns  104_S22_R1_kneaddata_merged
## MetaPhlAn   104_S22_merged_filtered_R1_kneaddata_paired_1
## sh_set5$raw whichever of those §10e picked up
## Reduce all of them to <id>_<ME|S#>. Without this the FAILED drop below matches
## nothing, and the pairing silently finds either no KO columns (arms [1] and [2]
## stop) or no MetaPhlAn columns (arm [3] prints "not run").
key <- function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)
colnames(KO) <- key(colnames(KO))

## Four libraries failed and must go before anything is normalised over them.
FAILED <- c("92_S19", "98_S21", "154_S27", "745_S10")
drop <- intersect(FAILED, colnames(KO))
if (length(drop)) {
  cat("dropping failed libraries:", paste(drop, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  KO <- KO[, setdiff(colnames(KO), drop), drop = FALSE]
}
## Columns that are empty or near-empty would give a CPM denominator of ~0.
tot <- colSums(KO, na.rm = TRUE)
if (any(tot <= 0)) {
  cat("dropping empty columns:", paste(colnames(KO)[tot <= 0], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  KO <- KO[, tot > 0, drop = FALSE]; tot <- tot[tot > 0]
}
## CPM within sample over the RETAINED rows — §10c's transform, applied here so
## the two cohorts' tables are built the same way.
KO <- sweep(KO, 2, tot, "/") * 1e6
cat(sprintf("Sheba KO table: %d KOs x %d samples after filtering; CPM within sample\n",
            nrow(KO), ncol(KO)))
## What fraction of each sample's gene-family abundance carries a KO. Low in both
## cohorts — the UniClust90 families largely have no KO mapping — and reported so
## the comparison is not read as a Sheba-specific shortfall.
##
## The denominator is 1e6, not the column sum of the file. HUMAnN 4 gene families
## are CPM and sum to 1,000,000 per sample, so the KO-mapped share is tot / 1e6.
## Summing the file instead adds UNGROUPED — which carries the raw count of
## unmapped reads — and the per-species stratified rows, which duplicate the
## unstratified totals. That gave 0.20%% against a true 5.3%%, and printing it
## beside Pittsburgh's 7.8%% would have invented the very shortfall this line
## exists to rule out.
cat(sprintf("  KO-mapped share of gene-family abundance: median %.1f%% over %d samples (Pittsburgh MF0015 7.8%%)\n",
            100 * median(tot / 1e6, na.rm = TRUE), length(tot)))
stopifnot(nrow(KO) > 500, ncol(KO) > 10)

## ---- the proteome side, KO-summed the same way as Pittsburgh ----------------
## WHICH CHANNELS. OS is the sheba_ontx arm — the superseded MS2 design, 29
## channels. The PRE-SPECIFIED primary is the pooled set (35 patients), and §12c
## found 30 of them with a metagenome profile at the 5M floor. Using OS discards
## about a fifth of the available pairs for no stated reason, so the pooled set
## is the default here; B12_USE_POOLED <- FALSE reverts to OS.
if (!exists("B12_USE_POOLED")) B12_USE_POOLED <- TRUE
PD <- NULL
if (isTRUE(B12_USE_POOLED)) {
  pf <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "sheba_pooled", "null_input.RData")
  if (file.exists(pf)) {
    e <- new.env(); load(pf, envir = e)
    cdp <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(e$qf$sheba))
    use <- as.character(cdp$Mixture) %in% e$KEEP_S & !cdp$is_norm & !cdp$excluded &
           !is.na(cdp$resp)
    PD <- list(a  = SummarizedExperiment::assay(e$qf$sheba, "psms"),
               rd = as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(e$qf$sheba[["psms"]])),
               d  = tibble::rownames_to_column(cdp[use, , drop = FALSE], "sample"))
    cat(sprintf("proteome: pooled pre-specified set, %d channels\n", nrow(PD$d)))
  } else cat("proteome: pooled set requested but not found at ", pf, " — using OS\n")
}
if (is.null(PD)) { PD <- OS; cat(sprintf("proteome: OS / sheba_ontx, %d channels\n", nrow(OS$d))) }

ko_of <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "sheba"],
                  annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "sheba"])
rw <- tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(PD$a)), protein = PD$rd$Protein) |>
  mutate(ko = unname(ko_of[protein])) |> filter(!is.na(ko))
Msum <- rowsum(PD$a[rw$row, PD$d$sample, drop = FALSE], group = rw$ko, na.rm = TRUE)
MPs  <- sweep(Msum, 2, colSums(Msum, na.rm = TRUE), "/")
cat(sprintf("Sheba proteome: %d KOs x %d channels\n", nrow(MPs), ncol(MPs)))

## ---- pair them --------------------------------------------------------------
## THE LINK IS BioReplicate, NOT THE SAMPLE NAME. OS$d$sample is a proteome
## channel — "3_128C", Mixture_Channel — so sh_id() on it returns id = "3" and
## family = NA, and the join to sh_set5 on (id, family) matched nothing: 0 pairs
## against 1,116 shared KOs. The proteome is keyed by channel and the metagenome
## by patient probe; the annotation is what joins them, exactly as §12c builds
## mp_probe.
if (!exists("mnum")) mnum <- function(x) gsub("\\D", "", as.character(x))
ann_s <- mp$sheba_annot_use |>
  distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate) |>
  mutate(k = paste(mnum(Mixture), as.character(Channel)))
lk <- PD$d |> select(sample, Mixture, Channel) |>
  mutate(k     = paste(mnum(Mixture), as.character(Channel)),
         bio   = ann_s$BioReplicate[match(k, ann_s$k)],
         probe = sub("[abc]$", "", tolower(trimws(bio))))
if (anyNA(lk$bio))
  stop(sum(is.na(lk$bio)), " proteome channels have no BioReplicate in ",
       "mp$sheba_annot_use — the Mixture/Channel keys disagree.", call. = FALSE)
## sh_set5 already holds one profile per patient (the rule fixed in
## PRESPEC_sheba_replication.md: earliest pre-treatment episode), which is what
## resolves one probe appearing as both
## its ME and S2 libraries. Assert it rather than assume it — a duplicated patient here
## would silently put one person on both sides of the own/mismatched comparison.
pairs <- lk |>
  inner_join(sh_set5 |> select(probe, raw, patient), by = "probe") |>
  mutate(mg = key(raw)) |>
  filter(mg %in% colnames(KO), sample %in% colnames(MPs)) |>
  distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE)
## ---- ARTEFACT CHECKS, before any coupling is computed -----------------------
## A false failure to replicate is the expensive outcome here, so the three ways
## this design differs from Pittsburgh's are measured rather than assumed.
##
## (i) SAME STOOL, OR ONLY SAME PATIENT? Pittsburgh's A1 joins on BioReplicate,
##     an MF number — a SAMPLE id — so its two layers come from one stool. Here
##     the join is proteome channel -> patient probe -> sh_set5, and sh_set5 took
##     the earliest pre-treatment episode per PATIENT. If a patient gave more
##     than one tube, the two layers are different collections, and the coupling
##     is attenuated for a biological reason with no measurement fault at all.
if (exists("tim")) {
  tub <- tim |> filter(probe_key %in% pairs$probe) |>
    group_by(probe_key) |> summarise(n_tubes = n_distinct(collected[nzchar(collected)]),
                                     .groups = "drop")
  multi <- sum(tub$n_tubes > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("\n  (i) tubes per paired patient: %d of %d have more than one\n",
              multi, nrow(tub)))
  if (multi > 0)
    cat("      -> the metagenome and proteome may be different collections for\n",
        "         those patients. Pittsburgh pairs one stool; this does not.\n", sep = "")
} else cat("\n  (i) tube check skipped: `tim` not in the session\n")

## (ii) ARE THE TWO LAYERS FROM THE SAME SIDE OF TREATMENT? §0a assigns Sheba
##      mixtures 3-5 to the on-treatment arm by falling back to mixture
##      membership when timing is missing, while the metagenome records mark the
##      S-series tubes pre-treatment. If those disagree, this correlates an
##      on-treatment proteome against a pre-treatment metagenome.
## sh_set5 is BUILT by filtering to pre-treatment, so counting `pre` in it is
## tautological. What matters is the proteome side: whether the channels paired
## here carry arm labels that disagree with the metagenome's timing.
cat(sprintf("  (ii) proteome arm labels among paired channels: %s\n",
            paste(names(table(as.character(PD$d$arm))), table(as.character(PD$d$arm)),
                  sep = "=", collapse = ", ")))
cat("       (all metagenome profiles are pre-treatment by construction; §0a assigns\n",
    "       Sheba mixtures 3-5 to the on-treatment arm by MIXTURE when timing is\n",
    "       missing, so an `ontx` label here does not establish on-treatment\n",
    "       sampling — the metagenome records mark the S-series tubes pre-treatment.)\n",
    sep = "")

## (iii) WHICH PROTEOME SET? OS is the sheba_ontx arm — the SUPERSEDED MS2
##       design. The pre-specified primary is the pooled set (§12c: 35 patients,
##       30 with a profile at the 5M floor). Using OS costs about a fifth of the
##       available pairs. Set B12_USE_POOLED to switch.
cat(sprintf("  (iii) proteome set: %s, %d channels\n",
            if (isTRUE(B12_USE_POOLED) && !identical(PD, OS)) "pooled (pre-specified primary)" else "OS / sheba_ontx",
            ncol(MPs)))

## Where the pairing loses samples, stated step by step — "0 pairs" on its own
## says nothing about which join failed.
cat(sprintf("  pairing: %d proteome channels -> %d with a probe -> %d matched to a\n    profile -> %d with a KO column\n",
            nrow(lk), sum(!is.na(lk$probe)),
            sum(lk$probe %in% sh_set5$probe),
            nrow(pairs)))
.unmatched <- setdiff(key(sh_set5$raw), colnames(KO))
if (length(.unmatched))
  cat(sprintf("  NOTE: %d of %d sh_set5 profiles have no KO column: %s\n",
              length(.unmatched), nrow(sh_set5),
              paste(head(.unmatched, 6), collapse = ", ")))
if (anyDuplicated(pairs$patient))
  stop("a patient appears twice in the pairing: ",
       paste(unique(pairs$patient[duplicated(pairs$patient)]), collapse = ", "),
       "\nsh_set5 should carry one profile per patient.", call. = FALSE)
kos_s <- intersect(rownames(MPs), rownames(KO))
cat(sprintf("\npaired patients: %d (expected about 24, mixtures %s)\n  shared KOs: %d\n",
            nrow(pairs), paste(sort(unique(as.character(pairs$Mixture))), collapse = ","), length(kos_s)))
if (nrow(pairs) < 10 || length(kos_s) < 200)
  stop("too few pairs or shared KOs to test: ", nrow(pairs), " / ", length(kos_s))

## ---- own against every mismatched pairing -----------------------------------
coup <- function(k, i, j) {
  x <- MPs[k, pairs$sample[i]]; y <- KO[k, pairs$mg[j]]
  ok <- is.finite(x) & x > 0 & is.finite(y)
  if (sum(ok) < MIN_KO) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[ok] + EPS), log(y[ok] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
}
K <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(j)
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) coup(kos_s, i, j), 0), numeric(nrow(pairs)))
own <- diag(K)
## MEDIAN, not mean — A1 uses the median of the mismatched row in Pittsburgh, and
## the two cohorts' headline numbers must be the same statistic to be comparable.
mis <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
rk  <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) mean(K[i, -i] >= own[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(own, mis, paired = TRUE))
cat(sprintf("\n[1] own %.3f against mismatched %.3f; delta %+.4f, own higher in %d of %d, p = %.4g\n    patients with own-p < 0.05: %d\n",
            median(own, na.rm = TRUE), median(mis, na.rm = TRUE),
            median(own - mis, na.rm = TRUE), sum(own > mis, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(pairs),
            w$p.value, sum(rk < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)))
## POWER, stated before the result. Pittsburgh's full-profile delta is +0.006 at
## n = 47 and did not reach significance THERE; at this n it cannot. The
## variable-core arm is the test — +0.033, p = 0.00028 at n = 47. Read [2] first.

## ---- the same on the most variable core KOs ---------------------------------
Gs <- KO[kos_s, pairs$mg, drop = FALSE]
core <- names(which(rowMeans(Gs > 0) >= 0.9))
sdc  <- apply(log1p(Gs[core, , drop = FALSE]), 1, sd)
top  <- core[order(-sdc)][seq_len(min(200, length(core)))]
Kt <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(j)
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) coup(top, i, j), 0), numeric(nrow(pairs)))
ot <- diag(Kt)
mt <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) median(Kt[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
rkt <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) mean(Kt[i, -i] >= ot[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(ot, mt, paired = TRUE))
cat(sprintf("\n[2] top %d variable core KOs: delta %+.4f, own higher in %d of %d, p = %.4g\n    patients with own-p < 0.05: %d\n",
            length(top), median(ot - mt, na.rm = TRUE), sum(ot > mt, na.rm = TRUE),
            nrow(pairs), wt$p.value, sum(rkt < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)))

## ---- verdict, fixed before the result is seen -------------------------------
## [2b] supplies the power figures the third branch quotes. If it did not run —
## an older copy of this script, or an error above — say so rather than indexing
## objects that may be something else entirely.
if (!exists("B12_POWER") || !is.numeric(B12_POWER)) {
  B12_SHIFTS <- c(0.033); B12_POWER <- NA_real_; mde <- NA_real_
  cat("\nNOTE: [2b] did not run, so the power figures below are unavailable.\n")
}
## Turns on the POWERED arm. [1] cannot resolve at this n and is context.
d_top <- median(ot - mt, na.rm = TRUE)
gen_rep <- wt$p.value < 0.05 && d_top > 0
cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", if (gen_rep)
"REPLICATES. Weak, patient-specific coupling is present in a second cohort at a
different site, against a different search database and a different acquisition,
and it is again carried by the variable KOs rather than the full profile. Because
both pairings are within Sheba, the cohort-level differences that constrain every
other cross-cohort comparison in this study cancel here. Pillar 1 becomes a
two-cohort result and the only replicated finding in the paper: lead with it, and
say why this design is immune to the confounding that limits the rest." else if (d_top > 0)
sprintf("POSITIVE IN SIGN ONLY. The powered arm's estimate is %+.4f against
Pittsburgh's +0.033 — an order of magnitude smaller — with own higher in %d of
%d and p = %.2f. This is not a replication and should not be reported as one.
Whether it is a failure to replicate or a failure to measure cannot be settled
here: the overall coupling in this cohort is itself about half Pittsburgh's
(own %.3f against 0.238), on fewer shared gene families and a lower KO-mapped
share, so the quantity being tested is weaker before any comparison is made.",
d_top, sum(ot > mt, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(pairs), wt$p.value,
median(diag(K), na.rm = TRUE)) else
sprintf("DOES NOT REPLICATE. The powered arm gives %+.4f — no advantage for a
patient's own metagenome, own higher in %d of %d. Read this with [2b] and not
without it: the estimate is negative, and the design resolves a Pittsburgh-sized
shift only %.0f%% of the time, needing %s to reach 80%%. What can be said is that
this test does not detect the effect and cannot rule it out; what cannot be said
is that it trends toward replication.",
d_top, sum(ot > mt, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(pairs),
100 * B12_POWER[which.min(abs(B12_SHIFTS - 0.033))],
if (is.na(mde)) paste0(">", max(B12_SHIFTS)) else sprintf("%+.3f", mde)), "\n")
## ---- [2b] what this test could and could not have seen ----------------------
## "Does not replicate" and "cannot tell" are different claims, and only one of
## them is supportable without this. Two quantities decide which:
##
##   (a) a bootstrap interval on the observed delta. If Pittsburgh's +0.033 lies
##       INSIDE it, the data are compatible with that effect and with none, and
##       the honest statement is that the test is uninformative at this
##       precision. If it lies OUTSIDE, the design did have the resolution and
##       the effect is not there — a different and stronger statement.
##
##   (b) the delta this design could detect. Resample Sheba's own coupling matrix
##       to Pittsburgh-sized shifts and ask how often each is recovered at
##       p < 0.05. That gives the smallest effect this n could have seen, rather
##       than asserting underpowered.
##
## Neither rescues the result. Both make its limits quantitative instead of
## rhetorical, which is what the manuscript can actually use.
## Names here are deliberately ugly. `pw` collides with §10d's pathway tibble and
## `grid` with the package of that name, and a collision does not error — it
## silently hands the verdict the wrong object, which is how this failed with
## "comparison (==) is possible only for atomic and list types".
B12_NB <- 2000L
dif <- ot - mt                                   # per-patient delta, powered arm
set.seed(1202)
bs <- replicate(B12_NB, median(sample(dif, length(dif), replace = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
ci <- quantile(bs, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
PITT_DELTA <- 0.0333
inside <- PITT_DELTA >= ci[1] && PITT_DELTA <= ci[2]
cat(sprintf("\n[2b] bootstrap on the powered arm: delta %+.4f, 95%% CI %+.4f to %+.4f (%d draws)\n",
            median(dif, na.rm = TRUE), ci[1], ci[2], B12_NB))
cat(sprintf("     Pittsburgh's %+.4f lies %s this interval\n",
            PITT_DELTA, if (inside) "INSIDE" else "OUTSIDE"))

## Detectable effect: shift each patient's delta by d and re-test, so the null
## variance is Sheba's own rather than an assumed one.
B12_SHIFTS <- c(0.005, 0.010, 0.020, 0.033, 0.050, 0.075)
B12_POWER <- vapply(B12_SHIFTS, function(d) {
  mean(replicate(400L, {
    x <- sample(dif, length(dif), replace = TRUE) + d
    suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x)$p.value) < 0.05
  }), na.rm = TRUE)
}, 0)
print(data.frame(shift = B12_SHIFTS, power = round(B12_POWER, 2)))
mde <- if (any(B12_POWER >= 0.8)) B12_SHIFTS[which(B12_POWER >= 0.8)[1]] else NA_real_
cat(sprintf("     smallest shift detected in 80%% of resamples: %s\n",
            if (is.na(mde)) paste0("> ", max(B12_SHIFTS)) else sprintf("%+.3f", mde)))
cat("     READING: if the discovery cohort's effect lies inside the CI AND below\n",
    "     the detectable shift, this test is uninformative about it and the\n",
    "     manuscript should say exactly that — not that the effect is absent,\n",
    "     and not that it trends.\n", sep = "")

## ---- [2c] RETIRED 27 Sep 2026 — moved to B14 --------------------------------
## This compared Pittsburgh's per-patient deltas against `dif`, but the two were
## different arms: `dif` is Sheba's POWERED arm (200 most variable gene
## families) while the Pittsburgh object it read — cpl_pat, and after a fix that
## never landed, cpl_stats — holds the FULL-PROFILE deltas. It never ran, because
## its condition looked for columns cpl_pat does not carry, and that failure was
## the only thing preventing a mismatched comparison. B14 computes both cohorts'
## per-patient deltas at both resolutions and tests the cohort difference arm by
## arm, which is the comparison this was meant to be.
cat("\n[2c] retired: the cohort-difference test runs in B14, arm by arm.\n")

## NAMES ARE PREFIXED b12_ BECAUSE THIS SCRIPT IS SOURCED INTO THE KNIT.
## `source(..., local = TRUE)` inside a knitr chunk evaluates in the knit
## environment, so every top-level assignment here overwrites a global of the
## same name. MGg, MGm, MPg and clr all collide with section 11c, and MGm in
## particular was silently replaced by this arm's 30-patient Sheba matrix — which
## then went into figure_inputs.rds under the Pittsburgh name and broke C2 with
## "0 channels in both layers". Do not reintroduce a bare name here.
## ---- [3] the clade arm, and what it is exposed to ---------------------------
## Mirrors B6: per genus, within patients, MetaPhlAn abundance against proteome
## abundance, on centred log-ratios. Unlike [1] and [2] this arm is NOT immune to
## the handling difference — Sheba's metagenomic Bacteroidota is ~3% against
## Pittsburgh's ~35% on the same database and read length, so if the handling
## that produces that also depletes Bacteroidota reads, a decoupling here is
## induced rather than replicated. Run it, report it with the caveat attached.
cl <- NULL
if (all(vapply(c("pep_g_s", "pep_ph_s", "sh_mpa_raw"), exists, logical(1)))) {
  b12_clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  b12_gen <- count(pep_g_s, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  ## pep_g_s$row indexes OS$a, so the clade arm stays on OS even when the
  ## coupling arms use the pooled proteome. Take the channels the two share, and
  ## carry that vector through — assigning pairs$sample as rownames after an
  ## intersect would silently mislabel every row.
  cs <- intersect(pairs$sample, colnames(OS$a))
  if (length(cs) < 10) {
    cat(sprintf("\n[3] clade arm not run: only %d paired channels are in OS\n", length(cs)))
    cl <- NULL
  } else {
  b12_den <- sapply(b12_gen, function(g)
    colSums(OS$a[pep_g_s$row[pep_g_s$tax == g], cs, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  rownames(b12_den) <- cs
  b12_MPg <- b12_den / rowSums(b12_den)
  b12_MGg <- sh_mpa_raw |>
    filter(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 5, grepl("\\|g__", clade_name)) |>
    mutate(genus = sub(".*\\|g__", "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
    pivot_longer(-genus, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(raw = key(raw)) |>
    filter(raw %in% pairs$mg, genus %in% b12_gen) |>
    group_by(raw, genus) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = genus, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
  b12_MGm <- as.matrix(b12_MGg[, -1]); rownames(b12_MGm) <- b12_MGg$raw
  gg <- intersect(colnames(b12_MGm), colnames(b12_MPg))
  sm <- pairs$sample[match(rownames(b12_MGm), pairs$mg)]
  keep <- !is.na(sm) & sm %in% rownames(b12_MPg)
  b12_MGm <- b12_MGm[keep, , drop = FALSE]; sm <- sm[keep]
  if (length(gg) >= 6 && length(sm) >= 10 && !anyNA(sm)) {
    A <- b12_clr(b12_MGm[, gg, drop = FALSE]); Bp <- b12_clr(b12_MPg[sm, gg, drop = FALSE])
    b12_phy <- pep_g_s |> select(row, genus = tax) |>
      inner_join(pep_ph_s |> select(row, phylum = tax), by = "row") |>
      count(genus, phylum) |> group_by(genus) |> slice_max(n, n = 1) |> ungroup()
    cl <- tibble(genus = gg, phylum = b12_phy$phylum[match(gg, b12_phy$genus)],
                 rho = vapply(gg, function(g) suppressWarnings(
                   cor(A[, g], Bp[, g], method = "spearman")), 0))
    md <- function(p) median(cl$rho[cl$phylum %in% p], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("\n[3] clade arm: %d genera over %d patients (CLR)\n    Bacteroidota %+.3f | Bacillota %+.3f\n",
                nrow(cl), nrow(A), md("Bacteroidota"), md(c("Bacillota", "Firmicutes"))))
    cat("    CAVEAT: this arm is exposed to the handling difference (see above).\n",
        "    It bounds the claim; it does not confirm it.\n", sep = "")
  } else cat(sprintf("\n[3] clade arm not run: %d shared genera, %d patients\n",
                     length(gg), length(sm)))
  }
} else cat("\n[3] clade arm not run: needs pep_g_s, pep_ph_s and sh_mpa_raw from \u00a710e/\u00a75c\n")

saveRDS(list(K = K, own = own, mis = mis, pairs = pairs, top = top,
             K_top = Kt, own_top = ot, mis_top = mt, clade = cl,
             delta = dif, boot_ci = ci,
             power_grid = data.frame(shift = B12_SHIFTS, power = B12_POWER),
             mde = mde, pitt_delta = PITT_DELTA, pitt_inside_ci = inside),
        file.path(OUT, "sheba_coupling.rds"))
cat("\nwritten to", OUT, "\n")
```

## B13 — sheba clade

R3 in the second cohort: does Bacillota couple between layers and

Source: `B13_sheba_clade.R`

```{r B13_sheba_clade, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B13 — R3 in the second cohort: does Bacillota couple between layers and
##       Bacteroidota not?
## ============================================================================
##
## READ THIS FIRST. THIS IS NOT A BLIND TEST.
## B12's arm [3] has already run this analysis on 30 Sheba patients and returned
## Bacteroidota +0.236, Bacillota +0.203 — no clade gap, a slight inversion. It
## is the same procedure as section 11c: per genus, within patients, MetaPhlAn
## abundance against proteome abundance on centred log-ratios, median by clade.
## (A reviewer described B12 [3] as a gene-family own-versus-stranger test. It
## is not; the code is unambiguous.)
##
## So this script cannot confirm or refute R3 in a way B12 [3] has not already
## informed, and it must not be reported as though it could. What it can do is
## establish whether B12 [3]'s answer reflects the cohort or differences in
## procedure, with every arm and the decision rule written before it runs:
##
##   [A] REPRODUCTION  B12 [3] exactly: Sheba's native MetaPhlAn (vJun23). Must
##                     reproduce B12's per-genus values, or nothing below is
##                     comparable and the script stops.
##   [B] PRIMARY       the one procedural difference from section 11c that matters:
##                     Pittsburgh's own database, mpa_vJan25, from the full
##                     46-library re-profiling. Everything else as [A].
##   [C] SENSITIVITY   [B] on the MS2 plexes only. Pittsburgh was acquired by
##                     MS2; Sheba's mixture 1 by SPS-MS3.
##
## Each arm reports the clade gap — Bacillota median minus Bacteroidota median —
## with a bootstrap interval over patients, beside Pittsburgh's gap computed the
## same way on its own data. The reading turns on the INTERVAL, as the coupling
## test's power analysis did: an interval containing both zero and Pittsburgh's
## gap is uninformative, not a failure to replicate.
##
## Two differences from section 11c remain in every arm and cannot be removed:
## Sheba pairs PATIENTS where Pittsburgh pairs STOOLS (7 of 30 gave more than one
## tube), and Sheba's metagenomes carry about a tenth of Pittsburgh's
## Bacteroidota under a different preservation and extraction protocol.
##
## Base R throughout, so that no masked dplyr verb can alter a result.
## Requires, in the analysis session: OS, pep_g_s, pep_ph_s, sh_mpa_raw (section
## 10e), MGm, MPm, gen_coupling (section 11c), and B12's saved output.

local({

  B_BOOT <- 2000L; SEED <- 1301L; FLOOR <- 200L; MIN_CLADE <- 3L
  MS2_MIX <- c("3", "4", "5")

  ## ---- inputs --------------------------------------------------------------
  need <- c("OS", "pep_g_s", "pep_ph_s", "sh_mpa_raw", "MGm", "MPm", "gen_coupling", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B13 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
        ". Run analysis_v17.Rmd through section 11c and B12 first.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f12)) {
    cat("B13 SKIPPED: B12 output not found at ", f12, "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }
  b12 <- readRDS(f12)
  pairs <- as.data.frame(b12$pairs)[, c("sample", "mg")]
  pairs <- pairs[!duplicated(pairs$sample) & !duplicated(pairs$mg), , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("B13: %d paired patients from B12\n", nrow(pairs)))

  ## Pittsburgh's database, re-profiled for all 46 Sheba libraries
  find_vjan <- function() {
    cand <- c(Sys.getenv("ICB_MPA_VJAN25"),
              file.path(paths$out_dir, "merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt"),
              file.path(paths$out_dir, "reprofile", "merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt"),
              file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), "merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt"))
    cand <- cand[nzchar(cand)]
    hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
  }
  f_vjan <- find_vjan()

  ## ---- helpers, base R -----------------------------------------------------
  key <- function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)   # B12's own
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  sp  <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))
  clade <- function(p) ifelse(p %in% c("Bacillota", "Firmicutes"), "Bacillota",
                       ifelse(p %in% "Bacteroidota", "Bacteroidota", "other"))
  gap_of <- function(r, cl) median(r[cl == "Bacillota"], na.rm = TRUE) -
                            median(r[cl == "Bacteroidota"], na.rm = TRUE)

  ## MetaPhlAn merged table -> library x genus, percent
  mg_matrix <- function(tab) {
    tab <- as.data.frame(tab, check.names = FALSE)
    cn  <- as.character(tab[[1]])
    sel <- nchar(gsub("[^|]", "", cn)) == 5 & grepl("\\|g__", cn)
    if (!any(sel)) stop("no genus-level rows in the MetaPhlAn table")
    X <- as.matrix(tab[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    G <- rowsum(X, sub(".*\\|g__", "", cn[sel]))          # genus x library
    M <- t(G); rownames(M) <- key(rownames(M))
    if (anyDuplicated(rownames(M))) M <- rowsum(M, rownames(M))
    M
  }
  read_mpa <- function(f) {
    h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    if (is.na(h)) stop(f, ": no clade_name header")
    t <- read.delim(f, skip = h - 1, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"; t
  }

  ## genus -> phylum, majority over peptide rows (B12's rule)
  jj <- merge(data.frame(row = pep_g_s$row, genus = pep_g_s$tax),
              data.frame(row = pep_ph_s$row, phylum = pep_ph_s$tax), by = "row")
  tb <- table(jj$genus, jj$phylum)
  phy_of <- setNames(colnames(tb)[apply(tb, 1, which.max)], rownames(tb))

  gen_floor <- names(which(table(pep_g_s$tax) >= FLOOR))
  psm_rows  <- table(pep_g_s$tax)

  ## ---- one arm -------------------------------------------------------------
  run_arm <- function(MGlib, chans, label) {
    ## B12 [3] intersects the paired channels with OS$a's columns; so does this
    prs <- pairs[pairs$sample %in% chans & pairs$sample %in% colnames(OS$a) &
                 pairs$mg %in% rownames(MGlib), , drop = FALSE]
    den <- vapply(gen_floor, function(g)
      colSums(OS$a[pep_g_s$row[pep_g_s$tax == g], prs$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
      numeric(nrow(prs)))
    if (nrow(prs) == 1) den <- matrix(den, nrow = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, gen_floor))
    rownames(den) <- prs$sample
    ok <- rowSums(den) > 0
    if (any(!ok)) cat(sprintf("  [%s] dropping %d patient(s) with no evidence in any floor genus\n",
                              label, sum(!ok)))
    den <- den[ok, , drop = FALSE]; prs <- prs[ok, , drop = FALSE]
    MPg <- den / rowSums(den)
    MGm_s <- MGlib[prs$mg, intersect(colnames(MGlib), gen_floor), drop = FALSE]
    rownames(MGm_s) <- prs$sample
    gg <- intersect(colnames(MGm_s), colnames(MPg))
    A  <- clr(MGm_s[, gg, drop = FALSE]); B <- clr(MPg[rownames(MGm_s), gg, drop = FALSE])
    stopifnot(identical(rownames(A), rownames(B)), identical(colnames(A), colnames(B)))
    rho <- vapply(gg, function(g) sp(A[, g], B[, g]), 0)
    cl  <- clade(unname(phy_of[gg]))
    tab <- data.frame(genus = gg, phylum = unname(phy_of[gg]), clade = cl, rho = rho,
                      mg_nonzero = colMeans(MGm_s[, gg, drop = FALSE] > 0),
                      psm_rows = as.integer(psm_rows[gg]), row.names = NULL)
    n_bt <- sum(cl == "Bacteroidota"); n_bc <- sum(cl == "Bacillota")
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] %d patients, %d genera (%d Bacillota, %d Bacteroidota)\n",
                label, nrow(A), length(gg), n_bc, n_bt))
    if (n_bt < MIN_CLADE || n_bc < MIN_CLADE) {
      cat(sprintf("  NOT ESTIMABLE: fewer than %d genera in a clade at the %d-row floor\n",
                  MIN_CLADE, FLOOR))
      return(list(label = label, table = tab, n = nrow(A), gap = NA_real_,
                  ci = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), estimable = FALSE))
    }
    ## zero-inflation: a genus absent from most metagenomes contributes ties, not signal
    thin <- tab$genus[tab$mg_nonzero < 0.5]
    if (length(thin))
      cat("  metagenome non-zero in fewer than half the patients: ",
          paste(sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", thin, 100 * tab$mg_nonzero[tab$genus %in% thin]),
                collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    g0 <- gap_of(rho, cl)
    set.seed(SEED)
    bt <- vapply(seq_len(B_BOOT), function(b) {
      i <- sample.int(nrow(A), nrow(A), replace = TRUE)
      gap_of(vapply(gg, function(g) sp(A[i, g], B[i, g]), 0), cl)
    }, 0)
    ci <- unname(quantile(bt, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE))
    cat(sprintf("  median rho  Bacillota %+.3f | Bacteroidota %+.3f\n",
                median(rho[cl == "Bacillota"], na.rm = TRUE),
                median(rho[cl == "Bacteroidota"], na.rm = TRUE)))
    cat(sprintf("  clade gap %+.3f, 95%% bootstrap interval %+.3f to %+.3f (%d draws)\n",
                g0, ci[1], ci[2], B_BOOT))
    list(label = label, table = tab, n = nrow(A), gap = g0, ci = ci, boot = bt,
         estimable = TRUE)
  }

  ## ---- Pittsburgh, the same way, on its own data -----------------------------
  ph_p <- setNames(gen_coupling$phylum, gen_coupling$genus)[colnames(MGm)]
  Ap <- clr(MGm); Bp <- clr(MPm)
  rho_p <- vapply(colnames(MGm), function(g) sp(Ap[, g], Bp[, g]), 0)
  chk <- max(abs(rho_p - setNames(gen_coupling$rho_clr, gen_coupling$genus)[colnames(MGm)]))
  if (!is.finite(chk) || chk > 1e-8)
    stop("Pittsburgh comparator does not reproduce section 11c (max |diff| ", signif(chk, 3),
         "). MGm may have been overwritten — see figure-inputs' alignment guard.", call. = FALSE)
  cl_p <- clade(unname(ph_p))
  gap_p <- gap_of(rho_p, cl_p)
  set.seed(SEED)
  bt_p <- vapply(seq_len(B_BOOT), function(b) {
    i <- sample.int(nrow(Ap), nrow(Ap), replace = TRUE)
    gap_of(vapply(colnames(Ap), function(g) sp(Ap[i, g], Bp[i, g]), 0), cl_p)
  }, 0)
  ci_p <- unname(quantile(bt_p, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE))
  cat(sprintf("\n[Pittsburgh] %d patients, %d genera; reproduces section 11c exactly\n",
              nrow(Ap), ncol(Ap)))
  cat(sprintf("  clade gap %+.3f, 95%% bootstrap interval %+.3f to %+.3f\n",
              gap_p, ci_p[1], ci_p[2]))

  ## ---- the three arms --------------------------------------------------------
  chans_all <- pairs$sample
  chans_ms2 <- pairs$sample[sub("_[^_]+$", "", pairs$sample) %in% MS2_MIX]
  cat(sprintf("\nchannels: %d paired; %d in MS2 plexes (%s)\n", length(chans_all),
              length(chans_ms2), paste(MS2_MIX, collapse = ", ")))
  if (!length(chans_ms2))
    cat("  WARNING: no paired channel parsed into mixtures ", paste(MS2_MIX, collapse = "/"),
        "; example names: ", paste(head(chans_all, 3), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

  armA <- run_arm(mg_matrix(sh_mpa_raw), chans_all, "A reproduction, vJun23")
  ## [A] must reproduce B12 [3] genus by genus, not only in its medians
  if (!is.null(b12$clade)) {
    ref <- as.data.frame(b12$clade)
    m <- merge(armA$table[, c("genus", "rho")], ref[, c("genus", "rho")], by = "genus",
               suffixes = c("", "_b12"))
    d <- max(abs(m$rho - m$rho_b12), na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("  reproduces B12 [3] on %d of %d genera: max |difference| %.2e\n",
                nrow(m), nrow(ref), d))
    if (nrow(m) < nrow(ref) || !is.finite(d) || d > 1e-6)
      stop("arm A does not reproduce B12 [3]; the arms below would not be comparable.",
           call. = FALSE)
  }

  armB <- armC <- NULL
  if (is.na(f_vjan)) {
    cat("\n[B], [C] NOT RUN: the vJan25 re-profiled table was not found. Put\n",
        "  merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt in ", paths$out_dir,
        " or set ICB_MPA_VJAN25.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("\nvJan25 table: ", f_vjan, "\n", sep = "")
    MG_vjan <- mg_matrix(read_mpa(f_vjan))
    lost <- setdiff(pairs$mg, rownames(MG_vjan))
    if (length(lost)) cat("  paired libraries absent from the vJan25 table: ",
                          paste(lost, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    armB <- run_arm(MG_vjan, chans_all, "B primary, vJan25")
    if (length(chans_ms2)) armC <- run_arm(MG_vjan, chans_ms2, "C MS2 only, vJan25")
  }

  ## ---- the reading, fixed before the run --------------------------------------
  read_arm <- function(a) {
    if (is.null(a) || !isTRUE(a$estimable)) return("not estimable")
    lo <- a$ci[1]; hi <- a$ci[2]
    if (lo > 0 && hi >= gap_p) "replicates"
    else if (lo > 0)           "replicates, smaller"
    else if (hi >= gap_p)      "uninformative"
    else                       "contradicts the discovery magnitude"
  }
  verdicts <- c(A = read_arm(armA), B = read_arm(armB), C = read_arm(armC))
  cat("\n---- reading (decided on B; A and C reported whatever they show) ----\n")
  for (k in names(verdicts)) cat(sprintf("  [%s] %s\n", k, verdicts[[k]]))
  cat("\n", switch(verdicts[["B"]],
    "replicates" =
"The second cohort shows a positive clade gap whose interval includes the
discovery cohort's. Because B12 [3] was seen before this ran, report it as a
procedure-aligned re-analysis that recovers the clade structure, not as a
blind replication — and say what changed from B12 [3].",
    "replicates, smaller" =
"A positive gap in the second cohort, credibly smaller than the discovery
cohort's. The clade ordering holds; its size does not transfer.",
    "uninformative" =
"The interval contains both zero and the discovery cohort's gap. The second
cohort cannot resolve the clade structure either way — the same position as
the coupling test. Report it as uninformative, not as a failure to replicate.",
    "contradicts the discovery magnitude" =
"The interval excludes the discovery cohort's gap and does not exclude zero.
The second cohort does not show the clade structure at the discovery
cohort's size. R3 is then a first-cohort result, and whether that reflects the
cohorts or their handling is open — the metagenomes differ tenfold in
Bacteroidota under different preservation.",
    "not estimable" =
"Too few genera per clade clear the floor in the primary arm. Report that the
second cohort cannot test R3 at this resolution."), "\n", sep = "")

  out <- list(pittsburgh = list(gap = gap_p, ci = ci_p, n = nrow(Ap), rho = rho_p, clade = cl_p),
              A = armA, B = armB, C = armC, verdicts = verdicts,
              vjan25_file = f_vjan, seed = SEED, n_boot = B_BOOT)
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B13_sheba_clade"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(out, file.path(od, "sheba_clade.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b13_clade <<- out
})
```

## B13b — sheba family

the Sheba clade contrast at FAMILY level.

Source: `B13b_sheba_family.R`

```{r B13b_sheba_family, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B13b — the Sheba clade contrast at FAMILY level.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY. B13 is the Sheba arm of the per-GENUS test and computes nothing else, so
## "the comparison is inconclusive in Sheba" rests entirely on three measurable
## Bacteroidota genera. Family level may do better: Sheba's Bacteroidota is 17.4%
## of the proteome against 4.2% of the metagenome, so the peptide evidence is
## there and it is the metagenome side that is thin. Pooling genera into families
## raises evidence per unit and may clear the floor that genus level could not.
##
## WHAT IT IS. B13's run_arm with three substitutions and nothing else changed:
##   pep_g_s -> pep_fa_s,  "\\|g__" -> "\\|f__",  pipe depth 5 -> 4.
## The statistic is CLR per taxon across patients, exactly as B13 and Fig. 2a.
## Raw is reported alongside because the SI quotes both at family level.
##
## RUN IN THE ANALYSIS SESSION. Needs OS, pep_ph_s, pep_tax2, lca_rank2, paths,
## and B12's saved pairs. pep_fa_s does not exist anywhere and is built here —
## it is the one line missing from §10's block, which builds pep_fa for
## Pittsburgh and stops.
##
##   source("B13b_sheba_family.R")
##
## Env: B13B_FLOOR (default 200, B13's FLOOR), B13B_NBOOT (2000), B13B_MPA
## (a Sheba MetaPhlAn merged table; default: sh_mpa_raw from the session).
##
## UNTESTED. Written against B13 and §B8 without being run — there is no R and no
## Sheba data outside the analysis session. Expect to fix paths, not statistics.
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OS", "pep_ph_s", "pep_tax2", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B13b SKIPPED, not in scope:", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n"); return(invisible()) }

  FLOOR <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B13B_FLOOR", "200"))
  NBOOT <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B13B_NBOOT", "2000"))

  ## ---- B12's pairs, as B13 reads them --------------------------------------
  f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f12)) { cat("B13b SKIPPED: no B12 output at ", f12, "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  pairs <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)[, c("sample","mg")]
  pairs <- pairs[!duplicated(pairs$sample) & !duplicated(pairs$mg), , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("B13b: %d paired patients from B12\n", nrow(pairs)))

  ## ---- the missing object ---------------------------------------------------
  pep_fa_s <- pep_tax2(OS, "sheba", "family_name")
  cat(sprintf("pep_fa_s built: %d rows, %.1f%% of the Sheba matrix (genus is %.1f%%)\n",
      nrow(pep_fa_s), 100*nrow(pep_fa_s)/nrow(OS$a),
      if (exists("pep_g_s")) 100*nrow(pep_g_s)/nrow(OS$a) else NA_real_))

  ## ---- helpers, copied from B13 verbatim ------------------------------------
  key <- function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  sp  <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))
  clade <- function(p) ifelse(p %in% c("Bacillota","Firmicutes"), "Bacillota",
                       ifelse(p %in% "Bacteroidota", "Bacteroidota", "other"))
  gap_of <- function(r, cl) median(r[cl=="Bacillota"], na.rm=TRUE) - median(r[cl=="Bacteroidota"], na.rm=TRUE)

  ## B13's mg_matrix, at FAMILY depth: 4 pipes and |f__ instead of 5 and |g__
  mg_matrix_fam <- function(tab) {
    tab <- as.data.frame(tab, check.names = FALSE)
    cn  <- as.character(tab[[1]])
    sel <- nchar(gsub("[^|]", "", cn)) == 4 & grepl("\\|f__", cn)
    if (!any(sel)) stop("no family-level rows in the MetaPhlAn table")
    X <- as.matrix(tab[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    G <- rowsum(X, sub(".*\\|f__", "", cn[sel]))
    M <- t(G); rownames(M) <- key(rownames(M))
    if (anyDuplicated(rownames(M))) M <- rowsum(M, rownames(M))
    M
  }
  read_mpa <- function(f) {
    h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    if (is.na(h)) stop(f, ": no clade_name header")
    t <- read.delim(f, skip = h - 1, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"; t
  }

  mpaf <- Sys.getenv("B13B_MPA")
  tab <- if (nzchar(mpaf)) read_mpa(mpaf) else
         if (exists("sh_mpa_raw")) sh_mpa_raw else
         stop("no Sheba MetaPhlAn table: set B13B_MPA or load sh_mpa_raw")
  MGlib <- mg_matrix_fam(tab)

  ## ---- family -> phylum, majority over peptide rows (B13's rule) ------------
  jj <- merge(data.frame(row = pep_fa_s$row, family = pep_fa_s$tax),
              data.frame(row = pep_ph_s$row, phylum = pep_ph_s$tax), by = "row")
  tb <- table(jj$family, jj$phylum)
  phy_of <- setNames(colnames(tb)[apply(tb, 1, which.max)], rownames(tb))
  fam_floor <- names(which(table(pep_fa_s$tax) >= FLOOR))

  ## ---- B13's run_arm, families in place of genera ---------------------------
  prs <- pairs[pairs$sample %in% colnames(OS$a) & pairs$mg %in% rownames(MGlib), , drop = FALSE]
  den <- vapply(fam_floor, function(t)
    colSums(OS$a[pep_fa_s$row[pep_fa_s$tax == t], prs$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
    numeric(nrow(prs)))
  if (nrow(prs) == 1) den <- matrix(den, nrow = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, fam_floor))
  rownames(den) <- prs$sample
  ok <- rowSums(den) > 0
  if (any(!ok)) cat(sprintf("  dropping %d patient(s) with no evidence in any floor family\n", sum(!ok)))
  den <- den[ok, , drop = FALSE]; prs <- prs[ok, , drop = FALSE]
  MPf <- den / rowSums(den)
  MGm <- MGlib[prs$mg, intersect(colnames(MGlib), fam_floor), drop = FALSE]
  rownames(MGm) <- prs$sample
  ff  <- intersect(colnames(MGm), colnames(MPf))
  MGm <- MGm[, ff, drop = FALSE]; MPf <- MPf[rownames(MGm), ff, drop = FALSE]
  cl  <- clade(unname(phy_of[ff]))

  ## ---- THE GATE, before any correlation is printed --------------------------
  cat(sprintf("\n%d patients, %d families in both layers\n", nrow(MGm), length(ff)))
  print(table(clade = cl))
  nbt <- sum(cl == "Bacteroidota")
  if (nbt < 4) {
    cat(sprintf("\nSTOP: %d Bacteroidota families clear the %d-row floor.\n", nbt, FLOOR))
    cat("A median over fewer than four values with no interval is not a result.\n")
    cat("Report Sheba as unresolved at family level, as it is at genus level.\n")
    cat("Families present:", paste(ff[cl=="Bacteroidota"], collapse=", "), "\n")
    assign("b13b", list(gated = TRUE, n_bacteroidota = nbt, families = ff, clade = cl), envir = .GlobalEnv)
    return(invisible())
  }

  ## ---- the contrast, CLR primary and raw alongside --------------------------
  rho_of <- function(A, B) vapply(colnames(A), function(t) sp(A[,t], B[,t]), 0)
  r_clr <- rho_of(clr(MGm), clr(MPf))
  r_raw <- rho_of(MGm, MPf)
  tab_out <- data.frame(family = ff, phylum = unname(phy_of[ff]), clade = cl,
                        rho_clr = r_clr, rho_raw = r_raw,
                        rows = as.integer(table(pep_fa_s$tax)[ff]))
  print(tab_out[order(tab_out$clade, -tab_out$rho_clr), ], row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

  set.seed(9601); n <- nrow(MGm)
  bs <- function(f) replicate(NBOOT, { i <- sample(n, replace = TRUE)
    gap_of(rho_of(f(MGm[i,,drop=FALSE]), f(MPf[i,,drop=FALSE])), cl) })
  for (nm in c("CLR","raw")) {
    f <- if (nm == "CLR") clr else identity
    g <- gap_of(rho_of(f(MGm), f(MPf)), cl); v <- bs(f)
    q <- quantile(v, c(.025,.975), na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("\n%-4s gap %+.3f  95%% [%+.3f, %+.3f]   Bacillota %+.3f  Bacteroidota %+.3f",
        nm, g, q[1], q[2],
        median(rho_of(f(MGm), f(MPf))[cl=="Bacillota"], na.rm=TRUE),
        median(rho_of(f(MGm), f(MPf))[cl=="Bacteroidota"], na.rm=TRUE)))
  }
  cat("An interval containing both zero and the Pittsburgh value is uninformative,\n")
  cat("not a failure to replicate - the same reading rule the SI fixes for genus.\n")
  assign("b13b", list(gated = FALSE, table = tab_out, n = n, families = ff), envir = .GlobalEnv)
})
```

## B13c — sheba family sweep

what actually limits Sheba at family level, and the floor sweep.

Source: `B13c_sheba_family_sweep.R`

```{r B13c_sheba_family_sweep, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B13c — what actually limits Sheba at family level, and the floor sweep.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS REPLACES B13b's STOP. B13b halted at "2 Bacteroidota families clear
## the 200-row floor" and I read that as the metagenome being the binding
## constraint. That was asserted, not measured, and the 200-row floor is
## calibrated on Pittsburgh's 47 patients, not Sheba's 30. Two separate things
## can exclude a family and B13b did not distinguish them:
##
##   MP side   the family has fewer than FLOOR peptide rows
##   MG side   MetaPhlAn does not report that family in this cohort
##
## This script reports both sides separately, prints every family with its
## correlation regardless of floor, and sweeps the floor. It decides nothing.
##
## A SWEEP IS NOT THRESHOLD-SHOPPING HERE. The main text already reports the
## contrast "across a twentyfold range of evidence thresholds", so a floor sweep
## is the established method for this comparison, not a new post hoc choice made
## after seeing a blocked result. Report the whole sweep, not the best point on
## it.
##
## HOW TO READ IT. A median over two or three families is unstable; the bootstrap
## interval will say so. Report the interval and the family count together, and
## apply the paper's existing rule: an interval containing both zero and the
## Pittsburgh value is uninformative, not a failure to replicate.
##
##   source("B13c_sheba_family_sweep.R")
##
## Env: B13C_FLOORS (default "25,50,100,200,400"), B13C_NBOOT (2000),
##      B13C_MPA (Sheba MetaPhlAn merged table; default sh_mpa_raw).
## UNTESTED against real data.
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OS", "pep_ph_s", "pep_tax2", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B13c SKIPPED, not in scope:", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n"); return(invisible()) }

  FLOORS <- as.integer(strsplit(Sys.getenv("B13C_FLOORS", "25,50,100,200,400"), ",")[[1]])
  NBOOT  <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B13C_NBOOT", "2000"))
  ## B13C_DROP: families to exclude, comma-separated. Use it to ask whether a
  ## conclusion DEPENDS on one family, not to improve a result. Report both runs.
  DROP   <- trimws(strsplit(Sys.getenv("B13C_DROP", ""), ",")[[1]]); DROP <- DROP[nzchar(DROP)]

  f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f12)) { cat("B13c SKIPPED: no B12 output at ", f12, "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  pairs <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)[, c("sample","mg")]
  pairs <- pairs[!duplicated(pairs$sample) & !duplicated(pairs$mg), , drop = FALSE]

  pep_fa_s <- pep_tax2(OS, "sheba", "family_name")

  key <- function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  sp  <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))
  clade <- function(p) ifelse(p %in% c("Bacillota","Firmicutes"), "Bacillota",
                       ifelse(p %in% "Bacteroidota", "Bacteroidota", "other"))
  gap_of <- function(r, cl) median(r[cl=="Bacillota"], na.rm=TRUE) - median(r[cl=="Bacteroidota"], na.rm=TRUE)

  mg_matrix_fam <- function(tab) {
    tab <- as.data.frame(tab, check.names = FALSE)
    cn  <- as.character(tab[[1]])
    sel <- nchar(gsub("[^|]", "", cn)) == 4 & grepl("\\|f__", cn)
    if (!any(sel)) stop("no family-level rows in the MetaPhlAn table")
    X <- as.matrix(tab[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    G <- rowsum(X, sub(".*\\|f__", "", cn[sel])); M <- t(G); rownames(M) <- key(rownames(M))
    if (anyDuplicated(rownames(M))) M <- rowsum(M, rownames(M))
    M
  }
  read_mpa <- function(f) {
    h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    t <- read.delim(f, skip = h - 1, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"; t
  }
  mpaf <- Sys.getenv("B13C_MPA")
  MGlib <- mg_matrix_fam(if (nzchar(mpaf)) read_mpa(mpaf) else
           if (exists("sh_mpa_raw")) sh_mpa_raw else stop("no Sheba MetaPhlAn table"))

  jj <- merge(data.frame(row = pep_fa_s$row, family = pep_fa_s$tax),
              data.frame(row = pep_ph_s$row, phylum = pep_ph_s$tax), by = "row")
  tb <- table(jj$family, jj$phylum)
  phy_of <- setNames(colnames(tb)[apply(tb, 1, which.max)], rownames(tb))
  rows_of <- table(pep_fa_s$tax)

  ## ---- 1. WHICH SIDE BINDS -------------------------------------------------
  mp_fams <- names(rows_of); mg_fams <- colnames(MGlib)
  diag1 <- data.frame(
    family = union(mp_fams, mg_fams),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  diag1$phylum <- unname(phy_of[diag1$family])
  diag1$clade  <- clade(diag1$phylum)
  diag1$pep_rows <- as.integer(rows_of[diag1$family]); diag1$pep_rows[is.na(diag1$pep_rows)] <- 0L
  diag1$mg_mean_pct <- sapply(diag1$family, function(f)
    if (f %in% mg_fams) round(mean(MGlib[, f], na.rm = TRUE), 3) else NA_real_)
  diag1$in_MG <- diag1$family %in% mg_fams
  bt <- diag1[diag1$clade == "Bacteroidota", ]
  bt <- bt[order(-bt$pep_rows), ]
  cat("==== every Bacteroidota family seen on either side ====\n")
  print(bt[, c("family","pep_rows","in_MG","mg_mean_pct")], row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("\nBacteroidota families: %d with any peptide row, %d detected by MetaPhlAn, %d on both sides\n",
      sum(bt$pep_rows > 0), sum(bt$in_MG), sum(bt$pep_rows > 0 & bt$in_MG)))
  cat("Which side binds: compare the two counts above against the floor sweep below.\n")

  ## ---- 2. every family's rho, NO FLOOR -------------------------------------
  all_f <- intersect(names(rows_of), colnames(MGlib))
  if (length(DROP)) {
    hit <- intersect(DROP, all_f)
    cat(sprintf("\nB13C_DROP excluding %d famil%s: %s\n", length(hit),
                if (length(hit) == 1) "y" else "ies", paste(hit, collapse = ", ")))
    miss <- setdiff(DROP, all_f)
    if (length(miss)) cat("  not present, ignored:", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    all_f <- setdiff(all_f, DROP)
  }
  prs <- pairs[pairs$sample %in% colnames(OS$a) & pairs$mg %in% rownames(MGlib), , drop = FALSE]
  den <- vapply(all_f, function(t)
    colSums(OS$a[pep_fa_s$row[pep_fa_s$tax == t], prs$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
    numeric(nrow(prs)))
  rownames(den) <- prs$sample
  ok <- rowSums(den) > 0; den <- den[ok, , drop=FALSE]; prs <- prs[ok, , drop=FALSE]
  MPf <- den / rowSums(den)
  MGm <- MGlib[prs$mg, all_f, drop = FALSE]; rownames(MGm) <- prs$sample
  cl_all <- clade(unname(phy_of[all_f]))
  rho_of <- function(A,B) vapply(colnames(A), function(t) sp(A[,t], B[,t]), 0)
  r_clr <- rho_of(clr(MGm), clr(MPf)); r_raw <- rho_of(MGm, MPf)
  tab_all <- data.frame(family = all_f, clade = cl_all,
                        pep_rows = as.integer(rows_of[all_f]),
                        rho_clr = round(r_clr,3), rho_raw = round(r_raw,3))
  cat(sprintf("\n==== all %d families present in both layers, %d patients, NO floor ====\n",
      length(all_f), nrow(MGm)))
  print(tab_all[order(tab_all$clade, -tab_all$pep_rows), ], row.names = FALSE)

  ## ---- 3. the floor sweep ---------------------------------------------------
  cat("\n==== floor sweep ====\n")
  cat(sprintf("%6s %6s %6s %9s %9s %9s %22s\n",
      "floor","nBaci","nBact","medBaci","medBact","gapCLR","95% interval"))
  out <- lapply(FLOORS, function(fl) {
    k <- which(tab_all$pep_rows >= fl); if (length(k) < 3) return(NULL)
    f <- tab_all$family[k]; cl <- tab_all$clade[k]
    A <- clr(MGm[, f, drop=FALSE]); B <- clr(MPf[, f, drop=FALSE])
    r <- rho_of(A, B)
    nb <- sum(cl=="Bacillota"); nt <- sum(cl=="Bacteroidota")
    g  <- gap_of(r, cl)
    ci <- c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    if (nt >= 2 && nb >= 2) {
      set.seed(9601); n <- nrow(MGm)
      v <- replicate(NBOOT, { i <- sample(n, replace=TRUE)
        gap_of(rho_of(clr(MGm[i,f,drop=FALSE]), clr(MPf[i,f,drop=FALSE])), cl) })
      ci <- quantile(v, c(.025,.975), na.rm=TRUE)
    }
    cat(sprintf("%6d %6d %6d %+9.3f %+9.3f %+9.3f   [%+.3f, %+.3f]\n", fl, nb, nt,
        median(r[cl=="Bacillota"],na.rm=TRUE), median(r[cl=="Bacteroidota"],na.rm=TRUE),
        g, ci[1], ci[2]))
    data.frame(floor=fl, n_bacillota=nb, n_bacteroidota=nt, gap=g, lo=ci[1], hi=ci[2])
  })
  cat("A median over two or three families is unstable: read the interval, not the point.\n")
  assign("b13c", list(diag = diag1, all = tab_all, sweep = do.call(rbind, out)), envir = .GlobalEnv)
})
```

## B14 — coupling magnitude

how large can the patient-specific advantage be, in either cohort?

Source: `B14_coupling_magnitude.R`

```{r B14_coupling_magnitude, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B14 — how large can the patient-specific advantage be, in either cohort?
## ============================================================================
##
## The own-versus-stranger comparison has been read as a hypothesis test —
## "is the advantage above zero in both cohorts?" — and on that reading the
## second cohort "does not replicate". But Pillar 1's claim is that a patient's
## own gene abundance adds very little, and the question that claim raises is one
## of MAGNITUDE: how large can the advantage plausibly be? This script answers it
## for both cohorts on the same axis, for both arms:
##
##   full profile   every shared gene family (Pittsburgh 1,320; Sheba 1,116)
##   powered arm    the 200 most variable core gene families, where section 11a's
##                  restriction found the advantage concentrated
##
## For each: the median per-patient advantage (own minus the median of strangers)
## with a bootstrap interval over patients, and the median own coupling beside it
## so the advantage can be read against the scale of the coupling itself.
##
## The cohorts are kept separate — they differ in sampling time, preservation and
## pairing unit (Sheba pairs patients, Pittsburgh stools) — so no pooled estimate
## is formed. The bootstrap resamples patients with each patient's stranger median
## held fixed; that ignores the dependence between a patient's strangers and the
## other resampled patients, which makes the intervals somewhat narrow, and is
## stated rather than corrected.
##
## Base R throughout. Requires cpl_MP, cpl_G, cpl_kos, cpl_pat, cpl_stats
## (section 11a) and B12's saved output.

local({

  B_BOOT <- 2000L; SEED <- 1401L; EPS <- 1e-9; TOP_N <- 200L

  need <- c("cpl_MP", "cpl_G", "cpl_kos", "cpl_pat", "cpl_stats", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B14 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
        ". Run analysis_v17.Rmd through section 11a first.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f12)) {
    cat("B14 SKIPPED: B12 output not found at ", f12, "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }
  b12 <- readRDS(f12)
  for (k in c("own", "mis", "own_top", "mis_top"))
    if (is.null(b12[[k]])) stop("B12 output lacks `", k, "`; re-run B12.", call. = FALSE)
```
