```{r B14_coupling_magnitude, eval=FALSE}
  ## ---- Pittsburgh, full profile: section 11a's own per-patient statistics -----
  dP_full <- cpl_stats$own - cpl_stats$mismatched
  ownP_full <- cpl_stats$own

  ## ---- Pittsburgh, powered arm: section 11a-b's restriction, recomputed -------
  ## The per-patient values were never exported, only their medians, so the
  ## restriction is rebuilt exactly as A1b builds it and checked against the
  ## recorded medians before anything is resampled.
  MP <- cpl_MP; G <- cpl_G; kos <- cpl_kos; pat <- as.data.frame(cpl_pat)
  Gp   <- G[kos, pat$bio, drop = FALSE]
  pres <- rowMeans(Gp > 0)
  core <- names(pres)[pres >= 0.9]
  sd_core <- apply(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]), 1, sd)
  top <- head(names(sort(sd_core, decreasing = TRUE)), TOP_N)
  coup_on <- function(k, s, b) {
    x <- MP[k, s]; y <- G[k, b]; keep <- is.finite(x) & x > 0
    if (sum(keep) < 30) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS), log(y[keep] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }
  n <- nrow(pat)
  K <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(j)
         vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) coup_on(top, pat$sample[i], pat$bio[j]), 0),
         numeric(n))
  ownP_top <- diag(K)
  misP_top <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  dP_top <- ownP_top - misP_top

  ## ---- Sheba, both arms, from B12 --------------------------------------------
  dS_full <- b12$own - b12$mis;          ownS_full <- b12$own
  dS_top  <- b12$own_top - b12$mis_top;  ownS_top  <- b12$own_top

  ## ---- reproduce the recorded medians before resampling anything --------------
  REC <- c(pitt_full = 0.0062, pitt_top = 0.0333, sheba_full = -0.0017, sheba_top = -0.0061)
  got <- c(pitt_full = median(dP_full, na.rm = TRUE), pitt_top = median(dP_top, na.rm = TRUE),
           sheba_full = median(dS_full, na.rm = TRUE), sheba_top = median(dS_top, na.rm = TRUE))
  ## WHICH ENTRIES STILL GATE THE RUN (13 Oct 2026). The two Pittsburgh medians
  ## were recorded on the 55-channel set. The corrected set is 53 channels --
  ## TMT1_126 relabelled MF0017, TMT7_127N and TMT8_126 dropped (see
  ## pitt_sample_corrections.R) -- so they CANNOT reproduce, and a gate on them
  ## only stops the run. They are printed against the record with their
  ## difference, and the new values are what the manuscript must quote.
  ## The two Sheba medians are untouched by the correction and still gate: they
  ## are what catches an overwritten MGm or a stale B12 output, which is the
  ## failure this check was written for. Set ICB_B14_GATE_PITT=1 to gate all four
  ## again once the Pittsburgh record here is updated to the corrected values.
  GATED <- names(REC) %in% if (identical(Sys.getenv("ICB_B14_GATE_PITT"), "1")) names(REC)
                           else c("sheba_full", "sheba_top")
  bad <- abs(got - REC) > 0.0015
  cat("reproducing the recorded medians:\n")
  print(round(rbind(recorded = REC, recomputed = got, difference = got - REC), 4))
  if (any(bad & !GATED))
    cat("  superseded by the 13 Oct 2026 sample correction, reported and not gated: ",
        paste(names(REC)[bad & !GATED], collapse = ", "),
        "\n  (the Pittsburgh set is 53 channels where the record was made on 55)\n", sep = "")
  if (any(!bad & !GATED))
    cat("  unchanged despite the correction: ",
        paste(names(REC)[!bad & !GATED], collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  if (any(bad & GATED))
    stop("the recomputed medians do not match the record for: ",
         paste(names(REC)[bad & GATED], collapse = ", "),
         ". The intervals below would describe different quantities.", call. = FALSE)

  ## ---- estimation --------------------------------------------------------------
  ## ADDED 11 Oct 2026: the Hodges-Lehmann estimate, ALONGSIDE the median --
  ## nothing is removed. Every advantage in the paper is quoted beside a
  ## Wilcoxon signed-rank P, and the location estimate belonging to that test is
  ## the HL pseudomedian, not the median of the paired differences. The two were
  ## treated as interchangeable until the ulcerative-colitis cohort showed they
  ## are not (median +0.012, HL +0.006, and in that cohort the per-subject
  ## differences span -0.045 to +0.045 between the tenth and ninetieth
  ## percentiles -- the regime where a median is unstable and HL is not).
  ##
  ## The median columns stay because the reproducibility gate above checks
  ## medians against the record, and because the supplement reports both. The
  ## figure reads `hl`/`hl_lo`/`hl_hi` when they are present and says on its
  ## axis which estimator it drew; without them it falls back to the median and
  ## prints a message. So adding these columns is what switches S3A over.
  ##
  ## wilcox.test() gives the estimate, the interval and the P from one call, so
  ## the interval cannot drift from the P printed next to it -- unlike a
  ## separate bootstrap, which is how the two estimators diverged unnoticed.
  boot_med <- function(d) {
    d <- d[is.finite(d)]; set.seed(SEED)
    m  <- replicate(B_BOOT, median(sample(d, replace = TRUE)))
    w  <- suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(d, conf.int = TRUE))
    c(n = length(d), median = median(d), lo = unname(quantile(m, .025)),
      hi = unname(quantile(m, .975)),
      hl = unname(w$estimate), hl_lo = w$conf.int[1], hl_hi = w$conf.int[2],
      hl_p = w$p.value)
  }
  rows <- list(
    c(cohort = "Pittsburgh", arm = "full profile"),
    c(cohort = "Pittsburgh", arm = "200 most variable"),
    c(cohort = "Sheba",      arm = "full profile"),
    c(cohort = "Sheba",      arm = "200 most variable"))
  est <- rbind(boot_med(dP_full), boot_med(dP_top), boot_med(dS_full), boot_med(dS_top))
  own <- c(median(ownP_full, na.rm = TRUE), median(ownP_top, na.rm = TRUE),
           median(ownS_full, na.rm = TRUE), median(ownS_top, na.rm = TRUE))
  tab <- data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), est, own_coupling = own,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  tab$excludes_zero <- tab$lo > 0 | tab$hi < 0
  ## `excludes_zero` stays on the MEDIAN interval, which is what the record and
  ## the gate above are about. The HL interval is reported separately below; if
  ## the two ever disagree about zero, that disagreement is the finding and must
  ## be visible rather than collapsed into one flag.
  tab$hl_excludes_zero <- tab$hl_lo > 0 | tab$hl_hi < 0
  cat("\nown-minus-stranger advantage, median per patient, 95% bootstrap interval\n")
  print(transform(tab, median = round(median, 4), lo = round(lo, 4), hi = round(hi, 4),
                  own_coupling = round(own_coupling, 3))[
          , c("cohort", "arm", "n", "median", "lo", "hi", "own_coupling",
              "excludes_zero")], row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nthe same advantage as Hodges-Lehmann, with the Wilcoxon signed-rank",
      "\ninterval and P -- this is what the main text now reports\n")
  print(transform(tab, hl = round(hl, 4), hl_lo = round(hl_lo, 4),
                  hl_hi = round(hl_hi, 4), hl_p = signif(hl_p, 3))[
          , c("cohort", "arm", "n", "hl", "hl_lo", "hl_hi", "hl_p",
              "hl_excludes_zero")], row.names = FALSE)
  if (any(tab$excludes_zero != tab$hl_excludes_zero))
    cat("\n  NOTE: median and Hodges-Lehmann intervals disagree about zero in ",
        sum(tab$excludes_zero != tab$hl_excludes_zero), " arm(s). ",
        "Say so in the text rather than picking the convenient one.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- do the cohorts differ? matched arms only -------------------------------
  ## Formerly B12 [2c], which compared Pittsburgh's FULL-profile deltas against
  ## Sheba's POWERED-arm deltas and never ran. Here each arm is compared with its
  ## own counterpart. Patients are resampled independently within each cohort.
  diff_ci <- function(a, b) {
    a <- a[is.finite(a)]; b <- b[is.finite(b)]; set.seed(SEED + 1L)
    m <- replicate(B_BOOT, median(sample(a, replace = TRUE)) - median(sample(b, replace = TRUE)))
    c(difference = median(a) - median(b), lo = unname(quantile(m, .025)),
      hi = unname(quantile(m, .975)))
  }
  dtab <- data.frame(arm = c("full profile", "200 most variable"),
                     rbind(diff_ci(dP_full, dS_full), diff_ci(dP_top, dS_top)))
  dtab$distinguishable <- dtab$lo > 0 | dtab$hi < 0
  cat("\nPittsburgh minus Sheba, per arm, 95% bootstrap interval\n")
  print(transform(dtab, difference = round(difference, 4), lo = round(lo, 4),
                  hi = round(hi, 4)), row.names = FALSE)

  ## ---- the reading --------------------------------------------------------------
  ## HL upper bounds, matching what the paper reports. This printed the
  ## MEDIAN interval's upper end until 11 Oct, so it said +0.013 for the
  ## Pittsburgh full profile where the text now says +0.011.
  up <- function(co, ar) tab$hl_hi[tab$cohort == co & tab$arm == ar]
  cat(sprintf("\nUPPER BOUNDS on the advantage, in Spearman units:
  full profile       Pittsburgh %+.3f | Sheba %+.3f   (own coupling ~%.2f / ~%.2f)
  200 most variable  Pittsburgh %+.3f | Sheba %+.3f\n",
    up("Pittsburgh", "full profile"), up("Sheba", "full profile"),
    tab$own_coupling[1], tab$own_coupling[3],
    up("Pittsburgh", "200 most variable"), up("Sheba", "200 most variable")))
  cat("\nREADING: both cohorts are asked the same question — how large can a\n",
      "patient's own-metagenome advantage be? — and neither is asked to clear zero.\n",
      "Where both intervals include zero, the cohorts agree that the advantage is\n",
      "negligible at that resolution. Where one excludes zero and the other does\n",
      "not, compare the second cohort's upper bound against the first cohort's\n",
      "estimate: an upper bound at or above it means the second cohort cannot rule\n",
      "the first's effect out, which is not the same as failing to replicate it.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- a forest plot, base graphics so it renders anywhere ----------------------
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B14_coupling_magnitude"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  grDevices::pdf(file.path(od, "coupling_magnitude.pdf"), width = 6, height = 3.2)
  op <- par(mar = c(4, 12, 1.5, 1))
  y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(tab)))
  plot(tab$median, y, xlim = range(c(tab$lo, tab$hi, 0)) + c(-.01, .01), yaxt = "n",
       ylab = "", xlab = "own minus stranger (Spearman), median and 95% interval",
       pch = 19, col = ifelse(tab$cohort == "Pittsburgh", "#1b6ca8", "#b5651d"))
  segments(tab$lo, y, tab$hi, y, lwd = 2,
           col = ifelse(tab$cohort == "Pittsburgh", "#1b6ca8", "#b5651d"))
  abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  axis(2, at = y, labels = paste0(tab$cohort, ": ", tab$arm), las = 1, cex.axis = .8)
  par(op); grDevices::dev.off()

  out <- list(table = tab, difference = dtab, pitt_top_kos = top, seed = SEED, n_boot = B_BOOT,
              per_patient = list(pitt_full = dP_full, pitt_top = dP_top,
                                 sheba_full = dS_full, sheba_top = dS_top))
  saveRDS(out, file.path(od, "magnitude.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b14_magnitude <<- out
})
```

## B15 — omnibus

does the overall profile separate responders from non-responders?

Source: `B15_omnibus.R`

```{r B15_omnibus, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B15 — does the overall profile separate responders from non-responders?
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_omnibus_signatures.md before this was run. Every
## differential result in this study is univariate; nothing asks whether the
## profiles differ as a whole. This is one statistic per layer, so it does not
## enlarge the 565-set correction family.
##
## PERMANOVA is implemented here rather than taken from a package, for one
## reason: the permutation must be WITHIN PLEX for the proteome. Labelling batch
## explains a large share of variance in these data, and an unrestricted shuffle
## would test response confounded with plex — it would be expected to separate
## whether or not response does anything. Restricting the shuffle conditions on
## plex by construction, and it is the same scheme used everywhere else here.
##
## Dispersion is tested alongside location and reported whatever it shows. A
## PERMANOVA p can reflect groups differing in SPREAD rather than in POSITION;
## without the dispersion test the two are indistinguishable.
##
## THE RESTRICTION IS NOT A REFINEMENT — IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Simulated with no
## response effect at all, feature-specific batch structure, and response
## imbalanced across plexes as it is here, the unrestricted test returned P < 0.05
## in six of six replicates while the within-plex test returned none. Note also
## that CLR removes a uniform per-sample multiplier, so a batch effect that scales
## every feature equally vanishes under the transform and needs no restriction;
## it is the feature-specific part of batch that confounds, and that is what these
## data have.
##
## Base R only. Requires OP (and, for the metagenome arms, MG_FILES, mg_meta,
## mg_clean, and optionally the Sheba MetaPhlAn table).

local({

  B_PERM <- 10000L; SEED <- 1501L

  need <- c("OP", "paths")   # qf is optional; the PSM aggregate is the fallback
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B15 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }

  ## ---- say what is available before doing anything ---------------------------
  av <- c("qf","OP","OS","mpa_raw","sh_mpa_raw","mg_clean","mg_meta","MG_FILES","SAMP_PRIMARY")
  cat("available: ", paste(av[vapply(av, exists, logical(1))], collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("missing:   ", paste(av[!vapply(av, exists, logical(1))], collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-9); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }

  ## Gower-centred matrix from a distance; trace is the total sum of squares.
  gower <- function(D) {
    A <- -0.5 * D^2
    n <- nrow(A); J <- diag(n) - matrix(1/n, n, n)
    J %*% A %*% J
  }
  ## pseudo-F for a two-level grouping, from the centred matrix
  pseudoF <- function(G, g) {
    if (!all(is.finite(G))) return(NA_real_)   # caller reports the cause
    n <- length(g); lv <- levels(factor(g))
    H <- matrix(0, n, n)
    for (l in lv) { i <- which(g == l); H[i, i] <- 1 / length(i) }
    ss_b <- sum(diag(H %*% G)); ss_t <- sum(diag(G)); ss_w <- ss_t - ss_b
    if (!is.finite(ss_w) || ss_w <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    (ss_b / (length(lv) - 1)) / (ss_w / (n - length(lv)))
  }
  ## mean distance from each sample to its own group centroid, difference between groups
  disper <- function(G, g) {
    lv <- levels(factor(g))
    m <- vapply(lv, function(l) { i <- which(g == l)
      Gi <- G[i, i, drop = FALSE]
      mean(pmax(diag(Gi) - 2 * rowMeans(Gi) + mean(Gi), 0)) }, 0)
    unname(abs(diff(m)))
  }
  ## shuffle labels, optionally within strata
  shuffle <- function(g, strata = NULL) {
    if (is.null(strata)) return(sample(g))
    out <- g
    for (s in unique(strata)) { i <- which(strata == s); out[i] <- sample(g[i]) }
    out
  }

  run <- function(M, g, strata, label, note) {
    ## GUARD EVERY STAGE AND SAY WHICH ONE FAILED.
    ## A single non-finite value anywhere propagates into the distance matrix and
    ## surfaces as "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" inside the statistic,
    ## which says nothing about the cause. These checks name it instead.
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] input: %d samples x %d features%s\n", label,
                nrow(M), ncol(M), note))
    if (!nrow(M) || !ncol(M))
      stop(label, ": empty matrix (", nrow(M), " x ", ncol(M), "). ",
           "Check that the sample names in the design match the matrix columns, ",
           "and that any feature filter has not removed everything.", call. = FALSE)
    ## samples with no response label (pooled channels) are not part of this test
    lab_ok <- !is.na(g)
    if (any(!lab_ok))
      cat(sprintf("  dropping %d sample(s) with no response label\n", sum(!lab_ok)))
    M <- M[lab_ok, , drop = FALSE]; g <- g[lab_ok]
    strata <- if (is.null(strata)) NULL else strata[lab_ok]
    keep <- is.finite(rowSums(M))
    if (any(!keep))
      cat(sprintf("  dropping %d sample(s) with non-finite values\n", sum(!keep)))
    M <- M[keep, , drop = FALSE]; g <- g[keep]
    strata <- if (is.null(strata)) NULL else strata[keep]
    g <- droplevels(factor(g))
    if (nlevels(g) < 2 || min(table(g)) < 3) {
      cat(sprintf("  NOT TESTABLE: %s\n",
                  paste(names(table(g)), table(g), sep = "=", collapse = ", ")))
      return(NULL)
    }
    ## AN UNDERPOWERED ARM IS NOT A NULL RESULT. Below eight in the smaller group
    ## a whole-profile test cannot detect effects of the size reported anywhere in
    ## this literature, so its p-value says nothing either way and must not be
    ## read as absence of separation.
    underpowered <- min(table(g)) < 8
    Cl <- clr(M)
    if (!all(is.finite(Cl)))
      stop(label, ": ", sum(!is.finite(Cl)), " non-finite value(s) after the ",
           "log-ratio transform, in ", sum(rowSums(!is.finite(Cl)) > 0),
           " sample(s). Check for zero-total samples.", call. = FALSE)
    D <- as.matrix(dist(Cl))
    if (!all(is.finite(D)))
      stop(label, ": the distance matrix is not finite.", call. = FALSE)
    G <- gower(D)
    F0 <- pseudoF(G, g); d0 <- disper(G, g)
    set.seed(SEED)
    nullF <- numeric(B_PERM); nullD <- numeric(B_PERM)
    for (b in seq_len(B_PERM)) {
      gp <- shuffle(g, strata)
      nullF[b] <- pseudoF(G, gp); nullD[b] <- disper(G, gp)
    }
    pF <- (1 + sum(nullF >= F0, na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(is.finite(nullF)))
    pD <- (1 + sum(nullD >= d0, na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(is.finite(nullD)))
    ## variance explained by response, as a fraction of total
    n <- length(g); lv <- levels(g); H <- matrix(0, n, n)
    for (l in lv) { i <- which(g == l); H[i, i] <- 1 / length(i) }
    r2 <- sum(diag(H %*% G)) / sum(diag(G))
    cat(sprintf("  tested: %d samples (%s), %d features\n", n,
                paste(names(table(g)), table(g), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), ncol(M)))
    cat(sprintf("  location   pseudo-F %.3f, R2 %.4f, P = %.4f (%s)\n",
                F0, r2, pF,
                if (is.null(strata)) "unrestricted"
                else sprintf("within %s", paste(sort(unique(strata)), collapse = "/"))))
    cat(sprintf("  dispersion difference %.4f, P = %.4f\n", d0, pD))
    verdict <- if (underpowered)
        sprintf("NOT INTERPRETABLE: only %d in the smaller group; this arm cannot detect separation and its P says nothing either way",
                min(table(g)))
      else if (pF < 0.05 && pD >= 0.05) "the profiles differ in position"
      else if (pF < 0.05) "UNRESOLVED: location and spread both separate; not reportable as separation"
      else "no separation of the profile as a whole"
    cat("  -> ", verdict, "\n", sep = "")
    ## PCoA coordinates for the figure: eigen-decomposition of the same centred
    ## matrix the test used, so the plot and the p-value describe one object.
    ev <- eigen(G, symmetric = TRUE)
    k  <- which(ev$values > 1e-9)[seq_len(2)]
    k  <- k[!is.na(k)]
    crd <- if (length(k) == 2)
      data.frame(sample = rownames(M), resp = as.character(g),
                 strata = if (is.null(strata)) NA_character_ else as.character(strata),
                 PCo1 = ev$vectors[, k[1]] * sqrt(ev$values[k[1]]),
                 PCo2 = ev$vectors[, k[2]] * sqrt(ev$values[k[2]]),
                 row.names = NULL) else NULL
    varex <- if (length(k) == 2) ev$values[k] / sum(ev$values[ev$values > 0]) else c(NA, NA)
    list(label = label, n = n, n_group = table(g), features = ncol(M), F = F0,
         r2 = r2, p_location = pF, dispersion = d0, p_dispersion = pD,
         verdict = verdict, underpowered = underpowered, strata = !is.null(strata),
         pcoa = crd, var_explained = varex)
  }

  out <- list()

  ## ---- [1] metaproteome, Pittsburgh, within plex ------------------------------
  ## THE PROTEOME ARM MUST RUN ON PROTEINS, NOT PSMs.
  ## OP$a is the PSM matrix: 151,712 rows over 55 channels in 6 plexes, where a
  ## PSM measured in one plex is NA in the other five BY CONSTRUCTION. No row is
  ## ever complete across plexes, so a complete-case filter there returns nothing
  ## — which is exactly what it did. The analysis works at the protein level that
  ## aggregateFeatures builds ("protein" in qf), the same universe every other
  ## result here uses, and that is what this test uses too.
  prot_matrix <- function() {
    if (exists("qf") && "pitt" %in% names(qf)) {
      qs <- qf[["pitt"]]
      cat("  assays in qf$pitt: ", paste(names(qs), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
      if ("protein" %in% names(qs)) {
        a <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(qs, "protein")
        cat(sprintf("proteome: using the 'protein' assay, %d proteins x %d channels\n",
                    nrow(a), ncol(a)))
        return(a)
      }
    }
    if (exists("ap")) { cat("proteome: using `ap` from the session\n"); return(ap) }
    cat("proteome: no 'protein' assay available; aggregating PSMs by Protein.\n",
        "  This aggregate is NOT the universe the rest of the study uses, which is\n",
        "  aggregateFeatures' robust summary, so the result is indicative only.\n",
        sep = "")
    if (!"Protein" %in% names(OP$rd))
      stop("OP$rd has no Protein column; columns are: ",
           paste(head(names(OP$rd), 15), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    if (nrow(OP$rd) != nrow(OP$a))
      stop("OP$rd has ", nrow(OP$rd), " rows against OP$a's ", nrow(OP$a),
           "; they must correspond row for row.", call. = FALSE)
    A <- OP$a; A[!is.finite(A)] <- NA
    ## NOT ifelse(): it is not guaranteed to preserve dim here, and rowsum then
    ## rejects the group vector with "incorrect length for group".
    B <- A; B[is.na(B)] <- 0
    grp <- as.character(OP$rd$Protein)
    num <- rowsum(B, grp, reorder = TRUE)
    cnt <- rowsum((!is.na(A)) * 1.0, grp, reorder = TRUE)
    num[cnt == 0] <- NA
    cat(sprintf("  aggregated to %d proteins\n", nrow(num)))
    num
  }
  AP <- tryCatch(prot_matrix(), error = function(e) { cat("  ", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

  if (is.null(AP)) cat("\n[metaproteome] SKIPPED: no protein-level matrix available\n") else {
    dd <- OP$d[!is.na(OP$d$resp) & OP$d$sample %in% colnames(AP), , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("  %d of %d channels carry a response label and are in the matrix\n",
                nrow(dd), nrow(OP$d)))
    A <- AP[, dd$sample, drop = FALSE]
    A[!is.finite(A)] <- NA

    ## COMPLETENESS IS REQUIRED PER PLEX, NOT PER CHANNEL.
    ## Requiring a value in all 55 channels discards any protein missing a single
    ## channel anywhere: 869 of 13,385 survived, 6.5%, and the survivors are the
    ## ubiquitous abundant end of the proteome — the part least likely to differ
    ## by response. That is not a neutral filter, it is a filter aimed away from
    ## the effect. A protein quantified in every plex is measurable on the axis
    ## this test uses, so the requirement is presence in every plex, and the
    ## per-plex mean fills a missing channel within a plex that does have it.
    plex <- as.character(dd$Mixture)
    seen <- vapply(split(seq_len(ncol(A)), plex),
                   function(j) rowSums(!is.na(A[, j, drop = FALSE])) > 0, logical(nrow(A)))
    ok_plex <- rowSums(seen) == ncol(seen)
    ok_chan <- rowSums(is.na(A)) == 0
    cat(sprintf("  complete across all channels: %d (%.1f%%); present in every plex: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
                sum(ok_chan), 100*sum(ok_chan)/nrow(A), sum(ok_plex), 100*sum(ok_plex)/nrow(A)))
    ok <- ok_plex
    if (sum(ok) > sum(ok_chan)) {
      A <- A[ok, , drop = FALSE]
      miss <- which(is.na(A), arr.ind = TRUE)
      if (nrow(miss)) {
        pm <- vapply(split(seq_len(ncol(A)), plex), function(j)
                rowMeans(A[, j, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(nrow(A)))
        A[miss] <- pm[cbind(miss[, "row"], match(plex[miss[, "col"]], colnames(pm)))]
        cat(sprintf("  %d channel-level gaps filled with that protein's mean in its own plex\n",
                    nrow(miss)))
      }
      still <- rowSums(is.na(A)) == 0
      if (any(!still)) { cat(sprintf("  %d proteins still incomplete after filling; dropped\n",
                                     sum(!still))); A <- A[still, , drop = FALSE] }
      ok <- rep(TRUE, nrow(A))
    }
    cat(sprintf("  universe for the test: %d proteins\n", nrow(A)))
    ## the "protein" assay is already on a log scale; return it to intensities so
    ## the composition and its log-ratio transform mean what they say
    Mp <- t(A)
    if (max(Mp, na.rm = TRUE) < 100) { cat("  values look log-scaled; exponentiating\n")
      Mp <- 2^Mp }
    tot <- rowSums(Mp)
    if (any(tot <= 0)) { cat(sprintf("  dropping %d channel(s) with zero total\n", sum(tot <= 0)))
      Mp <- Mp[tot > 0, , drop = FALSE]; dd <- dd[tot > 0, , drop = FALSE]; tot <- tot[tot > 0] }
    Mp <- Mp / tot
    out$proteome <- run(Mp, dd$resp, as.character(dd$Mixture),
                        "metaproteome, Pittsburgh", "")
  }

  ## ---- [2] metagenome, species level ------------------------------------------
  sp_matrix <- function(f, cleaner) {
    h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    t <- read.delim(f, skip = if (is.na(h)) 1 else h - 1, check.names = FALSE,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"
    sel <- grepl("\\|s__", t$clade_name) & !grepl("\\|t__", t$clade_name)
    if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
    X <- as.matrix(t[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    rownames(X) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", t$clade_name[sel])
    M <- t(X); rownames(M) <- cleaner(rownames(M))
    M[, colSums(M, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  }

  ## The MetaPhlAn tables may be in the session as data frames (mpa_raw,
  ## sh_mpa_raw, both in the figure bundle) or only as file paths (MG_FILES, a
  ## full-knit object). Accept either, and build the design from whatever
  ## response labels are present rather than requiring mg_meta.
  sp_from_df <- function(df, cleaner) {
    tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
    write.table(df, tf, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
    on.exit(unlink(tf), add = TRUE)
    sp_matrix(tf, cleaner)
  }
  cleaner_pitt <- if (exists("mg_clean")) mg_clean else identity
  Mg <- NULL
  if (exists("mpa_raw")) Mg <- tryCatch(sp_from_df(mpa_raw, cleaner_pitt), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(Mg) && exists("MG_FILES") && !is.null(MG_FILES$mpa) && file.exists(MG_FILES$mpa))
    Mg <- sp_matrix(MG_FILES$mpa, cleaner_pitt)
  ## response per metagenome library: mg_meta if present, else OP$d by sample name
  pitt_design <- if (exists("mg_meta")) {
    data.frame(sample = mg_meta$sample, resp = as.character(mg_meta$resp))
  } else if (exists("OP")) {
    data.frame(sample = OP$d$sample, resp = as.character(OP$d$resp))
  } else NULL
  if (!is.null(Mg) && !is.null(pitt_design)) {
    mg_meta <- pitt_design
    if (!is.null(Mg)) {
      i <- intersect(rownames(Mg), mg_meta$sample)
      cat(sprintf("metagenome Pittsburgh: %d of %d libraries matched to the design\n",
                  length(i), nrow(Mg)))
      if (length(i) >= 8) {
        g <- mg_meta$resp[match(i, mg_meta$sample)]
        out$metagenome_pitt <- run(Mg[i, , drop = FALSE], g, NULL,
                                   "metagenome species, Pittsburgh", "")
      } else cat("  too few matched libraries; check the name cleaner\n")
    }
  } else cat("\n[metagenome, Pittsburgh] SKIPPED: MetaPhlAn table not in the session\n")

  ## Sheba, if its table and design are available
  if (exists("sh_mpa_raw")) {
    Ms <- tryCatch(sp_from_df(sh_mpa_raw,
            function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)),
            error = function(e) NULL)
    ## A METAGENOME-ONLY TEST DOES NOT NEED THE PROTEOME PAIRING.
    ## B12's pairs cover only patients with BOTH layers, which here is 24 of 38
    ## and leaves 5 non-responders — too few to test. Prefer any design that maps
    ## metagenome libraries directly to a response label; fall back to the pairs
    ## only if none exists, and say what was lost.
    ## design: SAMP_PRIMARY if present, else B12's saved pairs joined to OS$d
    ## BUILD THE SHEBA DESIGN TO COVER AS MANY LIBRARIES AS POSSIBLE.
    ## Three routes are tried and the widest usable one wins, because a
    ## metagenome-only test should not inherit the proteome's coverage:
    ##   [1] a patient key in SAMP_PRIMARY matched to the library prefix
    ##   [2] B12's pairs carrying response from SAMP_PRIMARY (all Sheba channels)
    ##   [3] B12's pairs carrying response from OS$d (the narrowest; 24 patients)
    mg_keys <- if (!is.null(Ms)) rownames(Ms) else character(0)
    SP <- if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY")) tryCatch(as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
    if (!is.null(SP) && "cohort" %in% names(SP)) SP <- SP[SP$cohort %in% c("sheba","Sheba"), , drop = FALSE]
    cand <- list()

    ## [1] any column of SAMP_PRIMARY whose values match the library keys, whole
    ## or by leading patient number
    if (!is.null(SP) && "resp" %in% names(SP) && length(mg_keys)) {
      pref <- sub("_.*$", "", mg_keys)              # "101_S1" -> "101"
      for (cl in names(SP)) {
        v <- as.character(SP[[cl]]); if (all(is.na(v))) next
        hit_full <- sum(v %in% mg_keys)
        hit_pref <- sum(v %in% pref)
        if (hit_full >= 12) {
          d <- data.frame(mg = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% mg_keys, ]
          cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl)]] <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), ]
        } else if (hit_pref >= 12) {
          m <- data.frame(pref = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% pref, ]
          m <- m[!duplicated(m$pref), ]
          d <- data.frame(mg = mg_keys, pref = pref)
          d <- merge(d, m, by = "pref")[, c("mg","resp")]
          cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl, " (prefix)")]] <- d
        }
      }
    }
    ## [2] and [3] B12's pairs, response from the wider source first
    f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
    if (file.exists(f12)) {
      pr <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)
      if (all(c("sample","mg") %in% names(pr))) {
        if (!is.null(SP) && all(c("sample","resp") %in% names(SP))) {
          d <- merge(pr[, c("sample","mg")],
                     data.frame(sample = SP$sample, resp = as.character(SP$resp)), by = "sample")
          cand[["B12 pairs + SAMP_PRIMARY"]] <- d[, c("mg","resp")]
        }
        if (exists("OS")) {
          d <- merge(pr[, c("sample","mg")],
                     data.frame(sample = OS$d$sample, resp = as.character(OS$d$resp)), by = "sample")
          cand[["B12 pairs + OS$d"]] <- d[, c("mg","resp")]
        }
      }
    }
    ## A candidate with only ONE response level must score zero. Otherwise
    ## min(table(...)) returns that single group's size and a design with no
    ## contrast at all wins the comparison.
    score <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$resp) & d$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
      d <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), , drop = FALSE]
      tb <- table(droplevels(factor(d$resp)))
      if (!nrow(d) || length(tb) < 2) return(c(0, 0))
      c(nrow(d), min(tb)) }
    if (length(cand)) {
      sc <- t(vapply(cand, score, c(0, 0)))
      colnames(sc) <- c("libraries", "smaller_group")
      cat("Sheba design candidates:\n"); print(sc)
      ## prefer the largest smaller-group, then the most libraries
      best <- order(-sc[, 2], -sc[, 1])[1]
      cat("  using: ", rownames(sc)[best], "\n", sep = "")
      sd <- cand[[best]]
      sd <- sd[!is.na(sd$resp) & sd$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
      sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$mg), , drop = FALSE]

      ## ONE LIBRARY PER PATIENT. Seven Sheba patients gave more than one tube,
      ## and deduplicating on the LIBRARY key keeps them all: 101_S1 and 101_ME
      ## are two rows with one response label. Repeated samples from a patient
      ## resemble each other more than anything else, which inflates
      ## between-group separation.
      ##
      ## MEASURED, 28 Sep 2026: simulated with NO response effect whatsoever, 28
      ## patients of whom 7 contribute a repeat tube, keeping the repeats gave
      ## P < 0.05 in six of eight replicates; one library per patient gave one of
      ## eight, the nominal rate. This is not a small correction — it is the
      ## difference between a test and an artefact. The first run of this arm
      ## returned P = 0.0059 on 35 libraries and is not to be believed until it
      ## is repeated under this rule.
      ##
      ## Keep one library per patient, preferring the S-series, which is the read
      ## length that matches the discovery cohort.
      sd$patient <- sub("_.*$", "", sd$mg)
      sd$series  <- ifelse(grepl("_ME", sd$mg), "ME", "S")
      nlib <- nrow(sd)
      sd <- sd[order(sd$patient, sd$series != "S"), , drop = FALSE]
      sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$patient), , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(sd) < nlib)
        cat(sprintf("  %d of %d libraries dropped as repeat tubes from the same patient\n",
                    nlib - nrow(sd), nlib))

      ## SEQUENCING SERIES IS A BATCH VARIABLE AND MUST BE CONDITIONED ON.
      ## This cohort was sequenced in two series at different read lengths. If
      ## response is imbalanced across them, an unrestricted permutation tests
      ## response confounded with series — the same failure the within-plex
      ## restriction prevents on the proteome side, where simulation gave false
      ## positives in six of six replicates.
      tb <- table(sd$series, sd$resp)
      if (nrow(tb) > 1) {
        cat("  sequencing series against response:\n"); print(tb)
        pf <- tryCatch(fisher.test(tb)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
        cat(sprintf("  series x response association: P = %.4f\n", pf))
        cat("  -> permutation will be restricted WITHIN SERIES\n")
      }
    } else sd <- NULL
    if (!is.null(Ms) && !is.null(sd) && all(c("mg", "resp") %in% names(sd))) {
      i <- intersect(rownames(Ms), sd$mg)
      cat(sprintf("metagenome Sheba: %d of %d libraries matched to the design\n",
                  length(i), nrow(Ms)))
      if (length(i) >= 8) {
        st <- if ("series" %in% names(sd) && length(unique(sd$series)) > 1)
                sd$series[match(i, sd$mg)] else NULL
        out$metagenome_sheba <- run(Ms[i, , drop = FALSE],
                                    sd$resp[match(i, sd$mg)], st,
                                    "metagenome species, Sheba", "")
      }
      else cat("  too few matched libraries; check the name cleaner\n")
    } else cat("\n[metagenome, Sheba] SKIPPED: need sh_mpa_raw and a design with mg/resp\n")
  }

  ## ---- [3] WHAT CARRIES THE SEPARATION, AND ALPHA DIVERSITY -------------------
  ## POST HOC. Both blocks below were written after seeing that the pre-treatment
  ## cohort separates while no published taxon replicates, and are reported as
  ## follow-ups to that result, never as tests of it.
  ##
  ## A whole-profile test has power against many weak, correlated effects exactly
  ## where per-taxon tests corrected for multiplicity have none, so "nothing
  ## replicates" and "the profile separates" are not in conflict. Whether the
  ## published taxa are what separates it is a different question, and it is
  ## answered by removing them and by testing them alone.
  PUB <- c("Faecalibacterium","Oscillospiraceae","Akkermansia_muciniphila",
           "Bifidobacterium_longum","Collinsella_aerofaciens","Enterococcus_faecium",
           "Faecalibacterium_prausnitzii","Bacteroides_caccae","Dorea_formicigenerans",
           "Holdemania_filiformis","Bacteroidales")
  decompose <- function(M, g, strata, label) {
    hit <- colnames(M)[colnames(M) %in% PUB]
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] decomposition: %d of %d features are published taxa\n",
                label, length(hit), ncol(M)))
    if (!length(hit)) { cat("  none present at this rank; nothing to decompose\n"); return(NULL) }
    wo <- run(M[, setdiff(colnames(M), hit), drop = FALSE], g, strata,
              paste(label, "- published taxa REMOVED"), "")
    on <- if (length(hit) >= 3)
            run(M[, hit, drop = FALSE], g, strata,
                paste(label, "- published taxa ONLY"), "") else NULL
    cat("\n  reading: if REMOVED still separates, the signal is not in the published\n",
        "  taxa. If ONLY separates, they carry it in aggregate despite no single\n",
        "  one replicating. Both can hold — weak effects are not exclusive.\n", sep = "")
    list(without = wo, only = on, n_published = length(hit))
  }

  ## alpha diversity: one number per sample, the standard first description
  alpha <- function(M, g, label) {
    P <- M / rowSums(M)
    sh <- apply(P, 1, function(x) { x <- x[x > 0]; -sum(x * log(x)) })
    ri <- rowSums(M > 0)
    ev <- sh / log(pmax(ri, 2))
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] alpha diversity by response\n", label))
    out <- lapply(list(Shannon = sh, richness = ri, evenness = ev), function(v) {
      w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(v ~ g))
      c(NR = median(v[g == "NR"]), R = median(v[g == "R"]), P = w$p.value) })
    print(round(do.call(rbind, out), 4))
    M <- do.call(rbind, out)
    ## PER-SAMPLE VALUES, NOT ONLY THE MEDIANS. ED Fig. 2b drew bar charts of
    ## these medians because medians were all this function returned -- no
    ## distribution, no uncertainty, and the Sheba richness bars read as a
    ## difference the text says is absent. The panel can only draw boxplots if
    ## the values come with the summary, so they are attached here. The matrix
    ## is returned as before, so nothing that reads this output breaks.
    attr(M, "values") <- data.frame(
      sample = rep(rownames(P), 3L),
      metric = rep(c("Shannon", "richness", "evenness"), each = nrow(P)),
      value  = c(sh, ri, ev),
      resp   = rep(as.character(g), 3L),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    M
  }

  if (!is.null(out$metagenome_sheba) && exists("Ms") && !is.null(Ms) && !is.null(sd)) {
    i  <- intersect(rownames(Ms), sd$mg)
    gg <- sd$resp[match(i, sd$mg)]
    st <- if ("series" %in% names(sd) && length(unique(sd$series)) > 1) sd$series[match(i, sd$mg)] else NULL
    ## the family and order ranks are not in the species matrix; decompose on what is
    out$sheba_decomp <- decompose(Ms[i, , drop = FALSE], gg, st, "Sheba metagenome")
    out$sheba_alpha  <- alpha(Ms[i, , drop = FALSE], factor(gg), "Sheba metagenome")
  }
  if (!is.null(out$metagenome_pitt) && exists("Mg") && !is.null(Mg) && exists("mg_meta")) {
    i  <- intersect(rownames(Mg), mg_meta$sample)
    gg <- mg_meta$resp[match(i, mg_meta$sample)]
    out$pitt_decomp <- decompose(Mg[i, , drop = FALSE], gg, NULL, "Pittsburgh metagenome")
    out$pitt_alpha  <- alpha(Mg[i, , drop = FALSE], factor(gg), "Pittsburgh metagenome")
  }

  ## ---- ALL THREE ARMS, EACH ON ITS OWN TERMS ---------------------------------
  ## THE RAW P IS THE RESULT HERE, and correcting across the arms would be wrong.
  ## Multiplicity correction answers selection: the 565-set family needs it
  ## because those sets were CHOSEN from a survey and the claim is that a chosen
  ## one is extreme. Neither condition holds for these three arms. They were
  ## fixed before the run, each asks a different question of different data, and
  ## the pre-specification commits to reporting every one whatever it shows, so
  ## there is no selection to correct for. Nor are they exchangeable under a
  ## common null, which a family has to be.
  ##
  ## The correction WOULD apply to a disjunctive claim — "some layer somewhere
  ## separates" — so that claim is not made. Each arm is reported as itself, and
  ## the across-arm figure is printed underneath as context for anyone who wants
  ## to read the three together.
  ## `out` now also holds alpha-diversity matrices and decomposition lists, and
  ## `a$p_location` on a matrix raises "$ operator is invalid for atomic
  ## vectors". Keep only the arms themselves.
  arms <- Filter(function(a) is.list(a) && !is.null(a$p_location) &&
                             isTRUE(is.finite(a$p_location)), out)
  if (length(arms) >= 1) {
    pv <- vapply(arms, function(a) a$p_location, 0)
    q  <- if (length(pv) > 1) p.adjust(pv, "BH") else pv
    cat("\n---- the pre-specified arms, all reported ----\n")
    print(data.frame(arm = vapply(arms, function(a) a$label, ""),
                     n = vapply(arms, function(a) a$n, 0L),
                     P = round(pv, 4),
                     across_arms = round(q, 4),
                     row.names = NULL))
    cat("  P is the result for each arm. `across_arms` is a Benjamini-Hochberg\n",
        "  value over the three, given only for a reader who wants to treat them\n",
        "  as one family; the analysis does not, for the reason above.\n", sep = "")
    for (i in seq_along(arms)) out[[names(arms)[i]]]$p_across_arms <- q[i]
  }

  ## ---- what this does and does not license -------------------------------------
  cat("\n---- reading, fixed before the run ----\n")
  cat("A separation here is NOT evidence for the chaperone result and does not\n",
      "change its correction. A null here does NOT retract it: an omnibus test\n",
      "over thousands of features has little power against a difference carried\n",
      "by a few hundred. This is reported as its own sentence.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B15_omnibus"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(out, file.path(od, "omnibus.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b15_omnibus <<- out
})
```

## B16 — published signatures

do the published response signatures appear in these cohorts?

Source: `B16_published_signatures.R`

```{r B16_published_signatures, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B16 — do the published response signatures appear in these cohorts?
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_omnibus_signatures.md before this was run. The
## manuscript tests the metagenome at phylum level only, so it cannot say whether
## these cohorts reproduce the species associations the field already reports.
## That determines how everything else here generalises.
##
## THIS IS CONFIRMATORY, NOT EXPLORATORY. The list below is fixed, externally
## defined, and this study had no part in choosing it, so it does not enlarge the
## 565-set correction family. Each taxon is tested ONE-SIDED in its published
## direction; a taxon moving the other way does not replicate and is not a
## discovery.
##
## TIMEPOINT IS THE CRUX. Published signatures are almost entirely
## PRE-TREATMENT. Sheba is sampled before treatment; Pittsburgh during it.
## SHEBA IS THEREFORE PRIMARY here despite being smaller, and Pittsburgh is
## secondary. A failure in Pittsburgh alone says nothing about whether the cohort
## is typical, because timepoint and cohort are confounded there. Fixed now so it
## cannot be chosen after seeing which cohort agrees.
##
## Base R only.

local({

  ## ---- THE LIST. Fixed before the run; do not edit after seeing output. -------
  SIG <- data.frame(
    ## NOMENCLATURE RESOLUTION, not a new hypothesis. The pre-specified taxon is
    ## Gopalakrishnan's Ruminococcaceae; this database has no family of that name
    ## and places the clade under Oscillospiraceae, so the name is mapped and the
    ## direction, source and correction denominator are unchanged. The mapping is
    ## approximate: GTDB split the old Ruminococcaceae across several families,
    ## and Oscillospiraceae carries its core (Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcus,
    ## Oscillibacter) but not all of it.
    ##
    ## NOT INDEPENDENT of the Faecalibacterium row: this database nests
    ## Faecalibacterium INSIDE Oscillospiraceae, so the two Gopalakrishnan entries
    ## are one signal at two ranks and must not be counted as two replications.
    taxon = c("Faecalibacterium", "Oscillospiraceae", "Akkermansia_muciniphila",
              "Bifidobacterium_longum", "Collinsella_aerofaciens",
              "Enterococcus_faecium", "Faecalibacterium_prausnitzii",
              "Bacteroides_caccae", "Dorea_formicigenerans",
              "Holdemania_filiformis", "Bacteroidales"),
    level = c("g", "f", "s", "s", "s", "s", "s", "s", "s", "s", "o"),
    higher_in = c("R","R","R","R","R","R","R","R","R","R","NR"),
    source = c("Gopalakrishnan 2018","Gopalakrishnan 2018 (as Ruminococcaceae)","Routy 2018",
               "Matson 2018","Matson 2018","Matson 2018","Frankel 2017",
               "Frankel 2017","Frankel 2017","Frankel 2017","Gopalakrishnan 2018"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  if (!exists("paths")) { cat("B16 SKIPPED: paths not in the session\n"); return(invisible()) }

  clr1 <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-9); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }

  ## MetaPhlAn table -> matrix at one rank, rows = libraries
  rank_matrix <- function(f, rank, cleaner) {
    h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    t <- read.delim(f, skip = if (is.na(h)) 1 else h - 1, check.names = FALSE,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"
    tag <- paste0("\\|", rank, "__")
    deeper <- c(o = "\\|f__", f = "\\|g__", g = "\\|s__", s = "\\|t__")[[rank]]
    sel <- grepl(tag, t$clade_name) & !grepl(deeper, t$clade_name)
    if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
    X <- as.matrix(t[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
    rownames(X) <- sub(paste0(".*\\|", rank, "__"), "", t$clade_name[sel])
    M <- t(X); rownames(M) <- cleaner(rownames(M))
    if (anyDuplicated(rownames(M))) M <- rowsum(M, rownames(M))
    M
  }

  ## A table may be a path or a data frame already in the session (mpa_raw,
  ## sh_mpa_raw, both in the figure bundle). Accept either, as B15 does.
  as_path <- function(x) {
    if (is.character(x) && length(x) == 1 && file.exists(x)) return(x)
    if (is.data.frame(x)) {
      tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
      write.table(x, tf, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
      return(tf)
    }
    NULL
  }
  test_cohort <- function(f, cleaner, samples, resp, label, primary) {
    cat(sprintf("\n================ %s%s ================\n", label,
                if (primary) "  [PRIMARY: timepoint-matched]" else "  [secondary]"))
    f <- as_path(f)
    if (is.null(f)) { cat("  table not available\n"); return(NULL) }
    res <- list()
    for (rk in unique(SIG$level)) {
      M <- rank_matrix(f, rk, cleaner)
      if (is.null(M)) next
      i <- intersect(rownames(M), samples)
      if (length(i) < 8) next
      g <- factor(resp[match(i, samples)])
      if (rk == unique(SIG$level)[1]) {
        cat(sprintf("  %d libraries matched; %s\n", length(i),
                    paste(names(table(g)), table(g), sep = "=", collapse = ", ")))
        ## A SIGNATURE TEST ON A HANDFUL OF NON-RESPONDERS IS NOT A TEST.
        ## With very few in the smaller group, no published effect size would be
        ## detected, and "nothing replicates" would be a statement about the
        ## design rather than the cohort. Say so where it cannot be missed.
        if (min(table(g)) < 8)
          cat("  *** UNDERPOWERED: only ", min(table(g)), " in the smaller group. ",
              "Non-replication here\n      is uninformative about this cohort. ",
              "Extend the design to every library\n      with a response label ",
              "before reading this arm.\n", sep = "")
      }
      C <- clr1(M[i, , drop = FALSE] / 100)
      for (k in which(SIG$level == rk)) {
        tx <- SIG$taxon[k]
        if (!tx %in% colnames(C)) {
          res[[tx]] <- data.frame(SIG[k, ], n = length(i), detected = FALSE,
                                  med_R = NA, med_NR = NA, p = NA_real_)
          next
        }
        x <- C[, tx]
        alt <- if (SIG$higher_in[k] == "R") "greater" else "less"
        w  <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x[g == "R"], x[g == "NR"], alternative = alt))
        w2 <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x[g == "R"], x[g == "NR"]))
        ## A one-sided p near 1 means the data lean the OTHER way. Without the
        ## observed direction beside it, "does not replicate" hides the
        ## difference between no effect and an opposite effect.
        mr <- median(x[g == "R"]); mn <- median(x[g == "NR"])
        obs <- if (mr > mn) "R" else if (mr < mn) "NR" else "-"
        res[[tx]] <- data.frame(SIG[k, ], n = length(i), detected = TRUE,
                                med_R = mr, med_NR = mn, observed = obs,
                                opposite = obs != "-" && obs != SIG$higher_in[k],
                                p = w$p.value, p_two = w2$p.value)
      }
    }
    if (!length(res)) { cat("  nothing testable\n"); return(NULL) }
    d <- do.call(rbind, res); rownames(d) <- NULL
    ## BH across the taxa that were testable in THIS cohort
    d$q <- NA_real_
    ok <- d$detected & is.finite(d$p)
    d$q[ok] <- p.adjust(d$p[ok], "BH")
    d$replicates <- ok & d$q < 0.05
    attr(d, "underpowered") <- min(table(g)) < 8
    print(data.frame(taxon = d$taxon, level = d$level,
                     published = d$higher_in,
                     observed = if ("observed" %in% names(d)) d$observed else NA,
                     p_1sided = ifelse(is.na(d$p), NA, round(d$p, 4)),
                     q = ifelse(is.na(d$q), NA, round(d$q, 3)),
                     replicates = d$replicates), row.names = FALSE)
    if ("opposite" %in% names(d) && any(d$opposite, na.rm = TRUE))
      cat("  leaning OPPOSITE to the published direction: ",
          paste(d$taxon[which(d$opposite)], collapse = ", "),
          "\n    (a one-sided p near 1 is not absence of effect; it is effect the other way)\n",
          sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("  %d of %d testable taxa replicate at q < 0.05; %d not detected\n",
                sum(d$replicates, na.rm = TRUE), sum(ok), sum(!d$detected)))
    if (all(c("Faecalibacterium","Oscillospiraceae") %in% d$taxon[d$detected]))
      cat("  NOTE: Faecalibacterium is nested inside Oscillospiraceae in this\n",
          "        database, so those two rows are one signal at two ranks.\n", sep = "")
    d
  }

  out <- list()

  ## ---- PRIMARY: Sheba, pre-treatment ------------------------------------------
  ## SAME SOURCE AS B15, so the two analyses describe the same samples. B15 used
  ## sh_mpa_raw from the session; the vJan25 re-profiling is used only if that is
  ## absent, and which one was taken is printed.
  f_sheba <- NULL; sheba_src <- NA_character_
  if (exists("sh_mpa_raw")) { f_sheba <- sh_mpa_raw; sheba_src <- "sh_mpa_raw (session)" }
  if (is.null(f_sheba)) {
    cand <- c(Sys.getenv("ICB_MPA_VJAN25"),
              file.path(paths$out_dir, "merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt"),
              file.path(paths$out_dir, "reprofile", "merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt"))
    cand <- cand[nzchar(cand)]
    hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
    if (length(hit)) { f_sheba <- hit[1]; sheba_src <- paste("vJan25 file:", basename(hit[1])) }
  }
  cat("Sheba table: ", sheba_src, "\n", sep = "")
  ## Same design problem as B15: a metagenome-only test must not inherit the
  ## proteome's coverage. The widest usable mapping wins. Reproduced from B15 so
  ## the two analyses run on the same Sheba samples.
  Ms_keys <- NULL
  if (is.data.frame(f_sheba)) {
    Ms_keys <- sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", names(f_sheba)[-1])
  } else if (!is.null(f_sheba)) {
    kh <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f_sheba, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
    th <- read.delim(f_sheba, skip = if (is.na(kh)) 1 else kh - 1, nrows = 1,
                     check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    Ms_keys <- sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", names(th)[-1])
  }
  Ms <- NULL
    ## BUILD THE SHEBA DESIGN TO COVER AS MANY LIBRARIES AS POSSIBLE.
    ## Three routes are tried and the widest usable one wins, because a
    ## metagenome-only test should not inherit the proteome's coverage:
    ##   [1] a patient key in SAMP_PRIMARY matched to the library prefix
    ##   [2] B12's pairs carrying response from SAMP_PRIMARY (all Sheba channels)
    ##   [3] B12's pairs carrying response from OS$d (the narrowest; 24 patients)
    ## mg_keys comes from the table header read above; do NOT re-derive it from
    ## Ms, which is not built yet here — that silently emptied every candidate.
    mg_keys <- if (is.null(Ms_keys)) character(0) else unique(Ms_keys)
    cat(sprintf("Sheba: %d distinct library keys in the table\n", length(mg_keys)))
    SP <- if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY")) tryCatch(as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
    if (!is.null(SP) && "cohort" %in% names(SP)) SP <- SP[SP$cohort %in% c("sheba","Sheba"), , drop = FALSE]
    cand <- list()

    ## [1] any column of SAMP_PRIMARY whose values match the library keys, whole
    ## or by leading patient number
    if (!is.null(SP) && "resp" %in% names(SP) && length(mg_keys)) {
      pref <- sub("_.*$", "", mg_keys)              # "101_S1" -> "101"
      for (cl in names(SP)) {
        v <- as.character(SP[[cl]]); if (all(is.na(v))) next
        hit_full <- sum(v %in% mg_keys)
        hit_pref <- sum(v %in% pref)
        if (hit_full >= 12) {
          d <- data.frame(mg = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% mg_keys, ]
          cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl)]] <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), ]
        } else if (hit_pref >= 12) {
          m <- data.frame(pref = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% pref, ]
          m <- m[!duplicated(m$pref), ]
          d <- data.frame(mg = mg_keys, pref = pref)
          d <- merge(d, m, by = "pref")[, c("mg","resp")]
          cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl, " (prefix)")]] <- d
        }
      }
    }
    ## [2] and [3] B12's pairs, response from the wider source first
    f12 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
    if (file.exists(f12)) {
      pr <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)
      if (all(c("sample","mg") %in% names(pr))) {
        if (!is.null(SP) && all(c("sample","resp") %in% names(SP))) {
          d <- merge(pr[, c("sample","mg")],
                     data.frame(sample = SP$sample, resp = as.character(SP$resp)), by = "sample")
          cand[["B12 pairs + SAMP_PRIMARY"]] <- d[, c("mg","resp")]
        }
        if (exists("OS")) {
          d <- merge(pr[, c("sample","mg")],
                     data.frame(sample = OS$d$sample, resp = as.character(OS$d$resp)), by = "sample")
          cand[["B12 pairs + OS$d"]] <- d[, c("mg","resp")]
        }
      }
    }
    ## A candidate with only ONE response level must score zero. Otherwise
    ## min(table(...)) returns that single group's size and a design with no
    ## contrast at all wins the comparison.
    score <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$resp) & d$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
      d <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), , drop = FALSE]
      tb <- table(droplevels(factor(d$resp)))
      if (!nrow(d) || length(tb) < 2) return(c(0, 0))
      c(nrow(d), min(tb)) }
    if (length(cand)) {
      sc <- t(vapply(cand, score, c(0, 0)))
      colnames(sc) <- c("libraries", "smaller_group")
      cat("Sheba design candidates:\n"); print(sc)
      ## prefer the largest smaller-group, then the most libraries
      best <- order(-sc[, 2], -sc[, 1])[1]
      cat("  using: ", rownames(sc)[best], "\n", sep = "")
      sd <- cand[[best]]
      sd <- sd[!is.na(sd$resp) & sd$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
      sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$mg), , drop = FALSE]

      ## ONE LIBRARY PER PATIENT. Seven Sheba patients gave more than one tube,
      ## and deduplicating on the LIBRARY key keeps them all: 101_S1 and 101_ME
      ## are two rows with one response label. Repeated samples from a patient
      ## resemble each other more than anything else, which inflates
      ## between-group separation.
      ##
      ## MEASURED, 28 Sep 2026: simulated with NO response effect whatsoever, 28
      ## patients of whom 7 contribute a repeat tube, keeping the repeats gave
      ## P < 0.05 in six of eight replicates; one library per patient gave one of
      ## eight, the nominal rate. This is not a small correction — it is the
      ## difference between a test and an artefact. The first run of this arm
      ## returned P = 0.0059 on 35 libraries and is not to be believed until it
      ## is repeated under this rule.
      ##
      ## Keep one library per patient, preferring the S-series, which is the read
      ## length that matches the discovery cohort.
      sd$patient <- sub("_.*$", "", sd$mg)
      sd$series  <- ifelse(grepl("_ME", sd$mg), "ME", "S")
      nlib <- nrow(sd)
      sd <- sd[order(sd$patient, sd$series != "S"), , drop = FALSE]
      sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$patient), , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(sd) < nlib)
        cat(sprintf("  %d of %d libraries dropped as repeat tubes from the same patient\n",
                    nlib - nrow(sd), nlib))

      ## SEQUENCING SERIES IS A BATCH VARIABLE AND MUST BE CONDITIONED ON.
      ## This cohort was sequenced in two series at different read lengths. If
      ## response is imbalanced across them, an unrestricted permutation tests
      ## response confounded with series — the same failure the within-plex
      ## restriction prevents on the proteome side, where simulation gave false
      ## positives in six of six replicates.
      tb <- table(sd$series, sd$resp)
      if (nrow(tb) > 1) {
        cat("  sequencing series against response:\n"); print(tb)
        pf <- tryCatch(fisher.test(tb)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
        cat(sprintf("  series x response association: P = %.4f\n", pf))
        cat("  -> permutation will be restricted WITHIN SERIES\n")
      }
    } else sd <- NULL
  if (!is.null(f_sheba) && !is.null(sd) && all(c("mg","resp") %in% names(sd))) {
    out$sheba <- test_cohort(f_sheba,
      function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x),
      sd$mg, as.character(sd$resp), "SHEBA, sampled before treatment", TRUE)
  } else {
    cat("\n[SHEBA] SKIPPED — this is the PRIMARY arm, so the analysis is incomplete.\n")
    cat("  Need the vJan25 table (or ICB_MPA_VJAN25) and SAMP_PRIMARY with mg/resp.\n")
  }

  ## ---- SECONDARY: Pittsburgh, on treatment -------------------------------------
  pitt_tab <- if (exists("mpa_raw")) mpa_raw
              else if (exists("MG_FILES") && !is.null(MG_FILES$mpa)) MG_FILES$mpa else NULL
  pitt_des <- if (exists("mg_meta")) data.frame(sample = mg_meta$sample, resp = as.character(mg_meta$resp))
              else if (exists("OP")) data.frame(sample = OP$d$sample, resp = as.character(OP$d$resp))
              else NULL
  if (!is.null(pitt_tab) && !is.null(pitt_des)) {
    out$pitt <- test_cohort(pitt_tab, if (exists("mg_clean")) mg_clean else identity,
                            pitt_des$sample, pitt_des$resp,
                            "PITTSBURGH, sampled during treatment", FALSE)
  }

  ## ---- reading, fixed before the run --------------------------------------------
  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  ns <- if (!is.null(out$sheba)) sum(out$sheba$replicates, na.rm = TRUE) else NA
  if (is.na(ns)) {
    cat("The primary arm did not run, so no conclusion about cohort typicality\n",
        "can be drawn. Pittsburgh alone cannot support one: its timepoint differs\n",
        "from the published studies', and timepoint is confounded with cohort.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (!is.null(out$sheba) && isTRUE(attr(out$sheba, "underpowered"))) {
    cat("The primary arm ran but is underpowered; no conclusion about cohort\n",
        "typicality follows from it either way.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (ns > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("%d published taxa replicate in the timepoint-matched cohort. These\n", ns))
    cat("cohorts are not atypical of the literature, so the weak cross-layer\n",
        "coupling reported here is a property of the method, not of an unusual\n",
        "sample.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("No published taxon replicates in the timepoint-matched cohort. Either\n",
        "these cohorts are atypical or the published signatures are weaker than\n",
        "reported; with 27 responders and 8 non-responders this design cannot\n",
        "separate the two, and the manuscript says so rather than adjudicating.\n",
        "A null here bounds the published effects; it does not refute them.\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.null(out$sheba) && !is.null(out$pitt)) {
    a <- out$sheba$replicates[match(SIG$taxon, out$sheba$taxon)]
    b <- out$pitt$replicates[match(SIG$taxon, out$pitt$taxon)]
    dis <- SIG$taxon[which(!is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & a != b)]
    if (length(dis))
      cat("\nDisagreeing between cohorts: ", paste(dis, collapse = ", "),
          "\n  Reported without interpretation — timepoint, handling and response\n",
          "  definition all differ, and this design cannot separate them.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B16_signatures"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(spec = SIG, results = out), file.path(od, "signatures.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b16_signatures <<- out
})
```

## B17 — sensitivity

two arbitrary choices, examined

Source: `B17_sensitivity.R`

```{r B17_sensitivity, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B17 — two arbitrary choices, examined
## ============================================================================
##
## [A] THE 200-ROW GENUS FLOOR. It gates five analyses — the genus coupling in
##     section 11c, the clade contrast, B12's clade arm, B13 and C2 — and has
##     never been varied. A genus at 180 peptide rows is excluded everywhere and
##     nothing shows what the results look like at 100 or at 400. The floor is
##     defensible; an unexamined floor is not.
##
## [B] THE "min group < 8" RULE. That threshold was invented in this project to
##     mark an arm as not interpretable. Sheba sits at exactly 8 and passes by one
##     patient, which is no way to decide. It is replaced here by the quantity the
##     rule was standing in for: the effect this design can actually detect.
##
## Neither block tests a hypothesis. [A] asks whether a reported result depends on
## a threshold, and [B] asks what a null from this design is worth. Both are
## reported whatever they show.
##
## Base R. Requires OP, pep_g, pep_ph, MGm, MPm, gen_coupling, paths.

local({

  FLOORS <- c(50L, 100L, 200L, 300L, 500L, 1000L)
  B_POW  <- 2000L; SEED <- 1701L

  need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "pep_ph", "MGm", "MPm", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B17 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }

  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  clade <- function(p) ifelse(p %in% c("Bacillota","Firmicutes"), "Bacillota",
                       ifelse(p %in% "Bacteroidota", "Bacteroidota", "other"))

  ## genus -> phylum, majority over peptide rows
  jj  <- merge(data.frame(row = pep_g$row,  genus  = pep_g$tax),
               data.frame(row = pep_ph$row, phylum = pep_ph$tax), by = "row")
  tb  <- table(jj$genus, jj$phylum)
  phy <- setNames(colnames(tb)[apply(tb, 1, which.max)], rownames(tb))
  cnt <- table(pep_g$tax)

  ## ---- [A] the floor ---------------------------------------------------------
  cat("=== [A] genus evidence floor ===\n")
  rows <- lapply(FLOORS, function(fl) {
    gen <- names(which(cnt >= fl))
    den <- vapply(gen, function(g)
      colSums(OP$a[pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
      numeric(nrow(OP$d)))
    rownames(den) <- OP$d$sample
    keep <- rowSums(den) > 0
    den <- den[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    MPg <- den / rowSums(den)
    S   <- intersect(rownames(MPg), rownames(MGm))
    gg  <- intersect(colnames(MPg), colnames(MGm))
    if (length(gg) < 6 || length(S) < 10)
      return(data.frame(floor = fl, genera = length(gg), patients = length(S),
                        n_baci = NA, n_bact = NA, baci = NA, bact = NA, gap = NA))
    A <- clr(MGm[S, gg, drop = FALSE]); B <- clr(MPg[S, gg, drop = FALSE])
    rho <- vapply(gg, function(g) suppressWarnings(
      cor(A[, g], B[, g], method = "spearman")), 0)
    cl <- clade(unname(phy[gg]))
    data.frame(floor = fl, genera = length(gg), patients = length(S),
               n_baci = sum(cl == "Bacillota"), n_bact = sum(cl == "Bacteroidota"),
               baci = median(rho[cl == "Bacillota"], na.rm = TRUE),
               bact = median(rho[cl == "Bacteroidota"], na.rm = TRUE),
               gap  = median(rho[cl == "Bacillota"], na.rm = TRUE) -
                      median(rho[cl == "Bacteroidota"], na.rm = TRUE))
  })
  tabA <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  print(transform(tabA, baci = round(baci, 3), bact = round(bact, 3),
                  gap = round(gap, 3)), row.names = FALSE)
  g200 <- tabA$gap[tabA$floor == 200L]
  ok <- is.finite(tabA$gap)
  cat(sprintf("\n  gap at the reported floor: %+.3f; across floors %d-%d: %+.3f to %+.3f\n",
              g200, min(tabA$floor[ok]), max(tabA$floor[ok]),
              min(tabA$gap[ok]), max(tabA$gap[ok])))
  cat(if (all(tabA$gap[ok] > 0))
        "  The clade gap is positive at every floor tried; the result does not\n  depend on the threshold.\n"
      else
        "  The clade gap CHANGES SIGN across floors. The reported value depends on\n  the threshold and must be presented with this table, not alone.\n")

  ## ---- [B] what this design can detect ---------------------------------------
  ## Replaces the invented "min group < 8" rule. For a two-group comparison at
  ## the observed group sizes, how often would an effect of a given size be
  ## detected? Reported as the smallest effect detected at least 80% of the time,
  ## which is the number a null result should be read against.
  cat("\n=== [B] detectable effect, in place of the n < 8 rule ===\n")
  detect <- function(n1, n2, d, B = B_POW, seed = SEED) {
    set.seed(seed)
    mean(replicate(B, {
      x <- rnorm(n1); y <- rnorm(n2, mean = d)
      suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x, y)$p.value) < 0.05
    }))
  }
  designs <- list("Sheba, 8 vs 26" = c(8, 26), "Pittsburgh, 30 vs 25" = c(30, 25),
                  "Sheba if 12 NR" = c(12, 26), "Sheba if 20 NR" = c(20, 26))
  grid <- seq(0.2, 2.0, by = 0.2)
  out <- lapply(names(designs), function(nm) {
    n <- designs[[nm]]
    pw <- vapply(grid, function(d) detect(n[1], n[2], d), 0)
    i  <- which(pw >= 0.8)[1]
    data.frame(design = nm, n_smaller = n[1], n_larger = n[2],
               mde_80 = if (is.na(i)) NA_real_ else grid[i],
               power_at_0.8sd = pw[which.min(abs(grid - 0.8))])
  })
  tabB <- do.call(rbind, out)
  print(transform(tabB, power_at_0.8sd = round(power_at_0.8sd, 2)), row.names = FALSE)
  ## VALIDATED 28 Sep 2026 against an independent implementation:
  ##   Sheba 8 vs 26        mde80 = 1.4 SD   (power 0.44 at 0.8 SD)
  ##   Pittsburgh 30 vs 25  mde80 = 1.0 SD   (power 0.79 at 0.8 SD)
  ##   Sheba with 12 NR     mde80 = 1.2 SD
  ##   Sheba with 20 NR     mde80 = 1.0 SD
  ## So the second cohort detects only differences of well over one standard
  ## deviation four times in five. Microbiome response effects are not that
  ## large, which is the honest reason its nulls bound rather than refute — a
  ## reason with a number attached, unlike the threshold it replaces.
  cat("\n  mde_80 is the group difference, in standard deviations, detected at least\n",
      "  80% of the time. A null from a design whose mde_80 is large bounds the\n",
      "  effect at that size; it does not exclude anything smaller. This is what\n",
      "  the discarded 'fewer than 8' rule was standing in for, and unlike that\n",
      "  rule it does not change its verdict on the strength of one patient.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B17_sensitivity"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(floor = tabA, power = tabB, floors = FLOORS, n_boot = B_POW),
          file.path(od, "sensitivity.rds"))
  write.csv(tabA, file.path(od, "genus_floor_sensitivity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b17_sensitivity <<- list(floor = tabA, power = tabB)
})
```

## B18 — survival

the protein state against time to progression

Source: `B18_survival.R`

```{r B18_survival, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B18 — the protein state against time to progression
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_survival.md before this was run.
##
## WHY. The discovery cohort's response label is "ever progressed", so a patient
## who progressed at thirty months is a non-responder alongside one who
## progressed at six weeks. That coding discards the outcome information this
## analysis uses.
##
## WHAT THIS IS NOT. Same patients, same proteomes, same pre-specified sets —
## only the outcome coding changes. It cannot confirm the binary result and must
## not be written up as replication. It can show whether the association is
## graded, which is more convincing biologically than a difference of means.
##
## THE CLOCK STARTS AT SAMPLING, not at treatment. Samples were collected across
## a wide window on treatment and a patient had to survive to sampling to be in
## this cohort; starting at treatment start would let patients sampled late look
## as though their proteome bought them time. That is immortal-time bias, and
## starting at sampling removes it by construction.
##
## `Response_PFS_12` IS NOT USED. It appears twice in the Pittsburgh clinical
## file, the copies disagree, the ambiguity was never resolved, and v12 took the
## first by position. The endpoint is built from dates instead.

local({

  MIN_EVENTS <- 20L       # below this the model is not interpreted
  SETS <- list(chaperone = "chap_new", ribosomal = "ribo_new")

  need <- c("OP", "SAMP_PRIMARY", "paths", "share_of")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B18 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }
  if (!requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("B18 SKIPPED: the survival package is not installed.\n"); return(invisible())
  }

  sp <- as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY)
  if ("cohort" %in% names(sp)) sp <- sp[sp$cohort %in% c("pitt", "Pittsburgh"), , drop = FALSE]

  ## ---- the endpoint ----------------------------------------------------------
  dcol <- c("Rx_start", "Prog_date", "Death_date", "LFU_date")
  have <- dcol %in% names(sp)
  if (!all(have)) {
    cat("B18 STOPPED: the clinical table lacks ", paste(dcol[!have], collapse = ", "),
        ".\n  Columns present: ", paste(head(names(sp), 40), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  if (any(grepl("^Response_PFS_12", names(sp))))
    cat("note: Response_PFS_12 is present and is deliberately NOT used (it is duplicated",
        "\n      in the source file with disagreeing values); the endpoint is built from dates.\n")

  ## `ifelse(inherits(x, "Date"), ...)` was the bug in the first version:
  ## inherits() returns ONE logical, so ifelse returned a length-1 vector that
  ## was then recycled, collapsing every date column to a single value and
  ## dropping all 75 samples. Parse properly, trying the formats these files
  ## actually use, and report what happened.
  asd <- function(x, nm) {
    if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(x)
    if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.Date(x, origin = "1970-01-01"))
    v <- trimws(as.character(x)); v[v %in% c("", "NA", "NaN", "#N/A", "-")] <- NA
    fmts <- c("%Y-%m-%d", "%d/%m/%Y", "%m/%d/%Y", "%d.%m.%Y", "%Y/%m/%d",
              "%d-%b-%y", "%d-%b-%Y", "%b %d, %Y", "%d %b %Y")
    best <- NULL; best_n <- -1L
    for (f in fmts) {
      d <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(v, format = f))
      k <- sum(!is.na(d))
      if (k > best_n) { best_n <- k; best <- d; best_f <- f }
    }
    cat(sprintf("  %-11s %3d of %3d parsed as %s%s\n", nm, best_n, sum(!is.na(v)), best_f,
                if (best_n < sum(!is.na(v))) "   <- some values unparsed" else ""))
    best
  }
  cat("\nparsing the date columns:\n")
  sp$rx <- asd(sp$Rx_start, "Rx_start"); sp$prog <- asd(sp$Prog_date, "Prog_date")
  sp$death <- asd(sp$Death_date, "Death_date"); sp$lfu <- asd(sp$LFU_date, "LFU_date")
  if (all(is.na(sp$rx))) {
    cat("\nB18 STOPPED: no Rx_start parsed. First few raw values:\n    ",
        paste(utils::head(as.character(sp$Rx_start), 5), collapse = " | "), "\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }

  ## Sampling date, from the timing columns this study already uses.
  ## days_before is POSITIVE for days BEFORE treatment start (the §2f convention),
  ## so the sampling date is rx - days_before. tp_days runs the other way.
  if ("days_before" %in% names(sp) && any(is.finite(as.numeric(sp$days_before)))) {
    sp$samp <- sp$rx - as.numeric(sp$days_before)
    cat(sprintf("  sampling date from days_before (%d finite)\n",
                sum(is.finite(as.numeric(sp$days_before)))))
  } else if ("tp_days" %in% names(sp) && any(is.finite(as.numeric(sp$tp_days)))) {
    sp$samp <- sp$rx + as.numeric(sp$tp_days)
    cat(sprintf("  sampling date from tp_days (%d finite)\n",
                sum(is.finite(as.numeric(sp$tp_days)))))
  } else {
    cat("B18 STOPPED: no usable sampling-time column. days_before present: ",
        "days_before" %in% names(sp), "; tp_days present: ", "tp_days" %in% names(sp), "\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }

  ## progression-free survival: progression OR death, whichever comes first.
  ## Work in numeric days throughout — ifelse() strips the Date class, which is
  ## the kind of silent coercion that produced the first failure.
  n_rx <- as.numeric(sp$rx); n_pr <- as.numeric(sp$prog)
  n_de <- as.numeric(sp$death); n_lf <- as.numeric(sp$lfu); n_sa <- as.numeric(sp$samp)
  ev <- pmin(n_pr, n_de, na.rm = TRUE)
  sp$event <- as.integer(is.finite(ev))
  end <- ifelse(sp$event == 1L, ev, n_lf)
  sp$time <- end - n_sa

  cat(sprintf("\nsamples: %d | with a sampling date: %d | with an event date: %d | with follow-up: %d\n",
              nrow(sp), sum(is.finite(n_sa)), sum(is.finite(ev)), sum(is.finite(n_lf))))
  bad <- !is.finite(sp$time) | sp$time <= 0
  if (any(bad)) {
    why <- ifelse(!is.finite(n_sa[bad]), "no sampling date",
           ifelse(!is.finite(end[bad]), "no event or follow-up date", "event at or before sampling"))
    cat(sprintf("dropping %d sample(s): %s\n", sum(bad),
                paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", names(table(why)), table(why)), collapse = ", ")))
    sp <- sp[!bad, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (!nrow(sp)) { cat("\nB18 STOPPED: no sample has a usable interval. See the counts above.\n")
                   return(invisible()) }

  ## ---- join to the proteome --------------------------------------------------
  d <- OP$d[!is.na(OP$d$resp), , drop = FALSE]
  key <- intersect(c("sample", "BioReplicate", "bio"), intersect(names(d), names(sp)))
  if (!length(key)) { cat("B18 STOPPED: no shared key between OP$d and the clinical table.\n")
                      return(invisible()) }
  m <- merge(d, sp[, c(key[1], "time", "event")], by = key[1])
  cat(sprintf("\n%d samples with both a proteome and a usable interval; %d events\n",
              nrow(m), sum(m$event)))
  if (!nrow(m)) return(invisible())

  ## EVENT COUNT FIRST, before any coefficient. A Cox model on a handful of
  ## events is not a test, and the pre-specification fixes the floor at 20.
  if (sum(m$event) < MIN_EVENTS)
    cat(sprintf("\n*** UNDERPOWERED: %d events, below the pre-specified floor of %d.\n",
                sum(m$event), MIN_EVENTS),
        "    Hazard ratios below are printed for completeness and are NOT interpreted.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- the two pre-specified quantities --------------------------------------
  strat <- if ("Mixture" %in% names(m)) "Mixture" else NULL
  if (is.null(strat)) cat("note: no Mixture column; the model is NOT stratified by batch\n")

  out <- lapply(names(SETS), function(nm) {
    obj <- SETS[[nm]]
    if (!exists(obj)) { cat("  ", nm, ": ", obj, " not in the session\n", sep = ""); return(NULL) }
    sh <- share_of(get(obj))[m$sample]
    m$y <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(sh, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))
    f <- if (is.null(strat)) survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y
         else stats::as.formula(sprintf("survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y + strata(%s)", strat))
    fit <- survival::coxph(f, data = m)
    s <- summary(fit)
    hr <- s$coefficients["y", "exp(coef)"]; p <- s$coefficients["y", "Pr(>|z|)"]
    ci <- s$conf.int["y", c("lower .95", "upper .95")]
    ## proportional hazards: a violated assumption makes the hazard ratio a
    ## summary of nothing in particular, so it is tested and reported
    zp <- tryCatch(survival::cox.zph(fit)$table["y", "p"], error = function(e) NA_real_)
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] HR per logit unit %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f), P = %.4f\n",
                nm, hr, ci[1], ci[2], p))
    cat(sprintf("     proportional hazards: P = %s%s\n",
                if (is.finite(zp)) sprintf("%.3f", zp) else "not testable",
                if (is.finite(zp) && zp < 0.05) "  <- VIOLATED; the HR is not a valid summary" else ""))
    dir_ok <- hr > 1      # pre-specified: higher share -> shorter time to progression
    cat(sprintf("     direction: %s the pre-specified one (higher share, shorter PFS)\n",
                if (dir_ok) "matches" else "OPPOSITE to"))
    data.frame(set = nm, n = nrow(m), events = sum(m$event), HR = hr,
               lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2], P = p, ph_P = zp, direction_ok = dir_ok)
  })
  res <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), out))

  ## ---- the reading, fixed before the run -------------------------------------
  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  if (is.null(res)) { cat("nothing testable.\n"); return(invisible()) }
  if (sum(m$event) < MIN_EVENTS) {
    cat("Too few events to interpret. Pillar 2 stands where it stood, and the\n",
        "outcome coding is not shown to be costing power either way.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (any(res$P < 0.05 & res$direction_ok)) {
    cat("The association is graded, and in the pre-specified direction. The binary\n",
        "'ever progressed' coding was costing power. Report this as a better-powered\n",
        "reanalysis OF THE SAME OBSERVATION — not as replication, and not as a second\n",
        "finding: the patients, the proteomes and the protein sets are unchanged.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (any(res$P < 0.05)) {
    cat("Significant in the OPPOSITE direction to the one fixed in advance.\n",
        "Report it, and reconsider the binary result rather than defending it.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("No graded association. The binary result was not being diluted by the\n",
        "outcome coding, and Pillar 2 stands where it stood. Reported.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(result = res, n = nrow(m), events = sum(m$event),
               min_events = MIN_EVENTS, data = m[, c("sample","time","event")]),
          file.path(od, "survival.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b18_survival <<- res
})
```

## B18b — survival checks

trying to break the survival result

Source: `B18b_survival_checks.R`

```{r B18b_survival_checks, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B18b — trying to break the survival result
## ============================================================================
##
## B18 returned HR 7.90 per logit unit for the chaperone share, P = 0.0076, 24
```
