```{r B18b_survival_checks, eval=FALSE}
## events, proportional hazards satisfied, direction as pre-specified. Before any
## of that is written down, four things have to be checked. None is optional and
## all are reported whatever they show.
##
## [1] SCALE. 7.90 is per LOGIT UNIT, and one logit unit takes the chaperone
##     share from 9.7% to 22.6% — more than a doubling, far outside anything
##     observed. Rescaled to the difference actually seen between arms it is
##     about 1.31. Reporting 7.90 would invite a reader to disbelieve the
##     analysis, and they would be right to.
##
## [2] WHO WAS DROPPED. 75 Pittsburgh rows became 40. Thirteen had no event or
##     follow-up date at all. If those patients differ by response, the estimate
##     is biased and the direction of the bias is knowable. This is the check
##     most likely to overturn the result.
##
## [3] INFLUENCE. At 24 events one or two patients can carry an effect this size.
##
## [4] A PERMUTATION P. Every other test in this study is a within-plex
##     permutation; a Wald p at this size may be optimistic, and the two should
##     agree before the number is quoted.
##
## Also worth noting and reporting: in the binary analysis the RIBOSOMAL set was
## the stronger signal (p = 0.015 against 0.026); here it does not reach
## significance while the chaperone set does. If both reflect one state they
## should move together, and that they do not is a fact about the data, not a
## detail to leave out.

local({

  need <- c("b18_survival", "OP", "SAMP_PRIMARY", "paths", "share_of", "chap_new")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B18b SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  if (!requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("B18b SKIPPED: survival not installed\n"); return(invisible()) }

  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival", "survival.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) { cat("B18b SKIPPED: run B18_survival.R first\n"); return(invisible()) }
  b <- readRDS(f)
  m <- b$data
  d <- merge(OP$d, m, by = "sample")
  d$y <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(share_of(chap_new)[d$sample], 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))
  strat <- "Mixture" %in% names(d)
  ff <- if (strat) survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y + strata(Mixture) else survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y
  fit <- survival::coxph(ff, data = d)
  beta <- coef(fit)["y"]; se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))["y"]

  ## ---- [1] an interpretable scale --------------------------------------------
  cat("=== [1] scale ===\n")
  sdy <- sd(d$y); iqr <- diff(quantile(d$y, c(.25, .75)))
  ## THE BETWEEN-ARM DIFFERENCE, COMPUTED (13 Oct 2026). This was
  ## `qlogis(0.109) - qlogis(0.097)`, the two median shares typed in from the
  ## run they were first measured on. Every hazard ratio the paper reports is
  ## expressed per this difference, so a stale pair of literals rescales the
  ## headline number silently -- and the corrected 53-sample cohort moves both
  ## medians. qlogis is monotonic, so the median of the logit equals the logit
  ## of the median and this reproduces the old expression exactly on the old
  ## data.
  arm <- median(d$y[d$resp == "NR"]) - median(d$y[d$resp == "R"])
  share_nr <- plogis(median(d$y[d$resp == "NR"]))
  share_r  <- plogis(median(d$y[d$resp == "R"]))
  cat(sprintf("  between-arm median share: NR %.3f against R %.3f (%.2f-fold); logit difference %.4f\n",
              share_nr, share_r, share_nr / share_r, arm))
  for (nm_u in list(c("per logit unit", 1), c("per SD of the predictor", sdy),
                    c("per IQR", iqr), c("per the observed between-arm difference", arm))) {
    u <- as.numeric(nm_u[[2]])
    cat(sprintf("  %-40s HR %5.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\n", nm_u[[1]],
                exp(beta*u), exp((beta-1.96*se)*u), exp((beta+1.96*se)*u)))
  }
  cat("  Report one of the last three. The per-logit-unit figure is true and\n",
      "  misleading, because no patient differs from another by a logit unit.\n", sep="")

  ## ---- [2] who was dropped ----------------------------------------------------
  cat("\n=== [2] who was dropped ===\n")
  keep <- OP$d$sample %in% m$sample
  tb <- table(retained = ifelse(keep, "in", "out"), resp = OP$d$resp)
  print(tb)
  pd <- tryCatch(fisher.test(tb)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  cat(sprintf("  response against retention: P = %s\n",
              if (is.finite(pd)) sprintf("%.3f", pd) else "not testable"))
  if (is.finite(pd) && pd < 0.10)
    cat("  *** DROPOUT IS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONSE. The retained set is not a random\n",
        "      subset, and the estimate is biased by an amount this design cannot\n",
        "      recover. This must be stated wherever the hazard ratio is stated.\n", sep="")
  else
    cat("  No association between dropout and response at this size, which does not\n",
        "  prove the dropout is uninformative but is the check available.\n", sep="")
  ## and the chaperone share itself, in and out
  sh_in  <- share_of(chap_new)[OP$d$sample[keep]]
  sh_out <- share_of(chap_new)[OP$d$sample[!keep]]
  cat(sprintf("  chaperone share: retained median %.3f (n=%d), dropped %.3f (n=%d), Wilcoxon P = %.3f\n",
              median(sh_in, na.rm=TRUE), sum(keep), median(sh_out, na.rm=TRUE), sum(!keep),
              suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(sh_in, sh_out)$p.value)))

  ## ---- [3] influence ----------------------------------------------------------
  cat("\n=== [3] influence ===\n")
  db <- residuals(fit, type = "dfbeta")
  db <- if (is.matrix(db)) db[, 1] else db
  ord <- order(abs(db), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
  cat("  three most influential samples, and the fit without each:\n")
  for (i in ord) {
    fi <- survival::coxph(ff, data = d[-i, , drop = FALSE])
    si <- summary(fi)$coefficients["y", ]
    cat(sprintf("    drop %-14s HR %6.2f, P = %.4f%s\n", d$sample[i],
                si["exp(coef)"], si["Pr(>|z|)"],
                if (si["Pr(>|z|)"] >= 0.05) "   <- the result does not survive this one" else ""))
  }
  ## and leaving out each of the most influential five together
  f5 <- survival::coxph(ff, data = d[-order(abs(db), decreasing = TRUE)[1:5], , drop = FALSE])
  s5 <- summary(f5)$coefficients["y", ]
  cat(sprintf("  without the five most influential: HR %.2f, P = %.4f\n",
              s5["exp(coef)"], s5["Pr(>|z|)"]))

  ## ---- [4] a permutation p, within plex ---------------------------------------
  cat("\n=== [4] permutation p, shuffling the predictor within plex ===\n")
  set.seed(1801); B <- 5000L
  obs <- abs(beta)
  null <- numeric(B)
  for (k in seq_len(B)) {
    dd <- d
    if (strat) for (s in unique(dd$Mixture)) {
      j <- which(dd$Mixture == s); dd$y[j] <- sample(dd$y[j])
    } else dd$y <- sample(dd$y)
    null[k] <- tryCatch(abs(coef(survival::coxph(ff, data = dd))["y"]),
                        error = function(e) NA_real_)
  }
  null <- null[is.finite(null)]
  pp <- (1 + sum(null >= obs)) / (1 + length(null))
  cat(sprintf("  Wald P = %.4f | permutation P = %.4f over %d draws\n",
              summary(fit)$coefficients["y","Pr(>|z|)"], pp, length(null)))
  if (pp > 0.05 && summary(fit)$coefficients["y","Pr(>|z|)"] < 0.05)
    cat("  *** The asymptotic p is optimistic at this size. Quote the permutation p.\n")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ## The figure and the manuscript both quote the per-arm-difference hazard
  ## ratio with the permutation p; save the interval and the shares that define
  ## the scale too, so neither has to carry a literal.
  saveRDS(list(hr_per_sd = exp(beta*sdy), hr_per_arm_diff = exp(beta*arm),
               hr_arm_lo = exp((beta - 1.96*se)*arm), hr_arm_hi = exp((beta + 1.96*se)*arm),
               arm_logit_diff = arm, share_NR = share_nr, share_R = share_r,
               dropout_P = pd, perm_P = pp, n = nrow(d), events = sum(d$event)),
          file.path(od, "checks.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

## B18c — firth

a stable estimate for an unstable likelihood.

Source: `B18c_firth.R`

```{r B18c_firth, eval=FALSE}
## B18c — a stable estimate for an unstable likelihood.
##
## Dropping influential observations took the hazard ratio from 7.9 to 53, which
## is what a near-monotone likelihood looks like: the significance is real but the
## coefficient is not determined. Firth's penalty removes the first-order bias and
## returns a finite estimate where the unpenalised MLE is heading for infinity.
##
## The first version of this script failed with "NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function
## call". Two causes, both handled below. After merging to 40 rows the Mixture
## factor keeps every level it had at 75, so plexes with no retained samples
## become all-zero dummy columns; and any NA in the predictor or the interval
## reaches the Fortran routine untouched. coxphf has no strata argument, so plex
## enters as a factor — a different model from B18's stratified fit, and reported
## as such.
local({
  if (!requireNamespace("coxphf", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("B18c: install.packages('coxphf') to run the penalised fit.\n"); return(invisible()) }
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival", "survival.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f)) { cat("B18c: run B18_survival.R first\n"); return(invisible()) }
  d <- merge(OP$d, readRDS(f)$data, by = "sample")
  d$y <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(share_of(chap_new)[d$sample], 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))

  ## ---- make the design matrix clean, and say what was removed ----------------
  keep <- is.finite(d$y) & is.finite(d$time) & is.finite(d$event) & d$time > 0
  if (any(!keep)) cat(sprintf("  dropping %d row(s) with a non-finite value\n", sum(!keep)))
  d <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  use_plex <- "Mixture" %in% names(d)
  if (use_plex) {
    d$Mixture <- droplevels(factor(d$Mixture))
    ev <- tapply(d$event, d$Mixture, sum)
    n  <- table(d$Mixture)
    cat("  plexes retained (events/samples): ",
        paste(sprintf("%s %d/%d", names(n), ev[names(n)], as.integer(n)), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    ## a plex contributing no events carries no information about the hazard and
    ## its dummy column is a route to separation; drop those samples and say so
    dead <- names(ev)[ev == 0]
    if (length(dead)) {
      cat("  dropping ", sum(d$Mixture %in% dead), " sample(s) in plexes with no events: ",
          paste(dead, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
      d <- d[!d$Mixture %in% dead, , drop = FALSE]; d$Mixture <- droplevels(d$Mixture)
    }
    if (nlevels(d$Mixture) < 2) { cat("  only one plex left; fitting without it\n"); use_plex <- FALSE }
  }
  cat(sprintf("  fitting on %d samples, %d events%s\n", nrow(d), sum(d$event),
              if (use_plex) sprintf(", %d plexes", nlevels(d$Mixture)) else ", no plex term"))

  fm <- if (use_plex) survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y + Mixture
        else           survival::Surv(time, event) ~ y
  X <- model.matrix(fm[-2], d)
  if (any(!is.finite(X))) { cat("  STOPPED: the model matrix still has non-finite entries\n")
                            return(invisible()) }
  zero <- apply(X[, -1, drop = FALSE], 2, function(c) all(c == 0))
  if (any(zero)) { cat("  STOPPED: all-zero columns: ", paste(names(zero)[zero], collapse=", "), "\n", sep="")
                   return(invisible()) }

  fit <- tryCatch(coxphf::coxphf(fm, data = d), error = function(e) {
    cat("  coxphf failed: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""); NULL })
  if (is.null(fit)) return(invisible())

  b <- coef(fit)[["y"]]; lo <- fit$ci.lower[["y"]]; hi <- fit$ci.upper[["y"]]
  ## THE BETWEEN-ARM DIFFERENCE, COMPUTED (13 Oct 2026) -- the same correction
  ## B18b_survival_checks.R already carries, which was never applied here. It was
  ## `qlogis(0.109) - qlogis(0.097)`, two median shares typed in from the run they
  ## were first measured on; on the 55-sample design the medians are 0.107 and
  ## 0.092, so the typed pair understates the difference by about a fifth and
  ## rescales every per-arm hazard ratio this script reports. qlogis is monotonic,
  ## so the median of the logit is the logit of the median and this reproduces the
  ## old expression exactly on the old data.
  sdy <- sd(d$y); arm <- median(d$y[d$resp == "NR"]) - median(d$y[d$resp == "R"])
  cat(sprintf("  between-arm difference used here: %.4f on the logit scale\n", arm))
  cat(sprintf("\nFirth-penalised%s:\n", if (use_plex) ", plex as a factor (NOT stratified)" else ""))
  cat(sprintf("  per SD                  HR %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\n", exp(b*sdy), lo^sdy, hi^sdy))
  cat(sprintf("  per arm difference      HR %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\n", exp(b*arm), lo^arm, hi^arm))
  cat(sprintf("  P = %.4f\n", fit$prob[["y"]]))
  cat("\nIf this agrees with the within-plex permutation P B18b reports, the significance does not\n",
      "depend on the asymptotics and the penalised interval can replace \"the\n",
      "magnitude is not well determined\" in the Results.\n", sep = "")
  saveRDS(list(beta = b, lo = lo, hi = hi, p = fit$prob[["y"]], n = nrow(d),
               events = sum(d$event), plex_as_factor = use_plex),
          file.path(paths$out_dir, "B18_survival", "firth.rds"))
})
```

## B19 — allocation

B19 / B20 — what the chaperone increase trades against, and who assembles it

Source: `B19_allocation.R`

```{r B19_allocation, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B19 / B20 — what the chaperone increase trades against, and who assembles it
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_allocation.md. Both are post hoc in the sense that
## matters: the protein state was found first. Declared as such wherever
## reported, and neither confirms the original observation.
##
## Base R plus what the session already has.

local({

  need <- c("OP", "paths", "pep_g", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "share_of")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B19 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B19_allocation"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)

  ## ==========================================================================
  ## B19 — what is displaced
  ## ==========================================================================
  ## Nothing new is computed. The existing 30-set table is read in BOTH
  ## directions: the negative side has been reported all along, the positive side
  ## never has. A per-sample share is compositional, so if chaperones are up by
  ## 1.2 points something is down by 1.2 points, and the paper has not said what.
  cat("=== B19: what the chaperone increase trades against ===\n")
  obs <- if (exists("pitt_obs")) pitt_obs else {
    f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "nulls_pitt", "observed_pitt.rds")
    if (file.exists(f)) as.data.frame(readRDS(f)) else NULL
  }
  if (is.null(obs) || !all(c("pathway","NES") %in% names(obs))) {
    cat("  observed set table not available; skipping B19\n")
  } else {
    bare <- function(x) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(x))
    o <- obs[!is.na(obs$NES), ]
    o$lab <- bare(o$pathway)
    up <- o[o$NES > 0, ]; up <- up[order(-up$NES), ]
    cat(sprintf("  %d of %d sets are higher in RESPONDERS (positive NES)\n", nrow(up), nrow(o)))
    cat("  the displaced side, strongest first:\n")
    print(data.frame(set = head(up$lab, 12), NES = round(head(up$NES, 12), 2), row.names = NULL))
    cat("\n  READ: if these fall in one or a few related functional classes, the\n",
        "  result is an allocation trade-off and the classes are named. If they are\n",
        "  scattered, the allocation framing is dropped. No significance is claimed\n",
        "  for this side: it was not pre-specified and sits in the same family that\n",
        "  yields nothing after correction.\n", sep = "")
    write.csv(up[, c("lab","NES")], file.path(od, "displaced_sets.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }

  ## ==========================================================================
  ## B20 — is the state assembled from the same organisms in every patient?
  ## ==========================================================================
  ## For each patient and genus, that genus's contribution to the patient's
  ## share of the set. One vector per patient over genera. The quantity is the
  ## BETWEEN-PATIENT consistency of those vectors.
  ##
  ## THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS INTERPRETABLE. The same procedure runs on
  ## the ribosomal set, which is already known to localise to one genus. A low
  ## correlation on its own could be sparsity or noise; low for chaperones and
  ## high for ribosomes, in the same samples by the same procedure, is the
  ## comparison the prediction was fixed on.
  cat("\n=== B20: is the state assembled from the same organisms in each patient? ===\n")

  ## `chap_new` and `ribo_new` are PROTEIN IDS, not row indices — the first
  ## version intersected them against pep_g$row and matched nothing. Rows come
  ## from OP$rd$Protein, exactly as chap_frac_of does it, and are then intersected
  ## with the rows pep_g can assign to a genus.
  contrib <- function(prots, label) {
    idx <- which(OP$rd$Protein %in% prots)
    if (!length(idx)) { cat("  ", label, ": no PSM rows for these proteins\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    j <- match(idx, pep_g$row)
    ok <- !is.na(j)
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s %d PSM rows, %d assignable to a genus (%.0f%%)\n",
                label, length(idx), sum(ok), 100*mean(ok)))
    if (!any(ok)) { cat("  ", label, ": none assignable to a genus\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    rws <- idx[ok]; gen <- pep_g$tax[j[ok]]
    A <- OP$a[rws, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE]
    A[!is.finite(A)] <- 0
    M <- rowsum(A, as.character(gen))          # genus x sample, this set's protein only
    tot <- colSums(M)
    keep <- tot > 0
    M <- sweep(M[, keep, drop = FALSE], 2, tot[keep], "/")   # each column sums to 1
    M <- M[rowSums(M) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s %d genera x %d samples carry this set\n", label, nrow(M), ncol(M)))
    M
  }

  ## TWO STATISTICS, NOT ONE. The first version used only the between-patient
  ## correlation, and simulation showed it cannot tell "a different genus in each
  ## patient" (the claim) from "no genus dominates anywhere" (noise): the two give
  ## +0.011 and -0.016. The discriminating quantity is WITHIN-patient
  ## concentration.
  ##   top share   — how much of the set one genus supplies in a patient.
  ##                 HIGH for a concentrated state, whether or not the same genus
  ##                 does it each time; LOW when nothing dominates.
  ##   modal top   — how often the SAME genus is the top contributor.
  ##                 HIGH when one organism carries the set everywhere; LOW when
  ##                 different organisms do it in different patients.
  ## Simulated at this shape: one genus everywhere 0.77 / 1.00; a different genus
  ## per patient 0.77 / 0.10; no structure 0.08 / 0.10. Only the pair identifies
  ## the claim, so only the pair is reported.
  consistency <- function(M, label) {
    if (is.null(M) || ncol(M) < 6) return(NULL)
    top_share <- apply(M, 2, max)
    top_genus <- rownames(M)[apply(M, 2, which.max)]
    modal <- max(table(top_genus)) / length(top_genus)
    C <- suppressWarnings(cor(M, method = "spearman"))
    v <- C[upper.tri(C)]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    set.seed(1901)
    bs <- replicate(2000, { i <- sample(ncol(M), ncol(M), replace = TRUE)
      g <- rownames(M)[apply(M[, i, drop = FALSE], 2, which.max)]
      c(median(apply(M[, i, drop = FALSE], 2, max)), max(table(g)) / length(g)) })
    ci_t <- quantile(bs[1, ], c(.025, .975)); ci_m <- quantile(bs[2, ], c(.025, .975))
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s top-contributor share %.3f (%.3f-%.3f) | same genus on top in %.0f%% (%.0f-%.0f%%) | pairwise r %.3f | %d genera, %d samples\n",
                label, median(top_share), ci_t[1], ci_t[2],
                100*modal, 100*ci_m[1], 100*ci_m[2], median(v), nrow(M), ncol(M)))
    list(label = label, top = median(top_share), top_lo = ci_t[1], top_hi = ci_t[2],
         modal = modal, modal_lo = ci_m[1], modal_hi = ci_m[2],
         r = median(v), n_genera = nrow(M), n_samples = ncol(M),
         top_genus = top_genus)
  }

  Mc <- contrib(chap_new, "chaperone")
  Mr <- contrib(ribo_new, "ribosomal")
  cc <- consistency(Mc, "chaperone")
  cr <- consistency(Mr, "ribosomal")

  if (!is.null(cc) && !is.null(cr)) {
    ## bootstrap the DIFFERENCE, resampling patients rather than pairs, so the
    ## interval reflects the unit that actually varies
    cat(sprintf("\n  concentration  chaperone %.3f vs ribosomal %.3f\n", cc$top, cr$top))
    cat(sprintf("  same genus on top  chaperone %.0f%% vs ribosomal %.0f%%\n",
                100*cc$modal, 100*cr$modal))
    cat(sprintf("  most frequent top contributor: chaperone %s, ribosomal %s\n",
                names(which.max(table(cc$top_genus))), names(which.max(table(cr$top_genus)))))
    cat("  No p-value is attached: the two sets differ in size, sparsity and how\n",
        "  many genera carry them, so a formal test would compare quantities that\n",
        "  are not exchangeable. The intervals are reported and the comparison is\n",
        "  described, not tested.\n", sep = "")
    cat("\n  ---- reading, fixed before the run ----\n")
    if (cc$modal_hi < cr$modal_lo && cc$top_hi > 0.3)
      cat("  Chaperone consistency is clearly BELOW ribosomal. The chaperone state is\n",
          "  assembled from different organisms in different patients while the\n",
          "  ribosomal one is not. This is the property that would make the state\n",
          "  invisible to a taxon-indexed measurement, and it is reported as the\n",
          "  explanation the paper offers — correlational, one cohort, not a\n",
          "  demonstration that this IS why the metagenome misses it.\n", sep="")
    else if (cc$modal_lo > cr$modal_hi)
      cat("  Chaperone consistency is ABOVE ribosomal, the opposite of the\n",
          "  prediction. Report it and abandon the functional-state reading.\n", sep="")
    else
      cat("  The two are not distinguishable. No support for the functional-state\n",
          "  reading; it is not offered, and this is reported as a null.\n", sep="")
  }

  saveRDS(list(chaperone = cc, ribosomal = cr), file.path(od, "assembly.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b20_assembly <<- list(chaperone = cc, ribosomal = cr)
})
```

## B20 — compositional sensitivity

Reviewer, Main Claim 1, Gap 3: recompute own-versus-stranger as an Aitchison

Source: `B20_compositional_sensitivity.R`

```{r B20_compositional_sensitivity, eval=FALSE}
## Reviewer, Main Claim 1, Gap 3: recompute own-versus-stranger as an Aitchison
## distance on CLR-transformed KO compositions, across three offsets and on the
## 200 most variable KOs. For a DISTANCE the own value should be SMALLER, so the
## advantage is delta_i = median_j d(i,j) - d(i,i), positive when own is closer.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr)})
FI <- file.path(Sys.getenv("ICB_OUT_DIR", "final_run"), "figure_inputs.rds")
o <- readRDS(FI); MP <- o$cpl_MP; Gp <- o$cpl_G; pat <- o$cpl_pat
pat <- pat[pat$sample %in% colnames(MP) & pat$bio %in% colnames(Gp), ]
MPs <- readRDS("MP_sheba.rds"); pubs <- readRDS("sheba_published.rds")

clr <- function(v, eps) { x <- log(v + eps); x - mean(x) }
ait <- function(MPx, Gx, ss, gg, kos, eps) {
  P <- apply(MPx[kos, ss, drop=FALSE], 2, clr, eps = eps)
  G <- apply(Gx [kos, gg, drop=FALSE], 2, clr, eps = eps)
  n <- length(ss)
  D <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) D[i, ] <- sqrt(colSums((G - P[, i])^2))
  D }
adv <- function(D) { n <- nrow(D)
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) median(D[i,-i]) - D[i,i], 0) }   # >0 = own closer
tst <- function(d) { w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(d, conf.int=TRUE, exact=TRUE))
  sprintf("HL %+8.4f (%+8.4f to %+8.4f)  P %.4f  %2d/%d", unname(w$estimate),
          w$conf.int[1], w$conf.int[2], w$p.value, sum(d>0), length(d)) }

cat("=== Aitchison distance, own closer than stranger? (positive = yes) ===\n")
for (eps in c(1e-9, 1e-6, 1e-3)) {
  k <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(Gp))
  cat(sprintf("  on treatment, all %4d KOs, offset %-6s %s\n", length(k), format(eps), tst(adv(ait(MP,Gp,pat$sample,pat$bio,k,eps)))))
}
## the 200 most variable KOs, defined on the metagenome as in the paper
k0 <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(Gp))
prev <- rowMeans(Gp[k0, pat$bio, drop=FALSE] > 0)
core <- k0[prev >= 0.9]
sdv <- apply(log(Gp[core, pat$bio, drop=FALSE] + 1e-9), 1, sd)
top <- names(sort(sdv, decreasing = TRUE))[1:200]
cat(sprintf("  on treatment, top %3d variable,  offset 1e-09 %s\n", length(top), tst(adv(ait(MP,Gp,pat$sample,pat$bio,top,1e-9)))))
cat("\n")
for (eps in c(1e-9, 1e-6, 1e-3)) {
  ks <- intersect(rownames(MPs), rownames(pubs$KO))
  cat(sprintf("  before treatment, all %4d KOs, offset %-6s %s\n", length(ks), format(eps),
              tst(adv(ait(MPs, pubs$KO, pubs$pairs$sample, pubs$pairs$mg, ks, eps)))))
}

cat("\n=== scale, so the effect sizes above are interpretable ===\n")
k <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(Gp))
D <- ait(MP, Gp, pat$sample, pat$bio, k, 1e-9)
cat(sprintf("  on treatment, all KOs: own distance median %.1f, stranger median %.1f, spread (SD of off-diagonal) %.1f\n",
            median(diag(D)), median(D[row(D)!=col(D)]), sd(D[row(D)!=col(D)])))
cat(sprintf("  the +5.8 advantage is %.1f%% of the own distance and %.2f SD of the stranger spread\n",
            100*5.7975/median(diag(D)), 5.7975/sd(D[row(D)!=col(D)])))
cat("\n  for comparison, Spearman on the same pairs:\n")
EPS <- 1e-12
K <- outer(seq_len(nrow(pat)), seq_len(nrow(pat)), Vectorize(function(i,j){
  x <- MP[k, pat$sample[i]]; kk <- x>0
  suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[kk]+EPS), log(Gp[k, pat$bio[j]][kk]+EPS), method="spearman"))}))
cat(sprintf("  own rho median %.4f, stranger median %.4f, spread %.4f; the +0.0039 advantage is %.1f%% of own and %.2f SD\n",
            median(diag(K)), median(K[row(K)!=col(K)]), sd(K[row(K)!=col(K)]),
            100*0.003905/median(diag(K)), 0.003905/sd(K[row(K)!=col(K)])))
```

## B21 — panel control

does the host inflammatory panel behave as a gut-inflammation measure?

Source: `B21_panel_control.R`

```{r B21_panel_control, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B21 — does the host inflammatory panel behave as a gut-inflammation measure?
## ============================================================================
##
## THIS IS A MEASUREMENT CHECK, NOT A CLINICAL TEST, and the distinction governs
## everything below including how a positive result may be written up.
##
## The panel is nine host proteins summed and expressed relative to total host
## protein: lactotransferrin, calprotectin (S100A8 and S100A9), myeloperoxidase,
## neutrophil elastase, cathepsin G, lysozyme C, lipocalin-2 and defensin 5. The
## Discussion leans on it as a measure of gut inflammatory activity, and on the
## observation that it runs inverse to the bacterial chaperone share. Before
## leaning on it further it is worth knowing whether it moves at all with a
## clinical state that should raise gut inflammation.
##
## Checkpoint blockade causes immune-related toxicity, much of it gastro-
## intestinal, so the panel should be higher in patients who experienced an
## adverse event. If it is, the panel is behaving as intended. If it is not, the
## Discussion's use of it is on weaker ground than it appears and should be
## reconsidered.
##
## WHAT THIS CANNOT BE. The recorded variable is any immune-related adverse
## event, coded 0/1, with no organ and no grade: rash, thyroiditis, fatigue and
## colitis are one category, and 70% of patients have one. The clinically
## meaningful question for calprotectin is COLITIS, which this column cannot
## answer. A positive result here is a statement that the panel tracks a coarse
## toxicity variable, not that it marks checkpoint colitis, and it must not be
## written up as the latter. A null is uninformative about colitis.
##
## Power, computed before the run: 18 against 43 detects a difference of about
## 1.0 standard deviations four times in five. Differences smaller than that will
## be missed, so a null bounds rather than excludes.

local({

  need <- c("OP", "SAMP_PRIMARY", "hs", "INFL", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B21 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }

  sp <- as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY)
  if ("cohort" %in% names(sp)) sp <- sp[sp$cohort %in% c("pitt","Pittsburgh"), , drop = FALSE]
  icol <- intersect(c("irae","irAE","IRAE"), names(sp))
  if (!length(icol)) { cat("B21 SKIPPED: no irAE column\n"); return(invisible()) }
  sp$ae <- sp[[icol[1]]]

  ## the panel, exactly as the manuscript defines it
  infl <- colSums(hs[INFL, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
          colSums(hs[,     OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  d <- data.frame(sample = OP$d$sample, Mixture = OP$d$Mixture,
                  resp = OP$d$resp, infl = infl[OP$d$sample])
  key <- intersect(c("sample","BioReplicate","bio"), intersect(names(d), names(sp)))
  if (!length(key)) { cat("B21 SKIPPED: no shared key\n"); return(invisible()) }
  d <- merge(d, sp[, c(key[1], "ae")], by = key[1])
  d <- d[is.finite(d$infl) & !is.na(d$ae), , drop = FALSE]
  d$ae <- factor(ifelse(d$ae == 1, "irAE", "none"), levels = c("none","irAE"))

  cat(sprintf("\n%d samples with both a proteome and an irAE record: %s\n", nrow(d),
              paste(names(table(d$ae)), table(d$ae), sep = "=", collapse = ", ")))
  if (min(table(d$ae)) < 8) {
    cat("*** too few in the smaller group to interpret; reporting counts only\n"); return(invisible())
  }

  ## WITHIN PLEX, like everything else here. The panel is plex-structured, which
  ## the manuscript already reports, so an unrestricted comparison would partly
  ## test batch.
  m <- lm(qlogis(pmin(pmax(infl, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)) ~ Mixture + ae, data = d)
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  row <- grep("^aeirAE$", rownames(co))
  est <- co[row, "Estimate"]; se <- co[row, "Std. Error"]

  set.seed(2101); B <- 10000L
  null <- numeric(B)
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    dd <- d
    for (s in unique(dd$Mixture)) { j <- which(dd$Mixture == s); dd$ae[j] <- sample(dd$ae[j]) }
    mm <- lm(qlogis(pmin(pmax(infl, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)) ~ Mixture + ae, data = dd)
    cc <- summary(mm)$coefficients
    r <- grep("^aeirAE$", rownames(cc))
    null[b] <- if (length(r)) cc[r, "Estimate"] else NA_real_
  }
  null <- null[is.finite(null)]
  p <- (1 + sum(abs(null) >= abs(est))) / (1 + length(null))

  cat(sprintf("\npanel in irAE against none, plex-adjusted: %+.3f logit units (SE %.3f)\n", est, se))
  cat(sprintf("  within-plex permutation P = %.4f over %d draws\n", p, length(null)))
  cat(sprintf("  raw medians: none %.4f, irAE %.4f\n",
              median(d$infl[d$ae == "none"]), median(d$infl[d$ae == "irAE"])))

  cat("\n---- reading, fixed before the run ----\n")
  if (p < 0.05 && est > 0)
    cat("The panel is higher in patients who experienced immune-related toxicity,\n",
        "which is how a gut-inflammation measure should behave. This supports USING\n",
        "the panel, and nothing more. It is not evidence about checkpoint colitis:\n",
        "the variable is any adverse event of any organ and grade. Write it as a\n",
        "measurement check.\n", sep = "")
  else if (p < 0.05)
    cat("The panel is LOWER in patients with recorded toxicity, which is the\n",
        "opposite of what a gut-inflammation measure should do. The Discussion's\n",
        "use of the panel needs reconsidering, not rewording.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("No difference detected. At this size a difference below about one\n",
        "standard deviation would be missed, so this does not show the panel is\n",
        "inert — but it also does not support leaning on it. Report the null and\n",
        "soften the Discussion's use of the panel accordingly.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B21_panel_control"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(est = est, se = se, p = p, n = nrow(d), tab = table(d$ae)),
          file.path(od, "panel_control.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b21_panel <<- list(est = est, p = p)
})
```

## B22 — attenuation

does the coupling predict the DNA-level null?

Source: `B22_attenuation.R`

```{r B22_attenuation, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B22 — does the coupling predict the DNA-level null?
## ============================================================================
##
## The manuscript currently asserts that the response-associated protein state is
## the kind of thing the weak coupling would hide. That is an assertion. It can
## be a calculation, and the calculation has a sharper form than a power
## argument.
##
## THE LOGIC. If gene capacity G relates to protein share P across patients with
## correlation r, then a response difference of d standard deviations in P
## appears in G as r*d standard deviations. That is the standard attenuation
## result for a proxy: regress G on P and the response shift propagates in
## proportion to the correlation. So the coupling measured in the first pillar
## PREDICTS the size of the DNA-level effect, and the prediction can be compared
## with the DNA-level effect actually observed.
##
## VERIFIED by simulation before this was written: building G with a known
## correlation to P and shifting P by a known amount, the predicted r*dP and the
## observed dG agree to within 0.01 over 3,000 replicates.
##
## WHAT THE IDENTITY ASSUMES, and the assumption is not free. It treats gene
## capacity as a noisy proxy for protein share — a single latent quantity
## measured two ways. If the response acts on the two layers through partly
## separate routes, which is exactly what the clade result suggests, the identity
## is an approximation and the prediction is a lower bound on how much the DNA
## layer could carry. Reported as such, never as an exact expectation.
##
## THE RIGHT r. Not 0.238. That number is the correspondence across gene families
## within a patient, which is a different quantity. What is needed is the
## correlation ACROSS PATIENTS between a set's gene capacity and that set's
## protein share — the relationship Figure 2c draws and the manuscript never
## quotes a coefficient for. It is computed here, batch-adjusted, as in that
## figure.
##
## THREE OUTCOMES, all reported:
##   observed DNA effect close to predicted  — the two pillars are one statement.
##     The DNA layer is not silent, it is attenuated by exactly the amount the
##     coupling says it should be.
##   observed much SMALLER than predicted    — something suppresses the signal
##     beyond attenuation; reported as unexplained.
##   observed much LARGER than predicted     — the DNA layer carries more than
##     the coupling allows, which would undercut the framing. Reported.

local({

  need <- c("OP", "MGm", "paths", "share_of", "chap_new", "ribo_new",
            "CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B22 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }

  ## ---- per-patient quantities -------------------------------------------------
  ## protein side: the set's share of microbial protein, as everywhere else
  ## DNA side: the set's share of gene abundance, from the KO-level matrix
  ## `cpl_kos` is a VECTOR of KO names, not a matrix — the first version
  ## intersected against its colnames and matched nothing. The gene matrix is
  ## `cpl_G`, with KOs as ROWS and patients indexed by `bio` rather than by
  ## sample, so the join to OP$d has to go through bio.
  if (!exists("cpl_G")) { cat("B22 STOPPED: cpl_G (the KO x patient gene matrix) not in the session\n")
                          return(invisible()) }
  Gm <- cpl_G
  cat(sprintf("gene matrix: %d rows x %d columns; rownames look like %s\n",
              nrow(Gm), ncol(Gm), paste(utils::head(rownames(Gm), 2), collapse = ", ")))
  ## orientation guard: KOs must be the rows
  if (!any(grepl("^K[0-9]{5}$", rownames(Gm)))) {
    if (any(grepl("^K[0-9]{5}$", colnames(Gm)))) { Gm <- t(Gm); cat("  transposed: KOs were columns\n") }
    else { cat("B22 STOPPED: no KO identifiers on either margin of cpl_G\n"); return(invisible()) }
  }
  dna_share <- function(kos) {
    k <- intersect(kos, rownames(Gm))
    if (!length(k)) { cat(sprintf("    0 of %d KOs present in the gene matrix\n", length(kos))); return(NULL) }
    cat(sprintf("    %d of %d KOs present in the gene matrix\n", length(k), length(kos)))
    colSums(Gm[k, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) / colSums(Gm, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  one <- function(prots, kos, label) {
    cat(sprintf("\n  %s:\n", label))
    P <- share_of(prots)[OP$d$sample]
    G <- dna_share(kos)
    if (is.null(G)) return(NULL)
    ## The gene matrix is keyed by bio. OP$d does not carry bio, but `cpl_pat`
    ## does — v17 builds it as sample/bio/resp precisely for this join, and the
    ## coupling analysis uses it the same way.
    pm <- NULL
    if (exists("cpl_pat")) {
      cp <- as.data.frame(cpl_pat)
      if (all(c("sample","bio") %in% names(cp))) pm <- cp[, c("sample","bio")]
    }
    if (is.null(pm)) {
      k <- intersect(c("bio","BioReplicate","probe_join"), names(OP$d))
      if (length(k)) pm <- data.frame(sample = OP$d$sample, bio = as.character(OP$d[[k[1]]]))
    }
    if (is.null(pm)) {
      cat("    no sample-to-bio mapping found. cpl_pat present: ", exists("cpl_pat"),
          "; OP$d columns: ", paste(utils::head(names(OP$d), 20), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
      return(NULL)
    }
    pd <- merge(data.frame(sample = OP$d$sample, resp = OP$d$resp,
                           Mixture = OP$d$Mixture, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                pm, by = "sample")
    pd$bio <- as.character(pd$bio)
    pd$P <- P[pd$sample]
    pd$G <- G[match(pd$bio, names(G))]
    d <- pd[is.finite(pd$P) & is.finite(pd$G), , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("    %d of %d samples have both layers\n", nrow(d), nrow(pd)))
    if (nrow(d) < 15) return(NULL)
    d$P <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(d$P, 1e-6), 1-1e-6))
    d$G <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(d$G, 1e-6), 1-1e-6))
    d$resp <- droplevels(factor(d$resp))
    if (nlevels(d$resp) < 2) return(NULL)

    ## batch-adjust both axes, as Figure 2c does, then correlate ACROSS PATIENTS
    rP <- residuals(lm(P ~ Mixture, data = d)); rG <- residuals(lm(G ~ Mixture, data = d))
    r  <- cor(rP, rG, method = "spearman")

    ## observed standardised effects on each layer, batch-adjusted
    eff <- function(x) {
      a <- x[d$resp == "NR"]; b <- x[d$resp == "R"]
      (mean(a) - mean(b)) / sd(x)
    }
    dP <- eff(rP); dG_obs <- eff(rG)
    dG_pred <- r * dP

    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] %d patients (%s)\n", label, nrow(d),
                paste(names(table(d$resp)), table(d$resp), sep="=", collapse=", ")))
    cat(sprintf("  coupling across patients, batch-adjusted:  r = %+.3f\n", r))
    cat(sprintf("  protein-layer effect:                      %+.3f SD\n", dP))
    cat(sprintf("  DNA-layer effect PREDICTED by the coupling: %+.3f SD\n", dG_pred))
    cat(sprintf("  DNA-layer effect OBSERVED:                  %+.3f SD\n", dG_obs))

    ## is a cohort this size able to see the predicted effect at all?
    n1 <- sum(d$resp == "NR"); n2 <- sum(d$resp == "R")
    set.seed(2201)
    pw <- mean(replicate(4000, {
      x <- rnorm(n1, dG_pred); y <- rnorm(n2)
      suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x, y)$p.value) < 0.05 }))
    cat(sprintf("  power to detect the predicted effect at %d vs %d: %.2f\n", n1, n2, pw))
    ## and what cohort would be needed
    need_n <- NA_integer_
    for (n in seq(20, 2000, by = 20)) {
      p <- mean(replicate(800, {
        suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(rnorm(n, dG_pred), rnorm(n))$p.value) < 0.05 }))
      if (p >= 0.8) { need_n <- n; break }
    }
    cat(sprintf("  patients per arm for 80%% power at the DNA layer: %s\n",
                if (is.na(need_n)) ">2000" else format(need_n)))
    data.frame(set = label, n = nrow(d), n_NR = n1, n_R = n2, r = r, dP = dP,
               dG_pred = dG_pred, dG_obs = dG_obs, power = pw, need_n = need_n)
  }

  res <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
    one(chap_new, CHAPERONE_KO, "chaperone"),
    one(ribo_new, RIBO_KO,      "ribosomal"))))

  cat("\n---- reading, fixed before the run ----\n")
  if (is.null(res)) { cat("nothing computable.\n"); return(invisible()) }
  ## THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS RULE WAS TOO LENIENT. It asked whether the
  ## observed and predicted DNA effects differ by less than half the PROTEIN
  ## effect, a window so wide that almost anything passes, and it reported
  ## "close to predicted" when the observed values were 13% and 30% of the
  ## prediction. The comparison has to be made against the precision of the
  ## DNA estimate, not against the size of the protein effect.
  se <- sqrt(1/res$n_NR + 1/res$n_R)
  res$gap_se <- (res$dG_pred - res$dG_obs) / se
  cat(sprintf("\n  the DNA estimate has SE %.3f SD at this cohort size\n", se[1]))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(res)))
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s predicted %+.3f, observed %+.3f (%.0f%% of predicted), gap %.2f SE\n",
                res$set[i], res$dG_pred[i], res$dG_obs[i],
                100*res$dG_obs[i]/res$dG_pred[i], res$gap_se[i]))
  if (all(abs(res$gap_se) < 2))
    cat("\n  The DNA estimate CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'attenuated exactly as predicted'\n",
        "  from 'absent': the prediction sits inside the estimate's own error. So the\n",
        "  observed DNA values support nothing on their own, and the argument must\n",
        "  rest on the two quantities that ARE measured — the coupling and the\n",
        "  protein effect — and on what they jointly imply: an effect of about\n",
        sprintf("  %.2f SD at the DNA layer, needing roughly %d patients per arm.\n",
                mean(res$dG_pred), round(mean(res$need_n, na.rm = TRUE))),
        "  That is the defensible claim. 'The DNA null matches the prediction' is\n",
        "  not, because this design could not have told the difference.\n", sep = "")
  else if (all(res$gap_se > 2))
    cat("\n  The DNA layer carries significantly LESS than attenuation predicts.\n",
        "  Something beyond the coupling suppresses it; report as unexplained.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("\n  The DNA layer carries MORE than the coupling allows for at least one\n",
        "  set. That undercuts the framing and is reported as such.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B22_attenuation"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(res, file.path(od, "attenuation.rds")); write.csv(res, file.path(od, "attenuation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  print(res, digits = 3)
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b22_atten <<- res
})
```

## B23 — profile replication

does the set-level response profile replicate across cohorts?

Source: `B23_profile_replication.R`

```{r B23_profile_replication, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B23 — does the set-level response profile replicate across cohorts?
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_profile.md before this was run.
##
## WHY. The second cohort's pre-specified test asks one question of eight
## non-responders and recovers the discovery effect about one run in three. But
## the same analysis scores EVERY set in both cohorts, and asking whether those
## two vectors correspond uses thirty paired values instead of one. It asks
## whether the SHAPE of the response-associated profile is the same, which is a
## question a cohort this size can actually answer.
##
## THE NULL CANNOT BE THE TEXTBOOK ONE. The sets are nested, overlapping and
## partly partition the proteome, so scores within a cohort are not independent
## and a correlation p computed as if they were would be wrong. The null is built
## by shuffling response within plex in the second cohort, recomputing that
## cohort's scores, and correlating against the first cohort's fixed vector.
##
## CIRCULARITY. The chaperone and ribosomal sets are in the vector and they are
## the sets the discovery cohort selected. A correlation driven entirely by them
## would be close to circular, so the analysis is repeated with the reported sets
## removed. THE VALUE WITH THEM REMOVED IS THE ONE THAT BEARS ON REPLICATION.
##
## POWER, simulated before the run. Twenty-four sets after the reported ones are
## removed is not many paired values: the test detects a profile 70% shared
## between cohorts about seven times in ten, and one 50% shared about three times
## in ten. A null therefore does not exclude a moderate correspondence, and the
## reading below says so.

local({

  B <- 2000L; SEED <- 2301L
  REPORTED <- c("O_chap", "chaperones", "O_chap_noGD", "O_remainder", "ribosomal", "O")

  if (!exists("paths")) { cat("B23 SKIPPED: paths missing\n"); return(invisible()) }
  bare <- function(x) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(x))

  ## ---- the two observed score vectors ----------------------------------------
  grab <- function(cands, label) {
    for (f in cands) if (file.exists(f)) {
      d <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f))
      if (all(c("pathway","NES") %in% names(d))) {
        cat(sprintf("  %-12s %s (%d sets)\n", label, basename(dirname(f)), nrow(d)))
        return(d)
      }
    }
    NULL
  }
  o1 <- if (exists("pitt_obs")) pitt_obs else
        grab(file.path(paths$out_dir, c("nulls_pitt","nulls_pitt_ext"), "observed_pitt.rds"), "cohort 1")
  ## the second cohort's observed vector must come from the PRE-SPECIFIED arm,
  ## identified by its observed NES for COG O, exactly as Figure 5a does
  PRIMARY_NES <- -1.48
  o2 <- NULL; d2 <- NA_character_
  for (dd in list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE)) {
    if (!grepl("sheba", dd, ignore.case = TRUE)) next
    f <- list.files(dd, "^observed.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
    if (!length(f)) next
    x <- try(as.data.frame(readRDS(f[1])), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(x, "try-error") || !all(c("pathway","NES") %in% names(x))) next
    v <- x$NES[bare(x$pathway) == "O"]
    if (length(v) && abs(v[1] - PRIMARY_NES) <= 0.05) { o2 <- x; d2 <- dd; break }
  }
  ## COMPUTE IT IF IT IS NOT ARCHIVED. The pre-specified arm's observed table is
  ## not on disk — the archiving gap recorded in the project notes — but this
  ## analysis does not need the archive. If the session can rebuild that cohort's
  ## scores for the permutation null, it can build the observed vector the same
  ## way, from the real labels. Doing so also tests something worth knowing: if
  ## the recomputed COG O score is the pre-specified -1.48, the arm IS
  ## reproducible in-session even though it was never archived.
  ## The second cohort's ranking statistic is `st_s` (from FS$res$t), not
  ## `stat_sheba` — that name does not exist. It is a plain named vector, so the
  ## observed scores are one fgsea call away and need no archive.
  st_s_obj <- if (exists("st_s")) st_s else if (exists("FS")) {
    v <- stats::setNames(FS$res$t, FS$res$feature); v[is.finite(v)] } else NULL
  if (is.null(o2) && !is.null(st_s_obj) && exists("SETS_S")) {
    cat(sprintf("  cohort 2 not on disk; scoring st_s (%d features) against SETS_S (%d sets)\n",
                length(st_s_obj), length(SETS_S)))
    st <- st_s_obj
    if (!is.null(st)) {
      sc <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(SETS_S, st)),
                     error = function(e) { cat("    fgsea failed: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep=""); NULL })
      if (!is.null(sc) && all(c("pathway","NES") %in% names(sc))) {
        v <- sc$NES[bare(sc$pathway) == "O"]
        cat(sprintf("    recomputed COG O score: %+.3f (pre-specified primary is %+.2f)\n",
                    if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_, PRIMARY_NES))
        if (length(v) && abs(v[1] - PRIMARY_NES) <= 0.08) {
          o2 <- sc; d2 <- "recomputed in-session"
          cat("    matches: the arm is reproducible in-session though not archived\n")
        } else {
          cat("    DOES NOT MATCH the pre-specified primary. The session is not\n",
              "    reproducing that arm either, which is a larger problem than the\n",
              "    missing archive. Not proceeding.\n", sep = "")
        }
      }
    }
  }
  if (is.null(o1) || is.null(o2)) {
    cat("\nB23 STOPPED: no observed vector for ",
        if (is.null(o2)) "the second cohort" else "the first cohort", ".\n",
        if (is.null(o2))
          paste0("  The pre-specified arm is neither archived nor rebuildable here.\n",
                 "  It needs stat_sheba, SETS_S and OS in the session, or the arm\n",
                 "  re-run with its observed table saved.\n") else "", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  cat("  cohort 2 from ", if (d2 == "recomputed in-session") d2 else basename(d2), "\n", sep = "")

  o1$key <- bare(o1$pathway); o2$key <- bare(o2$pathway)
  m <- merge(o1[, c("key","NES")], o2[, c("key","NES")], by = "key", suffixes = c("_1","_2"))
  m <- m[is.finite(m$NES_1) & is.finite(m$NES_2), , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("\n%d sets scored in both cohorts (of %d and %d)\n", nrow(m), nrow(o1), nrow(o2)))
  if (nrow(m) < 10) { cat("too few shared sets\n"); return(invisible()) }

  obs_all  <- cor(m$NES_1, m$NES_2, method = "spearman")
  keep     <- !(m$key %in% REPORTED)
  obs_excl <- if (sum(keep) >= 8) cor(m$NES_1[keep], m$NES_2[keep], method = "spearman") else NA_real_
  cat(sprintf("  all %d sets:                 rho = %+.3f\n", nrow(m), obs_all))
  cat(sprintf("  excluding the %d reported:   rho = %+.3f  (%d sets)\n",
              sum(!keep), obs_excl, sum(keep)))

  ## ---- the null ---------------------------------------------------------------
  ## THE NULL I FIRST SPECIFIED IS NOT FEASIBLE. It shuffled response within plex
  ## and refit the second cohort's model 2,000 times; that model is a fit per
  ## feature over thousands of features, so the cost is hours to days, not
  ## minutes. Rather than run 50 draws and call it a null, the design changed.
  ##
  ## WHAT IS DONE INSTEAD. The objection to a textbook correlation p was that the
  ## sets are nested and overlapping, so they are not independent. That objection
  ## is addressed directly: sets with identical membership are collapsed to one,
  ## and the correlation is computed on the distinct ones. The null then permutes
  ## which cohort-2 score pairs with which cohort-1 score, which breaks the
  ## correspondence while preserving both vectors' distributions.
  ##
  ## WHAT THAT NULL STILL ASSUMES. Collapsing identical sets does not make the
  ## remainder independent — sets can overlap heavily without being identical,
  ## and a label permutation treats them as exchangeable. The p below is
  ## therefore approximate and is reported as such. It is not a within-plex
  ## permutation and must not be described as one.
  memkey <- function(S) vapply(S, function(v) paste(sort(unique(v)), collapse = "\u0001"), "")
  dedup_keys <- NULL
  if (exists("SETS_S")) {
    mk <- memkey(SETS_S)
    first <- !duplicated(mk)
    dedup_keys <- bare(names(SETS_S)[first])
    cat(sprintf("\n  %d of %d sets have distinct membership\n", sum(first), length(SETS_S)))
  }
  md <- if (is.null(dedup_keys)) m else m[m$key %in% dedup_keys, , drop = FALSE]
  kd <- !(md$key %in% REPORTED)
  can <- nrow(md) >= 10 && sum(kd) >= 8
  if (!can) {
    cat("  too few distinct sets for a null; correlations above are descriptive only\n")
  } else {
    rho_d  <- cor(md$NES_1, md$NES_2, method = "spearman")
    rho_de <- cor(md$NES_1[kd], md$NES_2[kd], method = "spearman")
    cat(sprintf("  distinct sets only:          rho = %+.3f (%d sets)\n", rho_d, nrow(md)))
    cat(sprintf("  distinct, reported removed:  rho = %+.3f (%d sets)\n", rho_de, sum(kd)))
    set.seed(SEED)
    na_ <- replicate(B, cor(md$NES_1, sample(md$NES_2), method = "spearman"))
    ne_ <- replicate(B, cor(md$NES_1[kd], sample(md$NES_2[kd]), method = "spearman"))
    pa <- (1 + sum(na_ >= rho_d))  / (1 + B)
    pe <- (1 + sum(ne_ >= rho_de)) / (1 + B)
    cat(sprintf("  approximate P, distinct sets:            %.4f\n", pa))
    cat(sprintf("  approximate P, reported sets removed:    %.4f\n", pe))
    obs_all <- rho_d; obs_excl <- rho_de
  }
  ## ---- reading, fixed before the run -----------------------------------------
  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  if (!can) {
    cat("  No null, so no claim. The correlations above are descriptive only.\n")
  } else if (pe < 0.05 && obs_excl > 0) {
    cat("  The response-associated profile has the same shape in both cohorts,\n",
        "  across sets that were selected on neither. This is the strongest\n",
        "  replication statement the second cohort can support. Report it as a\n",
        "  statement about PROFILE SHAPE, not about any individual set, and keep\n",
        "  the caveat that a set name indexes different proteins in the two\n",
        "  cohorts.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (pa < 0.05 && obs_all > 0) {
    cat("  Positive only with the reported sets included, which is close to\n",
        "  circular: those are the sets the first cohort selected. Report as\n",
        "  uninformative, not as support.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (obs_excl < 0 && pe > 0.95) {
    cat("  The profiles are ANTI-correlated. Report it; the cross-cohort framing\n",
        "  needs reconsidering rather than rewording.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("  No correspondence detected. The second cohort does not reproduce the\n",
        "  first at the only resolution where it has the numbers to try, and that\n",
        "  weakens the paper's framing; it is reported for that reason, not despite\n",
        "  it. The null does NOT exclude a moderate correspondence: at twenty-four\n",
        "  sets this test misses a half-shared profile seven times in ten.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B23_profile"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(merged = m, rho_all = obs_all, rho_excl = obs_excl,
               p_all = if (can) pa else NA_real_, p_excl = if (can) pe else NA_real_,
               n_sets = nrow(m), source2 = d2), file.path(od, "profile.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b23_profile <<- list(rho_all = obs_all, rho_excl = obs_excl)
})
```

## B24 — leading edge

B24 / B25 — leading-edge overlap, and an interval for the second cohort

Source: `B24_leading_edge.R`

```{r B24_leading_edge, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B24 / B25 — leading-edge overlap, and an interval for the second cohort
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_leadingedge.md. Both post hoc with respect to the
## protein state, and declared so wherever reported.
##
## B24 asks a question neither the pre-specified test nor B23 reaches: do the
## same PROTEINS drive the enrichment in both cohorts? Enrichment comes from a
## subset of a set's members, the leading edge. Whether those overlap is
## replication evidence at protein resolution and does not depend on either
## cohort's p-value. It also avoids B23's circularity, since each cohort's
## leading edge comes from its own ranking rather than from a set one cohort
## selected.
##
## OVERLAP IS MEASURED IN KEGG ORTHOLOGY SPACE, NOT ON PROTEIN IDS.
## The first version compared protein identifiers and found ZERO shared proteins
## between the cohorts — correctly, because each cohort's database is built from
## its own metagenome assembly, so protein IDs are assembly artefacts that cannot
## match across cohorts by construction. The shared vocabulary is the annotation.
## Leading-edge proteins are therefore mapped to their primary KO, and overlap is
## measured over the KOs present in both cohorts' universes. This is also the
## better question: "the same orthologs drive it" is a claim about biology, where
## "the same protein IDs" would have been a claim about two assemblies.
##
## THE NULL IS ABUNDANCE-MATCHED, NOT HYPERGEOMETRIC. Both leading edges are
## biased toward abundant, well-measured proteins, so a random draw from the
## shared space would be too easy to beat.
##
## MEASURED before the run: two INDEPENDENT abundance-biased edges of 120 and 90
## proteins overlap by about 6 at this scale. A uniform null expects 2.7 and
## would call independent lists "replicating" at P < 0.05 in 57% of runs; the
## abundance-matched null expects 6.1. A hypergeometric test here would have
## manufactured a result.
##
## AND THE NULL MUST DRAW FROM THE SET, NOT THE UNIVERSE. The first run of this
## analysis returned P = 0.0005 for both sets and the result was an artefact of
## exactly that error. A leading edge can only contain members of its own set, so
## drawing the null from all 498 shared KOs compares against a space the edges
## could never have come from. For the chaperone set, whose membership is the
## same KO list in both cohorts, the effect is extreme: with edges of 9 and 7
## KOs, a null drawn from 498 expects an overlap of 0.1, while a null drawn from
## the set's own ~9-19 shared KOs expects 3.3 to 7.0 — that is, close to or equal
## to the observed 6. The test only means something if the null is drawn from the
## set's shared members, and if the set has enough of them for the edges to have
## had a choice.
##
## A NULL RESULT BOUNDS NOTHING, and that is fixed before the run: the set is not
## extreme in the second cohort (P = 0.155), so its leading edge is the top of a
## ranking that is not strongly ordered and is partly arbitrary.

local({

  B <- 2000L; SEED <- 2401L
  bare <- function(z) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(z))

  need <- c("stat_pitt", "SETS_P", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B24 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  st_s_obj <- if (exists("st_s")) st_s else NULL
  sets_s   <- if (exists("SETS_S")) SETS_S else NULL
  if (is.null(st_s_obj) || is.null(sets_s)) {
    cat("B24 SKIPPED: the second cohort needs st_s and SETS_S\n"); return(invisible()) }

  ## ---- score both cohorts, keeping the leading edges --------------------------
  score <- function(sets, stat, label) {
    r <- tryCatch(fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(sets, stat, minSize = 10, eps = 0),
                  error = function(e) { cat("  ", label, ": fgsea failed: ",
                                            conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep=""); NULL })
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    r <- as.data.frame(r); r$key <- bare(r$pathway)
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s %d sets scored over %d features\n", label, nrow(r), length(stat)))
    r
  }
  r1 <- score(SETS_P, stat_pitt, "cohort 1")
  r2 <- score(sets_s, st_s_obj,  "cohort 2")
  if (is.null(r1) || is.null(r2)) return(invisible())
  if (!"leadingEdge" %in% names(r1)) { cat("B24 STOPPED: fgsea returned no leadingEdge column\n")
                                       return(invisible()) }

  ## map proteins to KOs, per cohort
  if (!exists("annot_new")) { cat("B24 STOPPED: annot_new is needed to map proteins to KOs\n")
                              return(invisible()) }
  an <- as.data.frame(annot_new)
  ko_of <- function(prots, coh) {
    a <- an[an$cohort == coh & an$protein %in% prots & !is.na(an$ko_primary), ]
    unique(as.character(a$ko_primary))
  }
  univ1 <- ko_of(names(stat_pitt),  "pitt")
  univ2 <- ko_of(names(st_s_obj),   "sheba")
  shared_space <- intersect(univ1, univ2)
  cat(sprintf("\nKOs in each cohort's universe: %d and %d; shared: %d\n",
              length(univ1), length(univ2), length(shared_space)))
  if (length(shared_space) < 100) {
    cat("  too small a shared KO space for a meaningful overlap test\n"); return(invisible()) }

  ## abundance proxy for matching: the rank statistic's magnitude is NOT
  ## abundance, so use the protein's own signal where available
  ## abundance per KO in the first cohort, for matching the null
  ab <- if (exists("OP") && !is.null(OP$a)) {
    v  <- rowSums(OP$a, na.rm = TRUE)
    nm <- if (!is.null(OP$rd$Protein)) as.character(OP$rd$Protein) else rownames(OP$a)
    pa <- tapply(v, nm, sum)
    k  <- an$ko_primary[match(names(pa), an$protein)]
    ok <- !is.na(k)
    tapply(pa[ok], as.character(k[ok]), sum)[shared_space]
  } else setNames(rep(1, length(shared_space)), shared_space)
  ab[!is.finite(ab)] <- min(ab[is.finite(ab)], na.rm = TRUE)
  dec <- cut(rank(ab, ties.method = "first"), breaks = 10, labels = FALSE)
  names(dec) <- shared_space

  ## ---- B24: overlap, per set --------------------------------------------------
  cat("\n=== B24: leading-edge overlap ===\n")
  out <- lapply(c("O", "chaperones"), function(k) {
    i1 <- which(r1$key == k); i2 <- which(r2$key == k)
    if (!length(i1) || !length(i2)) { cat("  ", k, ": not scored in both\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    p1 <- unlist(r1$leadingEdge[[i1]]); p2 <- unlist(r2$leadingEdge[[i2]])
    le1 <- intersect(ko_of(p1, "pitt"),  shared_space)
    le2 <- intersect(ko_of(p2, "sheba"), shared_space)
    cat(sprintf("  %-12s leading edges: %d and %d proteins -> %d and %d shared KOs\n",
                k, length(p1), length(p2), length(le1), length(le2)))
    if (length(le1) < 5 || length(le2) < 5) {
      cat("               too few mapped KOs to test\n"); return(NULL) }
    ov <- length(intersect(le1, le2))
    set.seed(SEED)
    ## draw lists matched to le1 and le2 on abundance decile
    draw <- function(le) {
      tb <- table(dec[le])
      unlist(lapply(names(tb), function(d) {
        pool <- shared_space[dec[shared_space] == as.integer(d)]
        sample(pool, min(tb[[d]], length(pool)))
      }))
    }
    ## THE POOL IS THE SET'S OWN SHARED MEMBERS. A leading edge cannot contain a
    ## KO outside its set, so the null has to be drawn from the same place the
    ## edges were.
    set_kos <- intersect(union(ko_of(unlist(SETS_P[[which(bare(names(SETS_P)) == k)[1]]]), "pitt"),
                               ko_of(unlist(sets_s[[which(bare(names(sets_s)) == k)[1]]]), "sheba")),
                         shared_space)
    cat(sprintf("               the set has %d KOs in the shared space\n", length(set_kos)))
    if (length(set_kos) < max(length(le1), length(le2)) + 3) {
      cat("               NOT TESTABLE: the set has barely more shared KOs than the\n",
          "               edges contain, so the overlap is near-forced. Reported as\n",
          "               uninformative.\n", sep = "")
      return(data.frame(set = k, n1 = length(le1), n2 = length(le2), overlap = ov,
                        set_shared = length(set_kos), null_median = NA_real_, P = NA_real_))
    }
    pool_dec <- dec[set_kos]
    draw <- function(le) {
      tb <- table(pool_dec[le]); tb <- tb[!is.na(names(tb))]
      unlist(lapply(names(tb), function(d) {
        pool <- set_kos[!is.na(pool_dec) & pool_dec == as.integer(d)]
        if (!length(pool)) character(0) else sample(pool, min(tb[[d]], length(pool)))
      }))
    }
    nullov <- replicate(B, length(intersect(draw(le1), draw(le2))))
    p <- (1 + sum(nullov >= ov)) / (1 + B)
    cat(sprintf("               overlap %d KOs (%.0f%% of the smaller edge)\n",
                ov, 100*ov/min(length(le1), length(le2))))
    cat(sprintf("               abundance-matched null median %d; P = %.4f\n",
                stats::median(nullov), p))
    data.frame(set = k, n1 = length(le1), n2 = length(le2), overlap = ov,
               set_shared = length(set_kos),
               null_median = stats::median(nullov), P = p)
  })
  res <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), out))

  cat("\n---- reading, fixed before the run ----\n")
  if (!is.null(res) && any(is.na(res$P)))
    cat("  At least one set has too few shared KOs for its leading edges to have\n",
        "  had a choice, so the overlap there is near-forced and is not a test.\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(res) && any(res$P < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))
    cat("  The same proteins drive the signal in both cohorts, above an\n",
        "  abundance-matched null. This is replication at protein resolution and\n",
        "  does not depend on either cohort's set-level p. It is the strongest\n",
        "  statement the second cohort can make.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("  No overlap above the null. THIS BOUNDS NOTHING. The set is not extreme\n",
        "  in the second cohort, so its leading edge is the top of a\n",
        "  ranking that is not strongly ordered and is partly arbitrary. Reported\n",
        "  as uninformative, not as evidence against replication.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- B25: an interval for the second cohort --------------------------------
  cat("\n=== B25: an interval for the second cohort, not only a p ===\n")
  if (!exists("OS")) cat("  OS not in the session; cannot resample patients\n") else {
    i2 <- which(r2$key == "O")
    obs2 <- if (length(i2)) r2$NES[i2[1]] else NA_real_
    obs1 <- { i <- which(r1$key == "O"); if (length(i)) r1$NES[i[1]] else NA_real_ }
    cat(sprintf("  cohort 1 observed %+.2f | cohort 2 observed %+.2f\n", obs1, obs2))
    cat("  A bootstrap over patients within plex needs the second cohort's model\n",
        "  refitted per draw, which is the same cost that made B23's null\n",
        "  infeasible. Not attempted here. What CAN be stated without it is in\n",
        "  the pre-specification: the registered p is two-sided while the criterion\n",
        "  required NES < 0, so the test penalises direction twice. That is a\n",
        "  property of the test and is reported as such; the p is NOT recomputed.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B24_leading_edge"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(overlap = res, shared = length(shared_space)), file.path(od, "leading_edge.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b24_le <<- res
})
```

## B25 — interval

an interval for the second cohort, not only a p

Source: `B25_interval.R`

```{r B25_interval, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B25 — an interval for the second cohort, not only a p
## ============================================================================
##
## Pre-specified in PRESPEC_leadingedge.md. Post hoc with respect to the protein
## state, which was found first.
##
## WHY. The second cohort is reported as a p-value against a null: NES -1.48,
## P = 0.155, "not detected". That is the least informative summary an
## underpowered cohort can give. This study already established a better idiom in
## the coupling analysis, where reporting the estimate with its interval turned a
## failed replication into a magnitude comparison. The question is whether the
## second cohort's estimate is compatible with the first cohort's, with zero, or
## with both.
##
## THE QUANTITY CHANGED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS FEASIBLE. Bootstrapping the
## enrichment score would need the per-feature model refitted on every draw,
## which is the cost that defeated two earlier attempts here. The per-sample
## CHAPERONE SHARE needs no refitting: it is a ratio of column sums, computable
## per patient, and it is the quantity the manuscript already reports for the
## first cohort as 10.9% against 9.7%. The two cohorts are therefore compared on
## the same scale, which the NES comparison never was.
##
## COVERAGE CHECKED before the run: a stratified bootstrap of a median difference
## holds its nominal 95% at both cohort sizes (0.95 with 8 in the smaller arm,
## 0.97 with 30). The interval at the second cohort's size is wide — about 1.9
## standard deviations against 1.4 for the first — and that width IS the result:
## a median difference computed on eight observations is coarse, and an interval
## says so where a p-value does not.
##
## WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not replace the pre-specified test, which
## stands as the registered result. The registered criterion required NES < 0
## while its p is two-sided, penalising direction twice; that is noted in the
## paper as a property of the test and the p is NOT recomputed.

local({

  B <- 4000L; SEED <- 2501L

  need <- c("OP", "OS", "annot_new", "paths", "CHAPERONE_KO")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B25 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  an <- as.data.frame(annot_new)

  ## per-sample share of microbial protein for a KO set, in one cohort
  share <- function(O, coh) {
    prots <- an$protein[an$cohort == coh & an$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
    idx <- which(O$rd$Protein %in% prots)
    if (!length(idx)) { cat("  ", coh, ": no chaperone proteins matched\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    num <- colSums(O$a[idx, O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    den <- colSums(O$a[,   O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- data.frame(sample = O$d$sample, resp = O$d$resp,
                    Mixture = O$d$Mixture, f = num / den)
    d <- d[is.finite(d$f) & d$f > 0 & d$f < 1 & !is.na(d$resp), , drop = FALSE]
    d$resp <- droplevels(factor(d$resp))
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s %d samples (%s), %d chaperone proteins\n", coh, nrow(d),
                paste(names(table(d$resp)), table(d$resp), sep="=", collapse=", "), length(idx)))
    d
  }

  ## the estimate: difference in median share, NR minus R, in percentage points.
  ## Resampling is WITHIN PLEX AND WITHIN ARM, so each draw keeps the design's
  ## structure rather than reshuffling it.
  est <- function(d) 100 * (median(d$f[d$resp == "NR"]) - median(d$f[d$resp == "R"]))
  boot <- function(d, label) {
    if (is.null(d) || nlevels(d$resp) < 2 || min(table(d$resp)) < 4) {
      cat("  ", label, ": too few in one arm\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    o <- est(d)
    set.seed(SEED)
    bs <- replicate(B, {
      i <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(d)), list(d$Mixture, d$resp), drop = TRUE),
                         function(j) if (length(j)) sample(j, length(j), replace = TRUE) else j))
      est(d[i, , drop = FALSE])
    })
    bs <- bs[is.finite(bs)]
    ci <- quantile(bs, c(.025, .975))
    cat(sprintf("  %-10s NR minus R = %+.2f percentage points (95%% %+.2f to %+.2f)\n",
                label, o, ci[1], ci[2]))
    list(label = label, est = o, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2], n = nrow(d))
  }

  cat("=== chaperone share, both cohorts, same quantity and same scale ===\n")
  d1 <- share(OP, "pitt"); d2 <- share(OS, "sheba")
  cat("\n")
  r1 <- boot(d1, "cohort 1"); r2 <- boot(d2, "cohort 2")
  if (is.null(r1) || is.null(r2)) { cat("\nnot computable in both cohorts\n"); return(invisible()) }

  ## ---- the reading, fixed before the run -------------------------------------
  contains_zero <- r2$lo <= 0 && r2$hi >= 0
  contains_c1   <- r2$lo <= r1$est && r2$hi >= r1$est
  cat(sprintf("\n  cohort 2's interval contains zero: %s | contains cohort 1's estimate (%+.2f): %s\n",
              contains_zero, r1$est, contains_c1))
  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  if (contains_zero && contains_c1)
    cat("  The second cohort's estimate is compatible with the first cohort's AND\n",
        "  with no difference, and cannot distinguish them. That is what an\n",
        "  underpowered cohort shows, and it is more use to a reader than\n",
        "  \"not detected\": the cohorts are not in conflict, they are not\n",
        "  separable. Report the interval alongside the pre-specified p.\n", sep = "")
  else if (contains_zero && !contains_c1)
    cat("  The second cohort's interval contains zero but EXCLUDES the first\n",
        "  cohort's estimate. This is stronger than a null: that cohort rules out\n",
        "  an effect of the size reported. It weakens the paper and must be\n",
        "  reported.\n", sep = "")
  else if (!contains_zero)
    cat("  The second cohort's interval excludes zero: on this quantity it does\n",
        "  detect a difference, and the pre-specified enrichment test was the less\n",
        "  powerful summary. Report both, and do not substitute this for the\n",
        "  registered result.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B25_interval"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(cohort1 = r1, cohort2 = r2), file.path(od, "interval.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b25_interval <<- list(cohort1 = r1, cohort2 = r2)
})
```

## B26 — rank concordance

where the chaperone sets rank within each cohort's own ordering

Source: `B26_rank_concordance.R`

```{r B26_rank_concordance, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B26 — where the chaperone sets rank within each cohort's own ordering
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE ONES THAT FAILED.
##
## The profile correlation, the leading-edge overlap and the share interval all
## tried to compare quantities ACROSS cohorts, and all three failed on the same
## constraint: the two searches share no proteins, share only part of an
## annotation vocabulary, and the quantities that survive mean different things
## in the two places.
##
## This asks nothing across cohorts. Each cohort ranks its own sets using its own
## data, and the question is whether the same sets come out on top in both. The
## manuscript already treats rank as the honest summary for the discovery cohort,
## reporting the chaperone sets as 7th and 9th of 502 BECAUSE the corrected p
## does not clear. The symmetric statement for the second cohort is where its
## chaperone sets fall among its own.
##
## HOW MUCH A SHARED TOP POSITION COULD BE WORTH, bounded before the run. If a
## pre-specified set were placed at random within each cohort's ~30 sets, landing
## in the top one of both would happen about 1 time in 900, the top two about 1
## in 230, the top three about 1 in 100. Those are UPPER BOUNDS on how impressive
## the observation is, not p-values, and three things erode them:
##   - the sets are nested and overlapping, so positions are not independent
##     draws from a uniform distribution;
##   - COG O, its chaperone members and the chaperone set share most of their
##     membership, so those three clustering at the top is ONE fact, not three;
##   - the direction was pre-specified in the second cohort, which is declared in
##     advance and legitimate, but it halves the space a set could land in.
## The script therefore reports position and sign, and does not compute a p.
##
## WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT SUPPORT. Rank concordance is weaker than replication of
## significance and stronger than nothing. The sets are nested and overlapping,
## so a position is not a draw from a uniform distribution over sets, and the
## report below gives the position and the direction without converting either
## into a p-value. Direction was pre-specified for the second cohort (NES < 0),
## so a negative score there is the predicted sign, not a post hoc reading.

local({

  REPORTED <- c("O", "O_chap", "chaperones", "O_chap_noGD", "ribosomal")
  bare <- function(z) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(z))

  if (!exists("paths")) { cat("B26 SKIPPED: paths missing\n"); return(invisible()) }

  ## REUSE B23'S TABLE. That analysis already loaded both cohorts' observed
  ## vectors, identified the second cohort's PRE-SPECIFIED primary by its
  ## observed value, and saved the merged scores for every set present in both.
  ## Re-deriving them here would repeat the arm identification — the step that
  ## took four attempts to get right — for no gain. B23's conclusion was
  ## withdrawn; its data collection was sound and is what this needs.
  f23 <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B23_profile", "profile.rds")
  o1 <- o2 <- NULL; src2 <- NA_character_
  if (file.exists(f23)) {
    b23 <- readRDS(f23)
    m <- as.data.frame(b23$merged)
    if (all(c("key","NES_1","NES_2") %in% names(m))) {
      o1 <- data.frame(pathway = m$key, NES = m$NES_1)
      o2 <- data.frame(pathway = m$key, NES = m$NES_2)
      src2 <- paste0(basename(b23$source2), " (via B23)")
      cat(sprintf("using B23's merged table: %d sets scored in both cohorts\n", nrow(m)))
    }
  }
  if (is.null(o1)) {
    cat("B26 STOPPED: B23's saved table is not at ", f23, ".\n",
        "  Run B23_profile_replication.R once to produce it — its conclusion was\n",
        "  withdrawn but its data collection is what this analysis needs.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  cat("cohort 2 from ", src2, "\n\n", sep = "")

  rankrep <- function(o, label) {
    o <- o[is.finite(o$NES), ]; o$key <- bare(o$pathway)
    o <- o[order(o$NES), ]                       # most negative first = most NR-up
    o$rank_nr <- seq_len(nrow(o))
    cat(sprintf("=== %s: %d sets, ordered most non-responder-up first ===\n", label, nrow(o)))
    print(data.frame(rank = head(o$rank_nr, 8), set = head(o$key, 8),
                     NES = round(head(o$NES, 8), 2), row.names = NULL))
    r <- o[o$key %in% REPORTED, c("key","NES","rank_nr")]
    cat("\n  the reported sets in this cohort's own ordering:\n")
    print(data.frame(set = r$key, NES = round(r$NES, 2),
                     rank = sprintf("%d of %d", r$rank_nr, nrow(o)), row.names = NULL))
    list(tab = o, rep = r, n = nrow(o))
  }
  a <- rankrep(o1, "cohort 1"); cat("\n"); b <- rankrep(o2, "cohort 2")

  ## ---- the concordance statement ---------------------------------------------
  cat("\n=== concordance ===\n")
  both <- merge(a$rep, b$rep, by = "key", suffixes = c("_1","_2"))
  if (!nrow(both)) { cat("  no reported set scored in both\n"); return(invisible()) }
  both$same_sign <- sign(both$NES_1) == sign(both$NES_2)
  print(data.frame(set = both$key,
                   NES_1 = round(both$NES_1, 2), rank_1 = sprintf("%d/%d", both$rank_nr_1, a$n),
                   NES_2 = round(both$NES_2, 2), rank_2 = sprintf("%d/%d", both$rank_nr_2, b$n),
                   same_direction = both$same_sign, row.names = NULL))

  top1 <- both$key[both$rank_nr_1 <= 3]; top2 <- both$key[both$rank_nr_2 <= 3]
  cat(sprintf("\n  in the top three of its own cohort: %s (cohort 1), %s (cohort 2)\n",
              paste(top1, collapse = ", ") , paste(top2, collapse = ", ")))
  cat(sprintf("  same direction in both: %d of %d reported sets\n",
              sum(both$same_sign), nrow(both)))

  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  shared_top <- intersect(top1, top2)
  if (length(shared_top))
    cat("  ", paste(shared_top, collapse = ", "), " rank among the most\n",
        "  non-responder-associated sets in BOTH cohorts' own orderings, in the\n",
        "  direction pre-specified for the second cohort. The manuscript already\n",
        "  reports rank as the honest summary for the first cohort; this is the\n",
        "  same statement for the second. It is concordance of position and sign,\n",
        "  weaker than replicated significance and stronger than nothing, and it\n",
        "  is NOT converted into a p-value: the sets are nested and overlapping,\n",
        "  so a position is not a draw from a uniform distribution.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("  No reported set is near the top of both orderings. The cohorts do not\n",
        "  agree even on position, which is a stronger negative than the\n",
        "  pre-specified test gives and should be reported as such.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B26_rank"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(cohort1 = a$rep, cohort2 = b$rep, both = both,
               n1 = a$n, n2 = b$n, source2 = src2), file.path(od, "rank.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b26_rank <<- both
})
```

## B27 — what leads

what leads COG O in each cohort?

Source: `B27_what_leads.R`

