```{r B27_what_leads, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B27 — what leads COG O in each cohort?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY. The set-level scores show the two cohorts reaching a similar COG O rank
## from OPPOSITE internal structures:
##
##                                   Pittsburgh   Sheba
##   COG O                              -2.24     -1.48   agree
##   COG O chaperone members            -2.46     -1.39   agree
##   all chaperones                     -2.43     -1.38   agree
##   chaperones minus GroEL/DnaK        -2.23     +0.68   REVERSE
##   COG O remainder (proteases, ox.)   +0.79     -1.43   REVERSE
##   ribosomal                          -1.77     +1.13   REVERSE
##
## Every set containing GroEL and DnaK agrees; every set excluding them reverses.
## In Pittsburgh the signal is broadly chaperone and the remainder opposes it; in
## Sheba the remainder carries it and the broader chaperone set opposes.
##
## WHAT THIS ASKS. Which proteins actually lead the enrichment in each cohort,
## resolved to KEGG orthologs so the two can be named side by side. Three things
## follow from the answer and none is available from the set scores alone:
##   - whether GroEL and DnaK lead in BOTH, which would make them the replicating
##     unit and put the cross-cohort agreement exactly where the manuscript
##     already makes its abundance claim;
##   - what Sheba's remainder signal actually is — proteases, oxidative stress,
##     or a scatter — which decides whether the inversion has a biological
##     reading or is noise at eight non-responders;
##   - whether Pittsburgh's breadth is real breadth or a few extra orthologs.
##
## WHAT IT CANNOT DO. A leading edge is the top of a ranking, and Sheba's ranking
## is weakly ordered (the set is not extreme there, P = 0.155, and its top eight
## sets span 0.35 enrichment units). Its leading edge is therefore partly
## arbitrary. This is descriptive: it names what is there, and attaches no test.

local({

  bare <- function(z) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(z))
  need <- c("stat_pitt", "SETS_P", "annot_new", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) { cat("B27 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  st2 <- if (exists("st_s")) st_s else NULL
  S2  <- if (exists("SETS_S")) SETS_S else NULL
  if (is.null(st2) || is.null(S2)) { cat("B27 SKIPPED: needs st_s and SETS_S\n"); return(invisible()) }
  if (!requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE)) { cat("B27 SKIPPED: fgsea\n"); return(invisible()) }

  an <- as.data.frame(annot_new)
  ## The project defines the pair as gd_p via these two orthologs; take them from
  ## the same place rather than repeating the literals, so a change there follows
  ## through here.
  GD <- c("K04077", "K04043")        # GroEL (cpn60), DnaK — matches gd_p in v17
  if (exists("CHAPERONE_KO") && !all(GD %in% CHAPERONE_KO))
    cat("  warning: GroEL/DnaK orthologs are not both in CHAPERONE_KO; check the",
        " definitions have not diverged\n", sep = "")
  ## VERIFIED against KEGG, 28 Sep 2026. Only entries confirmed from genome.jp or
  ## kegg.jp are named; the rest are deliberately left blank rather than guessed.
  ## One correction worth keeping: Hsp33 is hslO = K04083, NOT K04085. K04085 is
  ## in this project's CHAPERONE_KO but its identity is unconfirmed here.
  ## ALL 19 MEMBERS OF CHAPERONE_KO RESOLVED against KEGG, 28 Sep 2026.
  ## 18 are legitimate members of BRITE 03110, "Chaperones and folding
  ## catalysts": 9 chaperones/HSPs, 3 AAA+ unfoldases, 6 foldases/PPIases.
  ## K04085 is not — see B28_chaperone_set_audit.R.
  ko_name <- c(
    K04077 = "GroEL",           K04043 = "DnaK",            K13993 = "HSP20 family",
    K03687 = "GrpE",            K03545 = "ClpA",            K07533 = "PrsA foldase",
    K04078 = "GroES",           K04079 = "HtpG",            K04080 = "IbpA",
    K04081 = "IbpB",            K03686 = "DnaJ",            K03695 = "ClpB",
    K03696 = "ClpC",            K01802 = "peptidylprolyl isomerase",
    K03775 = "SlyD",            K03767 = "cyclophilin A",   K03768 = "cyclophilin B",
    K03771 = "SurA",
    K04085 = "tusA (NOT a chaperone)",
    ## outside the set, seen in the leading edges
    K03671 = "thioredoxin (trxA)",  K03386 = "peroxiredoxin (ahpC)",
    K05838 = "ybbN, putative thioredoxin",
    K01304 = "pyroglutamyl-peptidase", K01415 = "endothelin-converting enzyme",
    K03544 = "ClpX",            K03667 = "HslU",            K04083 = "Hsp33/HslO")

  lead <- function(sets, stat, coh, label) {
    i <- which(bare(names(sets)) == "O")
    if (!length(i)) { cat("  ", label, ": COG O not in the set list\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    r <- tryCatch(fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(sets[i], stat, minSize = 10, eps = 0),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(r) || !"leadingEdge" %in% names(r)) {
      cat("  ", label, ": fgsea gave no leading edge\n", sep=""); return(NULL) }
    pr <- unlist(as.data.frame(r)$leadingEdge[[1]])
    a <- an[an$cohort == coh & an$protein %in% pr & !is.na(an$ko_primary), ]
    tb <- sort(table(as.character(a$ko_primary)), decreasing = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("\n=== %s: COG O leading edge ===\n", label))
    cat(sprintf("  NES %+.2f | %d proteins, %d with a KO, %d distinct orthologs\n",
                as.data.frame(r)$NES[1], length(pr), nrow(a), length(tb)))
    show <- head(tb, 12)
    cat("  the orthologs contributing most proteins:\n")
    for (k in names(show))
      cat(sprintf("    %-9s %3d protein%s %s\n", k, show[[k]],
                  if (show[[k]] == 1) " " else "s",
                  if (!is.na(ko_name[k]) && nzchar(ko_name[k])) paste0("(", ko_name[k], ")") else ""))
    gd <- sum(tb[intersect(names(tb), GD)])
    cat(sprintf("  GroEL/DnaK share of the mapped leading edge: %d of %d proteins (%.0f%%)\n",
                gd, nrow(a), 100 * gd / max(nrow(a), 1)))
    list(ko = names(tb), tb = tb, n = nrow(a), gd = gd,
         nes = as.data.frame(r)$NES[1], label = label)
  }

  a1 <- lead(SETS_P, stat_pitt, "pitt",  "discovery cohort")
  a2 <- lead(S2,     st2,       "sheba", "pre-treatment cohort")
  if (is.null(a1) || is.null(a2)) return(invisible())

  ## ---- what is shared, and is it only the two proteins? -----------------------
  cat("\n=== shared orthologs ===\n")
  both <- intersect(a1$ko, a2$ko)
  cat(sprintf("  %d orthologs lead in both (of %d and %d)\n",
              length(both), length(a1$ko), length(a2$ko)))
  if (length(both)) {
    nm <- vapply(both, function(k) if (!is.na(ko_name[k]) && nzchar(ko_name[k]))
      sprintf("%s (%s)", k, ko_name[k]) else k, "")
    cat("    ", paste(nm, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat(sprintf("  GroEL/DnaK lead in the discovery cohort: %s | in the pre-treatment cohort: %s\n",
              all(GD %in% a1$ko), all(GD %in% a2$ko)))

  ## ---- what is Sheba's signal, if not the broad chaperone set? ----------------
  cat("\n=== what the pre-treatment cohort's leading edge is made of ===\n")
  chap_kos <- if (exists("CHAPERONE_KO")) CHAPERONE_KO else character(0)
  in_chap <- intersect(a2$ko, chap_kos)
  not_chap <- setdiff(a2$ko, chap_kos)
  cat(sprintf("  chaperone orthologs: %d | non-chaperone COG O orthologs: %d\n",
              length(in_chap), length(not_chap)))
  if (length(not_chap))
    cat("    non-chaperone: ", paste(head(not_chap, 14), collapse = ", "),
        if (length(not_chap) > 14) " ..." else "", "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n  Read this against the set scores: the remainder of COG O inverts in\n",
      "  sign between the two cohorts. If the non-chaperone\n",
      "  orthologs above are a coherent group — proteases, or oxidative stress —\n",
      "  the inversion has a reading. If they are a scatter, it is what a weakly\n",
      "  ordered ranking at eight non-responders produces, and should be left\n",
      " alone.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B27_what_leads"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(pitt = a1, sheba = a2, shared = both), file.path(od, "what_leads.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b27 <<- list(pitt = a1, sheba = a2, shared = both)
})
```

## B28 — chaperone set audit

does the chaperone set contain a non-chaperone?

Source: `B28_chaperone_set_audit.R`

```{r B28_chaperone_set_audit, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B28 — does the chaperone set contain a non-chaperone?
## ============================================================================
##
## K04085 is in CHAPERONE_KO. KEGG gives it as tusA/sirA, the tRNA
## 2-thiouridine-synthesizing sulfur transfer protein. That is not a chaperone,
## not a folding catalyst, and not plausibly either. It is also one of the seven
## orthologs leading COG O in BOTH cohorts, so it is not inert.
##
## This quantifies what it contributes, so the decision to keep or drop it is
## made on its effect rather than on principle alone. Every reported chaperone
## result is recomputed without it.
##
## WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The manuscript's claim is about chaperone
## protein specifically — eleven-fold denser in Bacillota, elevated in
## non-responders, GroEL and DnaK carrying it by abundance. A reviewer who
## resolves the KO list will ask why a tRNA sulfurtransferase is in it, and the
## answer has to be either "it contributes nothing, here is the result without
## it" or "it has been removed".
local({
  need <- c("OP", "annot_new", "CHAPERONE_KO", "share_of", "paths")
  m <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(m)) { cat("B28 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(m, collapse=", "), "\n", sep=""); return(invisible()) }
  an <- as.data.frame(annot_new)
  SUSPECT <- "K04085"
  if (!SUSPECT %in% CHAPERONE_KO) { cat("K04085 is not in CHAPERONE_KO; nothing to audit\n")
                                    return(invisible()) }
  clean <- setdiff(CHAPERONE_KO, SUSPECT)

  for (coh in c("pitt", "sheba")) {
    p_all <- an$protein[an$cohort == coh & an$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
    p_cln <- an$protein[an$cohort == coh & an$ko_primary %in% clean]
    p_sus <- an$protein[an$cohort == coh & an$ko_primary == SUSPECT]
    cat(sprintf("\n%s: chaperone set %d proteins; %s contributes %d (%.1f%%)\n",
                coh, length(p_all), SUSPECT, length(p_sus),
                100 * length(p_sus) / max(length(p_all), 1)))
    if (coh == "pitt" && exists("OP")) {
      f_all <- share_of(p_all)[OP$d$sample]; f_cln <- share_of(p_cln)[OP$d$sample]
      d <- OP$d[!is.na(OP$d$resp), ]
      med <- function(f) {
        a <- f[OP$d$sample %in% d$sample[d$resp == "NR"]]
        b <- f[OP$d$sample %in% d$sample[d$resp == "R"]]
        c(100*median(a, na.rm=TRUE), 100*median(b, na.rm=TRUE))
      }
      ma <- med(f_all); mc <- med(f_cln)
      cat(sprintf("  per-sample share, with    %s: NR %.2f%% vs R %.2f%% (diff %+.2f)\n",
                  SUSPECT, ma[1], ma[2], ma[1]-ma[2]))
      cat(sprintf("  per-sample share, without %s: NR %.2f%% vs R %.2f%% (diff %+.2f)\n",
                  SUSPECT, mc[1], mc[2], mc[1]-mc[2]))
    }
  }
  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  cat("  If the difference is unchanged to two decimals, the reported results do\n",
      "  not depend on the mis-assigned ortholog and the paper can say so while\n",
      "  dropping it from the set definition. If it moves, the set has to be\n",
      "  rebuilt and every chaperone number recomputed before submission.\n", sep="")
})
```

## B29 — reverse direction

does a stranger's proteome explain your metagenome as well as your own?

Source: `B29_reverse_direction.R`

```{r B29_reverse_direction, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B29 — does a stranger's proteome explain your metagenome as well as your own?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY. The reported comparison fixes each patient's proteome and swaps the
## metagenome: own = cor(prot_i, meta_i), stranger = median over j of
## cor(prot_i, meta_j). That asks whether YOUR genes describe YOUR proteins
## better than a stranger's genes do.
##
## The reverse question is not the same one. Fix the metagenome and swap the
## proteome: own = cor(prot_j, meta_j), stranger = median over i of
## cor(prot_i, meta_j). That asks whether YOUR proteins are better described by
## YOUR genes than a stranger's proteins are. The own term is identical; the two
## stranger terms average over different sets, so the answers can differ.
##
## It matters because a near-zero advantage in the reported direction is
## consistent with two situations that have different meanings: the gene-to-
## protein link failing to carry individual information, or proteomes being so
## alike between people that there is little individual information to carry.
## The variance partition already argues for the first — patient identity adds
## 0.675% to the variance in protein abundance while gene abundance adds 0.010%,
## seventy times less — so there IS a patient-specific component and the
## metagenome recovers about a seventieth of it. This is a second, independent
## check of the same thing from the other side.
##
## NO NEW COMPUTATION IS NEEDED. K in the paired-mg-mp chunk is the full matrix,
## rows = proteome, columns = metagenome. The reported statistic takes row
## medians; this takes column medians.
##
## ONE ASYMMETRY TO REPORT, NOT TO HIDE. coup() restricts to the KOs the
## PROTEOME detects (keep <- x > 0), so every entry in a column uses a different
## KO set while every entry in a row uses one. Simulated at this size with
## detection counts between 400 and 900 KOs, that inflates the spread of the
## column-median stranger term by about 3% relative to the row-median one — real
## but small, so a materially weaker advantage in the reverse direction would not
## be explained by it. The script reports the KO counts so the asymmetry is
## visible.

local({

  need <- c("MP", "G", "pat", "kos", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("B29 SKIPPED: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), ".\n",
        "  These live in v17's paired-mg-mp chunk; run it first.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  EPS_ <- if (exists("EPS")) EPS else 1e-6

  coup <- function(s, b) {
    x <- MP[kos, s]; y <- G[kos, b]
    keep <- x > 0
    if (sum(keep) < 100) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS_), log(y[keep] + EPS_), method = "spearman"))
  }
  n <- nrow(pat)
  K <- outer(seq_len(n), seq_len(n),
             Vectorize(function(i, j) coup(pat$sample[i], pat$bio[j])))
  own <- diag(K)

  ## reported direction: fix the proteome, swap the metagenome (row medians)
  mis_row <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  ## reverse direction: fix the metagenome, swap the proteome (column medians)
  mis_col <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(j) median(K[-j, j], na.rm = TRUE), 0)

  rep1 <- function(d, lab) {
    w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(d, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided",
                                      exact = FALSE))
    cat(sprintf("  %-34s median %+.4f | own higher in %d of %d | P = %.3f\n",
                lab, median(d, na.rm = TRUE), sum(d > 0, na.rm = TRUE), length(d),
                w$p.value))
    median(d, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  cat(sprintf("own coupling: median %.3f over %d patients\n\n", median(own, na.rm = TRUE), n))
  a <- rep1(own - mis_row, "own minus stranger's METAGENOME")
  b <- rep1(own - mis_col, "own minus stranger's PROTEOME")

  ## the KO sets differ down a column but not along a row; show it
  kn <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) sum(MP[kos, pat$sample[i]] > 0), 0L)
  ## median() of an even-length integer vector is a double (48 paired patients
  ## gives x.5), which "%d" refuses -- format() prints either form correctly.
  cat(sprintf("\n  KOs detected per proteome: median %s, range %d to %d\n",
              format(median(kn)), min(kn), max(kn)))
  cat("  A row of K uses one KO set; a column uses a different one per entry, so\n",
      "  the reverse direction is the noisier comparison by construction.\n", sep = "")

  cat("\n---- reading ----\n")
  if (abs(b) <= abs(a) + 0.01)
    cat("  The advantage is as small in the reverse direction as in the reported\n",
        "  one. Neither layer describes the other's individual detail: the\n",
        "  decoupling is symmetric, and the near-zero advantage we report is not\n",
        "  an artifact of proteomes being alike between people.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("  The reverse direction gives a LARGER advantage. The decoupling is\n",
        "  asymmetric, and that asymmetry needs reporting: it would mean a\n",
        "  proteome carries individual information about its own metagenome that\n",
        "  the metagenome does not carry about the proteome.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B29_reverse"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(own = own, mis_row = mis_row, mis_col = mis_col, n = n),
          file.path(od, "reverse.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b29 <<- list(forward = a, reverse = b)
})
```

## B30 — elinav UC run

Stage 3 for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025, German UC cohort (99 paired subjects: 49 healthy,

Source: `B30_elinav_UC_run.R`

```{r B30_elinav_UC_run, eval=FALSE}
## Stage 3 for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025, German UC cohort (99 paired subjects: 49 healthy,
## 50 UC; one stool per subject; UC_64, a healthy control, has no metagenome in
## PRJEB81106 so it is never paired). Primary = MS1 PSM intensity. UC_94 (UC arm,
## 73 KOs) is below the 100-KO floor, so 98 are analysed: 49 healthy + 49 UC.
## Same design as B30_elinav_run.R (ISR).
## Sensitivities: spectral counts from the same PSMs; healthy only; UC only;
## MP multi-KO proteins dropped. Saves each coupling matrix.
## Diagnosis comes from the PXD057701 metadata.txt (Treatment, Human-UC_cohort rows).
## Paths from the environment, defaults as run. B30_elinav_ingest.R is sourced
## here and must travel with this script in the code deposit.
scripts <- Sys.getenv("B30_SCRIPTS", "external_coupling/scripts")
if (nzchar(scripts) && dir.exists(scripts)) setwd(scripts)
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_external_coupling.R"))
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_elinav_ingest.R"))
out  <- Sys.getenv("B30_OUT",   "external_coupling/elinav/b30")
edir <- Sys.getenv("ELINAV_DIR","external_coupling/elinav")
pxd  <- Sys.getenv("PXD057701_DIR",
                   "external_coupling/data_PXD057701")
meta <- read.delim(file.path(pxd, "metadata.txt"),
                   check.names = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
meta <- meta[meta$Project == "Human-UC_cohort", ]
dx <- setNames(meta$Treatment, paste0("UC_", meta$`Participant / Mouse ID`))
print(table(dx))
grp <- function(t) paste0("^(", paste(names(dx)[dx == t], collapse = "|"), ")$")
one <- function(label, tag, quant = "intensity", group = NULL, multi_ko = "first") {
  d <- load_elinav("UC", dir = edir, quant = quant, group = group, multi_ko = multi_ko)
  print(table(dx[d$subjects$mp], useNA = "ifany"))
  shared <- intersect(rownames(d$MP), rownames(d$G))
  det <- colSums(d$MP[shared, d$subjects$mp, drop = FALSE] > 0)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d MP KOs, %d MG KOs, %d shared; KOs detected per proteome median %d (range %d-%d)\n",
              label, nrow(d$MP), nrow(d$G), length(shared), as.integer(median(det)), min(det), max(det)))
  print(sort(det))
  set.seed(30)
  r <- run_external(d$MP, d$G, d$subjects, label,
                    quant = if (quant == "psm_count") "spectral" else "intensity")
  K <- attr(r, "K"); dimnames(K) <- list(paste0("MP_", d$subjects$mp), paste0("MG_", d$subjects$mg))
  ## Unrounded from 12 Oct 2026. round(K, 5) used to be applied here; at 1e-5 the
  ## signed-rank V shifts because the ranks of the smallest |d| reorder, so P values
  ## recomputed from a rounded matrix do not reproduce the reported ones (Elinav ISR
  ## metagenome swap: 0.9797 unrounded, 0.9878 rounded). Hodges-Lehmann estimates are
  ## unaffected. write.table writes 15 significant digits, which preserves every rank;
  ## the .rds beside it is bit-exact.
  write.table(K, file.path(out, paste0("elinav_UC_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".tsv")),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)
  saveRDS(K, file.path(out, paste0("elinav_UC_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".rds")))
  r
}
res     <- one("Elinav UC [LFQ MS1, PSM sum]", "primary")
res_sc  <- one("Elinav UC [PSM counts]", "psmcount", quant = "psm_count")
res_hc  <- one("Elinav UC healthy [LFQ MS1]", "healthy", group = grp("Healthy"))
res_uc  <- one("Elinav UC UC-only [LFQ MS1]", "uc", group = grp("UC"))
res_1ko <- one("Elinav UC MP single-KO [LFQ MS1]", "singleko_mp", multi_ko = "drop")
tab <- report(res, res_sc, res_hc, res_uc, res_1ko)
write.table(tab, file.path(out, "b30_elinav_UC_report.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
sessionInfo()
```

## B30 — elinav ingest

B30 ingest for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025 — replaces the load_elinav() stub in

Source: `B30_elinav_ingest.R`

```{r B30_elinav_ingest, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B30 ingest for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025 — replaces the load_elinav() stub in
## B30_external_coupling.R. Source B30 first, then this file.
##
## Inputs, all under ~/storage/external_coupling/elinav (built by elinav_*.sh):
##   MG  elinav_<C>_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv  single-end KneadData -> HUMAnN 4
##       alpha.1 -> stock uniref90_ko regroup, joined. Same chain as Tanca/Sheba.
##   MP  search_<C>/<subject>/psm.tsv  FragPipe 24.0 LFQ (MSFragger, Percolator,
##       Philosopher 1% FDR) against our IPHOMED-replica DB (their design, our
##       search). One RAW per subject.
##       mp_annot_<C>/elinav_<C>.emapper.annotations, elinav_<C>_kofam.tsv
##
## MP quantity: per subject, the MS1 `Intensity` of every target, non-contaminant
## PSM whose razor `Protein` is bacterial, summed per protein. psm.tsv holds only
## that run's own identifications, so match-between-runs transfers, which copy
## identifications ACROSS subjects, never enter the matrix. quant = "psm_count"
## gives spectral counts from the same PSMs (sensitivity).
## Human and contaminant proteins are excluded: the coupling is bacterial KOs.
## KO per protein: eggNOG KEGG_ko first, KOfam "*" where eggNOG has none; MP takes
## the first KO, MG keeps full abundance on every KO (the stock regroup rule).
##
## DEPOSIT NOTE, 12 Oct 2026. The MP side here is OUR search of THEIR deposited
## spectra, not their published identifications, so no second PRIDE deposit is
## involved: PXD058570 is not read anywhere in this chain. Supplementary Note 7
## is correct as written in naming PXD057701 for the spectra and PRJEB81106 for
## the metagenomes.
## This file reads, but does not build, five inputs that must be deposited with
## it or the chain stops here:
##   elinav_*.sh                              the RAW fetch, FragPipe search and
##                                            HUMAnN chain named at the top
##   mp_annot_<C>/bacteria_ids.txt            which razor proteins count as
##                                            bacterial; the whole MP matrix
##                                            depends on this list
##   mp_annot_<C>/elinav_<C>.emapper.annotations
##   mp_annot_<C>/elinav_<C>_kofam.tsv
##   the IPHOMED-replica search database      Note 7 states that a protein absent
##                                            from a database cannot be detected,
##                                            so the FASTA or its build script is
##                                            part of the result
##
## ONE FUNCTIONAL CHANGE for the deposit, marked inline below: a guard on the
## zero-bacterial-PSM path, which never fired on these cohorts and changes no
## number. Two diagnostics were also made honest under non-default arguments.
## Nothing else was touched: no filter, no threshold, no quantity.
## ============================================================================

## "ISR_IBD1_002" (search dirs) and "ISR_IBD1-002" (MG columns) -> one key
elinav_key <- function(x) gsub("-", "_", x)

load_elinav <- function(C = "ISR", dir = "external_coupling/elinav",
                        quant = c("intensity", "psm_count"), multi_ko = "first",
                        group = NULL) {
  quant <- match.arg(quant)
  multi_ko <- match.arg(multi_ko, c("first", "drop"))
  ann <- file.path(dir, paste0("mp_annot_", C))

  ## ---- MG: regrouped KO table, unstratified KO rows only
  g <- read.delim(file.path(dir, sprintf("elinav_%s_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv", C)),
                  check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
  g <- g[!grepl("|", rownames(g), fixed = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(g) <- elinav_key(colnames(g))
  G <- reduce_to_ko(g, tibble(feature = rownames(g), ko = rownames(g)))

  ## ---- MP: bacterial PSMs per subject, summed per razor protein
  bact <- readLines(file.path(ann, "bacteria_ids.txt"))
  subs <- basename(dirname(Sys.glob(file.path(dir, paste0("search_", C), "*", "psm.tsv"))))
  per <- lapply(subs, function(s) {
    p <- read.delim(file.path(dir, paste0("search_", C), s, "psm.tsv"), check.names = FALSE,
                    quote = "", colClasses = c(Protein = "character", Intensity = "numeric",
                                               `Is Decoy` = "character", `Is Contaminant` = "character"))
    p <- p[tolower(p$`Is Decoy`) == "false" & tolower(p$`Is Contaminant`) == "false" &
           p$Protein %in% bact, ]
    if (!nrow(p)) {
      ## Guard added 12 Oct 2026 for the deposit. data.frame(s = <length 1>,
      ## prot = <length 0>) errors with "arguments imply differing number of
      ## rows: 1, 0", so a subject with no bacterial target PSM used to kill the
      ## whole ingest with an error naming neither the subject nor the cause.
      ## It never fired on these cohorts; downstream handling already exists
      ## (an all-zero column gives an all-NA row in coupling_matrix, which
      ## own_vs_stranger drops), so this only changes the failure message.
      cat("  WARNING: no bacterial target PSMs for", s, "- subject will be dropped\n")
      return(data.frame(s = character(0), prot = character(0), v = numeric(0)))
    }
    v <- if (quant == "intensity") p$Intensity else rep(1, nrow(p))
    data.frame(s = rep(s, nrow(p)), prot = p$Protein, v = v)
  })
  long <- do.call(rbind, per)
  prots <- sort(unique(long$prot))
  m <- matrix(0, length(prots), length(subs), dimnames = list(prots, subs))
  agg <- aggregate(v ~ prot + s, data = long, FUN = sum)
  m[cbind(agg$prot, agg$s)] <- agg$v
  colnames(m) <- elinav_key(colnames(m))
  cat(sprintf("Elinav %s MP: %d bacterial PSMs, %d proteins%s\n", C, nrow(long), length(prots),
              if (quant == "intensity") sprintf("; zero-intensity PSMs %.1f%%", 100 * mean(long$v == 0)) else ""))

  ## ---- protein -> KO: eggNOG first, KOfam "*" where eggNOG has none
  el <- readLines(file.path(ann, sprintf("elinav_%s.emapper.annotations", C)))
  em <- read.delim(text = el[!startsWith(el, "##")], check.names = FALSE,
                   quote = "", comment.char = "", colClasses = "character")
  egg <- setNames(lapply(strsplit(em$KEGG_ko, ","), function(k) sub("^ko:", "", k[k != "-"])),
                  em[[1]])
  kf <- read.delim(file.path(ann, sprintf("elinav_%s_kofam.tsv", C)), header = FALSE,
                   comment.char = "#", quote = "",
                   col.names = c("sig", "orf", "ko", "thr", "score", "evalue", "desc"))
  kf <- kf[trimws(kf$sig) == "*", ]
  kof <- split(kf$ko, kf$orf)
  ko_list <- lapply(prots, function(o) {
    e <- egg[[o]]; if (length(e)) return(e)
    k <- kof[[o]]; if (length(k)) sort(unique(k)) else character(0)
  })
  names(ko_list) <- prots
  nk <- lengths(ko_list); has_egg <- vapply(prots, function(o) length(egg[[o]]) > 0, TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  %d proteins with a KO (%d eggNOG, %d KOfam-only); %d multi-KO; %.1f%% of MP signal on a KO\n",
              sum(nk > 0), sum(has_egg), sum(nk > 0 & !has_egg), sum(nk > 1),
              100 * sum(m[nk > 0, ]) / sum(m)))
  if (multi_ko == "drop") {
    ko_list[nk > 1] <- list(character(0))
    kept <- lengths(ko_list) > 0
    cat(sprintf("  multi_ko = \"drop\": %d proteins kept, %.1f%% of MP signal on a KO after the drop\n",
                sum(kept), 100 * sum(m[kept, ]) / sum(m)))
  }
  first <- vapply(ko_list, function(k) if (length(k)) k[1] else NA_character_, "")
  MP <- reduce_to_ko(m, tibble(feature = prots, ko = first))

  ## ---- one row per subject; both layers must be present
  ids <- intersect(colnames(MP), colnames(G))
  only <- setdiff(union(colnames(MP), colnames(G)), ids)
  if (length(only)) cat("  unpaired, dropped:", only, "\n")
  if (!is.null(group)) ids <- ids[grepl(group, ids)]
  list(MP = MP, G = G, subjects = tibble(mp = ids, mg = ids))
}
```

## B30 — elinav run

Stage 3 for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025, ISR cohort (48 paired subjects: 25 control,

Source: `B30_elinav_run.R`

```{r B30_elinav_run, eval=FALSE}
## Stage 3 for Valdes-Mas/Elinav 2025, ISR cohort (48 paired subjects: 25 control,
## 23 IBD; one stool per subject). Primary = MS1 PSM intensity, all 48.
## Sensitivities: spectral counts from the same PSMs; controls only; IBD only;
## MP multi-KO proteins dropped. Saves each coupling matrix.
## Paths from the environment, defaults as run, matching B30_elinav_UC_run.R.
scripts <- Sys.getenv("B30_SCRIPTS", "external_coupling/scripts")
if (nzchar(scripts) && dir.exists(scripts)) setwd(scripts)
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_external_coupling.R"))
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_elinav_ingest.R"))
out  <- Sys.getenv("B30_OUT",   "external_coupling/elinav/b30")
edir <- Sys.getenv("ELINAV_DIR","external_coupling/elinav")
one <- function(label, tag, quant = "intensity", group = NULL, multi_ko = "first") {
  d <- load_elinav("ISR", dir = edir, quant = quant, group = group, multi_ko = multi_ko)
  shared <- intersect(rownames(d$MP), rownames(d$G))
  det <- colSums(d$MP[shared, d$subjects$mp, drop = FALSE] > 0)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d MP KOs, %d MG KOs, %d shared; KOs detected per proteome median %d (range %d-%d)\n",
              label, nrow(d$MP), nrow(d$G), length(shared), as.integer(median(det)), min(det), max(det)))
  print(sort(det))
  set.seed(30)
  r <- run_external(d$MP, d$G, d$subjects, label,
                    quant = if (quant == "psm_count") "spectral" else "intensity")
  K <- attr(r, "K"); dimnames(K) <- list(paste0("MP_", d$subjects$mp), paste0("MG_", d$subjects$mg))
  ## Unrounded from 12 Oct 2026. round(K, 5) used to be applied here; at 1e-5 the
  ## signed-rank V shifts because the ranks of the smallest |d| reorder, so P values
  ## recomputed from a rounded matrix do not reproduce the reported ones (Elinav ISR
  ## metagenome swap: 0.9797 unrounded, 0.9878 rounded). Hodges-Lehmann estimates are
  ## unaffected. write.table writes 15 significant digits, which preserves every rank;
  ## the .rds beside it is bit-exact.
  write.table(K, file.path(out, paste0("elinav_ISR_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".tsv")),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)
  saveRDS(K, file.path(out, paste0("elinav_ISR_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".rds")))
  r
}
res     <- one("Elinav ISR [LFQ MS1, PSM sum]", "primary")
res_sc  <- one("Elinav ISR [PSM counts]", "psmcount", quant = "psm_count")
res_ctl <- one("Elinav ISR controls [LFQ MS1]", "controls", group = "^ISR_[0-9]")
res_ibd <- one("Elinav ISR IBD [LFQ MS1]", "ibd", group = "^ISR_IBD")
res_1ko <- one("Elinav ISR MP single-KO [LFQ MS1]", "singleko_mp", multi_ko = "drop")
tab <- report(res, res_sc, res_ctl, res_ibd, res_1ko)
write.table(tab, file.path(out, "b30_elinav_ISR_report.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
sessionInfo()
```

## B30 — external coupling

does the own-versus-stranger result hold in independent paired data?

Source: `B30_external_coupling.R`

```{r B30_external_coupling, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B30 — does the own-versus-stranger result hold in independent paired data?
## ============================================================================
##
## THE CLAIM BEING TESTED OUTSIDE OUR COHORTS. A patient's own metagenome
## describes their own proteome barely better than a stranger's. In Pittsburgh
## the advantage is +0.006 (27 of 47 patients, P = 0.166) and in Sheba −0.002;
## swapping the proteome instead of the metagenome gives the same answer (23 of
## 47). If that holds in healthy people, in another country, in another
## laboratory, with label-free rather than isobaric quantification, the claim
## stops being a property of our workflow.
##
## WHY THESE TWO DATASETS AND NOT A METATRANSCRIPTOME. Transcript abundance is
## not protein abundance, and the post-transcriptional layer is the thing this
## paper is about; an MG→MT result would either duplicate Franzosa 2014 or
## answer a different question. These are the public datasets that measure the
## same two layers we do, on the same material, per subject.
##
##   TANCA  Tanca et al., Microbiome 2017;5(1):79. 15 healthy Sardinian adults,
##          one stool each, shotgun MG + shotgun MP, searched against a
##          population-matched database built from the cohort's own metagenomes.
##          MP: PRIDE PXD005780 ("Relating human gut metagenome and
##          metaproteome"; NOT PXD004911, which is a mouse caecum study).
##          MG: ENA PRJEB19090 (not PRJNA319389, an unrelated project).
##          Their conclusion was that the two layers' PROFILES diverge and that
##          caution is due before drawing functional conclusions from MG. They
##          did not ask whether one subject's genes inform that subject's
##          proteins. That is the gap this script fills.
##
##   ELINAV Valdes-Mas et al., Cell 2025;188(4):1062-1083.e36. Metagenome-
##          informed metaproteomics, human cohorts incl. IBD.
##          MP: PRIDE PXD057701. MG: ENA PRJEB81106. Those two are what the
##          paper's own Data and code availability statement names, and the
##          Key Resources Table repeats them. PXD058570 is a SECOND PRIDE
##          record that also cites this paper (near-identical title, announced
##          2025-06-10 against PXD057701's 2025-08-10). RESOLVED 12 Oct 2026:
##          PXD058570 is not used. B30_elinav_ingest.R reads FragPipe psm.tsv
##          from OUR OWN search of their deposited spectra, not their published
##          identifications, so there is no second deposit to read; the UC run
##          script reads its subject metadata from data_PXD057701/ only, and
##          Supplementary Note 7 is correct in citing PXD057701 alone.
##          Their Figure 1H already reports a
##          "predicted vs unpredicted" split of bacterial proteins against gene
##          abundance, so they are closest to our question — but again at the
##          level of how many proteins track their genes across the cohort, not
##          whether the pairing is subject-specific.
##
## WHAT THIS SCRIPT IS. A harness. It does not download anything. Point it at
## two matrices per dataset and it runs the identical statistic to B29 so the
## numbers sit beside ours without re-derivation. The ingest for each dataset is
## a separate job: PRIDE gives raw files or search output, not a protein table,
## so expect to run the search yourself against that cohort's own metagenome if
## you want the comparison to be like-for-like with ours.
##
## QUANTIFICATION. Tanca 2017 quantified by spectral counting on an LTQ Orbitrap
## Velos; ours are PSM intensities. The advantage survives that difference for a
## structural reason: spectral counting's main bias is a property of the KO (long,
## abundant or readily ionized proteins collect more PSMs). Swapping the
## metagenome holds the proteome fixed, so the bias enters the own pairing and
## every stranger pairing identically; swapping the proteome compares proteomes
## that all carry the same KO-level bias against one metagenome. Either way it
## cancels out of the difference. Simulation agrees -- 90-104% of a small planted advantage
## retained even at 6,000 PSMs per sample, which at 12 replicates means
## indistinguishable from 100%. DEPOSIT NOTE: that simulation is a separate
## script and is not in this file. Deposit it alongside, or drop the claim --
## it is the support for Supplementary Note 7's statement that the bias
## cancels from the difference, so a reader will look for it.
##
## It does NOT cancel out of the own coupling, which spectral counting puts about
## 25% low. So Tanca's own coupling is not comparable with our 0.238 and must not
## be printed beside it as though it were. Report it anyway: it is the read on
## whether a dataset has the resolution to make its advantage meaningful.
##
## Their matched search database is deposited (PXD005780,
## matched_metagenomic_database.fasta, 25.3 M sequences), so a like-for-like
## re-search costs about a day of machine time and needs no assembly or gene
## calling. That makes an intensity-based run an affordable sensitivity analysis
## for the absolute coupling, not something to defer.
##
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## RESULT, TANCA 2017, run 9 Oct 2026. n = 15, proteome quantified by spectral
## counts from the authors' table; 860 KOs shared, median 349 detected per
## proteome (227-437), no missing cells.
##
##   own coupling              0.196   (spectral; NOT comparable with our 0.238)
##   swap the metagenome      -0.008  [-0.032, +0.012]   6/15   P = 0.38
##   swap the proteome        +0.013  [-0.062, +0.036]   9/15   P = 0.63
##   single-KO rule instead:  -0.011 and +0.015; the rule moves nothing
##
## THESE ARE NOT THE PUBLISHED NUMBERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE ESTIMATOR.
## own_vs_stranger() prints the MEDIAN of the per-subject differences with a
## percentile BOOTSTRAP interval. Supplementary Note 7 reports the
## HODGES-LEHMANN pseudomedian, with the interval and the P value from the same
## Wilcoxon signed-rank test; its table carries the median separately, in the
## "Median of differences" column. The mapping for this cohort:
##
##   metagenome swap  median -0.008  ->  the table's "Median of differences"
##                    6/15, P 0.38   ->  "own higher 6 of 15", P 0.389
##                                       (the table's advantage is the H-L,
##                                        -0.009, interval -0.024 to +0.011)
##   proteome swap    median +0.013  ->  the table's H-L is -0.011. A median
##                                       and a pseudomedian can differ in sign
##                                       on 15 skewed differences -- the wide,
##                                       asymmetric bootstrap interval above is
##                                       that skew -- so this is two estimators,
##                                       not a disagreement.
##
## ONE CELL DOES GENUINELY DISAGREE. The own coupling is median(diag(K)) under
## either convention, so it cannot differ by estimator: 0.196 here against the
## 0.22 that Supplementary Note 7 reports and reads against its pre-fixed
## 0.15-0.25 admissibility window. Both clear the window, so no conclusion
## turns on it, but the two cannot both be the current run. Settle which before
## this file is deposited.
##
## READING. The advantage replicates at zero in an independent cohort: healthy
## Sardinian adults, another laboratory, label-free quantification, a database
## built a different way. The two directions carry opposite signs and every
## interval spans zero, which is what noise looks like at this n. The useful
## statement is the BOUND, not the point estimate -- and the upper bounds very
## nearly coincide with ours: +0.012 here against +0.013 across all families in
## Pittsburgh. Three cohorts now bound the advantage below about +0.013.
##
## The own coupling of 0.196 did its job: the brief's rule was that a value in
## 0.15-0.25 means the data can resolve an advantage, so a near-zero result is
## informative rather than merely underpowered. That rule was set before the
## number was seen and it says no re-search is needed.
##
## WHAT IS NOT CONTROLLED. Tanca's ORFs are short-read fragments, so the KO map
## is effectively eggNOG-only (9 ORFs came from KOfam); the MG abundances use
## every deposited read (unmerged mates, 1.9-31.5 M clean reads per subject),
## not the authors' 200,000 merged reads, so they are on a different basis from
## the published profiles; S36, S61 and S65 have under 2 M read PAIRS deposited
## (1.1-1.8 M); S6, S13 and S20 were sequenced 2x101 on a separate instrument
## run, the other twelve 2x93; and the population is healthy rather than
## melanoma. (The ENA runs are bcl2fastq files split at 4 M read pairs, 38 for
## 15 subjects, rejoined per subject -- not re-sequencing, so not a difference.) A FragPipe intensity re-search would remove ONE of
## these differences and leave the rest, so it cannot attribute a gap in the
## absolute coupling to quantification. That is the argument against running it,
## and it is stronger than the cost argument.
##
## THE ONE THING THAT WOULD INVALIDATE THE COMPARISON. Our coupling is computed
## on KO-regrouped compositions, restricted to KOs the proteome detects, Spearman
## on logs. If an external dataset is reduced differently — protein groups rather
## than KOs, a different denominator, a completeness filter — the number is not
## comparable to 0.238 and should not be reported beside it. Reduce each dataset
## the way reduce_to_ko() does below, or state the difference.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})

EPS <- 1e-9
MIN_SHARED_KO <- 100     # as in the primary analysis
MIN_SUBJECTS  <- 10      # below this the stranger median is too thin to trust

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## reduce_to_ko(): both layers to KO compositions over their own denominator.
## This mirrors the primary analysis exactly; do not "improve" it here.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
reduce_to_ko <- function(mat, map, drop = c("UNMAPPED", "UNGROUPED", "UNINTEGRATED")) {
  stopifnot(!is.null(rownames(mat)), all(c("feature", "ko") %in% names(map)))
  map <- map |> filter(!ko %in% drop, !is.na(ko), ko != "")
  keep <- intersect(rownames(mat), map$feature)
  if (!length(keep)) stop("reduce_to_ko: no feature overlaps the KO map")
  ko <- map$ko[match(keep, map$feature)]
  agg <- rowsum(as.matrix(mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]), group = ko, na.rm = TRUE)
  sweep(agg, 2, colSums(agg, na.rm = TRUE), "/")   # composition per sample
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## coupling matrix: rows = proteomes, columns = metagenomes.
## Restricted to the KOs THIS PROTEOME detects, which is what makes the matrix
## asymmetric and the column medians the noisier margin (see B29).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
coupling_matrix <- function(MP, G, subjects) {
  kos <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(G))
  if (length(kos) < MIN_SHARED_KO)
    stop(sprintf("only %d shared KOs; need >= %d", length(kos), MIN_SHARED_KO))
  one <- function(i, j) {
    x <- MP[kos, subjects$mp[i]]; y <- G[kos, subjects$mg[j]]
    keep <- x > 0
    if (sum(keep) < MIN_SHARED_KO) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS), log(y[keep] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }
  n <- nrow(subjects)
  outer(seq_len(n), seq_len(n), Vectorize(one))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## the statistic, reported both directions as in B29
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
own_vs_stranger <- function(K, label, quant = c("intensity", "spectral")) {
  quant <- match.arg(quant)
  n <- nrow(K); own <- diag(K)
  row <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  col <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(j) median(K[-j, j], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  ## A proteome below MIN_SHARED_KO has an all-NA row, so its own coupling and
  ## both differences are NA. It is not an analysed subject: drop it before
  ## counting and resampling, as wilcox.test already does. (Its metagenome is
  ## still a stranger for everyone else.) Fixed 12 Oct 2026: the count used to
  ## divide by length(d) with the NA in it ("58/99" for the UC cohort's 58/98),
  ## and the bootstrap resampled the NA.
  n_an <- sum(!is.na(own))
  rep1 <- function(d, what) {
    d <- d[!is.na(d)]
    w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(d, mu = 0, exact = FALSE))
    bs <- replicate(2000, median(sample(d, length(d), replace = TRUE)))
    cat(sprintf("  %-28s %+.4f  [%+.4f, %+.4f]  own higher %2d/%2d  P = %.3f\n",
                what, median(d), quantile(bs,.025), quantile(bs,.975),
                sum(d > 0), length(d), w$p.value))
    median(d)
  }
  cat(sprintf("\n%s  (n = %d, %s)\n", label, n_an, quant))
  if (n_an < n) {
    ids <- if (is.null(rownames(K))) seq_len(n) else rownames(K)
    cat(sprintf("  %d paired; %d below the %d-KO floor and not analysed: %s\n",
                n, n - n_an, MIN_SHARED_KO, paste(ids[is.na(own)], collapse = ", ")))
  }
  cat(sprintf("  own coupling median %.3f%s\n", median(own, na.rm = TRUE),
              if (quant == "spectral")
                "   <- NOT comparable with an intensity-based coupling" else ""))
  a <- rep1(own - row, "swap the METAGENOME")
  b <- rep1(own - col, "swap the PROTEOME")
  tibble(dataset = label, n = n_an, quant = quant,
         own = median(own, na.rm = TRUE), adv_mg = a, adv_mp = b)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## run_external(): the whole thing for one dataset.
##   MP, G    KO-by-sample matrices, already through reduce_to_ko()
##   subjects data frame with columns mp and mg, one row per subject, giving
##            the column name of that subject's proteome and metagenome.
##            One row per SUBJECT — if a subject contributed several tubes,
##            choose one and say which; do not let a subject appear twice,
##            because that puts a near-own pairing into the stranger set and
##            biases the advantage toward zero.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_external <- function(MP, G, subjects, label,
                         quant = c("intensity", "spectral")) {
  quant <- match.arg(quant)
  stopifnot(all(c("mp","mg") %in% names(subjects)))
  if (anyDuplicated(subjects$mp) || anyDuplicated(subjects$mg))
    stop("a subject appears twice; see the note in run_external()")
  if (nrow(subjects) < MIN_SUBJECTS)
    stop(sprintf("%d subjects; below the floor of %d", nrow(subjects), MIN_SUBJECTS))
  miss <- c(setdiff(subjects$mp, colnames(MP)), setdiff(subjects$mg, colnames(G)))
  if (length(miss)) stop("columns not found: ", paste(head(miss,5), collapse=", "))
  K <- coupling_matrix(MP, G, subjects)
  dimnames(K) <- list(subjects$mp, subjects$mg)
  res <- own_vs_stranger(K, label, quant)
  attr(res, "K") <- K
  res
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## INGEST STUBS — fill these in once the files are on disk.
##
## DEPOSIT NOTE, revised 12 Oct 2026. The stubs below stop(), so this harness
## ALONE reproduces nothing. The deposit now carries B30_tanca_ingest.R, which
## REPLACES load_tanca() below — source this file first, then the ingest — plus
## tanca_mg.sh and its verified ena_runs.tsv manifest (38 runs, 76 files, 15
## subjects), B30_elinav_UC_run.R and B30_elinav_run.R.
## B30_elinav_ingest.R now ships too and REPLACES load_elinav() the same way.
## Still missing and required: the build scripts behind both ingests' inputs —
## elinav_*.sh (RAW fetch, FragPipe search, HUMAnN), the IPHOMED-replica search
## database, bacteria_ids.txt and the two annotation tables per cohort; and
## tanca_mp.sh and tanca_mg_singleko.sh on the Tanca side; and
## the v17 paired-mg-mp chunk, which is the code this statistic reproduces and
## the source of Note 7's Pittsburgh and Sheba rows. B29_reverse_direction.R is
## a companion to that chunk, not a substitute for it: it needs MP, G, pat, kos
## and paths from a live v17 session.
## A deposit of this file by itself is not the analysis.
## Each must return list(MP = , G = , subjects = ) with MP and G already
## KO-reduced and subjects one row per person.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## WRITTEN AND RUN 9 Oct 2026 on the server; this copy is the harness's record
## of what the ingest needs, not the ingest itself.
load_tanca <- function(dir) {
  stop("load_tanca(): overridden by B30_tanca_ingest.R; source it after this.\n",
       "  Needs: the MP quantification from PXD005780 (spectral counts),\n",
       "  the MG gene abundances for the same 15 subjects from ENA PRJEB19090,\n",
       "  a feature->KO map for each, and the subject key linking them.\n",
       "  Their MP was searched against a cohort-matched database, so the\n",
       "  protein identifiers are theirs, not UniProt — the KO map has to come\n",
       "  from annotating that database, exactly as we annotate ours.")
}

load_elinav <- function(dir) {
  stop("load_elinav(): overridden by B30_elinav_ingest.R; source it after this.\n",
       "  Needs: our FragPipe search of the PXD057701 spectra restricted to the\n",
       "  human cohort (the deposit includes mouse), the paired PRJEB81106\n",
       "  metagenomes, and the subject key. Note the MG accession carefully:\n",
       "  the Cell data-availability statement lists several accessions that\n",
       "  are OTHER people's datasets they reanalyzed, not their own.")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## report(): our numbers beside theirs, which is the only output that matters
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## THE OWN COUPLING AND THE ADVANTAGE GO IN SEPARATE TABLES, and the function
## is built so that they cannot be put back together by accident. The header
## says a spectral-counting own coupling must not be printed beside an
## intensity one, and the first version of this function did exactly that --
## it had a single `own` column and no idea what produced each number, so
## Tanca's 0.196 sat next to our 0.238 as though the gap meant something.
## The advantage is comparable across quantifications because the bias is a
## property of the KO and cancels when the proteome is held fixed; the
## absolute coupling is not. Hence: one table for the comparable quantity,
## one table per quantification for the incomparable one.
## OUR TWO ROWS ARE MEDIANS, like everything own_vs_stranger() prints, and so
## correspond to Supplementary Note 7's "Median of differences" column rather
## than to its "Advantage" column, which is the Hodges-Lehmann pseudomedian
## with a Wilcoxon interval. Sheba's proteome swap is NA because this harness
## was never run in that direction for that cohort; the paper's table carries
## its H-L value. Do not read this printout as reproducing that table.
report <- function(...) {
  ours <- tibble(
    dataset = c("Pittsburgh (this study)", "Sheba (this study)"),
    n = c(47L, 30L), quant = "intensity", own = c(0.238, 0.12),
    adv_mg = c(0.006, -0.002), adv_mp = c(-0.0002, NA_real_))
  out <- bind_rows(ours, ...)
  if (!"quant" %in% names(out) || anyNA(out$quant))
    stop("every row needs a `quant`; rerun run_external() with quant = ...",
         call. = FALSE)

  cat("\n==== own-minus-stranger advantage, MEDIAN of per-subject differences ====\n")
  cat("     (comparable across quantifications; NOT the paper's H-L column)\n")
  print(as.data.frame(out[c("dataset", "n", "quant", "adv_mg", "adv_mp")]),
        digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\n======== own coupling (COMPARABLE ONLY WITHIN A QUANTIFICATION) ======\n")
  for (q in unique(out$quant)) {
    cat(sprintf("  -- %s --\n", q))
    sub <- out[out$quant == q, c("dataset", "n", "own")]
    print(as.data.frame(sub), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(unique(out$quant)) > 1)
    cat("  Do not read across these blocks. Spectral counting puts the absolute\n",
        "  coupling roughly 25% low, so a gap between blocks is the method, not\n",
        "  the biology.\n", sep = "")

  cat("\nA near-zero advantage in an independent dataset means the result is a\n",
      "property of the measurement model, not of our cohorts or our workflow.\n",
      "A clearly positive one there would mean the opposite, and would have to\n",
      "be reported as such.\n", sep = "")
  invisible(out)
}

if (!interactive()) cat(
"B30 loaded. This is a harness, not a run.\n",
"  1. obtain and search each dataset (see the header for accessions)\n",
"  2. reduce both layers with reduce_to_ko()\n",
"  3. res <- run_external(MP, G, subjects, \"Tanca 2017\")\n",
"  4. report(res_tanca, res_elinav)\n", sep = "")
```

## B30 — tanca run

Stage 3 for Tanca et al. 2017 (15 healthy Sardinian adults, one stool each).

Source: `B30_tanca_run.R`

```{r B30_tanca_run, eval=FALSE}
## Stage 3 for Tanca et al. 2017 (15 healthy Sardinian adults, one stool each).
## Primary = spectral counts (PSMs) from the authors' MS_identifications.xlsx,
## which is the only quantity their deposit provides; ortholog assignment is
## eggNOG-first with KOfam filling gaps, MP taking the first KO.
## Sensitivity: the single-KO rule on both sides at once -- multi-KO ORFs dropped
## on the MP side and the MG table rebuilt by tanca_mg_singleko.sh.
##
## WRITTEN 12 Oct 2026. The 9 Oct Tanca numbers in B30_external_coupling.R's
## RESULT block were produced by running the harness's four steps by hand, so
## they had no script and no recorded seed. This reproduces them. Nothing here
## is a new analysis: both runs are already reported in Supplementary Note 7.
##
## Same design as B30_elinav_run.R and B30_elinav_UC_run.R. Paths from the
## environment, defaults as run. B30_tanca_ingest.R is sourced here and must
## travel with this script in the code deposit.
scripts <- Sys.getenv("B30_SCRIPTS", "external_coupling/scripts")
if (nzchar(scripts) && dir.exists(scripts)) setwd(scripts)
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_external_coupling.R"))
source(file.path(scripts, "B30_tanca_ingest.R"))
out  <- Sys.getenv("B30_OUT",   "external_coupling/tanca/b30")
tdir <- Sys.getenv("TANCA_DIR", "external_coupling/tanca")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

one <- function(label, tag, single_ko = FALSE, multi_ko = "first") {
  d <- load_tanca(dir = tdir, multi_ko = multi_ko, single_ko = single_ko)
  shared <- intersect(rownames(d$MP), rownames(d$G))
  det <- colSums(d$MP[shared, d$subjects$mp, drop = FALSE] > 0)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d MP KOs, %d MG KOs, %d shared; KOs detected per proteome median %d (range %d-%d)\n",
              label, nrow(d$MP), nrow(d$G), length(shared), as.integer(median(det)), min(det), max(det)))
  print(sort(det))
  set.seed(30)
  ## Tanca is spectral counting, not intensity. report() keeps the spectral rows
  ## in their own block because the absolute coupling is roughly a quarter low
  ## under spectral counts and must not be read against the TMT or LFQ values.
  r <- run_external(d$MP, d$G, d$subjects, label, quant = "spectral")
  K <- attr(r, "K"); dimnames(K) <- list(paste0("MP_", d$subjects$mp), paste0("MG_", d$subjects$mg))
  ## Unrounded, as for the Elinav runs: rounding at 1e-5 reorders the ranks of
  ## the smallest |d| and so shifts the signed-rank P, though not the
  ## Hodges-Lehmann estimate. The .rds beside the .tsv is bit-exact.
  write.table(K, file.path(out, paste0("tanca_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".tsv")),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)
  saveRDS(K, file.path(out, paste0("tanca_coupling_matrix_", tag, ".rds")))
  r
}

res     <- one("Tanca 2017 [spectral counts]", "primary")
res_1ko <- one("Tanca 2017 single-KO both sides [spectral counts]", "singleko", single_ko = TRUE)
## load_tanca() also offers multi_ko = "split" (PSMs divided equally between a
## multi-KO ORF's orthologs). It is not reported in the paper and is not run here.

tab <- report(res, res_1ko)
write.table(tab, file.path(out, "b30_tanca_report.tsv"), sep = "\t",
            quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
sessionInfo()
```

## B31 — build inputs

B31 INPUTS — build the per-level tables B31 consumes

Source: `B31_build_inputs.R`

```{r B31_build_inputs, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B31 INPUTS — build the per-level tables B31 consumes
## ============================================================================
##
## `run_b31()` takes tables, not object names, and the previous instructions
## named `ko_tbl` as though it already existed. It does not. This file builds
## it, and the other two levels, from objects that do.
##
## THE KO LEVEL IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS and it is the easiest, because it needs
## nothing from 01_metagenomics or 02_metaproteomics: v17 already exports both
## layers on one KO universe for the coupling analysis. B31's simulation says
## the interval is about +/-0.1 at ~1,300 features and uselessly wide at the 25
## genera and 44 pathways the old panels used, so run KO first and treat the
## other two as completeness.
##
## There is no KO-level differential abundance on the DNA side anywhere in the
## project -- 01 runs MaAsLin3 at genus and pathway only -- so build_ko() fits
## one here, on the same patients, the same KO universe and the same reduction
## the coupling analysis uses.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})
if (!requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE))
  stop("limma is needed to fit the per-feature contrasts", call. = FALSE)

EPS_B31 <- 1e-9   # as in the coupling analysis

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## build_ko(): both layers, one KO universe, one set of patients
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Needs MP, G, kos, pat and OP from the v17 session (the figures Rmd already
## loads them from figure_inputs.rds, so if your figures knit, this will run).
##
## The two designs differ on purpose. The proteome carries a TMT plex structure
## and every protein-level model in this paper conditions on it, so the protein
## fit has Mixture in it. The metagenome has no plex -- the libraries were not
## multiplexed that way -- so putting one in would be fitting a term that does
## not exist. The contrast is R - NR in both.
##
## The standard errors are limma's moderated ones. B31 treats them as known,
## which is the usual assumption for this kind of model; moderation makes them
## more stable across features, which matters because the likelihood weights
## each feature by its own precision.
build_ko <- function(min_per_arm = 5) {
  need <- c("MP", "G", "kos", "pat", "OP")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("build_ko(): missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
         "\n  These come from v17's figure_inputs.rds -- run the figures",
         " preflight first.", call. = FALSE)

  d <- OP$d[match(pat$sample, OP$d$sample), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!all(c("resp", "Mixture") %in% names(d)))
    stop("build_ko(): OP$d needs `resp` and `Mixture`", call. = FALSE)
  if (anyNA(d$sample))
    stop("build_ko(): some patients in `pat` are not in OP$d", call. = FALSE)

  ## ZEROS ARE MISSING, NOT SMALL. The first version of this function logged
  ## the compositions with the coupling analysis's 1e-9 pseudocount, which
  ## turns every undetected KO into an identical -20.7. That is not a small
  ## value, it is a sentinel, and it breaks the fit in the worst possible way
  ## for B31: a KO detected in all responders and no non-responders gets an
  ## enormous coefficient AND a tiny standard error, because the undetected
  ## samples carry no within-group variance. The likelihood weights each
  ## feature by its precision, so those artefacts dominate it -- the first run
  ## returned a disattenuated rho of -0.370 against an observed +0.001, which
  ## is impossible under the model and was the clue.
  ##
  ## The coupling analysis gets away with that pseudocount because it restricts
  ## to the KOs a proteome actually detects (keep <- x > 0) before correlating,
  ## so the zeros never reach a log. Here the equivalent is to treat them as
  ## missing and to require enough real observations per arm for a contrast to
  ## mean anything.
  zap <- function(M) { M[M <= 0] <- NA_real_; log(M) }
  enough <- function(M, grp, k) {
    ok <- vapply(levels(grp), function(g)
      rowSums(is.finite(M[, grp == g, drop = FALSE])) >= k, logical(nrow(M)))
    apply(ok, 1, all)
  }

  fitone <- function(M, design, cname, lab) {
    f <- limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(M, design))
    nbad <- sum(!is.finite(f$coefficients[, cname]) |
                !is.finite(f$stdev.unscaled[, cname]))
    if (nbad)
      cat(sprintf("  %s: %d feature(s) still inestimable; dropped\n", lab, nbad))
    if (!cname %in% colnames(f$coefficients))
      stop("contrast ", cname, " not in the fit; columns are ",
           paste(colnames(f$coefficients), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    tibble(feature = rownames(M),
           coef = unname(f$coefficients[, cname]),
           se   = unname(f$stdev.unscaled[, cname] * sqrt(f$s2.post))) |>
      filter(is.finite(coef), is.finite(se), se > 0)
  }

  MPk <- zap(as.matrix(MP[kos, pat$sample, drop = FALSE]))
  Gk  <- zap(as.matrix(G[kos, pat$bio,    drop = FALSE]))
  cat(sprintf("  zeros: proteome %.1f%% of cells, metagenome %.1f%%\n",
              100 * mean(!is.finite(MPk)), 100 * mean(!is.finite(Gk))))

  ## ESTIMABILITY, not just count. The first filtered run kept 864 KOs and limma
  ## reported "Partial NA coefficients for 537 probe(s)" -- most of them. The
  ## protein design is ~ Mixture + resp, and with 47% of the proteome missing,
  ## a KO can clear a per-arm count and still have no observation in some plex,
  ## which makes the Mixture term inestimable for that row. limma then returns
  ## partial coefficients whose standard errors mean nothing, and B31 weights by
  ## exactly those. So require the protein design to be fittable: every plex
  ## level present at least twice, on top of the per-arm requirement.
  plex_ok <- function(M, mix, k = 2) {
    ok <- vapply(levels(mix), function(g)
      rowSums(is.finite(M[, mix == g, drop = FALSE])) >= k, logical(nrow(M)))
    apply(ok, 1, all)
  }
  mixf <- droplevels(factor(d$Mixture))
  keep <- enough(MPk, d$resp, min_per_arm) & enough(Gk, d$resp, min_per_arm) &
          plex_ok(MPk, mixf)
  cat(sprintf("  %d of %d KOs clear >= %d per arm in both layers AND have every\n",
              sum(keep), length(keep), min_per_arm))
  cat(sprintf("  plex represented in the proteome (%d lost to plex gaps alone)\n",
              sum(enough(MPk, d$resp, min_per_arm) & enough(Gk, d$resp, min_per_arm) &
                  !plex_ok(MPk, mixf))))
  if (sum(keep) < 100)
    stop("only ", sum(keep), " KOs survive the detection requirement; lower ",
         "min_per_arm or accept that this level is not analysable", call. = FALSE)
  MPk <- MPk[keep, , drop = FALSE]; Gk <- Gk[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  ## protein conditions on plex; the metagenome has none
  mp <- fitone(MPk, model.matrix(~ Mixture + resp, d), "respR", "protein")
  mg <- fitone(Gk,  model.matrix(~ resp, d),           "respR", "metagenome")

  out <- inner_join(mg |> rename(mg_coef = coef, mg_se = se),
                    mp |> rename(mp_coef = coef, mp_se = se), by = "feature")
  cat(sprintf("build_ko(): %d KOs, %d patients\n", nrow(out), nrow(d)))
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## build_genus(): MaAsLin3 on the DNA side, the protein genus fit on the other
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## MaAsLin3 writes `coef` and `stderr` together; the existing cross-omic join in
## 02 §16b keeps logFC and DROPS stderr, which is why the old analysis could not
## correct for attenuation. Read the table, not that join.
##
## mp_tbl is your protein genus result (combined_genus_xx or equivalent). If it
## has no standard error, pass se_from_t = TRUE and it is recovered as logFC / t.
build_genus <- function(mp_tbl,
                        mg_tsv = file.path(paths$out_dir, "DA_combined_maaslin3.tsv"),
                        se_from_t = FALSE) {
  if (!file.exists(mg_tsv))
    stop("build_genus(): no MaAsLin3 table at ", mg_tsv,
         "\n  It is written by 01_metagenomics §7 as DA_combined_maaslin3.tsv.",
         call. = FALSE)
  mg <- readr::read_tsv(mg_tsv, show_col_types = FALSE)
  for (c0 in c("feature", "coef", "stderr"))
    if (!c0 %in% names(mg))
      stop("build_genus(): MaAsLin3 table has no `", c0, "` column", call. = FALSE)
  ## MaAsLin3 writes one row per (feature, value) of the model term; keep the
  ## response rows only, or the join silently multiplies features.
  if ("value" %in% names(mg) && dplyr::n_distinct(mg$value) > 1) {
    keep <- grep("^R$|respon", unique(mg$value), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
    if (length(keep) != 1)
      stop("build_genus(): cannot tell which `value` is the response contrast; ",
           "saw: ", paste(unique(mg$value), collapse = ", "),
           "\n  Filter it yourself and pass the table in.", call. = FALSE)
    mg <- mg |> filter(value == keep)
  }
  mg <- mg |> transmute(feature = as.character(feature),
                        mg_coef = coef, mg_se = stderr)

  mp <- as_tibble(mp_tbl)
  fcol <- intersect(c("feature", "Feature", "Genus", "Taxon"), names(mp))[1]
  if (is.na(fcol)) stop("build_genus(): no feature column in mp_tbl", call. = FALSE)
  if (se_from_t) {
    if (!all(c("logFC", "t") %in% names(mp)))
      stop("build_genus(): se_from_t needs `logFC` and `t`", call. = FALSE)
    mp <- mp |> mutate(mp_se = abs(logFC / t))
  } else {
    scol <- intersect(c("mp_se", "se", "SE", "stderr", "std.error"), names(mp))[1]
    if (is.na(scol))
      stop("build_genus(): mp_tbl has no standard error column. Pass ",
           "se_from_t = TRUE to recover it as logFC / t.", call. = FALSE)
    mp <- mp |> mutate(mp_se = .data[[scol]])
  }
  mp <- mp |> transmute(feature = as.character(.data[[fcol]]),
                        mp_coef = logFC, mp_se = mp_se)

  out <- inner_join(mg, mp, by = "feature")
  cat(sprintf("build_genus(): %d genera matched (%d DNA, %d protein)\n",
              nrow(out), nrow(mg), nrow(mp)))
  if (nrow(out) < 100)
    cat("  NOTE: B31's simulation puts the interval at this n near +/-0.4.",
        " Expect unresolved.\n", sep = "")
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## build_pathway(): READ THE WARNING
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The DNA side is HUMAnN/MetaCyc and the protein side is KEGG maps. They are
## different ontologies, and 02 §16a joins them BY PATHWAY NAME, with its own
## comment calling the join "imperfect but informative". A correlation computed
## across such a join is partly a measure of how well the names matched, and
## that error does not behave like the per-feature measurement error B31 models
## -- so B31 cannot correct for it and will quietly report a number that is too
## low for a reason it cannot see.
##
## Run it only with an explicit identifier mapping, not a name match. If all you
## have is the name join, the level is not analysable and should be left out.
build_pathway <- function(mg_tbl, mp_tbl, map = NULL) {
  if (is.null(map))
    stop("build_pathway(): refusing a name-based join across MetaCyc and KEGG.\n",
         "  Pass `map`, a data frame with columns mg_id and mp_id giving an\n",
         "  explicit correspondence. If you do not have one, drop this level:\n",
         "  the join error is not measurement error and B31 cannot correct it.",
         call. = FALSE)
  mg <- as_tibble(mg_tbl) |> transmute(mg_id = as.character(feature),
                                       mg_coef = coef, mg_se = stderr)
  mp <- as_tibble(mp_tbl)
  fcol <- intersect(c("feature", "Feature", "Pathway"), names(mp))[1]
  scol <- intersect(c("mp_se", "se", "SE", "stderr"), names(mp))[1]
  if (is.na(fcol) || is.na(scol))
    stop("build_pathway(): mp_tbl needs a feature column and a standard error",
         call. = FALSE)
  mp <- mp |> transmute(mp_id = as.character(.data[[fcol]]),
                        mp_coef = logFC, mp_se = .data[[scol]])
  out <- map |> as_tibble() |> inner_join(mg, by = "mg_id") |>
    inner_join(mp, by = "mp_id") |>
    transmute(feature = paste(mg_id, mp_id, sep = "|"),
              mg_coef, mg_se, mp_coef, mp_se)
  cat(sprintf("build_pathway(): %d mapped pairs\n", nrow(out)))
  out
}

cat("B31 inputs loaded.\n",
    "  ko <- build_ko()                       # needs only the v17 session\n",
    "  source('B31_crosslayer_attenuation.R')\n",
    "  run_b31(list(KO = ko), out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n",
    "\n",
    "  Add genus with build_genus(combined_genus_xx, se_from_t = TRUE), and\n",
    "  pathway only if you have a real MetaCyc-to-KEGG id map.\n", sep = "")
```

## B31 — crosslayer attenuation

how far do the two layers' response contrasts actually agree?

Source: `B31_crosslayer_attenuation.R`

```{r B31_crosslayer_attenuation, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B31 — how far do the two layers' response contrasts actually agree?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. The raw cross-layer scatter was WITHDRAWN from this project
## (RESULTS_AND_METHODS_v17 §2.3, MANUSCRIPT_v18 §R2) on a stated statistical
## ground: a contrast-versus-contrast comparison is attenuated. Both axes are
## noisy estimates of an effect, so the observed correlation is biased toward
## zero, and a near-zero value is exactly what you would see even if the two
## layers agreed perfectly. The old panels reported rho = 0.08 on 25 genera and
## read disagreement off it. That number is uninterpretable as drawn.
##
## This script measures the same agreement with the measurement error in the
## model, which is the only form in which the comparison can carry a claim.
##
## THE MODEL. For feature i, with xi and eta the true (unobserved) effects:
##
##     x_i | xi_i  ~ N(xi_i,  sx_i^2)        DNA-layer response effect
##     y_i | eta_i ~ N(eta_i, sy_i^2)        protein-layer response effect
##     (xi_i, eta_i) ~ MVN(0, Sigma)
##
## The two layers are separate assays on separate material, so their errors are
## independent, and the observed pair is therefore
##
##     (x_i, y_i) ~ MVN(0, Sigma + diag(sx_i^2, sy_i^2))
##
## rho_true = Sigma_12 / sqrt(Sigma_11 * Sigma_22) is estimated by maximum
## likelihood across features and bracketed by a profile-likelihood interval.
##
## Why this and not the textbook ratio r_obs / sqrt(Rxx*Ryy): that formula uses
## one average reliability per axis, and these standard errors are strongly
## heteroscedastic across features -- an abundant genus and a rare one are not
## measured to the same precision. The likelihood uses each feature's own two
## standard errors. The ratio estimate is printed too, as a cross-check: if the
## two disagree badly, the heteroscedasticity is doing the work and the ratio
## version should not be quoted.
##
## NO SELECTION ON SIGNIFICANCE. Every feature measurable in both layers enters.
## Filtering to features significant in either layer would bias the correlation
## in both axes at once -- each selected point sits where its own noise pushed
## it outward -- which is a second attenuation-like artefact on top of the one
## being corrected. The old panel's "5/7 verified pathways" annotation was drawn
## from exactly such a selected set.
##
## HOW BIG THE FEATURE SET HAS TO BE. The estimator was checked by simulation
## against known correlations, with heteroscedastic standard errors like real
## ones. It is close to unbiased once there are a couple of hundred features,
## and the observed correlation is attenuated about as hard as feared:
##
##     n     true rho    observed r    estimate    95% profile interval
##    200      0.00        +0.03         +0.03      [-0.18, +0.23]
##    200      0.30        +0.16         +0.31      [+0.10, +0.50]
##    200      0.60        +0.34         +0.64      [+0.46, +0.78]
##     44      0.00        -0.02         -0.01      [-0.44, +0.40]
##     44      0.30        +0.23         +0.36      [-0.15, +0.76]
##     25      0.00        -0.13         -0.31      [-0.83, +0.45]
##
## Read the n = 44 and n = 25 rows before running anything. At those sizes the
## interval for a true 0.0 and the interval for a true 0.3 overlap almost
## entirely: the design cannot tell the two apart, so no estimate from it can
## support a main-figure claim, whatever it comes out as. The old panels were
## 25 genera and 44 pathways. At n = 25 the point estimate is also biased away
## from zero in small samples (-0.31 for a true 0.00), which is a further reason
## to quote the interval and never the point estimate alone.
##
## So: run this at the LARGEST feature set each level admits, not the filtered
## set the old panels used, and expect only a KO-level run to be informative --
## the paper already works with 1,320 KOs measured in both layers, which is the
## regime where the interval is about +/-0.1. Genus and pathway are worth
## running for completeness, and should be reported as unresolved if that is
## what they are.
##
## WHAT A RESULT HERE CAN AND CANNOT SAY. A tight interval around zero would be
## a real finding: the layers' response contrasts are uncorrelated even after
## the noise is accounted for. A wide interval says the data cannot resolve the
## question, which is the honest outcome and must be reported as such rather
## than as absence of agreement. The identifiability diagnostic at the end says
## which of the two you are in BEFORE you look at the estimate.
##
## INPUT CONTRACT. One data frame per level, one row per feature:
##     feature   character, the shared identifier (genus name, or map id)
##     mg_coef   numeric, DNA-layer effect, R - NR
##     mg_se     numeric, its standard error
##     mp_coef   numeric, protein-layer effect, R - NR
##     mp_se     numeric, its standard error
##
## WHERE THESE COME FROM. The DNA side is MaAsLin3, which writes `coef` and
## `stderr` together (01_metagenomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd §7) -- note that the
## existing §16b join in 02_metaproteomics keeps `logFC` and DROPS `stderr`,
## which is why the old analysis could not do this. The protein side is the
## limma/msqrob fit; if your table carries logFC and t but no SE, recover it as
## se = logFC / t. Both effects must be on a R - NR contrast in the same
## direction; the script checks nothing about that, so verify it yourself.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})

MIN_FEATURES <- 12   # below this the likelihood is not worth fitting

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## the likelihood
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Parameterised as (log sx, log sy, atanh rho) so the optimiser is unconstrained
## and Sigma stays positive-definite for every value it can reach.
.nll <- function(par, x, y, vx, vy) {
  s1 <- exp(par[1]); s2 <- exp(par[2]); rho <- tanh(par[3])
  c12 <- rho * s1 * s2
  a <- s1^2 + vx            # per-feature marginal variances
  d <- s2^2 + vy
  det <- a * d - c12^2
  if (any(!is.finite(det)) || any(det <= 0)) return(1e10)
  ## quadratic form for a 2x2, written out rather than solved per feature
  q <- (d * x^2 - 2 * c12 * x * y + a * y^2) / det
  0.5 * sum(log(det) + q)
}

.fit <- function(x, y, vx, vy, rho_fixed = NA_real_) {
  start <- c(log(max(sd(x), 1e-6)), log(max(sd(y), 1e-6)), 0)
  if (is.na(rho_fixed)) {
    o <- optim(start, .nll, x = x, y = y, vx = vx, vy = vy,
               method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(reltol = 1e-10, maxit = 2000))
    list(nll = o$value, sx = exp(o$par[1]), sy = exp(o$par[2]), rho = tanh(o$par[3]))
  } else {
    f <- function(p) .nll(c(p, atanh(max(min(rho_fixed, 0.999), -0.999))), x, y, vx, vy)
    o <- optim(start[1:2], f, method = "Nelder-Mead",
               control = list(reltol = 1e-10, maxit = 2000))
    list(nll = o$value, sx = exp(o$par[1]), sy = exp(o$par[2]), rho = rho_fixed)
  }
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## crosslayer_rho(): the whole analysis for one level
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
crosslayer_rho <- function(d, label, grid = seq(-0.95, 0.95, by = 0.01)) {
  need <- c("feature", "mg_coef", "mg_se", "mp_coef", "mp_se")
  miss <- setdiff(need, names(d))
  if (length(miss)) stop(label, ": missing column(s) ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
                         "\n  see the INPUT CONTRACT at the top of this file",
                         call. = FALSE)
  d <- d |> filter(if_all(all_of(need[-1]), is.finite), mg_se > 0, mp_se > 0)
  n <- nrow(d)
  if (n < MIN_FEATURES)
    stop(label, ": only ", n, " features with both effects and both standard ",
         "errors; the model needs at least ", MIN_FEATURES, call. = FALSE)

  ## centre, because the model has no mean term: a shared offset between arms
  ## is not cross-layer agreement and must not be read as correlation
  x <- d$mg_coef - mean(d$mg_coef); y <- d$mp_coef - mean(d$mp_coef)
  vx <- d$mg_se^2; vy <- d$mp_se^2

  r_pear <- cor(x, y)
  r_spear <- cor(x, y, method = "spearman")

  ## --- method of moments, for the reliability figures and as a cross-check ---
  ## Reliability = true variance / observed variance. Observed variance is true
  ## plus mean error variance, so the subtraction below is the estimate. It can
  ## go negative, which is itself the answer: the spread of effects in that
  ## layer is entirely consistent with noise.
  Rxx <- 1 - mean(vx) / var(x)
  Ryy <- 1 - mean(vy) / var(y)
  atten <- if (Rxx > 0 && Ryy > 0) sqrt(Rxx * Ryy) else NA_real_
  r_ratio <- if (is.na(atten)) NA_real_ else r_pear / atten

  ## --- IS THERE ANYTHING TO CORRELATE? ---
  ## Reliability is true variance over observed variance. At or below zero, the
  ## spread of that layer's effect estimates is entirely accounted for by their
  ## own standard errors: the layer shows no response signal beyond noise. A
  ## correlation with a variable that does not vary is not defined, and the
  ## likelihood will happily run to the boundary and report rho near +/-1 with
  ## an interval spanning everything -- which is what the first clean KO run
  ## did. That is not a disagreement between layers and must not be read as one.
  ##
  ## The informative quantity in that case is an upper bound on the layer's own
  ## true effect SD, which is reported here instead of a correlation.
  if (is.na(atten) || Rxx <= 0.05 || Ryy <= 0.05) {
    flat <- c(if (Rxx <= 0.05) "metagenome", if (Ryy <= 0.05) "proteome")
    cat(sprintf("\n==== %s  (n = %d features) ====\n", label, n))
    cat(sprintf("  observed      Pearson %+.3f   Spearman %+.3f\n", r_pear, r_spear))
    cat(sprintf("  reliability   DNA %.2f   protein %.2f\n", Rxx, Ryy))
    cat("  NOT ESTIMABLE. The ", paste(flat, collapse = " and "),
        " layer shows no effect\n  variation beyond its own standard errors,",
        " so there is nothing for the\n  other layer to correlate with. This is",
```
