```{r B31_crosslayer_attenuation, eval=FALSE}
        " a statement about that layer,\n  not about agreement between them.\n",
        sep = "")
    bx <- sqrt(max(var(x) - mean(vx), 0)); by <- sqrt(max(var(y) - mean(vy), 0))
    cat(sprintf("  true effect SD, metagenome <= %.3f ; proteome <= %.3f\n", bx, by))
    cat(sprintf("  (median SE: metagenome %.3f, proteome %.3f)\n",
                median(sqrt(vx)), median(sqrt(vy))))
    return(tibble(level = label, n = n, r_pearson = r_pear, r_spearman = r_spear,
                  rel_mg = Rxx, rel_mp = Ryy, attenuation = atten,
                  rho_ratio = NA_real_, rho_true = NA_real_,
                  lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_,
                  sd_mg_true = bx, sd_mp_true = by))
  }

  ## --- the likelihood fit ---
  f0 <- .fit(x, y, vx, vy)
  prof <- vapply(grid, function(r) .fit(x, y, vx, vy, rho_fixed = r)$nll, 0)
  ok <- 2 * (prof - f0$nll) <= qchisq(0.95, 1)
  ci <- if (any(ok)) range(grid[ok]) else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)

  cat(sprintf("\n==== %s  (n = %d features) ====\n", label, n))
  cat(sprintf("  observed      Pearson %+.3f   Spearman %+.3f\n", r_pear, r_spear))
  cat(sprintf("  reliability   DNA %.2f   protein %.2f", Rxx, Ryy))
  cat(if (is.na(atten)) "   <- a layer's spread is all noise; see below\n" else
        sprintf("   attenuation factor %.2f\n", atten))
  if (!is.na(r_ratio))
    cat(sprintf("  ratio estimate  %+.3f   (cross-check only; assumes one SE per axis)\n",
                r_ratio))
  cat(sprintf("  DISATTENUATED rho %+.3f   95%% profile interval [%+.3f, %+.3f]\n",
              f0$rho, ci[1], ci[2]))

  ## CONSISTENCY CHECK. Under the fitted model the observed, unweighted
  ## correlation should be about
  ##     rho * s1 * s2 / sqrt((s1^2 + mean vx)(s2^2 + mean vy))
  ## If the fit implies an observed correlation far from the one actually in
  ## the data, the model does not describe these features and the estimate is
  ## an artefact of whichever handful of them the precision weighting trusted.
  ## This is not a hypothetical: the first KO run returned rho = -0.370 against
  ## an observed +0.001, because undetected values had been logged to a shared
  ## sentinel, giving those features huge effects with tiny standard errors.
  implied <- f0$rho * f0$sx * f0$sy /
    sqrt((f0$sx^2 + mean(vx)) * (f0$sy^2 + mean(vy)))
  cat(sprintf("  model implies an observed r of %+.3f; the data show %+.3f\n",
              implied, r_pear))
  if (abs(implied - r_pear) > 0.05) {
    cat("  *** INCONSISTENT. The fit does not reproduce the correlation that is\n",
        "      actually in the data, so the estimate above is not usable. The\n",
        "      usual cause is a few features with implausibly small standard\n",
        "      errors -- sentinel-coded zeros, singleton groups, a layer whose\n",
        "      SEs are on a different scale. Inspect the smallest SEs before\n",
        "      anything else, and do not report this number.\n", sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("      smallest DNA SE %.3g, smallest protein SE %.3g\n",
                min(sqrt(vx)), min(sqrt(vy))))
  }

  ## --- what could this have resolved? ---
  ## The interval width is the honest headline. A study that cannot separate
  ## rho = 0 from rho = 0.6 has not measured disagreement, whatever it estimated.
  w <- diff(ci)
  cat(sprintf("  interval width %.2f -- ", w))
  if (!is.finite(w)) {
    cat("unbounded: this design cannot measure cross-layer agreement at all.\n")
  } else if (w > 0.8) {
    cat("UNINFORMATIVE. Report as unresolved, not as disagreement.\n")
  } else if (ci[1] <= 0 && ci[2] >= 0) {
    cat(sprintf("zero is inside, but values above %+.2f are excluded.\n", ci[2]))
  } else {
    cat("zero is OUTSIDE the interval.\n")
  }

  tibble(level = label, n = n, r_pearson = r_pear, r_spearman = r_spear,
         rel_mg = Rxx, rel_mp = Ryy, attenuation = atten, rho_ratio = r_ratio,
         rho_true = f0$rho, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2],
         sd_mg_true = f0$sx, sd_mp_true = f0$sy)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## identifiability(): run BEFORE reading the estimate
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Simulates from the fitted error structure at known rho and reports how well
## each is recovered. If rho = 0 and rho = 0.5 both return intervals that span
## most of the range, the panel cannot carry a claim and should not go in a main
## figure -- which is the question this whole exercise was set up to answer.
identifiability <- function(d, label, truths = c(0, 0.3, 0.6), reps = 60, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  d <- d |> filter(if_all(c(mg_coef, mg_se, mp_coef, mp_se), is.finite),
                   mg_se > 0, mp_se > 0)
  vx <- d$mg_se^2; vy <- d$mp_se^2; n <- nrow(d)
  sx <- sqrt(max(var(d$mg_coef) - mean(vx), 0))
  sy <- sqrt(max(var(d$mp_coef) - mean(vy), 0))
  ## With a collapsed true SD there is no correlation to recover and every
  ## simulated fit runs to the boundary, which prints as "median +1.00" at
  ## every true value and looks like a catastrophic design rather than an
  ## undefined quantity. Say which it is.
  if (sx <= 1e-6 || sy <= 1e-6) {
    cat(sprintf("\n-- identifiability at %s's design: NOT APPLICABLE --\n", label))
    cat("   The ", if (sx <= 1e-6) "metagenome" else "proteome",
        " layer has no true effect variation to simulate from,\n",
        "   so cross-layer correlation is undefined at this level rather than\n",
        "   merely hard to measure.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat(sprintf("\n-- identifiability at %s's design (n = %d, %d reps) --\n",
              label, n, reps))
  for (r0 in truths) {
    est <- replicate(reps, {
      t1 <- rnorm(n); t2 <- r0 * t1 + sqrt(1 - r0^2) * rnorm(n)
      x <- sx * t1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(vx))
      y <- sy * t2 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(vy))
      .fit(x - mean(x), y - mean(y), vx, vy)$rho
    })
    cat(sprintf("   true %+.2f  ->  median %+.2f, central 90%% [%+.2f, %+.2f]\n",
                r0, median(est), quantile(est, .05), quantile(est, .95)))
  }
  cat("   If these ranges overlap heavily, the design cannot tell the\n",
      "   hypotheses apart and no estimate from it belongs in a main figure.\n",
      sep = "")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## run(): both levels, saved for the figure panel
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_b31 <- function(levels, out_dir = ".") {
  ## `levels` is a NAMED list of tables, one per level, each meeting the input
  ## contract: list(KO = ko_tbl, genus = genus_tbl, pathway = pw_tbl). Named,
  ## not positional, because which levels exist depends on what the run
  ## produced, and KO is the one most likely to be informative.
  if (!is.list(levels) || is.null(names(levels)) || any(names(levels) == ""))
    stop("run_b31(): pass a NAMED list, e.g. list(KO = ..., genus = ...)",
         call. = FALSE)
  res <- bind_rows(lapply(names(levels),
                          function(nm) crosslayer_rho(levels[[nm]], nm)))
  for (nm in names(levels)) identifiability(levels[[nm]], nm)

  od <- file.path(out_dir, "B31_crosslayer"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(summary = res,
               data = lapply(levels, function(d)
                 d |> select(feature, mg_coef, mg_se, mp_coef, mp_se))),
          file.path(od, "crosslayer.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", file.path(od, "crosslayer.rds"), "\n", sep = "")

  wide <- res |> filter(!is.finite(hi - lo) | (hi - lo) > 0.8)
  if (nrow(wide))
    cat("\nUNRESOLVED at: ", paste(wide$level, collapse = ", "),
        "\n  These cannot support a main-figure claim. Report them as",
        " unresolved,\n  not as disagreement, and do not promote a panel",
        " built only on them.\n", sep = "")
  invisible(res)
}

if (!interactive()) cat(
"B31 loaded. It does not fetch anything; build the two tables and call it.\n",
"  1. KO:      the 1,320 measured in both layers -- the level with the power\n",
"  2. genus:   MaAsLin3 coef + stderr (01 §7) joined to the protein genus fit\n",
"  3. pathway: the same at KEGG pathway level\n",
"     columns: feature, mg_coef, mg_se, mp_coef, mp_se\n",
"  4. run_b31(list(KO = ko, genus = g, pathway = pw), out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n",
sep = "")
```

## B32 — pathway crosslayer

the cross-layer comparison at set level, where it is well posed

Source: `B32_pathway_crosslayer.R`

```{r B32_pathway_crosslayer, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B32 — the cross-layer comparison at set level, where it is well posed
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY NOT AT KO LEVEL. B31 run per KO returned reliability at or below zero on
## the metagenome side: a single KO's response contrast on this cohort is pure
## noise, so there was nothing for the protein layer to correlate with and the
## question was not merely underpowered but undefined. Aggregation is the fix.
## A pathway NES pools at least ten KOs, which attacks the noise directly, and
## the metagenome side already uses every labelled sample above the depth floor
## (~68) rather than only the 47 with paired proteomes. The two layers' effects
## never have to come from the same patients -- the correlation is ACROSS
## FEATURES -- which is the step that was missed first time round.
##
## systems_MG_vs_MP.R already builds both layers on one KEGG map universe, from
## the same eggNOG annotation, joined on the map id. There is no cross-ontology
## name matching here; that problem belongs to the old 02 §16a code.
##
## WHAT THIS ADDS. fgsea returns an NES and no standard error, and B31 needs one
## per set per layer. This permutes the response labels, recomputes each layer's
## ranking statistic and its NES, and takes
##
##     effect = observed NES - mean(null NES)
##     se     = sd(null NES)
##
## per set. The standard error is the point of the exercise; the centring is
## secondary and worth stating accurately rather than oversold. This project
## measured the null for this design at SD ~1.15 with a displaced location
## (mean about +0.2 to +0.3), which is why fgsea's own p-values were dropped.
## A CONSTANT displacement would not matter at all here -- a correlation is
## shift-invariant, and B31 centres both axes anyway. What centring guards
## against is the part of the displacement that varies with SET SIZE, because
## the two layers score the same pathways and therefore share each set's size:
## a size-dependent bias enters both axes together and a correlation would read
## it as agreement. Simulated at plausible magnitudes that artefact is worth
## about 0.01 of correlation, so this is cheap insurance, not a rescue.
##
## THE ASSUMPTION, STATED. The permutation distribution is the distribution
## under the null of no response effect, so its SD estimates the standard error
## under the null rather than at the observed effect. With effects this small
## the two are close, but it is an approximation and the direction of any error
## is toward overstating precision. It is the same null the rest of the project
## uses for these sets, so at least it is the same approximation throughout.
##
## RUN THE PRE-CHECK FIRST. Whether this is worth doing at all is decided by
## one number you already have, and it costs seconds rather than the tens of
## minutes the permutation does. Reliability is the spread of a layer's true
## effects against its measurement noise, and the noise here is the NES null
## SD, measured on this design at about 1.15. So:
##
##     reliability ~ (var of observed NES across sets - 1.15^2) / var of observed
##
## Simulated at 120 pathways with that null SD, the width of B31's interval is:
##
##     true-effect SD    reliability    interval width at a true rho of 0.3
##           0.8             0.33                    1.24   -> UNRESOLVED
##           1.2             0.52                    0.70   -> usable
##           1.8             0.71                    0.46   -> good
##           2.5             0.83                    0.41   -> good
##
## B31 calls anything wider than 0.8 unresolved. So the question is simply
## whether the observed NES values spread wider than about 1.4 in SD. If they
## do not, the permutation run will not change the answer and should not be
## started. b32_precheck() below reads this straight off sysv.
##
## COST. One refit plus one fgsea per draw per layer. At B = 200 expect tens of
## minutes, not hours. Run it once and save.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})
if (!requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE)) stop("fgsea is required")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b32_precheck(): is the full run worth starting? Seconds, not minutes.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Uses the NES already in sysv and the measured null SD. This is cruder than
## the permutation -- one global SD rather than one per set -- but it answers
## the only question that matters before committing to the draws: is there more
## spread in these NES values than the null alone produces?
b32_precheck <- function(sysv, null_sd = 1.15) {
  both <- sysv |> filter(!is.na(NES_mp), !is.na(NES_mg))
  n <- nrow(both)
  rel <- function(v) 1 - null_sd^2 / var(v)
  rmg <- rel(both$NES_mg); rmp <- rel(both$NES_mp)
  cat(sprintf("\nb32_precheck: %d pathways scored in both layers\n", n))
  cat(sprintf("  observed NES SD   metagenome %.2f   proteome %.2f   (null %.2f)\n",
              sd(both$NES_mg), sd(both$NES_mp), null_sd))
  cat(sprintf("  implied reliability  metagenome %.2f   proteome %.2f\n", rmg, rmp))
  cat(sprintf("  observed Spearman %+.3f, sign agreement %.0f%%\n",
              cor(both$NES_mp, both$NES_mg, method = "spearman"),
              100 * mean(sign(both$NES_mp) == sign(both$NES_mg))))
  worst <- min(rmg, rmp)
  if (!is.finite(worst) || worst <= 0.05) {
    cat("  VERDICT: do not run. At least one layer's NES spread is no wider\n",
        "  than the null, so there is nothing to correlate and the permutation\n",
        "  will only confirm it at greater expense. Report the bound instead.\n",
        sep = "")
  } else if (worst < 0.4) {
    cat(sprintf("  VERDICT: marginal (worst reliability %.2f). Expect an interval\n",
                worst),
        "  near or past B31's 0.8 unresolved threshold. Worth running only if\n",
        "  you will report an unresolved result as a finding.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  VERDICT: worth running (worst reliability %.2f).\n", worst))
  }
  invisible(tibble(n = n, rel_mg = rmg, rel_mp = rmp,
                   sd_mg = sd(both$NES_mg), sd_mp = sd(both$NES_mp)))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## shuffle(): permute response, optionally within strata
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The protein layer is permuted WITHIN PLEX, as everywhere else in this
## project: with TMT2 and TMT5 each dominated by one arm, a free shuffle makes
## the contrast partly a between-plex comparison and the null too generous.
## The metagenomes carry no plex, so they are shuffled freely.
shuffle <- function(resp, strata = NULL) {
  if (is.null(strata)) return(sample(resp))
  out <- resp
  for (s in unique(strata)) { i <- which(strata == s); out[i] <- sample(resp[i]) }
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## layer_effects(): observed NES, null mean and null SD, per set
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
##   sets    named list of feature ids, FIXED -- computed once from the observed
##           data and reused for every draw. Rebuilding them per draw (for
##           example by re-applying a prevalence filter) would let the set
##           definitions move with the labels and the null would not be a null.
##   fitfun  function(resp) -> named numeric ranking statistic for that layer
##   resp    the observed response factor, aligned to whatever fitfun expects
##   strata  plex/batch for within-stratum shuffling, or NULL
layer_effects <- function(sets, fitfun, resp, strata = NULL, B = 200,
                          label = "layer", seed = 1) {
  one <- function(s, sd0) {
    set.seed(sd0)
    ss <- lapply(sets, intersect, names(s))
    ss <- ss[lengths(ss) >= 10]
    suppressWarnings(
      fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(ss, s, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000, eps = 0)) |>
      as_tibble() |> select(pathway, NES)
  }
  obs <- one(fitfun(resp), seed)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d sets scored on the observed labels\n", label, nrow(obs)))

  nul <- vector("list", B)
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    nul[[b]] <- one(fitfun(shuffle(resp, strata)), seed + b) |>
      rename(NES_null = NES) |> mutate(draw = b)
    if (b %% 25 == 0) cat(sprintf("  %s: %d/%d draws\n", label, b, B))
  }
  nul <- bind_rows(nul)

  nul |> group_by(pathway) |>
    summarise(mu = mean(NES_null, na.rm = TRUE),
              sd = sd(NES_null, na.rm = TRUE),
              nd = sum(is.finite(NES_null)), .groups = "drop") |>
    inner_join(obs, by = "pathway") |>
    ## A set whose null never varied, or that scored in too few draws, has no
    ## usable standard error. Drop it rather than hand B31 a tiny one -- that
    ## is exactly the failure mode that wrecked the first KO run.
    filter(nd >= 0.8 * B, is.finite(sd), sd > 1e-6) |>
    transmute(feature = pathway, coef = NES - mu, se = sd,
              nes_raw = NES, null_mu = mu, n_draws = nd)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b32_build(): both layers, joined, ready for B31
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
b32_build <- function(mp_sets, mp_fit, mg_sets, mg_fit,
                      mp_resp, mg_resp, mp_strata = NULL, B = 200) {
  mp <- layer_effects(mp_sets, mp_fit, mp_resp, mp_strata, B, "proteome")
  mg <- layer_effects(mg_sets, mg_fit, mg_resp, NULL,       B, "metagenome")
  cat(sprintf("\nnull location: proteome mean NES %+.3f, metagenome %+.3f\n",
              mean(mp$null_mu), mean(mg$null_mu)))
  cat("  (the project measured this displacement at about +0.2 to +0.3;",
      " both layers are centred on their own)\n", sep = "")
  out <- inner_join(mg |> transmute(feature, mg_coef = coef, mg_se = se),
                    mp |> transmute(feature, mp_coef = coef, mp_se = se),
                    by = "feature")
  cat(sprintf("%d pathways scored in both layers\n", nrow(out)))
  attr(out, "mp") <- mp; attr(out, "mg") <- mg
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## mg_ranker(): the metagenome side, as systems_MG_vs_MP.R computes it
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Returns a function(resp) -> named t-statistics, R - NR, so the ranking is
## rebuilt from scratch under each permutation rather than reshuffled after the
## fact. `mg` is that script's long table: sample, feature, cpm, resp.
mg_ranker <- function(mg_long, min_prev = 0.2) {
  w <- mg_long |> filter(!is.na(resp))
  samples <- unique(w$sample)
  ## Build the matrix explicitly. tapply(..., identity) silently returns a
  ## list-matrix if any feature-sample pair appears twice, and everything
  ## downstream would then fail in a way that points nowhere near the cause.
  if (anyDuplicated(w[c("feature", "sample")]))
    stop("mg_ranker: duplicated feature-sample pairs in the long table",
         call. = FALSE)
  feats <- unique(w$feature)
  M <- matrix(NA_real_, length(feats), length(samples),
              dimnames = list(feats, samples))
  M[cbind(match(w$feature, feats), match(w$sample, samples))] <- log2(w$cpm + 1)
  keep <- rowMeans(!is.na(M) & M > 0) >= min_prev
  M <- M[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("mg_ranker: %d features over the %.0f%% prevalence floor, %d samples\n",
              nrow(M), 100 * min_prev, ncol(M)))
  ## The response vector must be aligned to THIS matrix's column order, and the
  ## caller has no way to know it. Return it with the function rather than
  ## making them reconstruct it -- the previous instructions named a
  ## `mg_resp_vec` that never existed.
  resp_aligned <- w$resp[match(samples, w$sample)]
  f <- function(resp) {
    r <- M[, resp == "R", drop = FALSE]; n <- M[, resp == "NR", drop = FALSE]
    mr <- rowMeans(r, na.rm = TRUE); mn <- rowMeans(n, na.rm = TRUE)
    vr <- apply(r, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE); vn <- apply(n, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
    kr <- rowSums(is.finite(r)); kn <- rowSums(is.finite(n))
    se <- sqrt(vr / kr + vn / kn)                       # Welch, as in tt()
    t  <- (mr - mn) / se
    t[is.finite(t) & kr >= 3 & kn >= 3]
  }
  attr(f, "resp") <- droplevels(factor(resp_aligned))
  cat("  its aligned response vector is attr(mgf, 'resp') -- use that.\n")
  f
}

cat(
"B32 loaded. FIRST, with sysv already in the session:\n\n",
"  source('B32_pathway_crosslayer.R')\n",
"  b32_precheck(sysv)        # seconds; decides whether the rest is worth it\n\n",
"Only if it says so, after systems_MG_vs_MP.R has defined MP_SETS, MG_SETS,\n",
"`mg`:\n\n",
"  source('B32_pathway_crosslayer.R')\n",
"  mgf <- mg_ranker(mg)\n",
"  ## mp_fit must REFIT the protein contrast under permuted labels and return\n",
"  ## the ranking statistic -- reuse the machinery behind the 565-set survey.\n",
"  pw <- b32_build(MP_SETS, mp_fit, MG_SETS, mgf,\n",
"                  mp_resp = OP$d$resp, mg_resp = attr(mgf, 'resp'),\n",
"                  mp_strata = OP$d$Mixture, B = 200)\n\n",
"  source('B31_crosslayer_attenuation.R')\n",
"  run_b31(list(pathway = pw), out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n", sep = "")
```

## B33 — external clade

does the clade-specific coupling failure of Fig. 2a appear outside the

Source: `B33_external_clade.R`

```{r B33_external_clade, eval=FALSE}
## =============================================================================
## B33 — does the clade-specific coupling failure of Fig. 2a appear outside the
## two melanoma cohorts?
## =============================================================================
##
## THE CLAIM BEING TESTED. In Pittsburgh, a genus's abundance in the metagenome
## tracks its share of the proteome across Bacillota (median Spearman +0.35,
## 22 genera) but not across Bacteroidota (+0.02, 5 genera), a gap of +0.33.
## Sheba cannot resolve it: 3 measurable Bacteroidota genera, gap -0.01 with a
## 95% interval of -0.30 to +0.43.
##
## WHY THE QUANTITY HAS TO BE PINNED DOWN FIRST. The gap is parameterization-
## dependent and the paper now says so. Measured within clade -- each genus as a
## share of its OWN phylum's protein rather than of the whole assigned proteome
## -- the two clades agree equally well (+0.42 vs +0.36, gap +0.06, P = 0.48).
## So "the clade-specific failure" means one specific statistic, the share-of-
## whole-proteome one, and an external replication is only a replication if it
## computes that one. This script computes BOTH and prints them side by side so
## the distinction cannot be lost downstream.
##
## WHAT IS NOT WORTH COMPUTING. The clade TOTAL correlated between layers is
## degenerate under closure -- analysis_v17 B6b measured Bacteroidota -0.306 and
## Bacillota +0.010 while Bacillota's individual genera couple at 0.3-0.7. Those
## two numbers exclude the label-swap hypothesis and are not effect sizes. Do not
## promote them to a replication target.
##
## THE RECIPE, copied from analysis_v17 §B5 so the external numbers are
## comparable without re-derivation:
##   MP  Unipept pept2lca on tryptic peptides (equate_il, extra, names).
##       Genera with >= MIN_PSM peptide-spectrum rows are kept. Per subject,
##       sum PSM intensity over each genus's rows, then row-normalize over the
##       kept genera. Phylum per genus = majority phylum of that genus's rows.
##   MG  MetaPhlAn genus rows (clade_name with exactly 5 pipes and a |g__),
##       percent abundance, NOT renormalized -- this mirrors §B5, where MPg is
##       renormalized and MGg is left as MetaPhlAn reports it.
##   rho per genus = Spearman across subjects, raw and on CLR; report the median
##       within each phylum and the Bacillota-minus-Bacteroidota gap, with a
##       patient-resampling interval.
##
## WHY THIS IS PORTABLE. Neither layer depends on a cohort's search database or
## assembly: Unipept LCA is sequence-based, MetaPhlAn is reference-based. The
## CHOCOPhlAn mismatch that blocks comparing our two cohorts' STANDALONE profiles
## (Pittsburgh mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503, Sheba mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403)
## does not apply to the HUMAnN-internal profiles, which are
## mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403 for both. Tanca and Valdes-Mas went through
## the same HUMAnN v4.0.0.alpha.1 chain, so use the HUMAnN-internal profiles
## everywhere and all five cohorts sit on one database. STAGE 1 checks this and
## refuses to continue if a cohort disagrees.
##
## STAGES. Set B33_STAGE.
##   probe     minutes. Inventory: files, MetaPhlAn database version, subjects,
##             peptides, and how many genera per phylum each cohort can measure
##             on the MG side. Run this before committing anything.
##   unipept   hours, cached and resumable. Peptide -> LCA for every cohort.
##   analyze   minutes. The contrast.
##   all       probe, then unipept, then analyze.
##
## POSITIVE CONTROL. Set PITT_PEP / PITT_MPA to run the identical code path on
## Pittsburgh. If it does not return +0.35 / +0.02 the harness is wrong and no
## external number from it means anything. Do this before reporting any
## external result.
## =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(readr); library(httr2)
})

STAGE    <- Sys.getenv("B33_STAGE", "probe")
EDIR     <- Sys.getenv("ELINAV_DIR", "external_coupling/elinav")
TDIR     <- Sys.getenv("TANCA_DIR",  "external_coupling/tanca")
OUT      <- Sys.getenv("B33_OUT",    "external_coupling/b33")
MIN_PSM  <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B33_MIN_PSM", "200"))   # §B5's genus threshold
NBOOT    <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B33_NBOOT",   "2000"))
SEED     <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("B33_SEED",    "9601"))  # §B5's seed
CACHE    <- file.path(OUT, "unipept_lca_cache.tsv")
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
say <- function(...) cat(sprintf(...), "\n", sep = "")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## MetaPhlAn profiles: find them, read them, and check the database version
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## HUMAnN 4 writes its internal profile under the per-sample temp directory; the
## exact name has varied across the alpha builds, so glob broadly and take
## whatever carries a #mpa_ header line.
find_mpa <- function(root) {
  f <- list.files(root, pattern = "metaphlan.*\\.(tsv|txt)$", recursive = TRUE,
                  full.names = TRUE)
  f[!grepl("merged", basename(f))]
}

mpa_db <- function(f) {
  h <- tryCatch(readLines(f, n = 10, warn = FALSE), error = function(e) character(0))
  v <- grep("mpa_v", h, value = TRUE)
  if (!length(v)) return(NA_character_)
  sub(".*(mpa_v[A-Za-z0-9_]+).*", "\\1", v[1])
}

## sample id from the profile's path; HUMAnN names the temp dir after the sample
mpa_sample <- function(f)
  sub("(_humann_temp)?$", "", basename(dirname(f))) |>
  (\(x) ifelse(x %in% c(".", "/"), sub("\\..*$", "", basename(f)), x))()

read_mpa_genus <- function(files) {
  bind_rows(lapply(files, function(f) {
    d <- tryCatch(read.delim(f, comment.char = "#", header = FALSE,
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(d) || !ncol(d) >= 3) return(NULL)
    names(d)[1:3] <- c("clade_name", "taxid", "pct")
    d <- d[grepl("\\|g__", d$clade_name) &
             lengths(regmatches(d$clade_name, gregexpr("\\|", d$clade_name))) == 5, ]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    tibble(sample = mpa_sample(f),
           genus  = sub(".*\\|g__", "", d$clade_name),
           pct    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d$pct)))
  })) |>
    filter(!is.na(pct)) |>
    group_by(sample, genus) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## PSMs: peptide + intensity per subject, bacterial targets only
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Same filter as B30_elinav_ingest.R: target, non-contaminant, razor protein in
## bacteria_ids.txt. The peptide column is what Unipept takes, so modifications
## are stripped and I/L are equated by the API (equate_il = "true").
read_psms <- function(search_dir, bacteria_ids) {
  bact <- if (file.exists(bacteria_ids)) readLines(bacteria_ids) else NULL
  fs   <- Sys.glob(file.path(search_dir, "*", "psm.tsv"))
  if (!length(fs)) return(tibble())
  bind_rows(lapply(fs, function(f) {
    s <- basename(dirname(f))
    p <- tryCatch(read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, quote = "",
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(p) || !nrow(p)) return(NULL)
    pepcol <- intersect(c("Peptide", "Peptide Sequence", "Sequence"), names(p))[1]
    intcol <- intersect(c("Intensity", "MS1 Intensity"), names(p))[1]
    if (is.na(pepcol)) { warning("no peptide column in ", f); return(NULL) }
    keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(p))
    if ("Is Decoy" %in% names(p))       keep <- keep & tolower(p$`Is Decoy`) == "false"
    if ("Is Contaminant" %in% names(p)) keep <- keep & tolower(p$`Is Contaminant`) == "false"
    if (!is.null(bact) && "Protein" %in% names(p)) keep <- keep & p$Protein %in% bact
    p <- p[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(p)) return(NULL)
    tibble(sample = s,
           peptide = toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", p[[pepcol]])),
           intensity = if (is.na(intcol)) 1 else suppressWarnings(as.numeric(p[[intcol]])))
  })) |> filter(nchar(peptide) >= 5, nchar(peptide) <= 50)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Unipept pept2lca, cached. Identical request shape to §10.2 of the main Rmd.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
unipept_lca <- function(peptides, cache_path = CACHE, batch_size = 100) {
  peptides <- unique(peptides[!is.na(peptides)])
  cache <- if (file.exists(cache_path))
    suppressMessages(read_tsv(cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)) else
    tibble(peptide = character(), genus_name = character(), phylum_name = character())
  new <- setdiff(peptides, cache$peptide)
  say("Unipept: %d cached, %d to fetch", length(peptides) - length(new), length(new))
  if (!length(new)) return(filter(cache, peptide %in% peptides))
  batches <- split(new, ceiling(seq_along(new) / batch_size))
  blank_na <- function(x) ifelse(is.character(x) & x == "", NA_character_, x)
  for (i in seq_along(batches)) {
    b <- batches[[i]]
    body <- c(stats::setNames(as.list(b), rep("input[]", length(b))),
              list(equate_il = "true", extra = "true", names = "true"))
    req <- request("https://api.unipept.ugent.be/api/v2/pept2lca.json") |>
      req_method("POST") |> req_body_form(!!!body) |>
      req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = ~ 2 * .x) |> req_throttle(rate = 5 / 1)
    resp <- tryCatch(req_perform(req), error = function(e) {
      say("  batch %d ERROR: %s", i, conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
    if (is.null(resp)) next
    j <- resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)
    if (!length(j) || (is.data.frame(j) && !nrow(j))) next
    if (!is.data.frame(j)) j <- as.data.frame(j, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    add <- tibble(peptide = j$peptide,
                  genus_name  = blank_na(j$genus_name  %||% NA_character_),
                  phylum_name = blank_na(j$phylum_name %||% NA_character_))
    cache <- bind_rows(cache, add)
    ## written every batch: the fetch is hours long and must survive a kill
    write_tsv(cache, cache_path)
    if (i %% 25 == 0) say("  batch %d/%d", i, length(batches))
  }
  filter(cache, peptide %in% peptides)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The contrast
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Returns the per-genus rho table and the two medians, for both the share-of-
## whole-proteome parameterization and the within-clade one.
## NOTE (corrected 2026-11-09): neither of these is the Figure 2a quantity.
## Figure 2a plots the centred-log-ratio statistic rho_clr; both parameterizations
## here are on raw proportions. An earlier comment called the share-of-whole one
## "the Fig. 2a one", which is wrong.
clade_contrast <- function(psm, lca, mpa, label) {
  pep <- lca |> filter(!is.na(genus_name))
  d   <- psm |> inner_join(pep, by = "peptide")
  if (!nrow(d)) { say("%s: no peptide mapped to a genus", label); return(NULL) }

  ## §B5's threshold is on PSM ROWS per genus, pooled over subjects
  gen <- d |> count(genus_name) |> filter(n >= MIN_PSM) |> pull(genus_name)
  ## NOTE: this gate is on TOTAL genera clearing MIN_PSM, not on Bacteroidota
  ## specifically. There is no per-clade floor in this script; B13 is the one
  ## with a per-clade rule (MIN_CLADE <- 3L).
  if (length(gen) < 4) { say("%s: only %d genera at >= %d PSMs", label, length(gen), MIN_PSM); return(NULL) }
  d <- filter(d, genus_name %in% gen)

  MP <- d |> group_by(sample, genus_name) |> summarise(v = sum(intensity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = genus_name, values_from = v, values_fill = 0)
  MPm <- as.matrix(MP[, -1]); rownames(MPm) <- MP$sample
  MPm <- MPm / rowSums(MPm)                      # renormalized over kept genera, as §B5

  MG <- mpa |> filter(genus %in% gen) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = genus, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
  MGm <- as.matrix(MG[, -1]); rownames(MGm) <- MG$sample   # MetaPhlAn pct, NOT renormalized

  smp <- intersect(rownames(MGm), rownames(MPm))
  gg  <- intersect(colnames(MGm), colnames(MPm))
  if (length(smp) < 8 || length(gg) < 4) {
    say("%s: %d subjects and %d genera in both layers - too thin", label, length(smp), length(gg))
    return(NULL)
  }
  MGm <- MGm[smp, gg, drop = FALSE]; MPm <- MPm[smp, gg, drop = FALSE]
  say("%s: %d subjects, %d genera in both layers", label, length(smp), length(gg))

  ph <- d |> count(genus_name, phylum_name) |> group_by(genus_name) |>
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()
  phy <- setNames(ph$phylum_name[match(gg, ph$genus_name)], gg)
  phy[phy %in% "Firmicutes"] <- "Bacillota"
  phy[phy %in% "Bacteroidetes"] <- "Bacteroidota"

  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  rho <- function(A, B) vapply(colnames(A), function(g)
    suppressWarnings(cor(A[, g], B[, g], method = "spearman")), 0)

  ## within-clade parameterization: renormalize each layer inside each phylum
  within <- function(M) {
    out <- M
    for (p in unique(phy)) {
      j <- which(phy == p); if (!length(j)) next
      s <- rowSums(M[, j, drop = FALSE]); s[s == 0] <- NA
      out[, j] <- M[, j, drop = FALSE] / s
    }
    out
  }
  MGw <- within(MGm); MPw <- within(MPm)

  tab <- tibble(genus = gg, phylum = unname(phy),
                psm        = as.integer(table(d$genus_name)[gg]),
                rho_raw    = rho(MGm, MPm),
                rho_clr    = rho(clr(MGm), clr(MPm)),
                rho_within = rho(MGw, MPw))

  med <- function(col, p) median(tab[[col]][tab$phylum == p], na.rm = TRUE)
  gap <- function(col) med(col, "Bacillota") - med(col, "Bacteroidota")

  ## Patient resampling for the raw share-of-whole clade gap.
## NOTE (corrected 2026-11-09): this is NOT the Figure 2a gap. Figure 2a is
## computed on centred log-ratios (rho_clr); this bootstrap resamples raw rho.
  set.seed(SEED)
  bs <- replicate(NBOOT, {
    i <- sample(seq_along(smp), replace = TRUE)
    r <- rho(MGm[i, , drop = FALSE], MPm[i, , drop = FALSE])
    median(r[phy == "Bacillota"], na.rm = TRUE) - median(r[phy == "Bacteroidota"], na.rm = TRUE)
  })

  summ <- tibble(
    cohort = label, n_subjects = length(smp),
    n_bacillota = sum(phy == "Bacillota"), n_bacteroidota = sum(phy == "Bacteroidota"),
    bacillota_raw = med("rho_raw", "Bacillota"), bacteroidota_raw = med("rho_raw", "Bacteroidota"),
    gap_raw = gap("rho_raw"),
    gap_raw_lo = unname(quantile(bs, .025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    gap_raw_hi = unname(quantile(bs, .975, na.rm = TRUE)),
    gap_clr = gap("rho_clr"), gap_within = gap("rho_within"))

  say("  share-of-whole : Bacillota %+.3f | Bacteroidota %+.3f | gap %+.3f [%+.3f, %+.3f]",
      summ$bacillota_raw, summ$bacteroidota_raw, summ$gap_raw, summ$gap_raw_lo, summ$gap_raw_hi)
  say("  within-clade   : gap %+.3f   (Pittsburgh gives +0.06, P = 0.48)", summ$gap_within)
  say("  CLR            : gap %+.3f", summ$gap_clr)
  list(tab = tab, summ = summ)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Cohort registry
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COHORTS <- list(
  ELINAV_ISR = list(search = file.path(EDIR, "search_ISR"),
                    bact   = file.path(EDIR, "mp_annot_ISR", "bacteria_ids.txt"),
                    mg     = EDIR),
  ELINAV_UC  = list(search = file.path(EDIR, "search_UC"),
                    bact   = file.path(EDIR, "mp_annot_UC", "bacteria_ids.txt"),
                    mg     = EDIR),
  TANCA      = list(search = file.path(TDIR, "search"),
                    bact   = file.path(TDIR, "mp_annot", "bacteria_ids.txt"),
                    mg     = TDIR)
)
## positive control, only if both are pointed at something
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("PITT_PEP")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("PITT_MPA")))
  COHORTS$PITT <- list(search = Sys.getenv("PITT_PEP"), bact = "", mg = Sys.getenv("PITT_MPA"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## STAGE: probe
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
probe <- function() {
  rows <- lapply(names(COHORTS), function(k) {
    cc <- COHORTS[[k]]
    say("---- %s ----", k)
    psm_dirs <- Sys.glob(file.path(cc$search, "*", "psm.tsv"))
    mpa_f    <- find_mpa(cc$mg)
    dbs      <- unique(na.omit(vapply(head(mpa_f, 40), mpa_db, "")))
    say("  psm.tsv          %d", length(psm_dirs))
    say("  bacteria_ids     %s", if (file.exists(cc$bact)) "present" else "MISSING")
    say("  metaphlan files  %d", length(mpa_f))
    say("  metaphlan db     %s", if (length(dbs)) paste(dbs, collapse = ", ") else "NOT FOUND")
    g <- if (length(mpa_f)) read_mpa_genus(mpa_f) else tibble()
    nsub <- length(unique(g$sample)); ngen <- length(unique(g$genus))
    say("  MG subjects      %d", nsub)
    say("  MG genera        %d", ngen)
    ## peptide volume, from one subject, extrapolated -- a full read is the
    ## unipept stage's job, not the probe's
    np <- if (length(psm_dirs)) {
      s1 <- read_psms(dirname(dirname(psm_dirs[1])), cc$bact)
      nrow(s1)
    } else 0L
    say("  PSMs in subject 1 %d", np)
    tibble(cohort = k, n_psm_files = length(psm_dirs), n_mpa_files = length(mpa_f),
           mpa_db = paste(dbs, collapse = ","), mg_subjects = nsub, mg_genera = ngen,
           psms_subject1 = np)
  })
  out <- bind_rows(rows)
  write_tsv(out, file.path(OUT, "b33_probe.tsv"))
  say("")
  say("Wrote %s", file.path(OUT, "b33_probe.tsv"))
  dbs <- unique(unlist(strsplit(out$mpa_db[nzchar(out$mpa_db)], ",")))
  if (length(dbs) > 1)
    say("WARNING: more than one MetaPhlAn database across cohorts (%s). Cross-cohort genus comparison is not valid until this is one version.",
        paste(dbs, collapse = " / "))
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## STAGE: unipept / analyze
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_cohort <- function(k) {
  cc <- COHORTS[[k]]
  psm <- read_psms(cc$search, cc$bact)
  if (!nrow(psm)) { say("%s: no PSMs read from %s", k, cc$search); return(NULL) }
  say("%s: %d PSM rows, %d subjects, %d distinct peptides",
      k, nrow(psm), length(unique(psm$sample)), length(unique(psm$peptide)))
  lca <- unipept_lca(unique(psm$peptide))
  if (STAGE == "unipept") return(invisible(NULL))
  mpa <- read_mpa_genus(find_mpa(cc$mg))
  clade_contrast(psm, lca, mpa, k)
}

if (STAGE %in% c("probe", "all")) probe()
if (STAGE %in% c("unipept", "analyze", "all")) {
  res <- lapply(names(COHORTS), function(k) tryCatch(run_cohort(k),
    error = function(e) { say("%s FAILED: %s", k, conditionMessage(e)); NULL }))
  names(res) <- names(COHORTS)
  if (STAGE != "unipept") {
    ok <- Filter(Negate(is.null), res)
    if (length(ok)) {
      write_tsv(bind_rows(lapply(ok, `[[`, "summ")), file.path(OUT, "b33_clade_summary.tsv"))
      write_tsv(bind_rows(lapply(names(ok), function(k)
        mutate(ok[[k]]$tab, cohort = k))), file.path(OUT, "b33_clade_per_genus.tsv"))
      say("Wrote b33_clade_summary.tsv and b33_clade_per_genus.tsv to %s", OUT)
    }
    saveRDS(res, file.path(OUT, "b33_result.rds"))
  }
}
```

## B33 — survey crosslayer

the cross-layer comparison on the 565-set survey family

Source: `B33_survey_crosslayer.R`

```{r B33_survey_crosslayer, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B33 — the cross-layer comparison on the 565-set survey family
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY HERE, AFTER TWO FAILURES. Per KO (B31) the metagenome showed no effect
## variation beyond its own standard errors, so the correlation was undefined.
## Across the 68 shared KEGG pathways (B32) NEITHER layer's enrichment scores
## spread wider than the permutation null. The survey family is the remaining
## place worth trying, for one reason: it is where the protein signal provably
## is. The chaperone members rank 7th of 565 at NES about -2.2, far outside any
## 1.15 null, so the protein axis here has the variance that the KEGG maps
## lacked. If the metagenome has any set-level response signal at all, this is
## the family in which it would show.
##
## THE OBSTACLE, AND THE BRIDGE. SETS_P is defined over PROTEIN identifiers,
## and protein identifiers come from each cohort's own assembly -- the
## metagenome cannot be scored on them. Every protein does carry a KO, so the
## sets can be projected into KO space through annot_new$ko_primary. That is
## the same annotation bridge the paper already uses wherever the two layers or
## the two cohorts have to meet.
##
## WHAT THE PROJECTION COSTS, STATED PLAINLY. It is lossy and it is not an
## identity. Proteins with no KO drop out; several proteins sharing a KO
## collapse to one member; and the resulting set is the KO IMAGE of the protein
## set, not the protein set itself. So this does not compare "the same set" in
## two layers -- it compares the closest correspondence the annotation allows.
## project_sets() reports the retention per set so the cost is visible rather
## than assumed, and any set falling below the size floor after projection is
## dropped rather than scored on a remnant.
##
## BOTH LAYERS ARE SCORED IN KO SPACE, which is the symmetric choice. Scoring
## the proteome on its native protein sets and the metagenome on the KO image
## would give the two layers different set definitions and a correlation
## between them would partly measure that difference. Each layer uses its own
## full sample set: the proteome every labelled channel, the metagenome every
## labelled sample above the depth floor. The correlation runs across SETS, so
## the two layers never need the same patients -- which is what let B31's
## original 47-patient restriction be dropped.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tibble)})
if (!requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)) stop("limma is required")
if (!requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE)) stop("fgsea is required")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ko_map(): the one protein -> KO lookup both halves of this file use
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Written once because a bare setNames() over the annotation keeps whichever
## row came first when a protein appears twice -- two cohorts, or two KO
## assignments -- and the choice would then be invisible in both the set
## projection and the ranking. Collapse to distinct pairs and refuse to guess.
ko_map <- function(annot, cohort = NULL) {
  stopifnot(all(c("protein", "ko_primary") %in% names(annot)))
  a <- annot |> filter(!is.na(ko_primary), ko_primary != "", !is.na(protein))
  if (!is.null(cohort) && "cohort" %in% names(a)) a <- a |> filter(cohort == !!cohort)
  a <- a |> distinct(protein, ko_primary)
  dup <- unique(a$protein[duplicated(a$protein)])
  if (length(dup))
    stop(sprintf(paste0("ko_map: %d proteins carry more than one ko_primary",
                        " (e.g. %s). Resolve the annotation, or pass cohort=",
                        " if the duplicates are one protein per cohort."),
                 length(dup), paste(head(dup, 3), collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
  setNames(a$ko_primary, a$protein)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## project_sets(): protein-id sets -> KO sets, with the loss reported
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
project_sets <- function(sets, annot = annot_new, cohort = NULL,
                         universe = NULL, min_size = 10) {
  map <- ko_map(annot, cohort)

  out <- lapply(sets, function(p) {
    k <- unique(unname(map[intersect(p, names(map))]))
    k <- k[!is.na(k)]
    if (!is.null(universe)) k <- intersect(k, universe)
    k
  })
  rep <- tibble(set = names(sets), n_prot = lengths(sets), n_ko = lengths(out)) |>
    mutate(kept = ifelse(n_prot > 0, n_ko / n_prot, NA_real_))
  keep <- lengths(out) >= min_size
  cat(sprintf("project_sets: %d sets in, %d survive >= %d KOs\n",
              length(sets), sum(keep), min_size))
  ## median() returns a double; %d rejects one. Formatting, not arithmetic.
  cat(sprintf("  median %.0f proteins -> %.0f KOs per set (median retention %.0f%%)\n",
              median(rep$n_prot), median(rep$n_ko), 100 * median(rep$kept, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat("  The projected set is the KO image of the protein set, not the set",
      " itself.\n", sep = "")
  ## The correlation is computed ACROSS sets, so the number of surviving sets
  ## is the sample size of the whole analysis. B31's simulation puts the 95%
  ## interval at roughly [-0.8, +0.45] for 25 features -- wider than its own
  ## 0.8 unresolved threshold. Say so here rather than after the permutations.
  if (sum(keep) < 60)
    warning(sprintf(paste("only %d sets survive: that is the sample size for the",
                          "correlation, and below about 60 the interval is wider",
                          "than B31's unresolved threshold whatever the data say."),
                    sum(keep)), call. = FALSE)
  structure(out[keep], report = rep)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ko_ranker(): a function(resp) -> named per-KO statistic, refit each call
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Used for the proteome. `M` is a KO-by-sample matrix (MP), zeros treated as
## missing for the reason B31 learned the hard way: logging them to a shared
## floor gives undetected KOs huge effects with tiny standard errors.
## `strata` is the plex, entered as a covariate exactly as elsewhere.
ko_ranker <- function(M, strata = NULL, min_per_arm = 5) {
  L <- as.matrix(M); L[L <= 0] <- NA_real_; L <- log(L)
  function(resp) {
    ok <- vapply(levels(factor(resp)), function(g)
      rowSums(is.finite(L[, resp == g, drop = FALSE])) >= min_per_arm,
      logical(nrow(L)))
    k <- apply(ok, 1, all)
    ## ESTIMABILITY, as in B31's build_ko(). A KO can clear the per-arm count
    ## and still have no observation in some plex, which makes the plex term
    ## inestimable for that row; limma then returns partial coefficients whose
    ## standard errors mean nothing. Require every level present twice. The
    ## first run of this function warned on 627 probes for exactly this.
    if (!is.null(strata)) {
      sf <- droplevels(factor(strata))
      okp <- vapply(levels(sf), function(g)
        rowSums(is.finite(L[, sf == g, drop = FALSE])) >= 2, logical(nrow(L)))
      k <- k & apply(okp, 1, all)
    }
    X <- L[k, , drop = FALSE]
    d <- if (is.null(strata)) data.frame(resp = resp)
         else data.frame(resp = resp, s = droplevels(factor(strata)))
    des <- if (is.null(strata)) model.matrix(~ resp, d) else model.matrix(~ s + resp, d)
    cn <- grep("^resp", colnames(des), value = TRUE)[1]
    f <- limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(X, des))
    t <- f$coefficients[, cn] / (f$stdev.unscaled[, cn] * sqrt(f$s2.post))
    t <- t[is.finite(t)]
    t
  }
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## protein_matrix(): PSM rows -> protein rows
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## OP$a is NOT protein-level. Its rows are PSM rows -- pep_ph$row indexes into
## it, and figures_v2's S6A counts "that phylum's PSM rows" -- with OP$rd$Protein
## naming each row's parent protein. Several rows therefore share a protein, and
## PSMs within a protein are correlated, so fitting the contrast on OP$a
## directly and then averaging into KOs would weight each KO by how many PSMs
## its proteins happened to yield, which tracks abundance. Roll up first.
##
## The roll-up is a sum of intensities per protein, which is what the rest of
## figures_v2 does whenever it aggregates a group of these rows (colSums over
## the matching rows). NA is treated as absent, and a protein with no signal in
## a sample stays NA rather than becoming a zero -- ko_ranker()/prot_ranker()
## treats non-positive values as missing and that distinction has to survive
## the roll-up or the zeros come back in through the side door.
##
## IF THE SURVEY ALREADY HAS A PROTEIN-LEVEL STATISTIC, USE THAT INSTEAD. The
## 565-set family was scored on something, and whatever ranked those proteins
## is the authoritative statistic for this comparison; this helper is a
## reconstruction from OP and will not reproduce it exactly. Pass the real one
## as prot_fit and skip this function.
protein_matrix <- function(OP, samples = OP$d$sample) {
  stopifnot(!is.null(OP$rd$Protein), nrow(OP$a) == length(OP$rd$Protein))
  A <- as.matrix(OP$a[, samples, drop = FALSE])
  A[!is.finite(A) | A <= 0] <- NA_real_
  g <- OP$rd$Protein
  g[!is.na(g) & !nzchar(trimws(g))] <- NA          # "" is not a protein id
  keep <- !is.na(g)
  A <- A[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  g <- droplevels(factor(g[keep]))
  B <- A; B[is.na(B)] <- 0
  M <- rowsum(B, group = g, reorder = TRUE)
  ## rowsum() turned the all-missing cells into 0. Put them back: "nothing
  ## observed" has to stay distinguishable from "summed to nothing", because
  ## prot_ranker() reads non-positive as missing and a 0 here would come back
  ## in as a real low value.
  N <- rowsum((!is.na(A)) * 1L, group = g, reorder = TRUE)
  M[N == 0] <- NA_real_
  cat(sprintf("protein_matrix: %d PSM rows -> %d proteins, %d samples (%.0f%% missing)\n",
              nrow(A), nrow(M), ncol(M), 100 * mean(is.na(M))))
  M
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## prot_ranker(): the same fit, on the protein matrix
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Deliberately the same function. ko_ranker() takes a feature-by-sample
## matrix and knows nothing about what the rows are, so pointing it at the
## protein matrix gives the protein-level contrast with the identical
## treatment of zeros, the identical per-arm floor and the identical plex
## estimability requirement. Aliasing it rather than copying it means the two
## cannot drift apart, and no reviewer has to be told that the layers were
## fitted "comparably" -- they were fitted by the same code.
##
## The filters cost far less here, and the reason is worth stating: a KO is
## kept if ANY protein carrying it clears the floor, whereas at KO level the
## summed row had to clear it itself. Same thresholds, different unit.
prot_ranker <- ko_ranker

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ko_from_proteins(): the proteome ranking, without the coverage collapse
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ko_ranker() above refits per KO on MP, and on a matrix that is 47% zero the
## per-arm and per-plex requirements cut ~1,320 KOs to 350. That was the
## binding loss on the protein side: 7 of 21 sets fell below ten members in
## the proteome while all 21 survived in the metagenome.
##
## The protein-level statistic does not have that problem -- it is fitted over
## every protein in the analysis, thousands of them, and each KO inherits
## whatever proteins carry it. Mapping down to KO afterwards keeps far more
## KOs than fitting at KO level does.
##
## HOW THE PROTEINS ARE COMBINED. Default is the mean of the protein-level
## statistics for that KO. The alternative is Stouffer, sum(t)/sqrt(n), which
## rewards a KO whose many proteins all move together and is the better
## evidence model -- but it also makes the statistic grow with protein count,
## and protein count tracks abundance, so it introduces an abundance gradient
## into a ranking that is then scored for enrichment. Mean is the neutral
## choice and is the default; pass fun = "stouffer" deliberately if you want
## the other, and say which in the methods.
##
## `prot_fit` is function(resp) -> named protein-level statistic, so the
## permutation refits the proteins and re-derives the KO ranking from scratch.
## For a precheck on the observed labels only, pass function(r) stat_pitt.
ko_from_proteins <- function(prot_fit, annot = annot_new, cohort = NULL,
                             fun = c("mean", "stouffer"), min_prot = 1) {
  fun <- match.arg(fun)
  map <- ko_map(annot, cohort)
  function(resp) {
    st <- prot_fit(resp)
    k  <- map[intersect(names(st), names(map))]
    v  <- st[names(k)]
    agg <- if (fun == "mean") tapply(v, k, mean)
           else tapply(v, k, function(z) sum(z) / sqrt(length(z)))
    cnt <- tapply(v, k, length)
    out <- agg[cnt >= min_prot]
    out[is.finite(out)]
  }
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b33_precheck(): the cheap screen, before any permutation
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Same logic as B32's: if a layer's observed NES spread does not exceed the
## null, nothing downstream can rescue it. The null SD is taken as an argument
## because the 1.15 measured for this design need not hold for these sets --
## pass several values and see whether the verdict is stable.
b33_precheck <- function(sets, mp_rank, mg_rank, null_sd = 1.15, seed = 1) {
  ## DIAGNOSE BEFORE SCORING. The first run of this returned "0 sets scored in
  ## both layers", which tells you nothing about why. The usual cause is an
  ## identifier mismatch: the sets are KOs from annot_new$ko_primary, the
  ## proteome ranking is named by MP's rownames and the metagenome's by
  ## ko_cpm$feature, and if any of the three spells a KO differently -- bare
  ## K01234 against ko:K01234, say -- every intersection is empty and
  ## everything downstream is NA. Show the three vocabularies side by side.
  allko <- unique(unlist(sets))
  ov <- function(nm) length(intersect(allko, nm))
  cat(sprintf("\nidentifiers: %d distinct KOs across %d sets\n",
              length(allko), length(sets)))
  cat(sprintf("  sets      e.g. %s\n", paste(head(allko, 3), collapse = ", ")))
  cat(sprintf("  proteome  %d names, %d overlap the sets; e.g. %s\n",
              length(mp_rank), ov(names(mp_rank)),
              paste(head(names(mp_rank), 3), collapse = ", ")))
  cat(sprintf("  metagenome %d names, %d overlap the sets; e.g. %s\n",
              length(mg_rank), ov(names(mg_rank)),
              paste(head(names(mg_rank), 3), collapse = ", ")))
  if (ov(names(mp_rank)) == 0 || ov(names(mg_rank)) == 0) {
    cat("  STOP: a layer shares no identifiers with the sets. This is a naming\n",
        "  mismatch, not a result -- reconcile the three vocabularies above\n",
        "  before anything else.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  score <- function(s, lab) {
    ss <- lapply(sets, intersect, names(s)); ss <- ss[lengths(ss) >= 10]
    cat(sprintf("  %s: %d of %d sets keep >= 10 members\n",
                sub("NES_", "", lab), length(ss), length(sets)))
    if (!length(ss)) return(tibble(pathway = character(), !!lab := numeric()))
    set.seed(seed)
    suppressWarnings(fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(ss, s, minSize = 10, maxSize = 5000,
                                            eps = 0)) |>
      as_tibble() |> transmute(pathway, !!lab := NES)
  }
  both <- inner_join(score(mp_rank, "NES_mp"), score(mg_rank, "NES_mg"),
                     by = "pathway")
  n <- nrow(both)
  if (n < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("\nb33_precheck: %d sets scored in both layers -- too few to\n", n),
        "  say anything. See the per-layer counts above for which side lost\n",
        "  them, and the membership line for whether the KO bridge is to blame.\n",
        sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat(sprintf("\nb33_precheck: %d survey sets scored in both layers\n", n))
  for (ns in unique(c(null_sd, 1.15, 1.00, 0.85))) {
    rmg <- 1 - ns^2 / var(both$NES_mg); rmp <- 1 - ns^2 / var(both$NES_mp)
    cat(sprintf("  null SD %.2f -> reliability  metagenome %+.2f  proteome %+.2f\n",
                ns, rmg, rmp))
  }
  cat(sprintf("  observed NES SD   metagenome %.2f   proteome %.2f\n",
              sd(both$NES_mg), sd(both$NES_mp)))
  cat(sprintf("  observed Spearman %+.3f, sign agreement %.0f%%\n",
              cor(both$NES_mp, both$NES_mg, method = "spearman"),
              100 * mean(sign(both$NES_mp) == sign(both$NES_mg))))
  ## THE VERDICT NEEDS BOTH RELIABILITY AND n, and the first version used only
  ## reliability. On this family it called 14 sets "marginal" when the two
  ## reliabilities (0.27 and 0.52) were the best seen anywhere -- the problem
  ## was never the signal, it was that fourteen points cannot pin a correlation
  ## however clean each one is. Simulated at this attenuation the interval is
  ## about 1.9 wide at 14, 21 and even 60 sets, 0.89 at 150, and 0.45 at 565.
  ## So the set count is the binding constraint and is reported as such.
  rmg <- 1 - null_sd^2 / var(both$NES_mg)
  rmp <- 1 - null_sd^2 / var(both$NES_mp)
  worst <- min(rmg, rmp)
  att <- if (rmg > 0 && rmp > 0) sqrt(rmg * rmp) else NA_real_
  cat(sprintf("  attenuation factor %.2f\n", att))
  cat(if (!is.finite(worst))
        "  VERDICT: cannot be computed -- a layer has no NES variance at all.\n"
      else if (worst <= 0.05)
        "  VERDICT: do not run. Neither layer spreads wider than its null.\n"
      else if (n < 100)
        sprintf(paste0("  VERDICT: do not run. The reliabilities are workable",
                       " (%.2f and %.2f) but\n  %d sets cannot pin a correlation",
                       " at this attenuation -- the interval\n  would be about",
                       " 1.9 wide. The set count is the binding constraint,\n",
                       "  not the signal. You need roughly 150 sets before this",
                       " is worth\n  the permutations, and about 565 before it",
                       " is decisive.\n"), rmg, rmp, n)
      else if (worst < 0.4)
        "  VERDICT: marginal. Expect an interval near the 0.8 threshold.\n"
      else
        sprintf("  VERDICT: run it (worst reliability %.2f, %d sets).\n", worst, n))
  invisible(both)
}

cat("B33 loaded. In the Pittsburgh session:\n\n",
    "  source('B32_pathway_crosslayer.R')   # shuffle(), layer_effects(), mg_ranker()\n",
    "  source('B33_survey_crosslayer.R')\n\n",
    "  mgf  <- mg_ranker(mg)                       # metagenome, ~68 samples\n",
    "  mgr  <- attr(mgf, 'resp')                   # aligned for you\n",
    "  sets <- project_sets(SETS_P, annot_new)     # protein sets -> KO sets\n\n",
    "PROTEOME SIDE -- use the protein route, not ko_ranker(MP). Fitting per KO\n",
    "on MP cut 1,320 KOs to 350 and left 7 of 21 sets under ten members:\n\n",
    "  mps  <- intersect(colnames(OP$a), OP$d$sample)\n",
    "  plex <- OP$d$Mixture[match(mps, OP$d$sample)]\n",
    "  PM   <- protein_matrix(OP, mps)             # PSM rows -> protein rows\n",
    "  pf   <- prot_ranker(PM, strata = plex)      # function(resp) -> protein t\n",
    "  mpf  <- ko_from_proteins(pf)                # ... -> KO ranking\n",
    "  mpr  <- OP$d$resp[match(mps, OP$d$sample)]\n\n",
    "  b33_precheck(sets, mpf(mpr), mgf(mgr))      # seconds\n\n",
    "The old KO-level route is still there if you want the contrast:\n",
    "  mpf0 <- ko_ranker(MP[, mps], strata = plex)\n\n",
    "READ THIS BEFORE RUNNING IT. The coverage fix changes how many sets are\n",
    "SCORED; it cannot change how many EXIST. On SETS_P -- the 30 reported sets\n",
    "-- the ceiling is 30, and 21 after the KO projection. Fourteen sets gave\n",
    "reliabilities of 0.27 and 0.52, the best of the three attempts, and still a\n",
    "confidence interval about 1.9 wide; at this attenuation 21 and even 60 sets\n",
    "are no better. Roughly 150 sets are needed before the permutations are\n",
    "worth running and about 565 before the answer is decisive. So this is worth\n",
    "running only once `sets` is built from the actual 565-set survey family,\n",
    "which is assembled in analysis_v17.Rmd and is not among its exports --\n",
    "figures_v2 sees only the scored output (full_space_scored_10k.csv,\n",
    "nulls_pitt_full/). Everything downstream takes those memberships unchanged.\n\n",
    "If the precheck says run:\n",
    "  mp  <- layer_effects(sets, mpf, mpr, plex, B = 200, 'proteome')\n",
    "  mgL <- layer_effects(sets, mgf, mgr, NULL, B = 200, 'metagenome')\n",
    "  sv <- inner_join(mgL |> transmute(feature, mg_coef = coef, mg_se = se),\n",
    "                   mp  |> transmute(feature, mp_coef = coef, mp_se = se),\n",
    "                   by = 'feature')\n",
    "  source('B31_crosslayer_attenuation.R'); run_b31(list(survey = sv),\n",
    "                                                  out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n", sep = "")
```

## B34 — reliability splithalf

is the gene layer's reliability really zero, or are its SEs overstated?

Source: `B34_reliability_splithalf.R`

```{r B34_reliability_splithalf, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B34 — is the gene layer's reliability really zero, or are its SEs overstated?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS COMES FIRST. Every verdict so far rests on one quantity:
##
##     reliability = 1 - mean(se^2) / var(effect)
##
## and that quantity is only as good as the standard errors in it. B31 put the
## metagenome at -0.15, which is not "a bit of signal" but a NEGATIVE variance
## estimate -- the effects spread LESS than their own standard errors say they
## should. Two different things produce that:
##
##   (a) the true effect variance really is zero, or
##   (b) the standard errors are too large.
##
## (b) is not far-fetched. The gene side uses Welch standard errors on ~20
## samples per arm with no shrinkage, while the protein side gets limma's
## moderated ones; noisy, upward-biased variance estimates on one axis and
## shrunk ones on the other is exactly the asymmetry that would produce this.
## Nothing in B31 can tell (a) from (b), because B31 takes the standard errors
## as given.
##
## A split-half correlation does not. Split the patients, fit the contrast
## twice on disjoint halves, and correlate the two effect vectors ACROSS
## features. The two halves' errors are independent by construction, so their
## correlation measures how much of each half's effect vector is reproducible
## signal -- with no reference to any standard error at all. Spearman-Brown
## then rescales a half-sample reliability to the full sample:
##
##     R_full = 2 r / (1 + r)
##
## If split-half says ~0 too, the standard errors are vindicated and the gene
## layer has no reproducible feature-level response structure: (a), and the
## comparison is closed. If split-half is clearly positive while B31's
## model-based reliability is negative, it is (b), the standard errors are
## inflated, and the comparison is worth re-opening with better ones.
##
## THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RUNNING. Reproducible is not the same as
## response-related. A feature detected in most responders and few
## non-responders gets a positive effect in BOTH halves whatever the biology,
## and compositional closure, prevalence and abundance all impose structure
## that both halves share. Split-half alone cannot separate shared true signal
## from shared bias, and would report either as reliability.
##
## So the same split-half is run on PERMUTED response labels. Under permutation
## the response signal is destroyed and only the shared bias remains, so the
## permuted r is the floor that the observed r has to clear. A positive
## observed r that the permuted r matches is bias, not reliability. This is the
## difference between a diagnostic and a number.
##
## VALIDATED BEFORE SHIPPING, because a diagnostic that cannot be trusted is
## worse than none. Simulated at 400 features and 70 samples, with the true
## reliability known:
##
##   true R_full   0.000  0.149  0.412  0.612  0.814
##   2r/(1+r)      0.004  0.147  0.408  0.614  0.818
##   SE-based      0.003  0.151  0.413  0.610  0.815
##
## The two agree when the standard errors are right -- which is why a
## disagreement localises the fault. Inflating the reported standard errors
## while leaving the data alone:
##
##   true R_full 0.412, SE x1.0 -> split-half +0.41, SE-based +0.41
##   true R_full 0.412, SE x1.2 -> split-half +0.42, SE-based +0.16
##   true R_full 0.412, SE x1.4 -> split-half +0.41, SE-based -0.17
##
## THE LAST LINE IS WHY THIS MATTERS. A true reliability of 0.4 with standard
## errors overstated by 40% produces an SE-based estimate of -0.17 -- which is
## what B31 reported (-0.15). And pure absence of signal does NOT naturally
## produce -0.15: at 327 features with no signal the SE-based estimate sits at
## -0.00 and falls to -0.15 or below in only 4% of draws. So B31's number is
## either a 1-in-25 draw under no signal, or the central expectation under a
## real reliability near 0.4 with inflated standard errors. The two readings
## have opposite consequences for the paper and B31 cannot distinguish them.
##
## WHAT IT NEEDS. `mg` -- the long metagenome table systems_MG_vs_MP.R builds
## (sample, feature, cpm, resp) -- plus, for the proteome comparison, MP and
## OP. Nothing from `pat`: see the next section.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tibble)
})

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## mg_fit_wide(): the gene contrast on EVERY labelled metagenome, not 47
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B31 fits the gene side as G[kos, pat$bio] -- the 47 patients paired with a
## proteome. That restriction is not needed and never was. The correlation runs
## across FEATURES; the two layers are two vectors indexed by ortholog group,
## and nothing requires them to come from the same people. Pittsburgh has 82
## paired metagenomes of which 73 are labelled, and v17 section 10c already
## sets 72 metagenomes against 55 proteomes elsewhere. Using 47 throws away a
## third of the gene-side precision for no methodological gain.
##
## WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT WORTH, STATED CAREFULLY. It is tempting to say the
## standard errors fall by sqrt(73/47) so mean(se^2) falls by about a third and
## reliability must rise from -0.15 to about +0.2. That arithmetic is wrong,
## and I made it before writing this. Reliability is
##
##     var_true / (var_true + mean(se^2))
##
## and shrinking the error variance shrinks the OBSERVED variance with it. If
## var_true is genuinely zero, reliability is zero at every sample size: the
## numerator does not grow. More samples help only to the extent there is real
## variance presently buried in noise. The honest reason to run it is that it
## is free and that -0.15 is a point estimate with its own sampling error --
## not that it has to work.
##
## `zero_as`: "missing" matches B31 and B33 (undetected is not a small value;
## logging it to a shared floor hands undetected features large effects with
## small standard errors). "floor" reproduces mg_ranker's log2(cpm + 1) with a
## prevalence filter, for use as a sensitivity check -- not as the primary.
## `strata` conditions the contrast on a design variable, entered exactly as the
## plex is on the protein side. It is NOT optional in general: build_ko() fits
## the metagenome as ~ resp with the comment "the metagenome has none", and
## `mg`'s own sample names carry two provenances -- a shared run tag and
## Illumina _S indices -- so that comment has to be checked rather than
## assumed. If the split is real, leaving it out puts between-run differences
## into var(effect) and inflates the reliability.
mg_fit_wide <- function(mg_long, zero_as = c("missing", "floor"),
                        min_per_arm = 5, min_prev = 0.2, strata = NULL) {
  zero_as <- match.arg(zero_as)
  w <- mg_long |> filter(!is.na(resp))
  if (anyDuplicated(w[c("feature", "sample")]))
    stop("mg_fit_wide: duplicated feature-sample pairs in the long table",
         call. = FALSE)
  samples <- unique(w$sample); feats <- unique(w$feature)
  M <- matrix(NA_real_, length(feats), length(samples),
              dimnames = list(feats, samples))
  M[cbind(match(w$feature, feats), match(w$sample, samples))] <- w$cpm
  resp <- droplevels(factor(w$resp[match(samples, w$sample)]))
  if (nlevels(resp) != 2)
    stop("mg_fit_wide: need exactly two response levels, got ",
         paste(levels(resp), collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)

  ## NATURAL log, not log2, although mg_ranker() uses log2. The base is only a
  ## scale factor and every quantity here is invariant to it -- correlations,
  ## reliabilities and split-half r all are -- but build_ko() logs naturally,
  ## and matching it keeps the printed effect SDs and median SEs comparable
  ## between the 47-patient and the wide fit. Comparing 0.217 against a number
  ## that is 1/log(2) times larger would invite exactly the wrong conclusion.
  if (zero_as == "missing") {
    L <- M; L[!is.finite(L) | L <= 0] <- NA_real_; L <- log(L)
  } else {
    keep <- rowMeans(is.finite(M) & M > 0) >= min_prev
    L <- log(M[keep, , drop = FALSE] + 1)
  }
  cat(sprintf("mg_fit_wide: %d labelled samples (%s), %d features, zeros as %s\n",
              ncol(L), paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(resp), table(resp)),
                             collapse = " "),
              nrow(L), zero_as))

  gl <- levels(resp)                       # [1] is subtracted from [2]
  A <- L[, resp == gl[2], drop = FALSE]; B <- L[, resp == gl[1], drop = FALSE]
  ka <- rowSums(is.finite(A)); kb <- rowSums(is.finite(B))

  if (is.null(strata)) {
    ma <- rowMeans(A, na.rm = TRUE);  mb <- rowMeans(B, na.rm = TRUE)
    va <- apply(A, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE); vb <- apply(B, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
    out <- tibble(feature = rownames(L), coef = ma - mb,
                  se = sqrt(va / ka + vb / kb), n_hi = ka, n_lo = kb)
  } else {
    ## Aligned to THIS matrix's columns by the caller's own sample order --
    ## a strata vector in the long table's row order would be silently
    ## mismatched here, which is the kind of error that produces a plausible
    ## number rather than an error message.
    sf <- strata[match(colnames(L), names(strata))]
    if (anyNA(sf))
      stop(sprintf(paste0("mg_fit_wide: `strata` must be a NAMED vector covering",
                          " every sample in the\n  matrix; %d of %d missing."),
                   sum(is.na(sf)), length(sf)), call. = FALSE)
    sf <- droplevels(factor(sf))
    okp <- vapply(levels(sf), function(g)
      rowSums(is.finite(L[, sf == g, drop = FALSE])) >= 2, logical(nrow(L)))
    k <- apply(okp, 1, all) & ka >= min_per_arm & kb >= min_per_arm
    cat(sprintf("  conditioning on %d strata (%s); %d of %d features estimable\n",
                nlevels(sf), paste(levels(sf), collapse = ", "),
                sum(k), nrow(L)))
    des <- model.matrix(~ sf + resp)
    cn <- grep("^resp", colnames(des), value = TRUE)[1]
    f <- suppressWarnings(limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(L[k, , drop = FALSE], des)))
    out <- tibble(feature = rownames(L)[k],
                  coef = unname(f$coefficients[, cn]),
                  se = unname(f$stdev.unscaled[, cn] * sqrt(f$s2.post)),
                  n_hi = ka[k], n_lo = kb[k])
  }
  out <- out |> filter(n_hi >= min_per_arm, n_lo >= min_per_arm,
                       is.finite(coef), is.finite(se), se > 0)
  cat(sprintf("  %d features with >= %d observations in each arm; contrast is %s - %s\n",
              nrow(out), min_per_arm, gl[2], gl[1]))
  attr(out, "resp") <- resp
  attr(out, "matrix") <- L
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## se_reliability(): B31's quantity, for comparison on the same features
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
se_reliability <- function(coef, se) {
  v <- var(coef); m <- mean(se^2)
  c(reliability = 1 - m / v, var_obs = v, mean_se2 = m,
    var_true = v - m, sd_true = sqrt(max(v - m, 0)), median_se = median(se))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## effect functions: (idx, resp) -> named effect vector
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Each takes a subset of sample positions and a response vector over ALL
## samples, and returns the contrast fitted on that subset only. The
## split-half driver calls them on the two halves.

mg_effect_fun <- function(L, min_per_arm = 3) {
  function(idx, resp) {
    r <- droplevels(factor(resp[idx])); gl <- levels(r)
    if (length(gl) != 2) return(numeric(0))
    X <- L[, idx, drop = FALSE]
    A <- X[, r == gl[2], drop = FALSE]; B <- X[, r == gl[1], drop = FALSE]
    ka <- rowSums(is.finite(A)); kb <- rowSums(is.finite(B))
    e <- rowMeans(A, na.rm = TRUE) - rowMeans(B, na.rm = TRUE)
    e[is.finite(e) & ka >= min_per_arm & kb >= min_per_arm]
  }
}

## The proteome needs its plex term, and a half-sample can lose it. Features
## without every retained plex represented twice are dropped from that half,
## for the reason B31 and B33 both ran into: limma returns partial coefficients
## for an inestimable term and the standard errors mean nothing.
mp_effect_fun <- function(L, plex, min_per_arm = 3) {
  pf <- droplevels(factor(plex))
  function(idx, resp) {
    r <- droplevels(factor(resp[idx])); p <- droplevels(factor(pf[idx]))
    if (nlevels(r) != 2) return(numeric(0))
    X <- L[, idx, drop = FALSE]
    ok <- vapply(levels(r), function(g)
      rowSums(is.finite(X[, r == g, drop = FALSE])) >= min_per_arm,
      logical(nrow(X)))
    k <- apply(ok, 1, all)
    if (nlevels(p) > 1) {
      okp <- vapply(levels(p), function(g)
        rowSums(is.finite(X[, p == g, drop = FALSE])) >= 2, logical(nrow(X)))
      k <- k & apply(okp, 1, all)
    }
    if (!any(k)) return(numeric(0))
    d <- if (nlevels(p) > 1) data.frame(resp = r, s = p) else data.frame(resp = r)
    des <- if (nlevels(p) > 1) model.matrix(~ s + resp, d) else model.matrix(~ resp, d)
    cn <- grep("^resp", colnames(des), value = TRUE)[1]
    f <- suppressWarnings(limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(X[k, , drop = FALSE], des)))
    e <- f$coefficients[, cn]
    e[is.finite(e)]
  }
}

## mp_effect_fun() is the GENERAL stratified fitter -- it takes a
## feature-by-sample matrix and any design stratum, and the "mp" in the name
## only reflects where it was needed first. Use it for the gene side whenever
## that side has a stratum of its own:
##     splithalf_test(mp_effect_fun(Lg, run), rg, strata = run, ...)
## mg_effect_fun() is the unstratified Welch version and is correct only if the
## gene layer really has no design structure.
strat_effect_fun <- mp_effect_fun

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## splithalf(): the diagnostic
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## `strata` is the design stratum that must survive the split -- the plex on
## the proteome side, NULL on the gene side. Splitting is done within
## stratum x arm so each half keeps both arms of every stratum; a stratum with
## fewer than 4 members of an arm cannot give both halves two, and its samples
## are reported and dropped rather than silently unbalancing the fit.
##
## `permute` runs the same machinery on labels shuffled within stratum, which
## is the floor the observed value must clear.
splithalf <- function(effect_fun, resp, strata = NULL, B = 200, seed = 1,
                      permute = FALSE, method = c("pearson", "spearman"),
                      min_features = 30) {
  method <- match.arg(method)
  resp <- droplevels(factor(resp))
  st <- if (is.null(strata)) factor(rep("all", length(resp)))
        else droplevels(factor(strata))
  stopifnot(length(st) == length(resp))

  ## Report the cells the design cannot split, once, on the observed labels.
  obs_cells <- split(seq_along(resp), interaction(st, resp, drop = TRUE))
  bad <- obs_cells[lengths(obs_cells) < 4]
  if (length(bad))
    cat(sprintf("  %d sample(s) in %d stratum-arm cell(s) with < 4 members cannot\n  be split and are dropped from every draw\n",
                sum(lengths(bad)), length(bad)))
  if (!length(obs_cells[lengths(obs_cells) >= 4]))
    stop("splithalf: no stratum-arm cell has 4 members", call. = FALSE)

  ## The cells are rebuilt from whichever labels this draw uses, so the
  ## permuted runs follow exactly the same procedure as the observed ones. If
  ## the split were stratified on the observed labels while the labels moved,
  ## the null would be balanced where the observed is not and the comparison
  ## would be between two different designs.
  one <- function(rr) {
    cells <- split(seq_along(rr), interaction(st, rr, drop = TRUE))
    cells <- cells[lengths(cells) >= 4]
    if (!length(cells)) return(c(r = NA_real_, nf = 0))
    a <- unlist(lapply(cells, function(ix) sample(ix, floor(length(ix) / 2))),
                use.names = FALSE)
    bset <- setdiff(unlist(cells, use.names = FALSE), a)
    eA <- effect_fun(a, rr); eB <- effect_fun(bset, rr)
    f <- intersect(names(eA), names(eB))
    if (length(f) < min_features) return(c(r = NA_real_, nf = length(f)))
    c(r = suppressWarnings(cor(eA[f], eB[f], method = method)), nf = length(f))
  }
  shuffle_within <- function(r0) {
    out <- r0
    for (lv in levels(st)) {
      i <- which(st == lv)
      if (length(i) > 1) out[i] <- r0[sample(i)]
    }
    droplevels(out)
  }

  set.seed(seed)
  res <- vapply(seq_len(B),
                function(b) one(if (permute) shuffle_within(resp) else resp),
                c(r = 0, nf = 0))
  r <- res["r", ]; nf <- res["nf", ]
```
