```{r B38_species_direction, eval=FALSE}
  out |> mutate(sign_q = p.adjust(sign_p, "BH"), null_rate = p0) |>
    arrange(genus, desc(pct_NRup))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## check_sign(): the anchor
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_sign <- function(stat, chap, nr_up_sign) {
  v <- stat[intersect(names(stat), chap)]
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (length(v) < 10)
    stop("check_sign(): only ", length(v), " chaperone proteins found in the ",
         "statistic; cannot calibrate the direction", call. = FALSE)
  frac <- mean(sign(v) == nr_up_sign)
  cat(sprintf("sign check: %.0f%% of %d chaperone proteins read as NR-up under nr_up_sign = %+d\n",
              100 * frac, length(v), nr_up_sign))
  if (frac < 0.5)
    stop(sprintf(paste0("check_sign(): the chaperone set reads as R-up (%.0f%%",
                        " NR-up), but this paper establishes it is elevated in",
                        " non-responders.\n  The sign convention is inverted --",
                        " call with nr_up_sign = %+d."),
                 100 * frac, -nr_up_sign), call. = FALSE)
  invisible(frac)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## abundance_control(): is a species' protein direction just its abundance?
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## THE PANEL IS NOT INTERPRETABLE WITHOUT THIS. A species that is simply more
## abundant in responders has most of its proteins read R-up, and a sign test
## over its proteins cannot tell that from a species whose proteins are
## differentially regulated. The distinction is the whole difference between a
## composition result and a function result, and this paper argues for the
## second against the first.
##
## So: for each species, sum its PSM intensities per sample, fit the response
## contrast on that total with labelling batch in the model, and ask how much
## of the across-species variation in direction rate the abundance shift
## explains. A strong relationship means the direction counts are a taxonomic
## abundance readout wearing protein clothing.
##
## `rows` is the PSM-row-to-species table pep_species() returns.
abundance_control <- function(rows, counts, O, cohort_lbl) {
  d <- O$d
  if (!all(c("sample", "resp") %in% names(d)))
    stop("abundance_control(): O$d needs `sample` and `resp`", call. = FALSE)
  S <- d$sample
  tot <- colSums(O$a[, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  sp <- intersect(unique(rows$tax), counts$species)
  fit <- lapply(sp, function(x) {
    r <- rows$row[rows$tax == x]
    y <- colSums(O$a[r, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) / tot
    k <- is.finite(y) & y > 0
    if (sum(k) < 8 || n_distinct(d$resp[k]) < 2) return(NULL)
    dd <- data.frame(y = log(y[k]), resp = droplevels(factor(d$resp[k])))
    if ("Mixture" %in% names(d)) dd$mix <- droplevels(factor(d$Mixture[k]))
    f <- if (!is.null(dd$mix) && nlevels(dd$mix) > 1) lm(y ~ mix + resp, dd)
         else lm(y ~ resp, dd)
    cf <- coef(summary(f))
    rn <- grep("^resp", rownames(cf), value = TRUE)[1]
    if (is.na(rn)) return(NULL)
    tibble(species = x, abund_lfc = cf[rn, 1], abund_p = cf[rn, 4])
  })
  ab <- bind_rows(fit)
  if (!nrow(ab)) { cat("  abundance control: no species estimable\n"); return(counts) }
  out <- counts |> left_join(ab, by = "species")
  k <- is.finite(out$abund_lfc) & is.finite(out$pct_NRup)
  rho <- if (sum(k) >= 5)
    suppressWarnings(cor(out$abund_lfc[k], out$pct_NRup[k], method = "spearman")) else NA_real_
  cat(sprintf("\n  ABUNDANCE CONTROL [%s]: %d species with an estimable abundance shift\n",
              cohort_lbl, sum(k)))
  cat(sprintf("    Spearman(species abundance log-ratio, %% NR-up) = %+.3f\n", rho))
  cat(if (!is.finite(rho)) "    too few species to judge\n"
      else if (abs(rho) >= 0.6)
        "    STRONG. The direction counts track how abundant each species is between\n    arms, so this panel is a composition readout. Do not present it as a\n    protein-level result without residualising on the abundance shift.\n"
      else if (abs(rho) >= 0.35)
        "    MODERATE. Abundance explains part of it. Report both columns side by\n    side so a reader can see which species move for which reason.\n"
      else
        "    WEAK. The direction counts are not simply tracking species abundance,\n    which is what makes this a protein-level statement.\n")
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b38(): both cohorts

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
b38 <- function(lca, OP, stat_pitt, chap, OS = NULL, stat_sheba = NULL,
                nr_up_sign = -1, purity_min = 0.6, min_n = 3,
                genera = c("Blautia", "Dorea", "Coprococcus", "Anaerostipes",
                           "Roseburia", "Eubacterium", "Lachnoclostridium"),
                out_dir = NULL) {
  check_sign(stat_pitt, chap, nr_up_sign)
  cat("\n--- Pittsburgh ---\n")
  rp  <- pep_species(lca, OP, "pitt")
  pp  <- protein_species(rp, purity_min)
  cnt <- direction_counts(pp, stat_pitt, nr_up_sign, min_n, genera)
  res <- abundance_control(rp, cnt, OP, "Pittsburgh") |>
    mutate(cohort = "Pittsburgh")
  if (!is.null(OS) && !is.null(stat_sheba)) {
    cat("\n--- Sheba ---\n")
    rs   <- pep_species(lca, OS, "sheba")
    ps   <- protein_species(rs, purity_min)
    cnts <- direction_counts(ps, stat_sheba, nr_up_sign, min_n, genera)
    res  <- bind_rows(res, abundance_control(rs, cnts, OS, "Sheba") |>
                             mutate(cohort = "Sheba"))
  } else cat("\nSheba skipped: pass OS and stat_sheba to include it\n")

  cat(sprintf("\n%d species x cohort rows with >= %d proteins, in %d genera\n",
              nrow(res), min_n, n_distinct(res$genus)))
  ## Everything is printed, not a p-filtered slice. The first version showed
  ## only sign_p < 0.2, which is the subset most likely to be noise and reads
  ## as though it were the result.
  print(res |> arrange(cohort, genus, desc(pct_NRup)) |> as.data.frame())
  cat(sprintf("\nsurviving BH across the %d rows: %d\n", nrow(res),
              sum(res$sign_q < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat("\nREADING. The claim is PARTITION, not significance: species of the same\n",
      "genus pointing opposite ways is the result, and with a handful of\n",
      "proteins each almost none will clear the correction. Report the counts\n",
      "and say so. Two further limits belong in the legend: proteins within a\n",
      "species are not independent -- shared peptides and operon structure make\n",
      "the sign test anticonservative -- and species with more proteins are the\n",
      "better-detected ones, so coverage and abundance are confounded with\n",
      "which species can appear here at all.\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(out_dir)) {
    od <- file.path(out_dir, "B38_species_direction")
    dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    saveRDS(res, file.path(od, "species_direction.rds"))
    cat("saved -> ", file.path(od, "species_direction.rds"), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(res)
}

cat("B38 loaded. With v17's figure inputs in the session:\n\n",
    "  source('B38_species_direction.R')\n",
    "  sp <- b38(lca_all2, OP, stat_pitt, chap_new,\n",
    "            OS = OS, stat_sheba = st_s, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "lca_all2  the completed Unipept cache (v17 section 5c; both cohorts)\n",
    "stat_pitt the protein-level statistic; st_s is Sheba's\n",
    "chap_new  the chaperone protein set, used to anchor the sign\n\n",
    "If the cache has no species_name column, pep_species() says so -- the\n",
    "LCA would then have been fetched at a coarser rank and needs re-running.\n",
    "If the sign convention is inverted, check_sign() stops and tells you.\n",
    sep = "")
```

## B39 — unipept species

add the species rank to the frozen taxonomy, and prove it is the same

Source: `B39_unipept_species.R`

```{r B39_unipept_species, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B39 — add the species rank to the frozen taxonomy, and prove it is the same
##       taxonomy
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS IS A RE-QUERY AND NOT NEW ANNOTATION. v17's Unipept call already
## asks for the full lineage -- `extra = true`, `names = true` -- so every
## response carried species_name. The line that built the cache was
##
##     select(seq = peptide, taxon_rank, genus_name, family_name, phylum_name)
##
## and species was dropped there. Nothing was missed at the API; it was
## discarded on the way into the cache, and the frozen caches
## (unipept_lca.rds, unipept_lca_gained.rds, unipept_fill/) all inherit it.
##
## THE HAZARD, WHICH v17 STATES ITSELF: "a live query reflects today's Unipept
## database, not the one the analysis used." Unipept is rebuilt against
## UniProt releases, so a peptide's LCA can move between fetches. If the
## species layer comes from today's database while phylum, family and genus
## come from the frozen one, the figure would mix two taxonomies and nobody
## reading it would know.
##
## So this re-fetches EVERY rank, not just species, and checks the three
## frozen ranks reproduce. That check is the point of the file:
##
##   agreement high  -> the database has not moved for these peptides; take
##                      species from the new fetch and leave everything else
##                      frozen, because the frozen values are what the rest of
##                      the paper used.
##   agreement low   -> the database HAS moved. A species panel built on it
##                      would not be the taxonomy of Figure 3. Either re-freeze
##                      the whole taxonomy and re-run everything that depends
##                      on it, or drop the species panel. Do not take the
##                      species column alone.
##
## Cost: 35,077 peptides at 100 per request is about 350 POSTs against a public
## academic API. Run it once, save it, and never call it from a knit.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tibble); library(purrr)
})

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## pept2lca_full(): v17's call, with nothing thrown away
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Identical parameters to v17's pept2lca -- equate_il because mass spectrometry
## cannot tell isoleucine from leucine, extra and names for the lineage. The
## only change is that the result is kept whole.
pept2lca_full <- function(peps, batch = 100, pause = 0.1, verbose = TRUE) {
  peps <- unique(peps[nzchar(peps)])
  chunks <- split(peps, ceiling(seq_along(peps) / batch))
  if (verbose) cat(sprintf("pept2lca_full: %d peptides in %d requests\n",
                           length(peps), length(chunks)))
  i <- 0
  map_dfr(chunks, function(b) {
    i <<- i + 1
    if (verbose && i %% 25 == 0) cat(sprintf("  %d/%d\n", i, length(chunks)))
    body <- c(setNames(as.list(b), rep("input[]", length(b))),
              list(equate_il = "true", extra = "true", names = "true"))
    r <- try(httr::POST("https://api.unipept.ugent.be/api/v1/pept2lca.json",
                        body = body, encode = "form"), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(r, "try-error") || httr::status_code(r) != 200) {
      ## A dropped batch is 100 peptides silently missing from the result, which
      ## would look like unresolved peptides rather than a failed request.
      warning(sprintf("batch %d failed (%s)", i,
                      if (inherits(r, "try-error")) "no response"
                      else paste("HTTP", httr::status_code(r))), call. = FALSE)
      return(tibble(peptide = b, .failed = TRUE))
    }
    Sys.sleep(pause)
    as_tibble(httr::content(r, "parsed", simplifyVector = TRUE))
  })
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b39(): fetch, verify against the frozen cache, write only if it checks out
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
b39 <- function(lca_all2, out_dir = paths$out_dir, batch = 100,
                agree_min = 0.98, ranks = c("phylum_name", "genus_name",
                                            "family_name")) {
  stopifnot(all(c("peptide", "cohort", ranks) %in% names(lca_all2)))
  peps <- unique(lca_all2$peptide)
  new <- pept2lca_full(peps, batch = batch)
  if (".failed" %in% names(new)) {
    nf <- sum(new$.failed, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (nf) stop(sprintf(paste0("b39(): %d peptides are in failed batches.",
                                " Re-run -- a partial fetch would look like",
                                " unresolved peptides."), nf), call. = FALSE)
    new <- new |> select(-.failed)
  }
  if (!"species_name" %in% names(new))
    stop("b39(): the API response has no species_name. Columns returned: ",
         paste(names(new), collapse = ", "),
         "\n  Check that extra = 'true' and names = 'true' are being sent.",
         call. = FALSE)
  new <- new |>
    transmute(peptide, species_name = na_if(trimws(species_name), ""),
              across(all_of(ranks), ~ na_if(trimws(.x), ""))) |>
    distinct(peptide, .keep_all = TRUE)

  ## ---- the verification -----------------------------------------------
  cmp <- lca_all2 |> distinct(peptide, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(peptide, all_of(ranks)) |>
    inner_join(new, by = "peptide", suffix = c(".old", ".new"))
  cat(sprintf("\nverification: %d of %d frozen peptides returned by the API\n",
              nrow(cmp), length(peps)))
  ag <- vapply(ranks, function(r) {
    o <- cmp[[paste0(r, ".old")]]; n <- cmp[[paste0(r, ".new")]]
    k <- !is.na(o) & !is.na(n)
    if (!sum(k)) return(NA_real_)
    mean(o[k] == n[k])
  }, 0)
  for (r in ranks)
    cat(sprintf("  %-12s %.4f agreement on peptides resolved in both\n", r, ag[[r]]))
  worst <- min(ag, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(worst) || worst < agree_min)
    stop(sprintf(paste0("b39(): agreement %.4f is below %.2f -- the Unipept",
                        " database has moved since the\n  frozen cache was",
                        " built. A species layer from today's database is NOT",
                        " the\n  taxonomy the rest of the paper used. Either",
                        " re-freeze every rank and re-run\n  what depends on",
                        " it, or drop the species panel. Do not take species",
                        " alone."),
                 worst, agree_min), call. = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  -> agreement >= %.2f on every rank; the frozen taxonomy is reproduced,\n     so the species column can be added to it\n",
              agree_min))

  ## Species is ADDED to the frozen table; the frozen ranks are left exactly as
  ## they are, because those are the values every other figure used.
  out <- lca_all2 |>
    left_join(new |> select(peptide, species_name), by = "peptide")
  cat(sprintf("\nspecies resolved for %d of %d rows (%.1f%%); %d distinct species\n",
              sum(!is.na(out$species_name)), nrow(out),
              100 * mean(!is.na(out$species_name)),
              n_distinct(out$species_name, na.rm = TRUE)))
  od <- file.path(out_dir, "B39_unipept_species")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  f <- file.path(od, "lca_all3.rds")
  saveRDS(out, f)
  saveRDS(list(agreement = ag, n_compared = nrow(cmp), fetched = Sys.time()),
          file.path(od, "verification.rds"))
  cat("saved -> ", f, "\n  and the verification beside it\n", sep = "")
  invisible(out)
}

cat("B39 loaded. ONCE, in a session with network access:\n\n",
    "  source('B39_unipept_species.R')\n",
    "  lca_all3 <- b39(lca_all2, out_dir = paths$out_dir)   # ~350 requests\n\n",
    "Then B38 runs unchanged against it:\n\n",
    "  sp <- b38(lca_all3, OP, stat_pitt, chap_new,\n",
    "            OS = OS, stat_sheba = st_s, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "The species data was never missing from Unipept -- v17's call already sent\n",
    "extra = 'true', so every response carried species_name, and the select()\n",
    "that built the cache dropped it. This re-queries and keeps it.\n\n",
    "It re-fetches EVERY rank and refuses to write unless phylum, family and\n",
    "genus reproduce the frozen cache at >= 0.98. That is not a formality: a\n",
    "species layer from a moved database would not be the taxonomy of Figure 3,\n",
    "and the mixture would be invisible in the finished panel.\n", sep = "")
```

## B40 — table1

Table 1 (main), the cohort description

Source: `B40_table1.R`

```{r B40_table1, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B40 — Table 1 (main), the cohort description
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. figures_v2 builds p1c, a five-column tribble typed by hand
## -- cohort, n, R/NR, timing, acquisition, paired metagenomes -- and assembles
## it into nothing. Its own comment says why: "Its content is a Table 1, not a
## figure panel." This is that table, built from the metadata rather than typed,
## and it retires p1c from the orphan list.
##
## WHAT IT WILL NOT DO. The previous manuscript's version of this table carried
## six cells reading NEED TO COMPLETE. The failure mode to avoid is not an empty
## cell -- it is a cell quietly filled from the wrong column, or a variable
## dropped from the table because the data did not have it and nobody noticed.
## So every requested field is resolved explicitly against the metadata, and the
## ones that cannot be resolved are PRINTED AS MISSING with the names that were
## tried. An absent variable leaves the table and enters a list of what still
## has to be collected.
##
## The unit is the PATIENT, not the channel. A TMT channel is a measurement;
## age and sex belong to the person, and counting them per channel would weight
## patients by how often they were run.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tibble) })

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## read_meta(): 01_metagenomics' load_meta(), inlined
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## load_meta() is defined inside 01_metagenomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd and is not in
## the v17 figure session. Reproduced here rather than sourced, because sourcing
## that Rmd would run its whole pipeline. If the session DOES have load_meta,
## that one is used, so the two cannot drift.
##
## The PPI_H2RA cleanup is carried over deliberately: 01 found one value outside
## {0, 1} and set it to NA. Reading the file without that step would put a third
## level into the table and it would look like a real category.
read_meta <- function(path) {
  if (exists("load_meta", mode = "function")) {
    cat("read_meta: using the session's own load_meta()\n")
    return(b40_apply_patch(get("load_meta", mode = "function")(path), path))
  }
  ## A NULL path is the likely first error, not a missing file: `paths` in the
  ## v17 session does not carry the metadata entries 01_metagenomics defines,
  ## and file.exists(NULL) raises "invalid 'file' argument", which names
  ## neither the cause nor the fix.
  if (is.null(path) || !length(path) || !nzchar(path[1]) || is.na(path[1]))
    stop("read_meta(): the path is NULL or empty.\n",
         "  `paths` here has: ",
         if (exists("paths")) paste(names(paths), collapse = ", ") else "(no `paths` object)",
         "\n  The metadata entries are defined in 01_metagenomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd,",
         "\n  not in v17. Find the files and pass a path directly:\n",
         "    list.files(dirname(paths$out_dir), pattern = 'meta.*\\\\.tsv$',\n",
         "               recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!file.exists(path))
    stop("read_meta(): no file at ", path,
         "\n  In the v17 session `paths` may not carry the metadata entries that",
         "\n  01_metagenomics defines. Give the .tsv path directly.", call. = FALSE)
  m <- utils::read.table(path, sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
  if ("Response" %in% names(m))
    m$Response <- factor(m$Response, levels = c("Non_responder", "Responder"))
  if ("Cohort" %in% names(m)) m$Cohort <- factor(m$Cohort, levels = c("Sheba", "Pitt"))
  for (col in c("Response_RECIST", "Response_subtype_raw", "Source", "Time_point",
                "Pitts_subcohort", "Sequencing_Batch", "Sex", "Stage", "Histology",
                "PPI_H2RA", "Abx_3M_prior", "irAE", "Timepoint_discrete",
                "Treatment_regimen", "Sample_progression_timepoint"))
    if (col %in% names(m)) m[[col]] <- factor(m[[col]])
  for (col in c("Sample_days_pre", "Timepoint_days", "Line", "Age"))
    if (col %in% names(m)) m[[col]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m[[col]]))
  if ("PPI_H2RA" %in% names(m)) {
    v <- as.character(m$PPI_H2RA)
    bad <- !v %in% c("0", "1") & !is.na(v)
    if (any(bad)) cat(sprintf("  PPI_H2RA: %d value(s) outside {0,1} set to NA (as 01 does)\n",
                              sum(bad)))
    v[bad] <- NA; m$PPI_H2RA <- factor(v, levels = c("0", "1"))
  }
  m <- m[!is.na(m$Response), , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("read_meta: %d rows, %d columns from %s\n", nrow(m), ncol(m),
              basename(path)))
  b40_apply_patch(m, path)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b40_apply_patch(): clinical fields for patients the SDRF has and the
## metadata does not.
##
## WHY A SEPARATE FILE AND NOT AN EDIT TO metadata_pitt.tsv. That .tsv is the
## METAGENOMICS metadata, read by 01_metagenomics' load_meta() and joined to the
## abundance tables. MF0480 has a proteome and no metagenome (SDRF: Pitt_TMT3,
## analysed in primary analysis = yes, metagenome accession = not available), so
## a new row there would appear on the metagenome side as a sample with no
## profile. The patch is additive and read only by the scripts that build the
## clinical table and the deposited sample metadata.
##
## It is applied on BOTH paths out of read_meta, including the delegation to a
## live session's own load_meta(), because that branch returns early and would
## otherwise skip it silently -- the failure mode being a table that is correct
## when the script is sourced alone and wrong inside the analysis session.
## B41_supp_tables.R calls read_meta() too, so the deposited sample metadata
## picks the patch up without a change of its own.
##
## Columns absent from the patch come through as NA. Rows whose Patient is
## already in the metadata are ignored rather than overwriting it: this fills
## gaps, it does not revise curated values.
B40_PATCH_CANDIDATES <- c(
  "Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Pitt/pitt_clinical_patch.tsv",
  "pitt_clinical_patch.tsv")

b40_apply_patch <- function(m, path) {
  if (!is.data.frame(m) || !"Patient" %in% names(m)) return(m)
  ## PITTSBURGH ONLY. Until 12 Oct 2026 this ran on whatever it was given,
  ## and the candidate list falls back to a working-directory-relative path
  ## -- so read_meta() on metadata_sheba.tsv found the PITT patch and added
  ## MF0480, a Pittsburgh patient, to the Sheba cohort. Sheba went 36 rows
  ## to 37 and said so in one line that looks like success. B41 calls
  ## read_meta() too, so the deposited sample metadata carried it as well.
  ## The gate is on the metadata, not the filename, because the filename is
  ## the caller's choice: a frame whose Cohort column says Sheba is not the
  ## frame this patch describes.
  is_pitt <- if ("Cohort" %in% names(m))
               all(as.character(m$Cohort) %in% c("Pitt", NA))
             else grepl("pitt", basename(path), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (!is_pitt) {
    cat("  clinical patch: not applied (this is not the Pittsburgh metadata)\n")
    return(m)
  }
  cand <- c(file.path(dirname(path), "pitt_clinical_patch.tsv"),
            if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir))
              file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), B40_PATCH_CANDIDATES),
            B40_PATCH_CANDIDATES)
  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (!length(hit)) return(m)
  pp <- utils::read.table(hit[1], sep = "\t", header = TRUE, comment.char = "#",
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
  pp <- pp[!pp$Patient %in% as.character(m$Patient), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(pp)) { cat("  clinical patch: nothing to add\n"); return(m) }
  ## one frame, the metadata's columns, the metadata's factor levels
  add <- m[rep(NA_integer_, nrow(pp)), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(add) <- NULL
  for (col in intersect(names(pp), names(m))) {
    v <- pp[[col]]
    add[[col]] <- if (is.factor(m[[col]])) {
      lv <- union(levels(m[[col]]), setdiff(unique(as.character(v)), NA))
      factor(as.character(v), levels = lv)
    } else if (is.numeric(m[[col]])) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v)) else as.character(v)
  }
  ## widening a factor on the patch side must widen it on the metadata side too,
  ## or rbind() silently turns the added level into NA
  for (col in intersect(names(pp), names(m)))
    if (is.factor(m[[col]]) && !identical(levels(m[[col]]), levels(add[[col]])))
      m[[col]] <- factor(as.character(m[[col]]), levels = levels(add[[col]]))
  out <- rbind(m, add)
  cat(sprintf("  clinical patch: +%d patient(s) from %s (%s)\n", nrow(pp),
              basename(hit[1]), paste(pp$Patient, collapse = ", ")))
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b40_wilcox(): the two-sample Wilcoxon, computed here rather than dispatched
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## R CHANGED THE ANSWER BETWEEN 4.3 AND 4.6, which is why this exists.
##
## On 12 Oct 2026 a run gave 0.15 for Sheba's line of therapy where the same
## seven-against-twenty-one values give 0.0673548. The data was identical and
## so was the grouping: wilcox.test itself differed. R 4.3.3 refuses the exact
## test on tied data -- it warns "cannot compute exact p-value with ties" and
## falls back to the tie-corrected normal approximation. R 4.6.1 computes the
## exact conditional permutation test on the mid-ranks instead, and 0.15 is
## exactly twice the smaller one-sided tail of that distribution. Both are
## defensible; they are different tests, and on n = 7 against n = 21 with
## twenty-three tied values they differ by more than twofold.
##
## The manuscript reports the normal approximation, so that is what this
## computes, on any R version. exact_ties = TRUE gives R 4.6's answer; under
## R >= 4.6 that is also what a bare wilcox.test() returns, so a reader running
## the deposited code on a current R WILL see different numbers unless the
## Methods say which convention was used. Table 1's note says it.
##
## Written out here rather than dispatched: the algorithm is R's own, in base
## arithmetic with every name qualified, so no change to the search path, the
## S3 table or the stats namespace can move these numbers again.
b40_wilcox <- function(a, b, exact_ties = FALSE) {
  a <- a[is.finite(a)]; b <- b[is.finite(b)]
  n1 <- length(a); n2 <- length(b)
  if (n1 < 1L || n2 < 1L) return(NA_real_)
  r <- base::rank(c(a, b))
  W <- sum(r[seq_len(n1)]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2
  nt <- base::table(c(a, b))
  TIES <- any(nt > 1L)
  if (TIES && isTRUE(exact_ties)) {
    ## R >= 4.6: the exact conditional permutation test on the observed
    ## mid-ranks, two-sided as twice the smaller tail. Enumerated directly;
    ## refuses rather than approximating when the enumeration is too large.
    N <- n1 + n2
    ## Enumeration is only feasible for the small Sheba rows. Pittsburgh's
    ## 29-against-24 is 10^14 splits; R does it with a network algorithm this
    ## does not reimplement. In exact_ties mode we are asking for R >= 4.6's
    ## convention anyway, so defer to it there -- and say so, because the
    ## answer then depends on the R version, which is the whole point.
    if (choose(N, n1) > 5e6) {
      cat("    [b40_wilcox: ", format(choose(N, n1), big.mark = ","),
          " splits is beyond enumeration; deferring to this R's wilcox.test,",
          "\n     which is this test only on R >= 4.6]\n", sep = "")
      return(suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(a, b)$p.value))
    }
    obs <- sum(r[seq_len(n1)])
    ss  <- colSums(matrix(r[utils::combn(N, n1)], nrow = n1))
    return(min(1, 2 * min(mean(ss >= obs - 1e-9), mean(ss <= obs + 1e-9))))
  }
  if (!TIES && n1 < 50L && n2 < 50L) {
    p <- 2 * min(stats::pwilcox(W, n1, n2),
                 stats::pwilcox(W - 1, n1, n2, lower.tail = FALSE))
    return(min(1, p))
  }
  N <- n1 + n2
  z <- W - n1 * n2 / 2
  sigma <- sqrt((n1 * n2 / 12) * ((N + 1) - sum(nt^3 - nt) / (N * (N - 1))))
  if (!is.finite(sigma) || sigma <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  z <- (z - sign(z) * 0.5) / sigma
  min(1, 2 * min(stats::pnorm(z), stats::pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE)))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b40_selftest(): is this session's arithmetic the arithmetic we think it is?
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ADDED 12 Oct 2026, after a run returned 0.15 for Sheba's line of therapy
## where the same seven-against-twenty-one values give 0.0674. The values were
## verified identical, the groups were verified identical, and a diagnostic
## that called wilcox.test on two HARDCODED vectors returned 0.15 in that
## session and 0.0674 in a clean one. The data was never the problem: the
## function was. Something in the session -- a package on the search path or an
## object in the global environment -- was answering to the name wilcox.test.
##
## Every statistical call in this file is now namespace-qualified, which makes
## the table immune to that. This check exists so that if it happens again to
## something else, the session says so at source time rather than putting a
## wrong number in a submitted table.
##
## The two references are fixed: Sheba's line of therapy as the roster holds it
## (0.0673548), and the histology table as Table 1 prints it (0.0332424159).
b40_selftest <- function(verbose = TRUE) {
  ok <- TRUE
  w <- b40_wilcox(c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3), c(rep(1, 19), 2, 4))
  f <- stats::fisher.test(matrix(c(16, 18, 5, 0, 2, 0), nrow = 3,
                                 byrow = TRUE))$p.value
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(w, 0.0673547740, tolerance = 1e-6))) {
    ok <- FALSE
    cat("\n  *** stats::wilcox.test returns", format(w), "where it should return",
        "0.0673548.\n      Every Wilcoxon row in this table is suspect.\n")
  }
  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(f, 0.0332424159, tolerance = 1e-7))) {
    ok <- FALSE
    cat("\n  *** stats::fisher.test returns", format(f), "where it should return",
        "0.0332424159.\n      Every categorical row in this table is suspect.\n")
  }
  ## the other two numeric rows, so all three are pinned
  for (ref in list(list("Sheba days", c(0,0,1,1,1,1,38),
                        c(rep(0,12), rep(1,7), 2, 15, 65, 73), 0.4564773),
                   list("Pittsburgh days",
                        c(-8,10,-4,5,-4,-4,-3,-67,-38,-28,4,-50,-2,-24,-26,-10,
                          -14,-3,-9,0,-49,-73,-29,-30,-30,-5,-67,-2,-6),
                        c(-23,-24,-85,-90,-6,-58,-13,-12,-4,-5,-3,7,-54,-1,-6,27,
                          -6,-28,-5,-1,-49,-28,-4,-99), 0.7747451))) {
    got <- b40_wilcox(ref[[2]], ref[[3]])
    if (!isTRUE(all.equal(got, ref[[4]], tolerance = 1e-5))) {
      ok <- FALSE
      cat("\n  ***", ref[[1]], "reference: got", format(got), "expected",
          format(ref[[4]]), "\n")
    }
  }
  ## a masked METHOD is invisible to find(), so look for it directly
  meth <- c("wilcox.test.default", "fisher.test.default", "rank.default")
  meth <- meth[vapply(meth, function(nm)
    exists(nm, envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE), logical(1))]
  if (length(meth))
    cat("\n  note: ", paste(meth, collapse = ", "), " defined in the global",
        " environment.\n        UseMethod dispatches to it from any caller;",
        " this file no longer\n        depends on dispatch, but other scripts",
        " in this session will.\n", sep = "")
  masked <- Filter(function(nm) length(find(nm)) > 1,
                   c("wilcox.test", "fisher.test", "rank", "median", "table"))
  if (length(masked))
    cat("\n  note: these names resolve in more than one place --",
        paste(masked, collapse = ", "),
        "\n        this file calls stats:: explicitly, so the table is unaffected.\n")
  if (ok && verbose) cat("b40 self-test: wilcox and fisher agree with their references.\n")
  invisible(ok)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## the specification: what the table should contain, and where to look
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## `kind` is "cat" (counts and percentages) or "num" (median and range).
## `cols` lists candidate column names in order of preference -- the metadata
## for the two cohorts was harmonised but not perfectly, so a field may be
## spelled differently in each.
TABLE1_SPEC <- tribble(
  ~field,                  ~kind,  ~cols,
  "Age",                   "num",  c("Age", "age", "Age_at_start", "age_years"),
  "Sex",                   "cat",  c("Sex", "sex", "Gender"),
  "Stage",                 "cat",  c("Stage", "stage", "AJCC_stage"),
  "Histology",             "cat",  c("Histology", "histology"),
  "Treatment regimen",     "cat",  c("Treatment_regimen", "rx", "Regimen"),
  "Line of therapy",       "num",  c("Line", "line", "Line_of_therapy"),
  "Days from sample to treatment", "num",
                                   c("Sample_days_pre", "days_before", "tp_days"),
  "PPI or H2RA",           "cat",  c("PPI_H2RA", "PPI", "ppi_h2ra"),
  "Antibiotics within 3 months", "cat",
                                   c("Abx_3M_prior", "Abx_3M", "abx_3m_prior"),
  "Immune-related adverse event", "cat", c("irAE", "irae"),
  "Sequencing batch",      "cat",  c("Sequencing_Batch", "seq_batch"))
## The PRINTED Table 1 omits two of these rows -- antibiotics within three
## months, which is 100% "No" in both arms, and sequencing batch, a technical
## covariate the Methods already describe run by run. Both are kept here, so
## table1.csv stays the complete record and the deposit is not a subset of
## the paper. Table 1's note states that neither is given a row.
## Subcohort was removed: Pitts_subcohort and Treatment_regimen are the same
## variable (Adv_PD1_mel = anti-PD1 14/14, Adv_PD1_CTLA4_mel =
## anti-PD1+anti-CTLA4 38/38), so the table printed one row twice. Table 1
## had it struck by hand; it is struck here as well, or a re-run puts it
## back.
##
## Line of therapy stays in the spec, because the SHEBA metadata supplies it and
## Table 1 reports it there. metadata_pitt.tsv's `Line` is NA for
## all 72 patients, so on the PITTSBURGH side the row used to print as
## "median (range) | - | - | -" with every patient missing. That is fixed in
## .summ() below, which now drops a numeric field from a cohort's block when
## nothing in it is finite, the way the categorical branch already dropped a
## field with no levels. Removing the row from this spec instead would have
## taken Sheba's line with it. Lior_UPF_data.csv cannot fill the Pittsburgh
## side: only 3 of the 55 carry an explicit nL prefix in the free-text Rx.

.resolve <- function(df, cols) { h <- intersect(cols, names(df)); if (length(h)) h[1] else NA_character_ }

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B40_LEVELS: the raw metadata values, as the table prints them
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ADDED 12 Oct 2026. The metadata carries free text -- "MELANOMA (CONJUNCTIVAL)",
## "anti-PD1+anti-CTLA4", PPI as 0/1, the first batch as "August2024" -- and
## Table 1 prints none of those strings. Until now the relabelling was done BY
## HAND after the run, which is why re-running the script produced a table that
## did not match the paper and why nobody could tell the relabelling apart from
## an error. It is here now, so the script is the table's source.
##
## THE ORDER OF EACH VECTOR IS THE DISPLAY ORDER. .summ() otherwise sorts levels
## alphabetically, which puts Mucosal before "Uveal or conjunctival" and GTSH10
## before GTSH15 -- neither is the order the table uses.
##
## A value NOT in a map is kept verbatim and reported. A silent drop here would
## be indistinguishable from a patient who does not have the condition.
B40_LEVELS <- list(
  "Sex"                           = c("F" = "Female", "M" = "Male"),
  "Histology"                     = c("MELANOMA"                = "Cutaneous",
                                      "CHOROIDAL MELANOMA"      = "Uveal or conjunctival",
                                      "MELANOMA (CONJUNCTIVAL)" = "Uveal or conjunctival",
                                      "MUCOSAL MELANOMA"        = "Mucosal"),
  "Treatment regimen"             = c("anti-PD1"            = "Anti-PD-1",
                                      "anti-PD1+anti-CTLA4" = "Anti-PD-1 + anti-CTLA-4"),
  "PPI or H2RA"                   = c("0" = "No", "1" = "Yes"),
  "Antibiotics within 3 months"   = c("0" = "No", "1" = "Yes"),
  "Immune-related adverse event"  = c("0" = "No", "1" = "Yes"),
  ## August2024 is GTSH15. The two agree cell for cell on the full metadata --
  ## 12 patients, 6 non-responders and 6 responders -- and GTSH15 is the name
  ## the sequencing deposit and the rest of the manuscript use.
  "Sequencing batch"              = c("August2024" = "GTSH15",
                                      "GTSH10"     = "GTSH10",
                                      "GTSH14"     = "GTSH14"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b40_analysis_set() / b40_sheba_from_samples(): the roster, and Sheba's source
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ADDED 12 Oct 2026, after a plain run produced a table for 73 Pittsburgh and
## 36 Sheba patients instead of the paper's 53 and 35.
##
## TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, and only one of them is a restriction.
##
## PITTSBURGH is a restriction and nothing more. metadata_pitt.tsv carries 72
## patients, pitt_clinical_patch.tsv adds MF0480, and 53 of those 73 are in the
## analysed roster. Restricting to the roster reproduces the paper exactly:
## 29 non-responders and 24 responders, 12 without sex, stage, histology,
## antibiotics or adverse events, 13 without acid suppression, none without
## regimen or batch, and histology 16/18 cutaneous, 5/0 uveal or conjunctival,
## 2/0 mucosal.
##
## SHEBA IS A DIFFERENT SOURCE. metadata_sheba.tsv keys patients as p104, p11,
## p115; the roster keys them as 104, 11, 115. After dropping the leading "p"
## only 27 of the 35 analysed patients are in that file at all -- 122A, 154,
## 177, 745, 87A, 92, 94A and 98 are absent, four of them the failed metagenome
## libraries. The paper's Sheba block therefore cannot come from that file, and
## it does not: every Sheba number in Table 1 -- regimen 2/14 and 5/9 with 5 not
## recorded, line of therapy 1 (1-3) and 1 (1-4) with 7 not recorded, days +1
## (0 to +38) and 0 (0 to +73) with 5 not recorded -- is reproduced cell for
## cell by the clinical columns of the DEPOSITED SAMPLE METADATA, which carries
## regimen for 30 of the 35 where metadata_sheba.tsv carries it for 27.
##
## So B41 must run before B40: sample_table() writes the roster this reads.
## Which Wilcoxon convention the table reports. FALSE is the normal
## approximation, which is what Table 1 prints and what its note names.
## TRUE is R >= 4.6's exact test on tied data. Changing it changes three
## printed p-values, so change the note in the same edit.
B40_EXACT_TIES <- FALSE

B40_SAMPLE_META <- "B41_supp_tables/supp_data_sample_metadata.csv"

b40_samples <- function(path = NULL, out_dir = NULL) {
  cand <- c(path,
            if (!is.null(out_dir)) file.path(out_dir, B40_SAMPLE_META),
            if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir))
              file.path(paths$out_dir, B40_SAMPLE_META),
            B40_SAMPLE_META)
  hit <- cand[!is.na(cand) & nzchar(cand)]
  hit <- hit[file.exists(hit)]
  if (!length(hit))
    stop("b40_samples(): no deposited sample metadata found. Run B41's\n",
         "  sample_table() first -- it writes ", B40_SAMPLE_META, ", which is\n",
         "  the roster of what was actually measured. Tried:\n    ",
         paste(cand, collapse = "\n    "), call. = FALSE)
  m <- utils::read.csv(hit[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("NA", ""))
  cat("b40_samples: ", nrow(m), " rows from ", basename(hit[1]), "\n", sep = "")
  tf <- function(v) !is.na(v) & (v %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE", "T", "1"))
  m[tf(m$analysed) & !tf(m$reference_channel) & !tf(m$excluded) &
      !is.na(m$patient), , drop = FALSE]
}

## The analysed patients of one cohort, for b40()'s `keep` arguments.
b40_analysis_set <- function(cohort = c("pitt", "sheba"), path = NULL, out_dir = NULL) {
  cohort <- match.arg(cohort)
  m <- b40_samples(path, out_dir)
  pat <- unique(m$patient[grepl(if (cohort == "pitt") "^Pitt" else "^Sheba", m$cohort)])
  cat(sprintf("  %s analysis set: %d patients\n", cohort, length(pat)))
  sort(pat)
}

## Sheba as a per-patient frame, in the shape b40() expects. One row per
## patient: the clinical fields are patient-level, so a patient measured in two
## channels must not be counted twice.
b40_sheba_from_samples <- function(path = NULL, out_dir = NULL) {
  m <- b40_samples(path, out_dir)
  m <- m[grepl("^Sheba", m$cohort), , drop = FALSE]
  m <- m[!duplicated(m$patient), , drop = FALSE]
  d <- data.frame(
    Patient          = as.character(m$patient),
    Response         = factor(ifelse(m$response == "NR", "Non_responder",
                              ifelse(m$response == "R",  "Responder", NA)),
                              levels = c("Non_responder", "Responder")),
    Cohort           = factor("Sheba", levels = c("Sheba", "Pitt")),
    Treatment_regimen = factor(m$Treatment_regimen),
    Line              = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$Line)),
    Sample_days_pre   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(m$Sample_days_pre)),
    stringsAsFactors  = FALSE)
  d <- d[!is.na(d$Response), , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("b40_sheba_from_samples: %d patients (%s)\n", nrow(d),
              paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(table(d$Response)), table(d$Response)),
                    collapse = ", ")))
  d
}

b40_recode <- function(x, field, cohort_lbl) {
  map <- B40_LEVELS[[field]]
  if (is.null(map)) return(x)
  v  <- as.character(x)
  hit <- !is.na(v) & v %in% names(map)
  unk <- sort(unique(v[!is.na(v) & !hit]))
  if (length(unk))
    cat(sprintf("  [%s] %s: %d value(s) not in B40_LEVELS, kept verbatim: %s\n",
                cohort_lbl, field, sum(!is.na(v) & !hit), paste(unk, collapse = ", ")))
  v[hit] <- unname(map[v[hit]])
  lv <- unique(c(unname(map), unk))
  factor(v, levels = lv[lv %in% v])
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## summarise one field, within one cohort, split by response
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.summ <- function(d, col, kind, group) {
  g <- droplevels(factor(d[[group]]))
  x <- d[[col]]
  if (kind == "num") {
    x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
    ## Nothing recorded in this cohort -> no row, mirroring the categorical
    ## branch's `if (!length(lvls)) return(NULL)`. Without this a field that
    ## only one cohort carries printed in both, as "median (range)" with an em
    ## dash in every column and the whole cohort in `Not recorded` -- which is
    ## how Pittsburgh's line of therapy reached Table 1.
    if (!any(is.finite(x))) return(NULL)
    ## ONE SET OF VECTORS FOR BOTH THE SUMMARY AND THE TEST.
    ## This used to format the medians from x[g == l & is.finite(x)] and then
    ## test with wilcox.test(x ~ g), which is a formula evaluated through
    ## model.frame in another frame. On 12 Oct a run printed medians that were
    ## right beside p-values that were not: Sheba line of therapy came out at
    ## 0.150 where the same 7-against-21 split gives 0.0674, and Pittsburgh days
    ## at 0.773 where those 29 and 24 values give 0.7747. A displayed summary
    ## and a p-value that can disagree is a defect whatever the cause, so the
    ## two now read the same objects and the formula interface is gone.
    grp <- lapply(levels(g), function(l) x[g == l & is.finite(x)])
    fmt <- function(v) if (!length(v)) "—" else
      sprintf("%.0f (%.0f–%.0f)", stats::median(v), min(v), max(v))
    lv  <- lapply(grp, fmt)
    tot <- fmt(x[is.finite(x)])
    p <- tryCatch(
      if (length(grp) == 2 && sum(lengths(grp)) >= 8)
        b40_wilcox(grp[[1]], grp[[2]], exact_ties = B40_EXACT_TIES) else NA_real_,
      error = function(e) NA_real_)
    ## The n behind every numeric p, printed, because the summary alone cannot
    ## show whether the test saw the same patients.
    if (!is.na(p))
      cat(sprintf("    %-30s Wilcoxon on %d vs %d, p = %.4f  (%s)\n", col,
                  length(grp[[1]]), length(grp[[2]]), p,
                  if (isTRUE(B40_EXACT_TIES)) "exact, R >= 4.6" else
                    "normal approximation, as the manuscript reports"))
    tibble(level = "median (range)", !!!setNames(lv, levels(g)), Total = tot,
           n_missing = sum(!is.finite(x)), p = p)
  } else {
    ## A factor arriving here has already been through b40_recode(), whose
    ## level order IS the table's order. sort() would undo that.
    keep_order <- is.factor(x)
    lv0 <- if (keep_order) levels(x) else NULL
    x <- as.character(x); x[is.na(x) | !nzchar(trimws(x))] <- NA
    lvls <- if (keep_order) lv0[lv0 %in% x] else sort(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
    if (!length(lvls)) return(NULL)
    tb <- table(factor(x, levels = lvls), g)
    ## EXACT, NOT MONTE CARLO. This was `simulate.p.value = nrow(tb) > 2`,
    ## so every variable with more than two levels got a resampled p and
    ## the table changed on every run: over 200 reruns the histology row
    ## came back anywhere in 0.024-0.045. A 41-patient table with at most
    ## four levels is well inside what fisher.test enumerates exactly, so
    ## there is nothing to buy with simulation and a reproducible number
    ## to lose. workspace is raised for the one table that needs it;
    ## if a future variable ever exhausts even that, the fallback
    ## simulates with a FIXED seed rather than silently varying.
    p <- tryCatch(
      if (nrow(tb) >= 2 && ncol(tb) == 2 && sum(tb) >= 8)
        suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
          stats::fisher.test(tb, workspace = 2e7)$p.value,
          error = function(e) {
            ## SAY SO. A silent fallback would put a simulated number back
            ## into the table, which is the defect this block exists to
            ## remove. If this ever prints, the printed p is NOT exact.
            cat(sprintf(
              "  [exact Fisher exhausted its workspace on a %dx%d table; falling back to a SEEDED simulation]\n",
              nrow(tb), ncol(tb)))
            set.seed(1L)
            stats::fisher.test(tb, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e6)$p.value
          }))
      else NA_real_, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    cells <- lapply(levels(g), function(l) {
      n <- tb[, l]; sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, 100 * n / max(sum(n), 1)) })
    tibble(level = lvls, !!!setNames(cells, levels(g)),
           Total = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", rowSums(tb),
                           100 * rowSums(tb) / max(sum(tb), 1)),
           n_missing = sum(is.na(x)),
           p = c(p, rep(NA_real_, length(lvls) - 1)))
  }
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b40(): one cohort's block, and the coverage report
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## `meta` is a per-PATIENT table. Pass the metadata load_meta() returns, which
## is per sample, and give `patient_col` so it can be reduced.
## `keep` restricts to the patients actually analysed, matched on `key_col`.
## IT IS NOT OPTIONAL IN PRACTICE. The metadata TSVs are the METAGENOMICS
## cohorts -- 72 Pittsburgh rows against the 55 stool samples the Methods
## describe -- so a table built from them unrestricted describes a superset and
## matches no number in the paper. A Table 1 whose n disagrees with the Methods
## is worse than no Table 1.
b40_cohort <- function(meta, cohort_lbl, patient_col = "Patient",
                       resp_col = "Response", spec = TABLE1_SPEC,
                       keep = NULL, key_col = patient_col) {
  if (!resp_col %in% names(meta))
    stop(sprintf("b40_cohort(): no `%s` column in the %s metadata; it has %s",
                 resp_col, cohort_lbl, paste(names(meta), collapse = ", ")),
         call. = FALSE)
  d <- if (patient_col %in% names(meta))
    meta |> filter(!is.na(.data[[patient_col]])) |>
      distinct(.data[[patient_col]], .keep_all = TRUE)
  else { cat(sprintf("  [%s] no `%s` column -- rows are taken as patients\n",
                     cohort_lbl, patient_col)); meta }
  d <- d |> filter(!is.na(.data[[resp_col]]))
  if (!is.null(keep)) {
    if (!key_col %in% names(d))
      stop(sprintf("b40_cohort(): no `%s` column to restrict on; the metadata has %s",
                   key_col, paste(names(d), collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
    hit <- as.character(d[[key_col]]) %in% as.character(keep)
    cat(sprintf("  [%s] restricting on `%s`: %d of %d metadata rows matched, %d of %d requested identifiers found\n",
                cohort_lbl, key_col, sum(hit), nrow(d),
                length(intersect(as.character(keep), as.character(d[[key_col]]))),
                length(unique(keep))))
    if (sum(hit) == 0)
      stop("b40_cohort(): nothing matched. The identifier vocabularies differ --\n",
           "  metadata e.g. ", paste(head(unique(d[[key_col]]), 2), collapse = ", "),
           "\n  requested e.g. ", paste(head(unique(keep), 2), collapse = ", "),
           call. = FALSE)
    d <- d[hit, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  cat(sprintf("\n[%s] %d patients (%s)\n", cohort_lbl, nrow(d),
              paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(table(d[[resp_col]])),
                            table(d[[resp_col]])), collapse = ", ")))

  rows <- list(); missing <- character()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
    f <- spec$field[i]; col <- .resolve(d, spec$cols[[i]])
    if (is.na(col)) { missing <- c(missing, f); next }
    if (spec$kind[i] == "cat") d[[col]] <- b40_recode(d[[col]], f, cohort_lbl)
    ## SAMPLING TIME IN EACH COHORT'S OWN DIRECTION. `Sample_days_pre` is signed
    ## positive-before-first-dose for both cohorts, and one signed variable
    ## serving two cohorts that are sampled from opposite ends needed a footnote
    ## to explain it -- and still left Table 1 and Figure 1c reading in opposite
    ## directions, which is a reviewer comment whatever the footnote says. Each
    ## cohort now carries the quantity its own design is built on: the
    ## on-treatment cohort as days ON treatment (the negation, so Figure 1c and
    ## this row agree), the pre-treatment cohort as days BEFORE the first dose,
    ## which is what the stored values already are. The Wilcoxon is rank-based
    ## and two-sided, so negation leaves every p unchanged -- asserted below
    ## rather than assumed.
    if (identical(f, "Days from sample to treatment")) {
      if (grepl("on treatment", cohort_lbl, fixed = TRUE)) {
        .pre <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d[[col]]))
        d[[col]] <- -.pre
        f <- "Days on treatment at collection"
      } else {
        f <- "Days before first dose"
      }
    }
    s <- .summ(d, col, spec$kind[i], resp_col)
    if (is.null(s)) { missing <- c(missing, paste0(f, " (column `", col,
                                                   "` present but empty)")); next }
    rows[[f]] <- s |> mutate(field = f, source_column = col, .before = 1)
  }
  if (length(missing)) {
    cat("  NOT IN THE METADATA -- these stay out of the table and have to be\n")
    cat("  collected before submission:\n")
    for (m in missing) cat("    - ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  out <- bind_rows(rows)
  if (nrow(out)) out$cohort <- cohort_lbl
  attr(out, "missing") <- missing
  attr(out, "n") <- nrow(d)
  out
}

b40 <- function(meta_pitt, meta_sheba = NULL, out_dir = NULL,
                keep_pitt = NULL, keep_sheba = NULL, key_col = "Patient",
                labels = c(pitt = "Pittsburgh (on treatment)",
                           sheba = "Sheba (before treatment)")) {
  ## THE METADATA IS A SUPERSET OF THE ANALYSIS SET, and running without
  ## `keep` builds a table for a different population than the paper's.
  ## metadata_pitt.tsv carries 72 patients; the study analyses 53. On the
  ## full set histology even changes direction -- there are non-cutaneous
  ## RESPONDERS among the patients the study does not analyse, and the
  ## Results sentence "all seven were non-responders" is a statement about
  ## the 41 analysed patients with recorded histology, not about the
  ## metadata file. Pass the analysis set or know that you did not.
  if (is.null(keep_pitt) && is.null(keep_sheba))
    cat("\n  NOTE: no `keep` given, so this is EVERY patient in the metadata,\n",
        "  not the analysis set. The table in the manuscript is the analysis\n",
        "  set: pass keep_pitt = <patient ids> and keep_sheba = <patient ids>.\n\n",
        sep = "")
  a <- b40_cohort(meta_pitt, labels[["pitt"]], keep = keep_pitt, key_col = key_col)
  b <- if (!is.null(meta_sheba))
    b40_cohort(meta_sheba, labels[["sheba"]], keep = keep_sheba, key_col = key_col)
    else NULL
  tab <- bind_rows(a, b)
  miss <- unique(c(attr(a, "missing"), if (!is.null(b)) attr(b, "missing")))

  cat("\n--- Table 1 ---\n")
  print(as.data.frame(tab |> select(cohort, field, level, everything(),
                                    -source_column)), row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("\n%d field(s) could not be filled from the metadata.%s\n",
              length(miss),
              if (length(miss)) " They are listed above, per cohort." else ""))
  cat("\nTESTS ARE DESCRIPTIVE. The p-values compare responders with\n",
      "non-responders within a cohort -- Wilcoxon for continuous fields,\n",
      "Fisher for categorical -- and are not corrected across the table.\n",
      "They are there to show where the arms are unbalanced, not to test\n",
      "hypotheses, and the legend should say so.\n", sep = "")

  if (!is.null(out_dir)) {
    od <- file.path(out_dir, "B40_table1"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE,
                                                       recursive = TRUE)
    utils::write.csv(tab, file.path(od, "table1.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    ## a markdown version, ready to drop into the Supplementary Information
    md <- c("| Cohort | Variable | Level | Non-responder | Responder | Total | Missing | P |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
      r <- tab[i, ]
      gcols <- setdiff(names(tab), c("cohort", "field", "level", "Total",
                                     "n_missing", "p", "source_column"))
      md <- c(md, sprintf("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %s |",
                          r$cohort, r$field, r$level,
                          as.character(r[[gcols[1]]]),
                          if (length(gcols) > 1) as.character(r[[gcols[2]]]) else "—",
                          r$Total, r$n_missing,
                          if (is.na(r$p)) "" else sprintf("%.3f", r$p)))
    }
    writeLines(md, file.path(od, "table1.md"))
    cat("saved -> ", file.path(od, "table1.csv"), " and table1.md\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(list(table = tab, missing = miss))
}

b40_selftest()

cat("B40 loaded.\n\n",
    "  source('B40_table1.R')\n",
    "  mp <- read_meta(paths$pitt_metadata)    # or the .tsv path directly\n",
    "  ms <- read_meta(paths$sheba_metadata)\n",
    "  t1 <- b40(mp, ms, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "Every field in TABLE1_SPEC is resolved against the metadata by name. A\n",
    "field that cannot be resolved is reported as missing with the names tried,\n",
    "and stays OUT of the table -- an absent variable must look absent, not\n",
    "arrive filled from a column that happened to match.\n\n",
    "The unit is the patient. Pass the per-sample metadata and it reduces on\n",
    "`Patient`; a TMT channel is a measurement, not a person.\n\n",
    "read_meta() reproduces 01_metagenomics' load_meta(), including its PPI_H2RA\n",
    "cleanup, so the table matches that pipeline. If `paths` in this session has\n",
    "no metadata entries -- they are defined in 01, not v17 -- pass the .tsv\n",
    "paths directly.\n", sep = "")
```

the three outstanding supplementary tables

```{r B41_supp_tables, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B41 — the three outstanding supplementary tables
## ============================================================================
##
## WHAT IS OUTSTANDING, and why each is here rather than already written.
##
##   Supplementary Table 1   the frozen KO membership lists. CITED BY NUMBER in
##                           Methods ("the full list is given in Supplementary
##                           Table 1"), so the citation dangles until this runs.
##                           RENUMBERED 12 Oct 2026 from Supplementary Table 2:
##                           the cohort description that was Supplementary
##                           Table 1 is now main Table 1, and this is the only
##                           table left in the Supplementary Information.
##   per-set scoring table   565-set survey scores. ALREADY WRITTEN by
##                           B1c_score.R as full_space_scored_<N>k.csv. This
##                           script LOCATES and VERIFIES it; it does not score
##                           anything. Promised by Data availability.
##   sample-level metadata   one row per measured sample. Promised by Data
##                           availability. B40's table is per PATIENT; this one
##                           is per sample, and the two are not the same object.
##
## THE ONE RULE: EXPORTED, NOT REBUILT. The claim Methods makes about the KO
## lists is that they were frozen before any analysis. A table regenerated from
## the current annotation would be a different object that happens to look the
## same, and would quietly launder a later edit into a pre-specification claim.
## So this reads CHAPERONE_KO and RIBO_KO out of the session and refuses if they
## are not there. It never reconstructs them from KEGG, from a category name, or
## from the prose in the manuscript.
##
## WHAT IT DOES WITH A DISAGREEMENT. Methods states 54 ribosomal and 19
## chaperone KOs. If the session's vectors are a different length, this does NOT
## adjust to match the prose -- it prints the real counts, writes them, and says
## the manuscript needs changing. The frozen object is the evidence; the
## sentence about it is not.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tibble) })

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## helpers
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Resolve a column by trying candidate names in order. Returns NA_character_
## rather than guessing, and the caller is expected to report the NA. This is
## the same discipline as B40: a field that cannot be resolved must look
## absent, never arrive filled from a column that happened to match.
.col <- function(d, cands) {
  if (is.null(d)) return(NA_character_)
  hit <- cands[cands %in% names(d)]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
}

.tried <- function(cands) paste(cands, collapse = ", ")

.mkdir <- function(out_dir, sub = "B41_supp_tables") {
  if (is.null(out_dir)) return(NULL)
  od <- file.path(out_dir, sub)
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  od
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## find_meta(): locate the metadata files instead of printing a command
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B40 hits this every session: `paths` in the v17 figure environment carries
## only out_dir, because the metadata entries are defined in 01_metagenomics,
## which v17 does not source. B40 printed a list.files() call for the human to
## run. That is a step a script can take itself.
##
## THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS HUNG, and the reason is worth keeping written
## down: it called list.files(recursive = TRUE) from the home directory. On an
## analysis machine that walks the sequencing trees, the null draw directories
## and every package library -- hundreds of thousands of files to find a table
## with about ninety rows. Recursive search needs a bound, and R's list.files
## has no depth argument, so the traversal is done here one level at a time.
##
## It does NOT auto-pick when the evidence is thin. Choosing the wrong metadata
## file is the file-level version of the failure B40 is built to avoid -- a
## table that looks complete and is populated from the wrong source. So a
## candidate is only returned as a cohort's metadata when it is the single best
## scorer for that cohort; otherwise every candidate is printed with its score
## and the caller picks.

## directories that cannot hold a metadata table and can hold a million files
.PRUNE <- paste0("^(\\.|renv$|packrat$|node_modules$|__pycache__$|site-packages$",
                 "|Library$|miniconda3?$|anaconda3?$|envs?$|R$|x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library$",
                 "|nulls?_|null_|draws?$|fastq|bam$|sam$|bowtie|kneaddata|humann|metaphlan",
                 "|raw$|RAW$|mzML$|\\.Trash)")

.walk <- function(roots, pat, depth = 3L, max_dirs = 1500L, verbose = TRUE) {
  dirs <- unique(roots); seen <- character(0); hits <- character(0)
  for (lvl in 0:depth) {
    if (!length(dirs)) break
    hits <- c(hits, unlist(lapply(dirs, function(d)
      tryCatch(list.files(d, pattern = pat, ignore.case = TRUE,
                          full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE),
               error = function(e) character(0)))))
    seen <- c(seen, dirs)
    if (lvl == depth) break
    nxt <- unlist(lapply(dirs, function(d)
      tryCatch(list.dirs(d, recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE),
               error = function(e) character(0))))
    nxt <- nxt[!grepl(.PRUNE, basename(nxt))]
    nxt <- setdiff(unique(nxt), seen)
    if (length(seen) + length(nxt) > max_dirs) {
      nxt <- utils::head(nxt, max(0L, max_dirs - length(seen)))
      if (verbose)
        cat("  stopped expanding at ", max_dirs, " directories; raise max_dirs",
            " or pass a\n  narrower root if the file is deeper than this.\n", sep = "")
      dirs <- nxt; next
    }
    dirs <- nxt
  }
  if (verbose) cat("  scanned ", length(seen), " directories, ", length(unique(hits)),
                   " candidate file(s)\n", sep = "")
  unique(hits)
}

## The canonical locations, from 01_metagenomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd's own `paths`
## list. Checked before any search: these ARE the files load_meta() reads, and
## a search that has to rank candidates can only ever rediscover them.
META_PATHS <- c(
  pitt  = "Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Pitt/metadata_pitt.tsv",
  sheba = "Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics/Sheba/metadata_sheba.tsv")

find_meta <- function(roots = NULL, pattern = "meta", depth = 3L,
                      max_dirs = 1500L, max_files = 60L) {

  ## --- the known paths first ----------------------------------------------
  bases <- unique(c(
    tryCatch(here::here(), error = function(e) NULL),
    if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir))
      c(dirname(paths$out_dir), dirname(dirname(paths$out_dir))),
    getwd(), dirname(getwd())))
  bases <- bases[!vapply(bases, is.null, logical(1))]
  for (b in bases) {
    hit <- vapply(META_PATHS, function(rel) {
      f <- file.path(b, rel); if (file.exists(f)) f else NA_character_ }, "")
    if (all(!is.na(hit))) {
      cat("find_meta: found both at the canonical paths under\n   ", b, "\n", sep = "")
      for (nm in names(hit)) cat("  ", nm, ": ", hit[[nm]], "\n", sep = "")
      return(invisible(as.list(hit)))
    }
  }
  cat("find_meta: not at the canonical paths; searching\n")

  roots <- unique(c(roots,
    if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir)) c(paths$out_dir,
                                                      dirname(paths$out_dir),
                                                      dirname(dirname(paths$out_dir))),
    getwd(), dirname(getwd())))
  ## ~ is deliberately NOT a default root. It is where the hang came from.
  roots <- roots[!is.na(roots) & nzchar(roots)]
  roots <- roots[dir.exists(roots)]
  if (!length(roots)) { cat("find_meta: none of the candidate roots exist\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  cat("find_meta: depth ", depth, " from\n", sep = ""); for (r in roots) cat("   ", r, "\n")
  f <- .walk(roots, paste0(pattern, ".*\\.(tsv|csv|txt)$"), depth, max_dirs)
  if (length(f) > max_files) {
    cat("  more than ", max_files, " candidates; keeping the first ", max_files, "\n", sep = "")
    f <- f[seq_len(max_files)]
  }
  if (!length(f)) {
    cat("  nothing matching /", pattern, ".*\\.(tsv|csv|txt)/ within depth ", depth, ".\n",
        "  Try find_meta(roots = '<the 01_metagenomics directory>') or a larger\n",
        "  depth. Tables 2 and the scored survey do not need this file.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  ## score each file on what the table actually needs
  peek <- function(path) {
    sz <- tryCatch(file.info(path)$size, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    h <- tryCatch(utils::read.delim(path, nrows = 5, check.names = FALSE,
                                    sep = if (grepl("\\.csv$", path, TRUE)) "," else "\t"),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(h) || !ncol(h)) return(NULL)
    n <- names(h)
    has <- function(cands) any(tolower(n) %in% tolower(cands))
    ## counting lines means reading the file; skip it on anything large rather
    ## than reading a multi-gigabyte table to print a row count
    nr <- if (!is.na(sz) && sz < 5e6)
            tryCatch(length(readLines(path, warn = FALSE)) - 1L,
                     error = function(e) NA_integer_) else NA_integer_
    tibble(path = path, rows = nr, cols = ncol(h),
           patient = has(c("Patient", "bio", "PatientID", "subject")),
           response = has(c("Response", "resp", "Responder")),
           pitt  = grepl("pitt", path, TRUE) || has(c("Sequencing_Batch", "Subcohort")),
           sheba = grepl("sheba", path, TRUE),
           score = patient + response + has(c("Treatment_regimen", "Regimen")) +
                   has(c("Stage", "Histology", "Sex")))
  }
  tab <- bind_rows(lapply(f, peek))
  if (is.null(tab) || !nrow(tab)) { cat("  no readable candidates\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  tab <- tab |> arrange(desc(score), desc(cols))
  cat("\n"); print(as.data.frame(tab[, c("score", "rows", "cols", "patient",
                                         "response", "path")]), row.names = FALSE)

  pick <- function(flag, other) {
    c0 <- tab[tab[[flag]] & !tab[[other]] & tab$patient & tab$score >= 2, ]
    if (!nrow(c0)) return(NA_character_)
    if (nrow(c0) > 1 && c0$score[1] == c0$score[2]) return(NA_character_)
    c0$path[1]
  }
  out <- list(pitt = pick("pitt", "sheba"), sheba = pick("sheba", "pitt"))
  cat("\nchosen:\n")
  for (nm in names(out))
    cat("  ", nm, ": ", if (is.na(out[[nm]])) "AMBIGUOUS -- pick one from the table above"
        else out[[nm]], "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(out)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ko_names(): KEGG's own symbol and description for a set of KO identifiers
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ANNOTATION IS NOT MEMBERSHIP. The thing that must not be rebuilt is WHICH
## KOs are in each list -- that is the frozen object and the pre-specification
## claim rests on it. What each KO is CALLED is a label, it is the same label
## today as when the list was frozen, and a table of 73 bare identifiers is
## close to unreadable. So symbols are fetched, membership never is.
##
## Source is https://rest.kegg.jp/list/ko, one line per orthology group:
##     K03686\tdnaJ; molecular chaperone DnaJ
## symbol is everything before the first semicolon, description everything
## after. Lines without a semicolon carry a description and no symbol.
##
## Cached next to the outputs, so a second run does not refetch, and failure is
## not fatal: no network means a table with identifiers and no symbols, which
## is what the first run produced anyway.
ko_names <- function(ko, cache_dir = NULL, url = "https://rest.kegg.jp/list/ko",
                     timeout = 60) {
  blank <- tibble(KO = ko, symbol = NA_character_, description = NA_character_)
  cf <- if (!is.null(cache_dir)) file.path(cache_dir, "kegg_ko_list.tsv") else NULL

  ln <- NULL
  if (!is.null(cf) && file.exists(cf)) {
    ln <- tryCatch(readLines(cf, warn = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (length(ln)) cat("  ko_names: using cached ", cf, " (", length(ln), " lines)\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!length(ln)) {
    cat("  ko_names: fetching ", url, " ...\n", sep = "")
    old <- options(timeout = timeout); on.exit(options(old), add = TRUE)
    ln <- tryCatch(readLines(url, warn = FALSE), error = function(e) {
      cat("  ko_names: fetch failed (", conditionMessage(e), ").\n",
          "    The table keeps its KO identifiers and no symbols. Re-run with\n",
          "    network, or pass a KEGG list file via cache_dir.\n", sep = "")
      NULL })
    if (!length(ln)) return(blank)
    cat("  ko_names: ", length(ln), " orthology groups\n", sep = "")
    if (!is.null(cf)) tryCatch(writeLines(ln, cf), error = function(e) NULL)
  }

  pr <- strsplit(ln, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
  k  <- sub("^ko:", "", vapply(pr, function(x) if (length(x)) x[1] else "", ""))
  rs <- vapply(pr, function(x) if (length(x) > 1L) x[2] else "", "")
  semi <- grepl(";", rs, fixed = TRUE)
  map <- tibble(KO = k,
                symbol = ifelse(semi, sub(";.*$", "", rs), NA_character_),
                description = ifelse(semi, sub("^[^;]*;[[:space:]]*", "", rs), rs))
  map <- map[nzchar(map$KO) & !duplicated(map$KO), , drop = FALSE]

  i <- match(ko, map$KO)
  out <- tibble(KO = ko, symbol = map$symbol[i], description = map$description[i])
  cat("  ko_names: matched ", sum(!is.na(i)), " of ", length(ko), " KOs",
      if (any(is.na(i))) paste0("; unmatched: ",
        paste(utils::head(ko[is.na(i)], 8), collapse = ", ")) else "", "\n", sep = "")
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## .norm_id(): the one normalisation that is safe to apply silently
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The Sheba patient appears as "p11" in the metadata and "11" in the design
## tables, and as "122A" against "122". Case, a leading "p" and leading zeros
## are formatting; they can be normalised without deciding anything.
##
## A TRAILING LETTER IS NOT. "122A" may be that id's A sample or a
## different patient, and only the person who named them knows. So it is
## applied as a SECOND pass, to ids that failed the first, and every id it
## resolves is printed. Silently folding it in would manufacture joins.
.norm_id <- function(x) {
  y <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  y <- sub("^p", "", y)
  sub("^0+", "", y)
}
.strip_suffix <- function(x) sub("([0-9])[a-z]$", "\\1", x)

## ===========================================================================
## 1. Supplementary Table 1 — the frozen KO membership lists
## ===========================================================================
## annot is used ONLY to annotate (symbol, how many proteins carried the KO).
## It never decides membership. Pass annot = NULL to get the bare lists.
ko_membership <- function(annot = if (exists("annot_new")) annot_new else NULL,
                          expect  = c(chaperone = 19L, ribosomal = 54L),
                          out_dir = NULL, kegg = TRUE) {

  miss <- c("CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO")[!vapply(c("CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO"),
                                               exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("ko_membership: ", paste(miss, collapse = " and "), " not in the ",
         "session.\n  These are the FROZEN lists and must come from the ",
         "analysis session that\n  used them -- do not rebuild them from KEGG ",
         "to make this table run.", call. = FALSE)

  chap <- unique(as.character(get("CHAPERONE_KO")))
  ribo <- unique(as.character(get("RIBO_KO")))
  chap <- chap[!is.na(chap) & nzchar(chap)]
  ribo <- ribo[!is.na(ribo) & nzchar(ribo)]

  cat(sprintf("ko_membership: chaperone %d, ribosomal %d\n",
              length(chap), length(ribo)))

  ## --- the counts the manuscript states -----------------------------------
  got <- c(chaperone = length(chap), ribosomal = length(ribo))
  bad <- names(expect)[got[names(expect)] != expect]
  if (length(bad)) {
    cat("\n  *** COUNT DISAGREEMENT WITH THE MANUSCRIPT ***\n")
    for (b in bad)
      cat(sprintf("      %s: session has %d, Methods says %d\n",
                  b, got[[b]], expect[[b]]))
    cat("      The session object is the evidence. Change the sentence, not\n",
        "      the list, and check that nothing was appended after freezing.\n",
        sep = "")
  }

  ## --- disjointness --------------------------------------------------------
  ## The chaperone result's decomposition rests on "removing ribosomal members
  ## leaves -2.18 on a DISJOINT set". If these two lists overlap, that sentence
  ## is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that flatters the result.
  ov <- intersect(chap, ribo)
  if (length(ov)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n  *** THE TWO LISTS OVERLAP in %d KO(s): %s\n",
                length(ov), paste(ov, collapse = ", ")))
    cat("      The disjointness claim in Results does not hold as written.\n")
  } else {
    cat("  lists are disjoint, as Results claims\n")
  }

  tab <- bind_rows(
    tibble(KO = chap, set = "Chaperones and folding catalysts"),
    tibble(KO = ribo, set = "Ribosomal proteins")
  ) |> arrange(set, KO)

  ## --- K04085, the member the manuscript singles out -----------------------
  ## Methods: "The nineteenth, K04085, is annotated as a tRNA
  ## 2-thiouridine-synthesizing sulfur transfer protein and is not a chaperone
  ## or a folding catalyst; we retain it because the list was frozen." The table
  ## has to say that too, or a reader checking the list finds an anomaly the
  ## paper appears not to have noticed.
  tab$note <- ""
  if ("K04085" %in% tab$KO)
    tab$note[tab$KO == "K04085"] <-
      "Retained from the frozen list; annotated as a tRNA 2-thiouridine-synthesizing sulfur transfer protein, not a chaperone or folding catalyst"
  else
    cat("\n  note: K04085 is NOT in the session's chaperone list, but Methods\n",
        "        discusses it as the nineteenth member. One of the two is\n",
        "        out of date.\n", sep = "")

  ## --- annotation: symbol, and detection in each cohort --------------------
  tab$symbol <- NA_character_
  tab$n_proteins_pitt <- NA_integer_
  tab$n_proteins_sheba <- NA_integer_

  if (is.null(annot)) {
    cat("\n  annot not supplied: the table carries KO identifiers only.\n")
  } else {
    kc <- .col(annot, c("ko_primary", "KO", "ko", "KEGG_ko"))
    pc <- .col(annot, c("protein", "Protein", "ProteinID", "query"))
    sc <- .col(annot, c("Preferred_name", "preferred_name", "symbol", "Symbol",
                        "gene_symbol", "Gene_Name", "name"))
    cc <- .col(annot, c("cohort", "Cohort"))
    if (is.na(kc) || is.na(pc)) {
      cat("\n  annot has no usable KO/protein columns (tried ",
          .tried(c("ko_primary", "KO", "ko", "KEGG_ko")), " and ",
          .tried(c("protein", "Protein", "ProteinID", "query")),
          ");\n  the table carries KO identifiers only.\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      a <- annot
      a$.ko <- as.character(a[[kc]]); a$.pid <- as.character(a[[pc]])
      a <- a[!is.na(a$.ko) & nzchar(a$.ko), , drop = FALSE]

      cnt <- function(which_cohort) {
        s <- if (!is.na(cc) && !is.null(which_cohort))
               a[grepl(which_cohort, a[[cc]], ignore.case = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
             else a
        if (!nrow(s)) return(setNames(integer(0), character(0)))
        s <- s[!duplicated(paste(s$.ko, s$.pid)), , drop = FALSE]
        table(s$.ko)
      }
      if (is.na(cc)) {
        cat("\n  annot has no cohort column (tried ",
            .tried(c("cohort", "Cohort")),
            "); protein counts are pooled\n  across whatever it contains.\n",
            sep = "")
        pooled <- cnt(NULL)
        tab$n_proteins_pitt <- as.integer(pooled[tab$KO]); tab$n_proteins_pitt[is.na(tab$n_proteins_pitt)] <- 0L
        names(tab)[names(tab) == "n_proteins_pitt"] <- "n_proteins"
        tab$n_proteins_sheba <- NULL
      } else {
        cp <- cnt("pitt"); cs <- cnt("sheba")
        tab$n_proteins_pitt  <- as.integer(cp[tab$KO]); tab$n_proteins_pitt[is.na(tab$n_proteins_pitt)]  <- 0L
        tab$n_proteins_sheba <- as.integer(cs[tab$KO]); tab$n_proteins_sheba[is.na(tab$n_proteins_sheba)] <- 0L
      }

      if (!is.na(sc)) {
        sy <- a[!is.na(a[[sc]]) & nzchar(a[[sc]]) & a[[sc]] != "-", , drop = FALSE]
        if (nrow(sy)) {
          m <- tapply(as.character(sy[[sc]]), sy$.ko,
                      function(v) paste(unique(v), collapse = "/"))
          tab$symbol <- unname(m[tab$KO])
        }
        cat(sprintf("\n  symbols resolved from annot$%s for %d of %d KOs\n",
                    sc, sum(!is.na(tab$symbol)), nrow(tab)))
      } else {
        cat("\n  annot has no symbol column (tried ",
            .tried(c("Preferred_name", "symbol", "Symbol", "gene_symbol")),
            ");\n  the table carries KO identifiers without gene symbols.\n",
            sep = "")
      }
    }
  }

  ## --- members that were never measured ------------------------------------
  ## A frozen list member detected in no sample is not an error, but it changes
  ## how the table reads: the set as TESTED is smaller than the set as DEFINED.
  ## --- symbols: KEGG fills whatever the session's annotation could not ------
  ## Membership is already fixed by this point. This only labels it.
  if (kegg && (all(is.na(tab$symbol)) || any(is.na(tab$symbol)))) {
    cd <- if (!is.null(out_dir)) .mkdir(out_dir) else NULL
    kn <- ko_names(tab$KO, cache_dir = cd)
    if (!all(is.na(kn$symbol))) {
      fill <- is.na(tab$symbol) & !is.na(kn$symbol)
      tab$symbol[fill] <- kn$symbol[fill]
      tab$description  <- kn$description
      cat("  symbols now present for ", sum(!is.na(tab$symbol)), " of ",
          nrow(tab), "\n", sep = "")
    }
  }

  ## Only meaningful once counts exist. With annot absent every count is NA,
  ## and rowSums(na.rm = TRUE) of all-NA is 0 -- which would report every
  ## member as undetected. A diagnostic that fires when there is no data is
  ## worse than no diagnostic.
  ccols <- intersect(c("n_proteins", "n_proteins_pitt", "n_proteins_sheba"),
                     names(tab))
  counted <- length(ccols) > 0 &&
             any(!is.na(unlist(tab[, ccols, drop = FALSE])))
  if (counted) {
```
