```{r B41_supp_tables, eval=FALSE}
    tot <- rowSums(as.data.frame(tab[, ccols, drop = FALSE]), na.rm = TRUE)
    nd  <- tab[tot == 0, , drop = FALSE]
    cat(sprintf("\n  %d of %d members carry no detected protein in either cohort%s\n",
                nrow(nd), nrow(tab),
                if (nrow(nd)) paste0(": ", paste(nd$KO, collapse = ", ")) else ""))
    if (nrow(nd))
      cat("  The set as DEFINED is larger than the set as TESTED. Say which\n",
          "  number the Results quote.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("\n  no protein counts available, so detection is not reported\n")
  }

  tab <- tab |> relocate(any_of(c("KO", "symbol", "description", "set")))

  if (!is.null(out_dir)) {
    od <- .mkdir(out_dir)
    ## CLEAR THE OLD NUMBERING. This file was supp_table2_* until 12 Oct.
    ## Writing the new name without removing the old one leaves both in the
    ## deposit directory, and a deposit assembled from it would ship two
    ## numbering schemes for the same table.
    stale <- list.files(od, "^supp_table2_ko_membership\\.(csv|md)$",
                        full.names = TRUE)
    if (length(stale)) {
      cat("  removing", length(stale), "file(s) under the old numbering:",
          paste(basename(stale), collapse = ", "), "\n")
      unlink(stale)
    }
    utils::write.csv(tab, file.path(od, "supp_table1_ko_membership.csv"),
                     row.names = FALSE)
    ## markdown, for splicing into the SI
    hdr <- names(tab)
    md <- c(paste0("| ", paste(hdr, collapse = " | "), " |"),
            paste0("|", paste(rep("---", length(hdr)), collapse = "|"), "|"))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
      r <- vapply(tab[i, ], function(x) {
             x <- as.character(x); if (is.na(x)) "" else x }, character(1))
      md <- c(md, paste0("| ", paste(r, collapse = " | "), " |"))
    }
    writeLines(md, file.path(od, "supp_table1_ko_membership.md"))
    cat("\n  saved -> supp_table1_ko_membership.{csv,md} in ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(tab)
}

## ===========================================================================
## 2. The per-set scoring table — located and verified, never recomputed
## ===========================================================================
## B1c_score.R already writes this. Rescoring it here would produce a second
## number for the same quantity with no way to tell which one the manuscript
## quotes, so this only finds the file, checks it, and formats it for deposit.
scored_survey <- function(dir = NULL, expect_sets = c(500L, 700L),
                          out_dir = NULL) {

  cand <- unique(c(dir,
                   if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir)) paths$out_dir,
                   "nulls_pitt_full", "."))
  cand <- cand[!is.na(cand) & nzchar(cand)]
  cand <- cand[dir.exists(cand)]
  ## bounded, for the same reason find_meta is: a nulls directory holds one
  ## RDS per draw -- ten thousand of them -- and the scored CSV sits at its
  ## top level, not buried in it.
  hits <- if (length(cand))
            .walk(cand, "^full_space_scored_.*\\.csv$", depth = 2L,
                  max_dirs = 400L, verbose = FALSE) else character(0)
  ## "/Users/.../x.csv" and "./final_run/x.csv" are one file, and reporting them
  ## as two invites a choice between identical things.
  hits <- unique(normalizePath(hits, mustWork = FALSE))

  if (!length(hits)) {
    cat("scored_survey: no full_space_scored_*.csv under\n  ",
        paste(cand, collapse = "\n  "), "\n\n", sep = "")
    cat("  It is written by B1c_score.R, which scores the draws produced by\n",
        "  B1c_10k.sh:\n\n",
        "      Rscript B1c_score.R <nulls_dir>\n\n",
        "  Pass dir = <that directory> once it exists. Nothing here recomputes\n",
        "  the scores: a second scoring run would give the manuscript two\n",
        "  numbers for one quantity.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (length(hits) > 1) {
    cat("scored_survey: more than one scored file; using the one with most draws\n")
    for (h in hits) cat("   ", h, "\n")
  }
  ## "10k" sorts before "1k" alphabetically, so pick on the parsed number
  ndraw <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub(".*_([0-9]+)k\\.csv$", "\\1", hits)))
  f <- hits[which.max(ifelse(is.na(ndraw), -1L, ndraw))]
  s <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("scored_survey: %d rows from %s\n", nrow(s), f))

  need <- c("pathway", "size", "NES", "p_set", "rank", "q_bh", "p_wy")
  gone <- setdiff(need, names(s))
  if (length(gone))
    stop("scored_survey: ", f, " lacks ", paste(gone, collapse = ", "),
         ".\n  Columns present: ", paste(names(s), collapse = ", "),
         call. = FALSE)

  if (nrow(s) < expect_sets[1] || nrow(s) > expect_sets[2])
    cat(sprintf("\n  *** %d sets, outside the expected %d-%d. This may be a\n",
                nrow(s), expect_sets[1], expect_sets[2]),
        "      scoring of the reported family rather than the full space.\n",
        sep = "")

  for (p in c("p_set", "q_bh", "p_wy")) {
    v <- s[[p]]
    if (any(v < 0 | v > 1, na.rm = TRUE))
      cat(sprintf("  *** %s has values outside [0, 1]\n", p))
  }

  ## layer prefix, as the set names carry it ("reported:", "kegg:", ...)
  s$layer <- ifelse(grepl(":", s$pathway), sub(":.*$", "", s$pathway), "(unprefixed)")
  s <- s[order(s$p_set, -abs(s$NES)), , drop = FALSE]
  s$rank_by_p <- seq_len(nrow(s))

  cat(sprintf("\n  sets at FWER < 0.05: %d;  BH q < 0.05: %d;  of %d\n",
              sum(s$p_wy < .05, na.rm = TRUE), sum(s$q_bh < .05, na.rm = TRUE),
              nrow(s)))
  cat("  (the manuscript reports zero on both; a non-zero count here means the\n",
      "   text and this file disagree)\n", sep = "")
  print(utils::head(s[, c("rank_by_p", "layer", "pathway", "size", "NES",
                          "p_set", "q_bh", "p_wy")], 8))

  if (!is.null(out_dir)) {
    od <- .mkdir(out_dir)
    utils::write.csv(s[, c("rank_by_p", "layer", "pathway", "size", "NES",
                           "p_set", "rank", "q_bh", "p_wy")],
                     file.path(od, "supp_data_full_space_scored.csv"),
                     row.names = FALSE)
    cat("\n  saved -> supp_data_full_space_scored.csv in ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(s)
}

## ===========================================================================
## 3. Sample-level metadata — one row per MEASURED SAMPLE
## ===========================================================================
## B40's table is per patient, because sex and stage belong to a person. This
## one is per sample, because plex, channel, reference status and sequencing
## run belong to a measurement. They are different units and neither
## substitutes for the other.
##
## THE IDENTIFIER CHAIN, read out of the session rather than guessed:
##   OP$d$sample        TMT1_126        plex and channel, the measurement
##   pat$sample         TMT1_127N       the bridge table
##   pat$BioReplicate   MF0030          the patient
##   metadata$Patient   MF0030          1:1, 72 rows, 72 distinct patients
##   metadata$SampleID  MF0030pGTSH...  the METAGENOME run, not the proteome
##
## Two things that catch a first attempt. OP$d has no patient column at all,
## so a join straight from it returns nothing -- the bridge is mandatory. And
## metadata$SampleID looks like a sample key and is the metagenome's, so
## joining the proteome to it matches zero rows while looking reasonable.
##
## Reference channels carry no patient by construction. They are rows in this
## table because they are measurements, and their blank patient column is
## correct, not a failed join -- so the completeness test below ignores them.
## BRIDGE DEFAULT: smap, NOT pat. v17 builds pat as
##     pat <- OP$d |> inner_join(smap, by = "sample") |> mutate(bio = ...)
##     pat <- pat |> filter(bio %in% colnames(G), sample %in% colnames(MP))
## and that filter restricts it to patients WITH A METAGENOME that cleared the
## 5M read floor -- the paired 47. Bridging on pat therefore reports the other
## 8 proteome samples as having no patient, when smap names all of them:
## MF001A3A817, MF0480, MF1597, MF1628, MF1640, MF1672, MF1707, MF1735.
## They are unpaired, not unidentified, and a deposit must not conflate those.
## smap carries all 83 channels with their BioReplicate and applies no such
## filter, so it is the right bridge for a table whose unit is the measurement.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## b41_fill_pitt_dates(): the on-treatment cohort's sampling day, from the
## trial record's raw dates, checked against the metadata's
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Sign as in metadata_pitt.tsv: Rx_start minus the collection date, so a
## positive value is days BEFORE the first dose. Dates in Lior_UPF_data.csv are
## month/day/two-digit-year; an ISO date is accepted as well.
B41_UPF_CANDIDATES <- c("Lior_UPF_data.csv", file.path("..", "Lior_UPF_data.csv"))
b41_fill_pitt_dates <- function(out, path = NULL) {
  if (!"Sample_days_pre" %in% names(out)) out$Sample_days_pre <- NA_real_
  cand <- c(path,
            if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$out_dir))
              file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), "Lior_UPF_data.csv"),
            B41_UPF_CANDIDATES)
  hit <- cand[!is.na(cand) & file.exists(cand)]
  if (!length(hit)) {
    cat("  sampling dates: Lior_UPF_data.csv not found; the roster keeps the\n",
        "  metadata's dates only, and the deposit will lack MF1640's\n", sep = "")
    return(out)
  }
  u  <- utils::read.csv(hit[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  u  <- u[!duplicated(u$MF_ID), , drop = FALSE]
  pd <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x); d <- as.Date(x, "%m/%d/%y")
    i <- is.na(d); d[i] <- as.Date(x[i], "%Y-%m-%d"); d
  }
  dd <- stats::setNames(as.numeric(pd(u$Rx_start) - pd(u$Sample_collection_date)), u$MF_ID)
  is_p <- grepl("^Pitt", out$cohort)
  have <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(out$Sample_days_pre))
  upf  <- unname(dd[as.character(out$patient)])
  both <- is_p & !is.na(have) & !is.na(upf)
  bad  <- both & abs(have - upf) > 0.5
  cat(sprintf("  sampling dates: metadata and trial record agree for %d of %d Pittsburgh patients that carry both\n",
              sum(both & !bad), sum(both)))
  if (any(bad))
    stop("sampling dates DISAGREE between the metadata and Lior_UPF_data.csv: ",
         paste(sprintf("%s metadata %+g, trial record %+g", out$patient[bad], have[bad], upf[bad]),
               collapse = "; "), call. = FALSE)
  fill <- is_p & is.na(have) & !is.na(upf)
  if (any(fill)) {
    cat("  sampling dates filled from the trial record: ",
        paste(sprintf("%s %+g", out$patient[fill], upf[fill]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    ## keep the column's type: days are whole numbers, and an integer column
    ## silently turned double is a diff in every row of the deposit
    out$Sample_days_pre[fill] <- if (is.integer(out$Sample_days_pre)) as.integer(round(upf[fill])) else upf[fill]
  }
  left <- is_p & is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(out$Sample_days_pre)))
  if (any(left))
    cat("  sampling dates: no date anywhere for ", paste(unique(out$patient[left]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  out
}

sample_table <- function(meta_pitt = NULL, meta_sheba = NULL, out_dir = NULL,
                         bridge = if (exists("smap")) smap
                                  else if (exists("pat")) pat else NULL,
                         key_col = NULL, patient_col = NULL,
                         allow_partial = FALSE) {

  if (!exists("OP")) stop("sample_table: OP not in the session.", call. = FALSE)
  d <- OP$d
  ## 13 Oct 2026: the roster is written from the CORRECTED design only. A session
  ## whose OP predates pitt_sample_corrections.R still holds the empty channel and
  ## the duplicate patient and calls TMT1_126 by its corrupted name.
  if (!exists("PITT_DROP")) source("pitt_sample_corrections.R")
  stale <- intersect(as.character(d$sample), names(PITT_DROP))
  if (length(stale) || (!is.null(bridge) && any(grepl("MF001A3", as.character(unlist(bridge))))))
    stop("sample_table: this session predates the 13 Oct 2026 sample corrections (",
         paste(c(stale, "MF001A3A817")[seq_len(max(1, length(stale)))], collapse = ", "),
         " present). Re-run analysis_v17.Rmd first; see run_reanalysis_2026-10-13.R.",
         call. = FALSE)
  sc <- .col(d, c("sample", "Sample", "sample_id"))
  if (is.na(sc))
    stop("sample_table: no sample column in OP$d; names are ",
         paste(names(d), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  pick <- function(cands, default = NA) {
    cn <- .col(d, cands); if (is.na(cn)) rep(default, nrow(d)) else d[[cn]]
  }
  out <- tibble(
    cohort    = "Pittsburgh (on treatment)",
    sample    = as.character(d[[sc]]),
    plex      = as.character(pick(c("Mixture", "mixture", "plex", "Plex"))),
    channel   = as.character(pick(c("Channel", "channel", "TMT_channel"))),
    response  = as.character(pick(c("resp", "Response", "response"))),
    arm       = as.character(pick(c("arm", "Arm"))),
    reference_channel = pick(c("is_norm", "is_reference"), FALSE),
    excluded  = pick(c("excluded", "is_excluded"), FALSE),
    patient   = NA_character_,
    ## Sheba carries this because cd_s holds channels that never reached the
    ## matrix. Pittsburgh must carry it too: a column that is TRUE/FALSE for
    ## one cohort and empty for the other reads as "unknown", not "all of
    ## them", and a deposit should not need a reader to guess which.
    analysed  = if (!is.null(OP$a) && !is.null(colnames(OP$a)))
                  as.character(d[[sc]]) %in% colnames(OP$a) else NA)
  cat(sprintf("sample_table: %d proteome samples from OP$d\n", nrow(out)))
  if (!all(is.na(out$analysed)))
    cat(sprintf("  analysed (present in OP$a): %d of %d\n",
                sum(out$analysed %in% TRUE), nrow(out)))

  ## --- the bridge ----------------------------------------------------------
  if (is.null(bridge)) {
    cat("  no bridge table (expected `pat`). Without it OP$d cannot reach a\n",
        "  patient, because it carries no patient column.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    bs <- .col(bridge, c("sample", "Sample"))
    bp <- if (!is.null(patient_col) && patient_col %in% names(bridge)) patient_col
          else .col(bridge, c("BioReplicate", "bio", "Patient", "patient"))
    if (is.na(bs) || is.na(bp)) {
      cat("  bridge has no usable columns (tried sample and ",
          "BioReplicate/bio/Patient);\n  names are ",
          paste(names(bridge), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      i <- match(out$sample, as.character(bridge[[bs]]))
      out$patient <- as.character(bridge[[bp]])[i]
      nref <- sum(!out$reference_channel %in% TRUE)
      cat(sprintf("  patient via bridge$%s: %d of %d samples (%d of %d non-reference)\n",
                  bp, sum(!is.na(out$patient)), nrow(out),
                  sum(!is.na(out$patient) & !out$reference_channel %in% TRUE), nref))
      ## Name them. An unmatched sample is usually a real fact about the data
      ## -- here, a proteome with no paired metagenome -- and a bare count
      ## cannot be told apart from a partly broken key.
      um <- out$sample[is.na(out$patient) & !out$reference_channel %in% TRUE]
      if (length(um))
        cat("    without a patient in the bridge: ",
            paste(um, collapse = ", "), "\n",
            "    (with smap as the bridge this should be empty; if it is not,\n",
            "     the bridge is pat, which is filtered to the paired 47)\n", sep = "")
    }
  }

  ## --- channels measured but excluded (13 Oct 2026) ---------------------------
  ## Listed, not dropped: a deposit that silently loses a measured channel is less
  ## useful than one that marks it. Their patient is the one they were annotated as.
  out$exclusion_reason <- NA_character_
  ## length() first: with every channel restored (13 Oct 2026) PITT_DROP is
  ## empty, and any(character(0) %in% x) is FALSE, so without this guard the
  ## block below would run and rbind a zero-row frame built from empty lookups.
  if (length(PITT_DROP) && !any(names(PITT_DROP) %in% out$sample)) {
    xs <- names(PITT_DROP)
    out <- dplyr::bind_rows(out, tibble(
      cohort = "Pittsburgh (on treatment)", sample = xs,
      plex = sub("_.*$", "", xs), channel = sub("^.*_", "", xs),
      response = unname(PITT_DROP_RESP[xs]), arm = "pitt_ontx",
      reference_channel = FALSE, excluded = TRUE,
      patient = unname(PITT_DROP_PATIENT[xs]), analysed = FALSE,
      exclusion_reason = unname(PITT_DROP[xs])))
    cat("  excluded channels listed: ",
        paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", xs, PITT_DROP_PATIENT[xs]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }

  ## --- clinical fields, and the metagenome that metadata$SampleID names -----
  add_meta <- function(out, meta, label, want) {
    if (is.null(meta)) return(out)
    kc <- if (!is.null(key_col) && key_col %in% names(meta)) key_col else
            .col(meta, c("Patient", "patient", "bio", "PatientID", "subject"))
    if (is.na(kc)) {
      cat("  ", label, ": no patient column in the metadata; not joined\n", sep = "")
      return(out)
    }
    if (anyDuplicated(meta[[kc]]))
      cat("  ", label, ": metadata$", kc, " is not unique; first row per patient used\n", sep = "")
    m <- meta[!duplicated(meta[[kc]]), , drop = FALSE]
    key <- .norm_id(m[[kc]])
    i <- match(.norm_id(out$patient), key)
    ## second pass: a trailing letter, reported rather than assumed
    j <- is.na(i) & !is.na(out$patient)
    if (any(j)) {
      i2 <- match(.strip_suffix(.norm_id(out$patient[j])), key)
      if (any(!is.na(i2))) {
        res <- unique(stats::na.omit(data.frame(
          from = out$patient[j][!is.na(i2)],
          to   = as.character(m[[kc]])[i2[!is.na(i2)]])))
        cat("  ", label, ": matched by dropping a trailing letter -- ",
            paste(sprintf("%s->%s", res$from, res$to), collapse = ", "),
            "\n    Confirm these are the same patient; they are joined on that\n",
            "    assumption and nothing else distinguishes them.\n", sep = "")
        i[j] <- i2
      }
    }
    got <- intersect(want, names(m))
    for (g in got) out[[g]] <- m[[g]][i]
    um <- unique(out$patient[is.na(i) & !is.na(out$patient)])
    if (length(um))
      cat("  ", label, ": no metadata row for ", paste(um, collapse = ", "),
          "\n", sep = "")

    ## In the Pittsburgh metadata, SampleID is the METAGENOME run id
    ## (MF0030pGTSH10d20221212) and its suffix is the sequencing provenance
    ## RECONCILIATION A.1 is about. In the Sheba metadata, SampleID IS the
    ## patient ("p11"), so copying it into a metagenome column would invent a
    ## metagenome for every Sheba sample. Only treat it as a run id where it
    ## actually differs from the patient key.
    sid <- .col(m, c("SampleID", "sample_id"))
    if (!is.na(sid)) {
      same <- mean(as.character(m[[sid]]) == as.character(m[[kc]]), na.rm = TRUE)
      if (isTRUE(same > 0.5)) {
        cat("  ", label, ": metadata$", sid, " equals the patient key, so it is\n",
            "    not a metagenome run; no metagenome column filled\n", sep = "")
      } else {
        out$metagenome <- as.character(m[[sid]])[i]
        out$sequencing_run <- ifelse(is.na(out$metagenome), NA_character_,
          ifelse(grepl("pGTSH", out$metagenome), "pGTSH10d20221212",
          ifelse(grepl("_S[0-9]+$", out$metagenome), "_S<index>", "other")))
      }
    }
    if (sum(!is.na(i)) == 0)
      cat("  ", label, ": NOTHING joined -- 0 of ", nrow(out),
          " samples matched metadata$", kc, ". The ", length(got),
          " field(s) are present as empty columns.\n", sep = "")
    else
      cat("  ", label, ": joined ", length(got), " field(s) for ",
          sum(!is.na(i)), " of ", nrow(out), " samples\n", sep = "")
    miss <- setdiff(want, names(m))
    if (length(miss))
      cat("  ", label, ": absent from the metadata -- ",
          paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    out
  }

  ## the metadata's own spellings, checked against its header
  WANT_PITT <- c("Sex", "Stage", "Histology", "Treatment_regimen", "Line",
                 "Sample_days_pre", "PPI_H2RA", "Abx_3M_prior", "irAE",
                 "Sequencing_Batch", "Pitts_subcohort", "Source")
  WANT_SHEBA <- c("Treatment_regimen", "Line", "Sample_days_pre", "Source")
  out <- add_meta(out, meta_pitt, "Pittsburgh", WANT_PITT)
  ## SAMPLING DATES FROM THE TRIAL RECORD (13 Oct 2026). The metadata carries
  ## Sample_days_pre only for the patients it covers. Lior_UPF_data.csv carries
  ## the raw dates for every patient with a record -- including MF1640, which
  ## has its dates and nothing else and so is in no metadata file -- and the
  ## analysis times samples from those raw dates (analysis_v17 section 2f). So
  ## the deposited roster takes them too: where the metadata has a value the
  ## two must agree to the day, and where it has none the trial record fills it.
  out <- b41_fill_pitt_dates(out)

  ## --- Sheba ----------------------------------------------------------------
  ## The Sheba objects mirror Pittsburgh's but under different names and with
  ## no sample column anywhere:
  ##   cd_s   47x6   Mixture, Channel, resp, arm, is_norm, excluded   (= OP$d)
  ##   ann_s  47x4   Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate, k                (= pat)
  ##   MPs    matrix colnames "1_126"                                 (analysed)
  ## The sample id is Mixture_Channel, built here and checked against MPs'
  ## column names rather than assumed. cd_s is preferred over MPs because it
  ## carries the reference and excluded flags, and a sample-level deposit that
  ## silently drops excluded channels is less useful than one that marks them.
  sd_ <- NULL
  for (nm in c("cd_s", "d_s", "design_sheba")) if (exists(nm)) { sd_ <- get(nm); break }
  sb_ <- NULL
  for (nm in c("ann_s", "pat_s", "bridge_sheba")) if (exists(nm)) { sb_ <- get(nm); break }

  if (is.null(sd_)) {
    cat("  Sheba design table not found (tried cd_s, d_s, design_sheba); the\n",
        "  table covers the on-treatment cohort only, and the legend must say so\n",
        sep = "")
  } else {
    mx <- .col(sd_, c("Mixture", "mixture", "plex"))
    ch <- .col(sd_, c("Channel", "channel", "TMT_channel"))
    if (is.na(mx) || is.na(ch)) {
      cat("  Sheba design has no Mixture/Channel columns; names are ",
          paste(names(sd_), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      sid <- paste(as.character(sd_[[mx]]), as.character(sd_[[ch]]), sep = "_")
      ## does the constructed id match the analysed matrix?
      if (exists("MPs") && is.matrix(MPs) && !is.null(colnames(MPs))) {
        ov <- sum(colnames(MPs) %in% sid)
        cat(sprintf("  Sheba: %d design rows, %d of %d MPs columns matched by Mixture_Channel\n",
                    length(sid), ov, ncol(MPs)))
        if (ov == 0)
          cat("    *** the constructed id does not match MPs' columns. Sample ids\n",
              "        below are the design's, not the analysed matrix's.\n", sep = "")
      } else cat(sprintf("  Sheba: %d design rows\n", length(sid)))

      gets <- function(cands, default = NA) {
        cn <- .col(sd_, cands); if (is.na(cn)) rep(default, nrow(sd_)) else sd_[[cn]]
      }
      add <- tibble(
        cohort = "Sheba (before treatment)", sample = sid,
        plex = as.character(sd_[[mx]]), channel = as.character(sd_[[ch]]),
        response = as.character(gets(c("resp", "Response", "response"))),
        arm = as.character(gets(c("arm", "Arm"))),
        reference_channel = gets(c("is_norm", "is_reference"), FALSE),
        excluded = gets(c("excluded", "is_excluded"), FALSE),
        patient = NA_character_,
        analysed = if (exists("MPs") && is.matrix(MPs) && !is.null(colnames(MPs)))
                     sid %in% colnames(MPs) else NA)

      ## bridge on the PAIR, not on either column alone
      if (is.null(sb_)) {
        cat("  Sheba bridge not found (tried ann_s, pat_s); patient left empty\n")
      } else {
        bmx <- .col(sb_, c("Mixture", "mixture", "plex"))
        bch <- .col(sb_, c("Channel", "channel", "TMT_channel"))
        bbr <- .col(sb_, c("BioReplicate", "bio", "Patient", "patient"))
        if (any(is.na(c(bmx, bch, bbr)))) {
          cat("  Sheba bridge lacks Mixture/Channel/BioReplicate; names are ",
              paste(names(sb_), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
        } else {
          bkey <- paste(as.character(sb_[[bmx]]), as.character(sb_[[bch]]), sep = "_")
          i <- match(add$sample, bkey)
          add$patient <- as.character(sb_[[bbr]])[i]
          cat(sprintf("  Sheba: patient via %s$%s for %d of %d samples\n",
                      "ann_s", bbr, sum(!is.na(add$patient)), nrow(add)))
        }
      }
      add <- add_meta(add, meta_sheba, "Sheba", WANT_SHEBA)
      out <- bind_rows(out, add)
    }
  }

  ## --- did the metagenome actually enter the analysis? ---------------------
  ## metadata$SampleID names a metagenome RUN. That is not the same as a
  ## metagenome that reached the analysed matrix: G is built from reads passing
  ## the 5M floor, and five of the eight unpaired patients have a SampleID in
  ## the metadata while their bio is absent from colnames(G). Without this
  ## column the deposit would appear to give every one of them a metagenome.
  if (exists("G") && !is.null(colnames(G))) {
    nid <- if (exists("norm_id", mode = "function")) get("norm_id") else
             function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", as.character(x)))
    out$metagenome_analysed <- !is.na(out$patient) &
                               nid(out$patient) %in% colnames(G)
    cat(sprintf("  metagenome in the analysed matrix for %d of %d samples\n",
                sum(out$metagenome_analysed, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(out)))
    both <- sum(!is.na(out$metagenome) & !out$metagenome_analysed, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (both)
      cat(sprintf(paste0("    %d carry a run id but did not enter the matrix;",
                         " that gap is the point of this column\n"), both))
  } else {
    out$metagenome_analysed <- NA
    cat("  G not in the session; metagenome_analysed left empty\n")
  }

  ## --- refuse to write a table that joined nothing --------------------------
  ## Every clinical and metagenomic column hangs off the patient key. With it
  ## unresolved the file still has the right rows and headers and is empty in
  ## every column that matters -- the shape of a deposit nobody notices is
  ## wrong. Reference channels are excluded from the test: they have no patient
  ## by construction, and counting them would mask a real failure.
  real <- !(out$reference_channel %in% TRUE)
  joined <- sum(!is.na(out$patient[real])) > 0
  if (!joined) {
    cat("\n  *** NOT WRITTEN. The patient key did not resolve for any\n",
        "      non-reference sample. Pass the bridge explicitly:\n",
        "        sample_table(mp, ms, bridge = pat, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n",
        "      or name its patient column with patient_col =, and the\n",
        "      metadata's with key_col =. allow_partial = TRUE writes the\n",
        "      measurement columns alone, named _PARTIAL so it cannot be\n",
        "      deposited by mistake.\n", sep = "")
    if (!allow_partial) return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  if (!is.null(out_dir)) {
    od <- .mkdir(out_dir)
    fn <- if (joined) "supp_data_sample_metadata.csv"
          else "supp_data_sample_metadata_PARTIAL.csv"
    utils::write.csv(out, file.path(od, fn), row.names = FALSE)
    cat("\n  saved -> ", fn, " (", nrow(out), " rows, ", ncol(out),
        " columns) in ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(out)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## deposit_readme(): the three files, described where they will be read
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## A deposited table with an unexplained column is a table that gets used
## wrongly. The counts here are computed from the objects just written, not
## typed, so the README cannot drift from the files it describes.
deposit_readme <- function(res, out_dir) {
  if (is.null(out_dir)) return(invisible(NULL))
  od <- .mkdir(out_dir)
  n <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) "not written" else format(nrow(x), big.mark = ",")
  smp <- res$samples
  cnt <- function(f) if (is.null(smp) || !f %in% names(smp)) NA_integer_ else
                       sum(!is.na(smp[[f]]))
  L <- c(
  "# Supplementary data deposit",
  "",
  sprintf("Written by B41_supp_tables.R on %s.", format(Sys.Date())),
  "",
  "## supp_table1_ko_membership.csv",
  "",
  sprintf("The two frozen KO sets, %s rows. Membership is read from the", n(res$ko)),
  "analysis session's own CHAPERONE_KO and RIBO_KO and is never re-derived:",
  "the Methods claim is that the lists were fixed before any analysis, and a",
  "list regenerated later cannot support it. Gene symbols and annotations come",
  "from KEGG and are labels only. n_proteins_* is the number of distinct",
  "proteins carrying that orthology group in each cohort's annotation, which",
  "is a measure of coverage, not of abundance.",
  "",
  "## supp_data_full_space_scored.csv",
  "",
  sprintf("Per-set scores for the full survey, %s rows. Produced by", n(res$scored)),
  "B1c_score.R / B1d_distinct_fdr.R and copied here unchanged. p_set is the",
  "per-set permutation p, q_bh its Benjamini-Hochberg value, and p_wy the",
  "Westfall-Young family-wise p over the whole survey. No set clears 0.05 on",
  "either correction; that is the result, not a filtering step.",
  "",
  "## supp_data_sample_metadata.csv",
  "",
  sprintf("One row per measured sample, %s rows. The unit is the MEASUREMENT:", n(smp)),
  "plex, channel, reference status and sequencing run belong to a sample, not",
  "to a person. Main Table 1 is the per-patient view and the two are",
  "not interchangeable.",
  "",
  "Columns that are empty for a reason rather than by omission:",
  "",
  sprintf("- patient: empty for reference channels, and for the %d on-treatment",
          if (is.null(smp)) 0L else sum(is.na(smp$patient) &
            smp$cohort %in% "Pittsburgh (on treatment)")),
  "  proteomes with no paired metagenome; those samples have no entry in the",
  "  bridge table.",
  "- metagenome, sequencing_run: on-treatment cohort only. The pre-treatment",
  "  metadata's SampleID is the patient, not a sequencing run, so no run id",
  "  exists for it. Run ids split into the two naming regimes described in",
  "  RECONCILIATION A.1.",
  "- Line: absent from the on-treatment metadata at source, for every patient.",
  "- Sex, Stage, Histology, PPI_H2RA, Abx_3M_prior, irAE, Sequencing_Batch,",
  "  Pitts_subcohort: on-treatment cohort only; the pre-treatment metadata",
  "  carries regimen, line, timing and source and nothing else.",
  "- analysed: whether the PROTEOME sample reached the analysed abundance",
  "  matrix. FALSE marks reference channels and channels set aside before",
  "  analysis.",
  "- exclusion_reason: for the one on-treatment channel measured but excluded,",
  "  why. TMT7_127N (annotated MF1529) carries no sample signal: the 127N",
  "  reagent went on no sample in that plex, so MF1529 was never measured.",
  "  TMT1_126, annotated under a corrupted name, is MF0017.",
  "- metagenome_analysed: whether that patient's metagenome reached the gene",
  "  matrix. A sample can carry a run id and still be FALSE here, because the",
  "  gene matrix is built from runs passing a 5 million read floor. The paired",
  "  set the cross-layer analyses use is the rows where this is TRUE.",
  "",
  "Pre-treatment samples whose patient has no metadata row are measured",
  "samples with no clinical record; they are present here rather than dropped,",
  "so the gap is visible.")
  writeLines(L, file.path(od, "README.md"))
  cat("  saved -> README.md in ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(L)
}

## ===========================================================================
## b41() — all three, with a closing statement of what is still missing
## ===========================================================================
b41 <- function(meta_pitt = NULL, meta_sheba = NULL, scored_dir = NULL,
                out_dir = NULL, find = TRUE, key_col = NULL,
                patient_col = NULL, allow_partial = FALSE) {
  ## Tables 1 and 2 of the three need no metadata at all. Only the sample-level
  ## table does, and it degrades to the measurement fields without it, so a
  ## missing metadata path must not stop the other two.
  if (find && is.null(meta_pitt) && is.null(meta_sheba)) {
    cat("=== 0. no metadata passed; looking for it ===\n")
    fm <- find_meta()
    rd <- function(pth) if (is.null(pth) || is.na(pth)) NULL else
            tryCatch(read_meta(pth), error = function(e) {
              cat("  read_meta failed on ", pth, ": ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""); NULL })
    if (!is.null(fm)) { meta_pitt <- rd(fm$pitt); meta_sheba <- rd(fm$sheba) }
    if (is.null(meta_pitt))
      cat("\n  no Pittsburgh metadata resolved. The first two tables do not need\n",
          "  it; the third will carry the measurement fields and leave the\n",
          "  clinical ones out, which is the honest shape for it.\n", sep = "")
  }
  res <- list()
  cat("\n=== 1. Supplementary Table 1 — frozen KO membership ===\n")
  res$ko <- tryCatch(ko_membership(out_dir = out_dir),
                     error = function(e) { cat("FAILED: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""); NULL })
  cat("\n=== 2. per-set scoring table ===\n")
  res$scored <- tryCatch(scored_survey(dir = scored_dir, out_dir = out_dir),
                         error = function(e) { cat("FAILED: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""); NULL })
  cat("\n=== 3. sample-level metadata ===\n")
  res$samples <- tryCatch(sample_table(meta_pitt, meta_sheba, out_dir = out_dir,
                                       key_col = key_col, patient_col = patient_col,
                                       allow_partial = allow_partial),
                          error = function(e) { cat("FAILED: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = ""); NULL })

  ## A table that was refused is NULL, and a table whose joins failed is not
  ## "written" in any sense the caller cares about. The first version of this
  ## reported "all three tables written" over a samples table that had joined
  ## 0 of 55 rows, which is worse than reporting nothing at all.
  cat("\n=== status ===\n")
  ok <- function(x) !is.null(x) && (!is.data.frame(x) || nrow(x) > 0)
  lbl <- c(ko = "Supplementary Table 1 (KO membership)",
           scored = "per-set scoring table",
           samples = "sample-level metadata")
  for (nm in names(lbl))
    cat(sprintf("  %-38s %s\n", lbl[[nm]],
                if (ok(res[[nm]])) "written" else "NOT WRITTEN -- see above"))
  gone <- names(res)[!vapply(res, ok, logical(1))]
  if (!length(gone)) {
    cat("\n  all three complete.\n")
    deposit_readme(res, out_dir)
  }
  invisible(res)
}

cat("B41 loaded.\n\n",
    "  source('B41_supp_tables.R')\n",
    "  r <- b41(out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "With no metadata passed it calls find_meta() and searches for the files,\n",
    "printing every candidate with a score. It only ADOPTS one when that file\n",
    "is the unambiguous best for its cohort -- picking the wrong metadata file\n",
    "fills a table that then looks complete, which is the failure B40 exists\n",
    "to prevent. If it says AMBIGUOUS, pass the path yourself:\n\n",
    "  mp <- read_meta('<path>'); ms <- read_meta('<path>')\n",
    "  r  <- b41(mp, ms, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "The first two tables need NO metadata. Run them now regardless:\n",
    "  ko_membership(out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n",
    "  scored_survey(dir = '<the nulls directory>', out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n",
    "  sample_table(mp, ms, out_dir = paths$out_dir)\n\n",
    "ko_membership() READS CHAPERONE_KO and RIBO_KO out of the session and\n",
    "refuses if they are absent. It does not rebuild them: the claim the\n",
    "Methods make is that the lists were frozen before analysis, and a list\n",
    "regenerated now cannot support that claim. If the counts disagree with\n",
    "the manuscript's 19 and 54, the script says so and keeps the session's.\n\n",
    "scored_survey() LOCATES B1c_score.R's output. It never rescores -- two\n",
    "scorings of one quantity is how a paper ends up with two numbers for it.\n",
    sep = "")
```

## B42 — sheba mg inventory

Sheba metagenome library inventory: which libraries enter the primary

Source: `B42_sheba_mg_inventory.R`

```{r B42_sheba_mg_inventory, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B42 — Sheba metagenome library inventory: which libraries enter the primary
## pre-treatment analysis, and why the rest do not.
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. The SDRF is the proteome's view, one row per proteome run
## naming the metagenome from the same stool, so a sequenced metagenome library
## with no proteome row pointing at it is invisible in it. Fourteen of the 46
## profiled Sheba libraries are in that position. They are real libraries and
## belong in the SRA deposit, so the deposit needs this list.
##
## sheba_mg_inventory.R and sheba_mg_inventory2.R are read-only diagnostics of
## the input trees; neither classifies libraries. This does.
##
## Base R. Reads the collection records and the merged profile header only, so
## it runs without the analysis session. Writes two files: the internal copy,
## with exact collection dates and best response, and a deposit copy with the
## date coarsened to year-month and the response dropped.
## ============================================================================
TIM <- "final_run/sheba_sample_timing_all_records.csv"
MPA <- file.path(Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT", "/Volumes/Extreme Pro"),
                "metagenomics/ICB_melanoma/Sheba/combined_batches/metaphlan/merged_output/merged_abundance_table.txt")
OUT <- "final_run/B42_sheba_mg_inventory"

stopifnot(file.exists(TIM), file.exists(MPA))
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

tim <- read.csv(TIM, colClasses = "character")
tim$collected <- as.Date(tim$collected)
tim$days      <- as.numeric(tim$days_before_start)

## the library names, from the merged table's header
h    <- readLines(MPA, n = 4, warn = FALSE)
cols <- strsplit(grep("^#?clade_name", h, value = TRUE)[1], "\t")[[1]][-1]
libs <- sub("_.*$", "", cols)                        # keep the id for tube_of
fam  <- ifelse(grepl("^[^_]+_S[0-9]+", cols), "S",
        ifelse(grepl("^[^_]+_ME", cols), "ME", NA))
stopifnot(length(cols) == 46L, !anyNA(fam), sum(fam == "S") == 26L)

## §10e's tube_of, unchanged: S-series reads the arm's own record (94a/94b are
## two episodes); ME-series reads the stool bank, where A/B/C = before/during/
## after and a bare id is "before" except 822, whose bank tube is the during one.
tube_of <- function(id, family) {
  probe <- sub("[abc]$", "", tolower(id)); suf <- toupper(sub("^[0-9]+", "", id))
  if (family == "S") {
    r <- tim[tim$probe_key == probe & tim$file == "sheba_bar_ilan", ]
    k <- if (suf == "B") 2L else 1L
  } else {
    blk <- unname(c(A = "before", B = "during", C = "after")[suf])
    if (is.na(blk)) blk <- if (probe == "822") "during" else "before"
    r <- tim[tim$probe_key == probe & tim$file == "stool_bank" & tim$block == blk, ]
    k <- 1L
  }
  r <- r[order(r$collected), ]
  if (nrow(r) < k) stop("no collection record for ", id, call. = FALSE)
  r[k, c("patient", "collected", "days", "best_response")]
}
inv <- cbind(data.frame(library = cols, family = fam, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
             do.call(rbind, Map(tube_of, libs, fam)))
rownames(inv) <- NULL
inv$pre <- inv$days >= 0

## one metagenome per patient, the earliest pre-treatment episode -- the rule
## sh_set applies in §10e.
kept <- unlist(lapply(split(inv[inv$pre, ], inv$patient[inv$pre]), function(d)
          d$library[order(d$collected, d$library)][1]), use.names = FALSE)

EXCL_TIMING <- "11"      # 304 days before the first dose
BELOW_5M    <- "82"      # 3,847,028 reads
probe <- sub("[abc]$", "", tolower(sub("_.*$", "", inv$library)))
inv$status <- "in primary analysis"; inv$reason <- ""
drop <- function(i, why) { inv$status[i] <<- "excluded"; inv$reason[i] <<- why }
drop(!inv$pre,                                   "collected on or after treatment start")
drop(inv$pre & !inv$library %in% kept,           "a second library for the same patient; the earliest pre-treatment episode is used")
drop(inv$status != "excluded" & probe %in% EXCL_TIMING,
     "collected 304 days before the first dose, outside the pre-treatment window")
drop(inv$status != "excluded" & probe %in% BELOW_5M,
     "below the 5M read floor (3,847,028 reads)")

cat(sprintf("libraries %d | pre-treatment %d | patients %d | in primary analysis %d\n",
            nrow(inv), sum(inv$pre), length(unique(inv$patient[inv$pre])),
            sum(inv$status == "in primary analysis")))
print(table(inv$reason[inv$status == "excluded"]))
## EXPECTED: 46 | 37 | 34 | 32, and 9 / 3 / 1 / 1 by reason.
stopifnot(nrow(inv) == 46L, sum(inv$pre) == 37L,
          length(unique(inv$patient[inv$pre])) == 34L,
          sum(inv$status == "in primary analysis") == 32L)

inv <- inv[order(inv$status != "in primary analysis", inv$patient, inv$library), ]
write.table(inv, file.path(OUT, "sheba_metagenome_library_inventory.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

## The deposit copy: no exact collection day, no response label. Exact dates plus
## response for a 34-patient clinical cohort are quasi-identifiers, and the
## consent scope for public release is not settled.
dep <- data.frame(library = inv$library, library_series = inv$family,
                  host_subject_id = inv$patient,
                  collection_date = format(inv$collected, "%Y-%m"),
                  days_before_first_dose = inv$days,
                  in_primary_analysis = ifelse(inv$status == "in primary analysis", "yes", "no"),
                  exclusion_reason = inv$reason, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
write.table(dep, file.path(OUT, "sheba_metagenome_library_inventory_DEPOSIT.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
cat("written to ", OUT, "\n", sep = "")
```

## B42 — sheba share

the per-sample chaperone share in the PRE-TREATMENT cohort

Source: `B42_sheba_share.R`

```{r B42_sheba_share, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B42 — the per-sample chaperone share in the PRE-TREATMENT cohort
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. The discovery cohort's headline quantity is a per-sample
## share: chaperones take a median 10.9% of microbial protein in non-responders
## against 9.7% in responders, P = 0.024 by within-plex label permutation. That
## quantity has never been computed in the second cohort. Everything reported
## there so far is rank-based enrichment (NES -1.48, P = 0.155), which is a
## different statistic on the same proteins. This fills that gap.
##
## THE DIRECTION IS FIXED BEFORE THE RUN, and it is fixed by the discovery
## cohort, not by looking: non-responders carry the LARGER chaperone share, so
## on the logit scale the R - NR coefficient is NEGATIVE. The one-sided p below
## counts draws at or below the observed coefficient. The two-sided p is printed
## beside it so nothing is hidden by the choice.
##
## THIS RESULT IS REPORTED WHATEVER IT SHOWS. That is the condition under which
## running it is worth anything. Written down here because the alternative --
## trying quantities until one clears 0.05 -- is exactly what this paper's
## multiplicity section exists to rule out, and a reviewer is entitled to ask
## which tests were run and not reported.
##
## WHAT THE COHORT CAN DETECT. Eight non-responders against twenty-seven
## responders. Simulated power for a rank-based test at this design:
##
##     true shift (SD units)     two-sided      one-sided
##             0.3 (= discovery)       10%            16%
##             0.5                     21%            31%
##             0.8                     45%            59%
##             1.1                      -             82%
##
## So the cohort needs roughly 3.7 times the discovery effect for a fair chance.
## A null here is close to uninformative and must not be read as a refutation;
## it is what this many non-responders buys. The within-plex design recovers
## some of that by removing the plex variance component, which is why the
## discovery p beat its own naive power calculation -- but it cannot manufacture
## non-responders.
##
## THREE QUANTITIES, ONE TEST. The rows mirror the discovery cohort's table
## exactly -- all chaperones (the tested quantity), GroEL + DnaK, and the other
## chaperones -- so the two tables can be read side by side. Only the first row
## is a test; the other two are descriptive, labelled as such there and here.
## They are not a menu to choose a winner from.
##
## RUN FROM THE PROJECT ROOT, INSIDE THE ANALYSIS SESSION, like run_B40_B41.R:
##   source("B42_sheba_share.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

  ## ---- what this needs from the session ------------------------------------
  need <- c("OS", "chap_frac_of", "RESP_LEVELS", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("B42 needs the analysis session: missing ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
         ".\n  Run this with source() from the project root after the analysis ",
         "objects exist, the way run_B40_B41.R is run.", call. = FALSE)

  ## The Sheba chaperone protein set. `chap_new_s` is what the Sheba sets are
  ## built from in section 7; fall back to the annotation table if an older
  ## session does not carry it, and say which was used.
  chap_s <- if (exists("chap_new_s")) {
    cat("B42: chaperone set from chap_new_s\n"); chap_new_s
  } else if (exists("annot_new")) {
    cat("B42: chap_new_s absent; rebuilding from annot_new + CHAPERONE_KO\n")
    if (!exists("CHAPERONE_KO")) stop("neither chap_new_s nor CHAPERONE_KO is present")
    unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "sheba" &
                             annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO])
  } else stop("no Sheba chaperone set available", call. = FALSE)

  GD <- c("K04077", "K04043")
  gd_s <- if (exists("annot_new"))
    unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "sheba" &
                             annot_new$ko_primary %in% GD]) else character(0)
  if (!length(gd_s))
    cat("B42: no GroEL/DnaK proteins resolved for this cohort; ",
        "the descriptive split is skipped\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- is the within-plex design usable here at all? -----------------------
  ## A within-plex permutation needs plexes that carry BOTH arms. A plex with
  ## one arm only contributes nothing and its samples are carried by the plex
  ## term alone. This is printed before any test, because if it comes back thin
  ## the p below is not worth reading.
  d0 <- chap_frac_of(OS, chap_s)
  if (!nrow(d0)) stop("B42: no Sheba samples with a usable chaperone fraction", call. = FALSE)
  d0$Mixture <- droplevels(factor(d0$Mixture))
  d0$resp    <- factor(as.character(d0$resp), levels = RESP_LEVELS)
  tb <- table(d0$Mixture, d0$resp)
  cat("\nB42: Sheba plex structure for this quantity\n")
  print(tb)
  both <- rownames(tb)[rowSums(tb > 0) == 2L]
  cat(sprintf("  plexes carrying both arms: %d of %d; samples in them: %d of %d\n",
              length(both), nrow(tb), sum(tb[both, , drop = FALSE]), nrow(d0)))
  if (!length(both))
    stop("B42: no plex carries both arms, so a within-plex contrast does not exist. ",
         "The test is undefined for this cohort, which is a statement about the ",
         "design and should be reported as one.", call. = FALSE)

  ## ---- the test ------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Same model and same permutation scheme as the discovery cohort's
  ## perm_share(): logit share, plex as a fixed effect, labels shuffled WITHIN
  ## plex. The only difference is that the one-sided p is reported first.
  perm_share_1s <- function(d, B = 10000L, seed = 7401L, label = "") {
    d <- dplyr::filter(d, frac > 0, frac < 1)
    d <- droplevels(d)
    fit <- lm(qlogis(frac) ~ Mixture + resp, d)
    nm  <- grep("^resp", names(coef(fit)), value = TRUE)
    if (length(nm) != 1L)
      stop("B42: expected one response coefficient, found ", length(nm), call. = FALSE)
    obs <- coef(fit)[[nm]]
    set.seed(seed)
    keep <- list()
    nl <- replicate(B, {
      rp <- factor(ave(as.character(d$resp), d$Mixture, FUN = sample), levels = RESP_LEVELS)
      keep[[length(keep) + 1L]] <<- paste(rp, collapse = "")
      ## BY NAME, NOT BY POSITION. An earlier draft indexed this coefficient as
      ## 2 + nlevels(Mixture) - 1, which is arithmetically right and silently
      ## wrong the first time a plex drops out or a level is renamed. The house
      ## perm_share() names it; so does this.
      cf <- coef(lm(qlogis(d$frac) ~ d$Mixture + rp))
      cf[[grep("^rp", names(cf))[1L]]] })
    ## DISTINCT ASSIGNMENTS, NOT DRAWS. With few non-responders per plex the
    ## permutation space can be small enough to put a floor under the p, and a
    ## floor is invisible unless counted.
    ndist <- length(unique(unlist(keep)))
    ## AN INTERVAL, NOT ONLY A p. "Not significant" and "cannot distinguish this
    ## from the discovery effect" are different statements, and only the second
    ## is worth reporting at this sample size. The Wald interval comes from the
    ## same plex-adjusted model the permutation tests, so it is the precision of
    ## the quantity actually being tested. DISC is the discovery cohort's
    ## coefficient; `covers_discovery` says whether this cohort can exclude it.
    DISC <- -0.189
    se <- coef(summary(fit))[nm, "Std. Error"]
    ci <- obs + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se
    tibble::tibble(
      what = label, n = nrow(d),
      median_NR_pct = 100 * median(d$frac[d$resp == "NR"]),
      median_R_pct  = 100 * median(d$frac[d$resp == "R"]),
      fold = median(d$frac[d$resp == "NR"]) / median(d$frac[d$resp == "R"]),
      gap_logit = obs, se = se, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2],
      covers_discovery = ci[1] <= DISC && DISC <= ci[2],
      p_one_sided = (1 + sum(nl <= obs)) / (1 + B),
      p_two_sided = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(obs))) / (1 + B),
      distinct_perms = ndist, floor_p = 1 / (1 + B))
  }

  rows <- list(perm_share_1s(d0, label = "all chaperones (the tested quantity)"))
  if (length(gd_s)) {
    rows <- c(rows, list(
      perm_share_1s(chap_frac_of(OS, intersect(chap_s, gd_s)),
                    label = "GroEL + DnaK (descriptive)"),
      perm_share_1s(chap_frac_of(OS, setdiff(chap_s, gd_s)),
                    label = "other chaperones (descriptive)")))
  }
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)

  cat("\nB42: per-sample chaperone share, pre-treatment cohort\n")
  cat("  gap_logit = R - NR on the logit scale; NEGATIVE is the predicted\n",
      "  direction, a larger chaperone share in non-responders.\n", sep = "")
  print(as.data.frame(out), digits = 3)
  r1 <- out[1, ]
  cat(sprintf("\n  READING: the tested quantity gives %s, one-sided P = %.4f.\n",
              if (r1$gap_logit < 0) "a difference in the predicted direction"
              else "a difference AGAINST the predicted direction",
              r1$p_one_sided))
  if (r1$p_one_sided >= 0.05)
    cat(sprintf(paste("  This does not reach 0.05. At %d non-responders that outcome was the\n",
                      "  expected one; see the power table in this file's header. Report it.\n"),
                sum(d0$resp == "NR")))
  ## THE SENTENCE THAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH WRITING. A null at this size is only
  ## interesting if it also fails to exclude the effect it was looking for.
  cat(sprintf(paste("  PRECISION: coefficient %.3f, 95%% interval %.3f to %+.3f. The discovery\n",
                    "  cohort's -0.189 is %s this interval, so this cohort %s an effect of\n",
                    "  that size -- underpowered rather than absent.\n"),
              r1$gap_logit, r1$lo, r1$hi,
              if (r1$covers_discovery) "INSIDE" else "OUTSIDE",
              if (r1$covers_discovery) "cannot exclude" else "excludes"))

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B42_sheba_share")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(list(table = out, plex = tb, n_plex_both = length(both)),
          file.path(od, "sheba_share.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b42_sheba_share <<- out
})
```

## B43 — sheba full space

a full-space family for the PRE-TREATMENT cohort, out of curiosity

Source: `B43_sheba_full_space.R`

```{r B43_sheba_full_space, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B43 — a full-space family for the PRE-TREATMENT cohort, out of curiosity
## ============================================================================
##
## THE 565 SETS CANNOT BE SCORED IN THIS COHORT. They are not a list of pathway
## names; they are lists of PROTEIN IDENTIFIERS, built in B1_full_space_prep.R
## by intersecting each annotation layer with `names(stat)` -- the discovery
## cohort's analysis universe. The two cohorts are searched against databases
## built from their own assemblies and share NO protein identifiers at all
## (Supplementary Note 6). Intersected with this cohort's universe, every one of
## the 565 would return zero members. "The same 565" is not a computation that
## exists; it is a category error about what a set is here.
##
## WHAT IS BUILDABLE is the equivalent family on THIS cohort's own universe,
## from the same annotation layers. It is a different family -- different
## membership, different sizes, some sets absent entirely -- so it is comparable
## to the discovery family by NAME and not by content. That is the same caveat
## Supplementary Note 6 already makes about the thirty reported sets.
##
## WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES NOT GIVE YOU IS p-VALUES. Those need a within-plex
## permutation null per set, which is the server run (run_null.R), not a desk
## calculation. What it gives is the observed enrichment scores and, more to the
## point, their SPREAD -- which is the quantity that decides whether a discovery
## survey here could find anything at all.
##
## THE PREDICTION, written before running it: it will look null. The eighteen
## single-letter COG categories scored in both cohorts already have a spread of
## 1.11 here against a permutation null of about 1.14. A larger family drawn
## from the same data has no reason to behave differently, and a survey whose
## observed scores are indistinguishable from its null discovers nothing while
## spending a family-wise correction to do it. Recorded here so the run cannot
## be read as having confirmed anything it was not asked.
##
## FOR CURIOSITY, NOT FOR THE PAPER. PRESPEC_sheba_replication.md, dated
## 20 September 2026, fixes this cohort's role as a replication cohort before
## any of its permutation p-values were seen. Nothing here changes that.
##
##   source("B43_sheba_full_space.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

  ## `sets_s`, NOT `sets`. The analysis builds BOTH families in section 6a --
  ## sets on univ (Pittsburgh) and sets_s on univ_s (this cohort) -- and the
  ## first version of this script reached for `sets`, whose members are the
  ## other cohort's protein IDs. That is the same category error the header
  ## describes, made by the script itself. The equivalent family here is one
  ## object away, so building it costs nothing; what it cannot do is be the
  ## SAME 565 sets, because those are lists of proteins this cohort never saw.
  need <- c("sets_s", "st_s", "SETS_S", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("B43 needs the analysis session through section 7b; missing: ",
         paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  if (!requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE))
    stop("B43 needs fgsea", call. = FALSE)

  MIN_N <- 10L
  univ  <- names(st_s)

  ## THE OVERLAP CHECK COMES FIRST, because it is the whole point. If the
  ## annotation layers were built on the other cohort's protein IDs, every set
  ## empties here and the number below is zero -- which is the answer, not a bug.
  ## `sets` IS NOT ALWAYS A LIST. figures_v2.Rmd already records this trap --
  ## "`sets$COG` raised '$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors'" -- and
  ## sets[[L]] on an atomic vector throws "subscript out of bounds" rather than
  ## returning NULL, which is how this script failed on its first run. Test the
  ## container before indexing it, and say what was actually found.
  LAYERS <- c("KO", "COG", "Pfam", "KEGGmod", "KEGGpath")
  if (!is.list(sets_s)) {
    cat(sprintf("B43: `sets_s` is %s of length %d, not a list of layers.\n",
                class(sets_s)[1], length(sets_s)))
    cat("  The annotation layers are not available in this session in the form\n",
        "  B1_full_space_prep.R uses. Re-run the analysis through section 6a, or\n",
        "  pass the layer lists directly. No examined family can be built here.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("B43: `sets_s` carries %d layers: %s\n",
                length(sets_s), paste(names(sets_s), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  getlayer <- function(L) if (is.list(sets_s) && L %in% names(sets_s)) sets_s[[L]] else NULL
  ## The discovery family's size, for scale. If `sets` is present it is that
  ## cohort's layers on its own universe; this is reported only as a comparison.
  if (exists("sets") && is.list(sets))
    cat(sprintf("  (discovery layers for comparison: %s)\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(sets), vapply(sets, length, 0L)),
                      collapse = ", ")))
  cat("B43: members of each layer that exist in this cohort's universe\n")
  flat <- function(lst, tag) {
    if (is.null(lst) || !length(lst)) { cat(sprintf("  %-9s layer absent\n", tag)); return(list()) }
    hit <- vapply(lst, function(x) length(intersect(x, univ)), 0L)
    cat(sprintf("  %-9s %d sets, %d with >= %d members here (largest %d)\n",
                tag, length(lst), sum(hit >= MIN_N), MIN_N, max(hit)))
    s <- lapply(lst, function(x) intersect(x, univ))
    s <- s[lengths(s) >= MIN_N]
    if (!length(s)) return(list())
    setNames(s, paste0(tag, ":", names(s)))
  }
  examined <- do.call(c, lapply(LAYERS, function(L) flat(getlayer(L), L)))
  reported <- setNames(SETS_S, paste0("reported:", names(SETS_S)))
  FAM <- c(examined, reported); FAM <- FAM[!duplicated(names(FAM))]
  cat(sprintf("\n  family built on this cohort: %d sets (%d examined + %d reported)\n",
              length(FAM), length(examined), length(reported)))
  if (length(examined) == 0L)
    cat("  THE EXAMINED LAYERS ARE EMPTY HERE. That is the finding: the annotation\n",
        "  layers are keyed to the other cohort's proteins, so the only family this\n",
        "  cohort has is the thirty reported sets already scored.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- observed scores, no p-values ---------------------------------------
  if (!length(FAM)) {
    cat("\nB43: no set has ", MIN_N, " members in this cohort's universe. ",
        "Nothing to score.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  set.seed(1)
  res <- suppressWarnings(fgsea::fgsea(pathways = FAM, stats = st_s, nperm = 1L))
  nes <- res$NES[is.finite(res$NES)]
  cat(sprintf("\nB43: observed enrichment scores for %d scorable sets\n", length(nes)))
  cat(sprintf("  spread (sd) %.2f | range %+.2f to %+.2f | median |NES| %.2f\n",
              sd(nes), min(nes), max(nes), median(abs(nes))))
  cat("  the permutation null for sets of this kind has sd about 1.14\n")
  ## A VARIANCE TEST, NOT AN EYEBALL. A family carrying real signal is
  ## over-dispersed relative to its null; one that is not, is not.
  chi <- (length(nes) - 1) * var(nes) / 1.14^2
  cat(sprintf("  chi2_%d = %.1f, P(spread exceeds null) = %.4f -> %s\n",
              length(nes) - 1L, chi,
              pchisq(chi, length(nes) - 1L, lower.tail = FALSE),
              if (pchisq(chi, length(nes) - 1L, lower.tail = FALSE) < 0.05)
                "more spread than the null" else
                "INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE NULL -- a survey here finds nothing"))

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B43_sheba_full_space")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(list(family_sizes = vapply(FAM, length, 0L),
               observed = res[, c("pathway", "size", "NES")]),
          file.path(od, "sheba_full_space.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b43_sheba_full <<- res
})
```

## B44 — protein level chaperones

are the individually-shifted proteins disproportionately chaperones?

Source: `B44_protein_level_chaperones.R`

```{r B44_protein_level_chaperones, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B44 — are the individually-shifted proteins disproportionately chaperones?
## ============================================================================
##
## THE QUESTION. 6,939 proteins were tested in the discovery cohort; 604 reach
## p < 0.05 against 347 expected (1.74x) and NONE survives FDR, with direction
## balanced at 297 NR-up / 307 R-up (§4, 23 Sep 2026). That is why the analysis
## is set-level. This asks the threshold version of the same question: among the
## proteins that do move individually, are chaperones over-represented on the
## non-responder side?
##
## WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is the same data and the same contrast as the
## rank-based enrichment, read through a cut-off instead of a ranking. It is a
## SANITY CHECK, not independent evidence, and it must not be reported as a
## second result -- the enrichment already uses every protein and does not throw
## away the ranking. Written down because a threshold test on data that produced
## the hypothesis is the easiest thing in this file to over-read.
##
## THE ABUNDANCE TRAP, AND HOW THE PRIMARY TEST AVOIDS IT. Chaperones are among
## the most abundant proteins measured, and abundant proteins reach p < 0.05
## more often whatever the direction, so "are chaperones over-represented among
## the hits" is confounded by detection power. The PRIMARY test therefore
## conditions on being a hit and asks only about DIRECTION: given that a protein
## moved, does being a chaperone predict which way? Abundance cannot drive that.
## The unconditioned version is reported second, labelled as confounded.
##
## THRESHOLDS ARE SWEPT, not chosen. 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20 are all reported
## so that no single cut-off can be said to have been picked for its answer.
##
##   source("B44_protein_level_chaperones.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

  if (!exists("paths")) stop("B44 needs the analysis session (paths)", call. = FALSE)

  ## BOTH COHORTS, ONE BODY. The first version hard-coded FA and chap_new, which
  ## made it a Pittsburgh script that did not say so -- easy to mistake its
  ## output for a cross-cohort result. The cohorts are declared here and the
  ## analysis below runs once per cohort that is actually present, so a missing
  ## second cohort is reported rather than silently skipped.
  COHORTS <- list(
    list(label = "Pittsburgh, on treatment",  fit = "FA", chap = "chap_new"),
    list(label = "Sheba, before treatment",   fit = "FS", chap = "chap_new_s"))
  RESULTS <- list()

 for (CO in COHORTS) {
  if (!exists(CO$fit) || !exists(CO$chap)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n=== %s: SKIPPED (%s or %s absent) ===\n",
                CO$label, CO$fit, CO$chap)); next
  }
  cat(sprintf("\n================ %s ================\n", CO$label))
  FITOBJ  <- get(CO$fit)
  CHAPSET <- get(CO$chap)

  r <- as.data.frame(FITOBJ$res)
  pcol <- intersect(c("Protein", "protein", "feature", "rowname"), names(r))
  if (!length(pcol)) {
    if (!is.null(rownames(r))) { r$Protein <- rownames(r); pcol <- "Protein" }
    else stop("B44: no protein identifier column in FA$res", call. = FALSE)
  }
  names(r)[names(r) == pcol[1]] <- "Protein"
  stopifnot(all(c("logFC", "pval") %in% names(r)))
  r <- r[is.finite(r$pval) & is.finite(r$logFC), , drop = FALSE]
  ## SIGN CONVENTION, taken from §4 rather than assumed: logFC > 0 is R-up, so
  ## NR-up is logFC < 0. If this ever flips, the direction rows below flip with
  ## it and the test silently reverses, so it is asserted here.
  r$NRup <- r$logFC < 0
  r$chap <- r$Protein %in% CHAPSET
  cat(sprintf("B44: %d proteins with a finite test; %d are chaperones (%.1f%%)\n",
              nrow(r), sum(r$chap), 100 * mean(r$chap)))

  ## ---- is the abundance trap real here? ------------------------------------
  if (exists("det")) {
    d <- det[intersect(names(det), r$Protein)]
    if (length(d)) {
      cc <- r$chap[match(names(d), r$Protein)]
      cat(sprintf("  abundance (det): chaperones median %.2f vs others %.2f -- %s\n",
                  median(d[cc], na.rm = TRUE), median(d[!cc], na.rm = TRUE),
                  if (median(d[cc], na.rm = TRUE) > median(d[!cc], na.rm = TRUE))
                    "chaperones ARE more abundant, so the unconditioned test is confounded"
                  else "no abundance gap"))
    }
  }

  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20), function(th) {
    hit <- r$pval < th
    ## PRIMARY: direction among hits only.
    tb <- table(factor(r$chap[hit], c(TRUE, FALSE), c("chaperone", "other")),
                factor(r$NRup[hit], c(TRUE, FALSE), c("NR-up", "R-up")))
    f  <- if (all(dim(tb) == c(2, 2)) && sum(tb) > 0)
            fisher.test(tb) else list(estimate = NA, p.value = NA)
    ## SECONDARY, confounded: chaperone status against being an NR-up hit at all.
    tb2 <- table(factor(r$chap, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(hit & r$NRup, c(TRUE, FALSE)))
    f2 <- fisher.test(tb2)
    data.frame(threshold = th, hits = sum(hit),
               chap_hits = sum(hit & r$chap),
               chap_NRup = tb["chaperone", "NR-up"], chap_Rup = tb["chaperone", "R-up"],
               other_NRup = tb["other", "NR-up"], other_Rup = tb["other", "R-up"],
               OR_direction = unname(f$estimate), P_direction = f$p.value,
               OR_unconditioned = unname(f2$estimate), P_unconditioned = f2$p.value)
  }))
  ## THE BASELINE DIRECTION, PRINTED. An odds ratio is relative to the other
  ## proteins, so "11 of 11 chaperones NR-up" means nothing until you know what
  ## fraction of EVERYTHING went NR-up. In the second cohort that baseline is
  ## about four in five, which is why a clean sweep there is unremarkable and
  ## Fisher correctly says so; in the discovery cohort it is one in two. Leaving
  ## this out of the table is how a reader -- or the author -- mistakes a global
  ## shift for a set-specific one.
  out$other_pct_NRup <- 100 * out$other_NRup / (out$other_NRup + out$other_Rup)
  cat("\nB44: PRIMARY -- among proteins that moved, does chaperone status predict direction?\n")
  print(as.data.frame(out[, c("threshold","hits","chap_hits","chap_NRup","chap_Rup",
                              "other_NRup","other_Rup","other_pct_NRup",
                              "OR_direction","P_direction")]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  if (any(out$other_pct_NRup > 65 | out$other_pct_NRup < 35))
    cat("  NOTE: the non-chaperone baseline is far from 50%, so this cohort has a\n",
        "  GLOBAL direction skew. Rank-based enrichment is unaffected by it -- a\n",
        "  shift common to all proteins does not move the ranking -- but every\n",
        "  threshold statistic here is, and should be read against that baseline.\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n  SECONDARY (confounded by abundance; reported for completeness):\n")
  print(as.data.frame(out[, c("threshold","OR_unconditioned","P_unconditioned")]),
        digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

  ## ---- HOW MANY INDEPENDENT THINGS IS THAT? --------------------------------
  ## Fisher's test treats every protein as an independent observation. These are
  ## not: a chaperone "protein" is one organism's copy of one ortholog, so forty
  ## copies of GroEL from forty genomes move together and count forty times. If
  ## the NR-up chaperone hits collapse onto a handful of orthologs or a handful
  ## of genera, the p-value above is inflated by roughly that redundancy and the
  ## honest effective n is the number of distinct units, not the protein count.
  ## This does not weaken the direction; it bounds how much the p can be trusted.
  nrup_chap <- r$Protein[r$pval < 0.05 & r$chap & r$NRup]
  cat(sprintf("\nB44: the %d NR-up chaperone proteins at p < 0.05 decompose as\n",
              length(nrup_chap)))
  if (exists("annot_new")) {
    ## the cohort's OWN annotation rows, not Pittsburgh's
    .coh <- if (identical(CO$fit, "FS")) "sheba" else "pitt"
    ko <- annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == .coh &
                               annot_new$protein %in% nrup_chap]
    ko <- ko[!is.na(ko)]
    tb <- sort(table(ko), decreasing = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("  %d distinct orthologs; largest carries %d of %d proteins (%.0f%%)\n",
                length(tb), max(tb), length(ko), 100 * max(tb) / length(ko)))
    cat("  top orthologs: ",
        paste(sprintf("%s x%d", names(tb)[seq_len(min(5, length(tb)))],
                      as.integer(tb)[seq_len(min(5, length(tb)))]), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  } else cat("  (annot_new absent: ortholog decomposition skipped)\n")
  if (exists("pep_g")) {
    g <- tryCatch({
      .O  <- if (identical(CO$fit, "FS") && exists("OS")) OS else OP
      .pg <- if (identical(CO$fit, "FS") && exists("pep_g_s")) pep_g_s else pep_g
      gg <- .pg[.pg$row %in% which(.O$rd$Protein %in% nrup_chap), , drop = FALSE]
      gg[[intersect(c("tax","genus_name","genus"), names(gg))[1]]]
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(g)) {
      g <- g[!is.na(g)]; tg <- sort(table(g), decreasing = TRUE)
      cat(sprintf("  %d distinct genera; largest carries %.0f%% of the assigned evidence\n",
                  length(tg), 100 * max(tg) / sum(tg)))
    }
  }
  cat("  Treat the effective n as the smaller of those counts, not as ",
      length(nrup_chap), " proteins.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- THE EMPIRICAL NULL, which settles the independence argument ---------
  ## Counting "independent units" by hand is guesswork. Distinct orthologs ARE
  ## separate measurements -- GroEL and DnaK are different genes, different
  ## peptides, different quantifications -- so they are not duplicates the way
  ## forty genomes' copies of GroEL are. What they are not is uncorrelated: the
  ## heat-shock regulon co-regulates them, and the growth-state reading this
  ## paper argues for is one latent variable moving all of them together. Fisher
  ## assumes neither duplication nor correlation, so its p is anticonservative by
  ## an amount no table of "if k were really..." can pin down.
  ##
  ## So do not pin it down -- measure it. Draw random protein sets of the same
  ## size, MATCHED ON DETECTION COMPLETENESS by the recipe section 6c already
  ## uses for the set-level control, score each one with the same 2x2, and see
  ## where the real set falls. The null is built from the same correlated data,
  ## so whatever redundancy exists is in the null too.
  ##
  ## WHAT THIS NULL DOES NOT CAPTURE: a random set is not CO-REGULATED, so its
  ## members have less reason to move together than a real pathway's do. That
  ## makes this test competitive rather than self-contained, and mildly generous
  ## to the real set. The strictly correct null permutes SAMPLE labels and
  ## refits, which is the server job behind the set-level p already reported --
  ## and that p, 0.003 to 0.008, is the one to quote in the paper.
  if (exists("det")) {
    dd  <- det[intersect(names(det), r$Protein)]
    dd  <- dd[is.finite(dd)]
    tgt <- dd[intersect(names(dd), CHAPSET)]
    if (length(tgt) >= 20) {
      brk   <- quantile(dd, seq(0, 1, .2), na.rm = TRUE)
      cells <- table(cut(tgt, brk, include.lowest = TRUE))
      idx   <- split(names(dd), cut(dd, brk, include.lowest = TRUE))
      ## Haldane correction, so a zero cell gives a finite odds ratio instead of
      ## dropping the draw and quietly biasing the null.
      orf <- function(prots, th = 0.05) {
        hit <- r$pval < th
        a <- sum(hit &  (r$Protein %in% prots) &  r$NRup) + .5
        b <- sum(hit &  (r$Protein %in% prots) & !r$NRup) + .5
        c2<- sum(hit & !(r$Protein %in% prots) &  r$NRup) + .5
        d2<- sum(hit & !(r$Protein %in% prots) & !r$NRup) + .5
        (a / b) / (c2 / d2)
      }
      obs <- orf(CHAPSET)
      set.seed(91)
      nul <- replicate(1000, orf(unlist(lapply(names(cells), function(cl) {
        pool <- idx[[cl]]; n <- cells[[cl]]
        if (length(pool) < n) pool else sample(pool, n) }))))
      nul <- nul[is.finite(nul)]
      pe  <- (1 + sum(nul >= obs)) / (1 + length(nul))
      cat(sprintf(paste("\nB44: 1,000 abundance-matched random sets of the same size\n",
                        "  observed odds ratio %.1f; null median %.2f, 95th percentile %.2f\n",
                        "  %d of %d random sets reach it -> empirical P = %.4f%s\n"),
                  obs, median(nul), quantile(nul, .95), sum(nul >= obs), length(nul), pe,
                  if (pe <= 1/(1+length(nul))) " (the floor: no random set came close)" else ""))
      fp <- out$P_direction[out$threshold == 0.05]
      cat(sprintf("  Fisher gave %.1e on the same table. The gap between the two is what\n", fp))
      cat(sprintf("  the independence assumption was worth here%s.\n",
                  if (is.finite(fp) && fp < pe) ", and Fisher was the optimistic one"
                  else if (is.finite(fp) && fp > pe) ", and Fisher was the conservative one"
                  else ""))
    }
  } else cat("\nB44: `det` absent, so the matched-set null was not run.\n")

  r5 <- out[out$threshold == 0.05, ]
  cat(sprintf(paste("\n  READING at 0.05: %d chaperone proteins among %d hits, %d of them NR-up.",
                    "\n  Odds ratio %.2f for direction, P = %.3f. %s\n"),
              r5$chap_hits, r5$hits, r5$chap_NRup, r5$OR_direction, r5$P_direction,
              if (is.finite(r5$P_direction) && r5$P_direction < 0.05)
                "Consistent with the set-level result -- but the same data, read with a cruder instrument."
              else "Not significant. The ranking carries information a cut-off discards; that is the expected direction of the difference."))

  RESULTS[[CO$label]] <- out
 }

  if (!length(RESULTS)) stop("B44: neither cohort could be run", call. = FALSE)
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B44_protein_level")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(RESULTS, file.path(od, "protein_level_chaperones.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, " (", length(RESULTS), " cohort(s))\n", sep = "")
  b44_protein_level <<- RESULTS
})
```

## B45 — share panel data

the data behind the replacement Figure 5b, and the ED9 joint panel

Source: `B45_share_panel_data.R`

```{r B45_share_panel_data, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B45 — the data behind the replacement Figure 5b, and the ED9 joint panel
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. Figure 5b currently plots NES against NES. Supplementary
## methods already disclaim that axis -- "Normalized enrichment scores are
## quoted and ranked here as an ordering device within that family and carry no
## effect-size interpretation; significance rests on the permutation p in every
## case" -- so a main figure whose axis the SI says means nothing quantitative
## has to go. The replacement plots a quantity with units: the share of
## microbial protein going to a set, in both cohorts, with intervals.
##
## THE COMPARABILITY TRAP, AND WHY THIS SCRIPT DOES NOT PLOT FOLD OF MEDIANS.
## The two cohorts' shares are not on one scale: 10.9% against 4.17% for the
## same set, because each cohort's protein universe is built from its own
## assembly and the two share no protein identifiers. A ratio looks scale-free
## and is not -- a fold of medians is a function of the baseline share, so
## 1.12x on treatment and 1.16x before it are not the same quantity measured
## twice, and their near-equality is substantially coincidence. What IS
## baseline-free is the quantity the model actually estimates and the
## permutation actually tests: the odds ratio of the share, exp(-gap_logit).
## This script reports both -- fold of medians as the descriptive number for
## the legend, odds ratio with its interval as the thing to plot.
##
## THE SENTENCE THIS PANEL CAN CARRY. Not "the effect sizes agree" -- two point
## estimates landing close when one interval is wide is not agreement. The
## honest and already-computed statement is that the second cohort's interval
## COVERS the first cohort's estimate: it cannot exclude an effect of that
## size. Underpowered, not absent. `covers_discovery` is that test.
##
## THREE SECTIONS, EACH INDEPENDENT. Section 1 needs the cohort objects;
## sections 2 and 3 need the draw archives that figures_v2.Rmd loads at top
## level. Run whichever the session has; each says what it is missing.
##
##   source("B45_share_panel_data.R")
## ============================================================================

## The two observed values that identify the primary arm of each cohort's run.
## These are anchors for ARM IDENTIFICATION, not results: a directory is the
## primary one if its observed COG O matches. Do not quote them from here.
PITT_PRIMARY_NES  <- -2.41
SHEBA_PRIMARY_NES <- -1.48

local({

 ## =========================================================================
 ## SECTION 1 — the share panel: 2 cohorts x 3 quantities, ONE estimator
 ## =========================================================================
 need1 <- c("OP", "OS", "chap_frac_of", "RESP_LEVELS")
 miss1 <- need1[!vapply(need1, exists, logical(1))]
 if (length(miss1)) {
   cat("B45 section 1 SKIPPED, absent: ", paste(miss1, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
 } else {

  ## The four protein sets, each from its OWN cohort's annotation. Reaching for
  ## the discovery cohort's set when the second cohort's exists is a mistake
  ## already made once in this project; the names differ by a single suffix.
  getset <- function(nm) if (exists(nm)) get(nm) else NULL
  SETS <- list(
    list(q = "chaperones", pitt = getset("chap_new"), sheba = getset("chap_new_s")),
    list(q = "ribosomal",  pitt = getset("ribo_new"), sheba = getset("ribo_new_s")))
  bad <- vapply(SETS, function(s) is.null(s$pitt) || is.null(s$sheba), logical(1))
  if (any(bad))
    cat("B45: missing protein sets for: ",
        paste(vapply(SETS[bad], `[[`, "", "q"), collapse = ", "),
        " -- those rows will be absent\n", sep = "")
  SETS <- SETS[!bad]

  ## ---- the estimator, identical for both cohorts --------------------------
  ## logit share ~ plex + response, labels shuffled WITHIN plex. This is the
  ## house perm_share() with B42's one-sided p carried alongside, so the
  ## discovery cohort's published two-sided p and the second cohort's
  ## pre-specified one-sided p both come out of the same function rather than
  ## out of two functions that are "the same model" by assertion.
  ## NO HARDCODED REFERENCE. The first version of this script set
  ## DISC_GAP <- -0.189 and compared EVERY row to it, so the ribosomal and ratio
  ## rows were tested against the chaperone coefficient -- a reference that has
  ## nothing to do with them, which made their `covers_discovery` meaningless
  ## and TRUE by accident. The reference is now each quantity's OWN
```
