```{r B45_share_panel_data, eval=FALSE}
  ## on-treatment coefficient, taken from this same run, and it is computed
  ## only for the before-treatment rows. Self-consistent, and it cannot drift
  ## from the published value because it is not a copy of it.
  est <- function(d, label, cohort, B = 10000L, seed = 7401L) {
    d <- droplevels(dplyr::filter(d, is.finite(frac), frac > 0, frac < 1))
    if (!nrow(d) || dplyr::n_distinct(d$resp) < 2L) return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(qlogis(frac) ~ Mixture + resp, d)
    nm  <- grep("^resp", names(coef(fit)), value = TRUE)
    if (length(nm) != 1L)
      stop("B45: expected one response coefficient, found ", length(nm), call. = FALSE)
    obs <- coef(fit)[[nm]]
    se  <- coef(summary(fit))[nm, "Std. Error"]
    ci  <- obs + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se
    ## ONE SEED FOR EVERY ROW, DELIBERATELY -- and a consequence worth naming.
    ## Sharing the seed makes each row reproducible and matches the house
    ## perm_share(), but it also means every row is tested against the SAME
    ## sequence of label assignments. The rows' p-values are therefore
    ## dependent, and strongly so for quantities measured on the same samples.
    ## Read them side by side; do not combine them (no Fisher's method across
    ## rows, and no "three of three agree" arithmetic).
    set.seed(seed)
    keep <- character(0)
    nl <- replicate(B, {
      rp <- factor(ave(as.character(d$resp), d$Mixture, FUN = sample), levels = RESP_LEVELS)
      keep[length(keep) + 1L] <<- paste(rp, collapse = "")
      cf <- coef(lm(qlogis(d$frac) ~ d$Mixture + rp))
      cf[[grep("^rp", names(cf))[1L]]] })
    mNR <- median(d$frac[d$resp == "NR"]); mR <- median(d$frac[d$resp == "R"])
    tibble::tibble(
      cohort = cohort, quantity = label,
      n = nrow(d), n_NR = sum(d$resp == "NR"), n_R = sum(d$resp == "R"),
      plexes = dplyr::n_distinct(d$Mixture),
      median_NR_pct = 100 * mNR, median_R_pct = 100 * mR,
      ## DESCRIPTIVE, for the legend. Baseline-dependent; do not plot.
      fold_of_medians = mNR / mR,
      ## PLOT THIS. Baseline-free, and it is what the permutation tests.
      gap_logit = obs, se = se, lo_logit = ci[1], hi_logit = ci[2],
      or_NR_over_R = exp(-obs), or_lo = exp(-ci[2]), or_hi = exp(-ci[1]),
      p_one_sided = (1 + sum(nl <= obs)) / (1 + B),
      p_two_sided = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(obs))) / (1 + B),
      distinct_perms = length(unique(keep)), floor_p = 1 / (1 + B))
  }

  ## ---- SECTION 0: is the set even comparably represented? -----------------
  ## THE RIBOSOMAL BASELINE FALLS 17.4% -> 3.2% BETWEEN COHORTS, against 9.7%
  ## -> 3.6% for chaperones. A 5.5-fold drop against a 2.7-fold one is not
  ## obviously biology: the two cohorts' protein databases are built from their
  ## own assemblies and quantified by different MS methods, so a set can be
  ## under-recovered rather than under-expressed. A share whose denominator and
  ## numerator are differently affected is not a biological quantity, and no
  ## panel should carry the row until this table says the set is comparably
  ## covered on both sides.
  cat("\nB45 SECTION 0 - set coverage in each cohort, before any share is read\n")
  inv <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(SETS, function(s) dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
    c("pitt", "sheba"), function(co) {
      O <- if (co == "pitt") OP else OS
      pr <- s[[co]]
      det <- intersect(pr, O$rd$Protein)
      tibble::tibble(cohort = if (co == "pitt") "on treatment" else "before treatment",
                     quantity = s$q, n_in_set = length(unique(pr)),
                     n_quantified = length(unique(det)),
                     ## DEFINITIONAL, NOT REASSURING. The set is built from the
                     ## cohort's OWN annotation, so every member is already a
                     ## quantified row and this is 100% by construction. It is
                     ## printed only to show the set resolved against the right
                     ## matrix; it says nothing about coverage. The column that
                     ## carries coverage is pct_of_all_rows.
                     pct_definitional = 100 * length(unique(det)) / length(unique(pr)),
                     pct_of_all_rows = 100 * length(unique(det)) / dplyr::n_distinct(O$rd$Protein))
    }))))
  print(as.data.frame(inv), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  for (q in unique(inv$quantity)) {
    v <- inv$pct_of_all_rows[inv$quantity == q]
    if (length(v) == 2L && max(v) / min(v) > 2)
      cat(sprintf(paste("  WARNING: %s occupies %.2f%% of one cohort's rows and %.2f%% of",
                        "the\n    other's, a %.1f-fold difference. Check this before reading",
                        "its share\n    difference as biology.\n"), q, v[1], v[2], max(v)/min(v)))
  }
  b45_set_inventory <<- inv

  rows <- list()
  for (s in SETS) for (co in c("pitt", "sheba")) {
    O  <- if (co == "pitt") OP else OS
    pr <- s[[co]]
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- est(chap_frac_of(O, pr), s$q,
                                     if (co == "pitt") "on treatment" else "before treatment")
  }
  ## ---- the third row: the balance between the two classes -----------------
  ## chap / (chap + ribo) per sample. A FLAT ratio is the growth-state reading:
  ## more of the community's protein goes to this machinery as a whole, rather
  ## than chaperones being selectively induced. The discovery cohort gives
  ## -0.023 (p = 0.758); the second cohort has never been asked.
  if (length(SETS) == 2L) {
    for (co in c("pitt", "sheba")) {
      O <- if (co == "pitt") OP else OS
      dc <- chap_frac_of(O, SETS[[1]][[co]]); dr <- chap_frac_of(O, SETS[[2]][[co]])
      key <- intersect(dc$sample, dr$sample)
      if (length(key) < 6L) next
      dd <- dc[match(key, dc$sample), ]
      dd$frac <- dc$frac[match(key, dc$sample)] /
                 (dc$frac[match(key, dc$sample)] + dr$frac[match(key, dr$sample)])
      rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- est(dd, "chaperone:(chaperone+ribosomal)",
                                       if (co == "pitt") "on treatment" else "before treatment")
    }
  }
  S1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)

  ## ---- does the test cohort's interval cover the discovery estimate? ------
  ## Per quantity, and only for the test cohort. "Not significant" and "cannot
  ## distinguish this from the discovery effect" are different statements and
  ## only the second is worth reporting at seven non-responders.
  S1$ref_on_treatment <- NA_real_; S1$covers_on_treatment <- NA; S1$same_sign <- NA
  for (q in unique(S1$quantity)) {
    i1 <- which(S1$quantity == q & S1$cohort == "on treatment")
    i2 <- which(S1$quantity == q & S1$cohort == "before treatment")
    if (length(i1) == 1L && length(i2) == 1L) {
      r <- S1$gap_logit[i1]
      S1$ref_on_treatment[i2]  <- r
      S1$covers_on_treatment[i2] <- S1$lo_logit[i2] <= r && r <= S1$hi_logit[i2]
      ## A WIDE INTERVAL COVERS EVERYTHING, INCLUDING ZERO. Covering the
      ## discovery estimate is only informative if the interval does NOT also
      ## sit on the opposite side of it, so the sign is reported beside it.
      S1$same_sign[i2] <- sign(S1$gap_logit[i2]) == sign(r)
    }
  }

  cat("\nB45 SECTION 1 — share of microbial protein, one estimator, both cohorts\n")
  cat("  gap_logit = R - NR on the logit scale; NEGATIVE is the predicted\n",
      "  direction. or_NR_over_R = exp(-gap_logit) > 1 is the same direction\n",
      "  and is the baseline-free quantity to PLOT.\n", sep = "")
  print(as.data.frame(S1[, c("cohort","quantity","n","n_NR","n_R","plexes",
                             "median_NR_pct","median_R_pct","fold_of_medians",
                             "or_NR_over_R","or_lo","or_hi",
                             "p_one_sided","p_two_sided")]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n  precision and whether the second cohort can exclude the first's effect:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(S1[, c("cohort","quantity","gap_logit","se","lo_logit","hi_logit",
                             "ref_on_treatment","covers_on_treatment","same_sign",
                             "distinct_perms")]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  ## ---- the row-by-row verdict, so a panel is not built on a reversal ------
  for (q in unique(S1$quantity)) {
    i2 <- which(S1$quantity == q & S1$cohort == "before treatment")
    if (length(i2) != 1L || is.na(S1$same_sign[i2])) next
    cat(sprintf("  %-32s test cohort %s the discovery direction%s\n", q,
                if (isTRUE(S1$same_sign[i2])) "AGREES with" else "REVERSES",
                if (isTRUE(S1$covers_on_treatment[i2]))
                  "; interval covers the discovery estimate" else
                  "; interval EXCLUDES the discovery estimate"))
  }

  ## ---- the comparability check, stated numerically ------------------------
  ch <- S1[S1$quantity == "chaperones", ]
  if (nrow(ch) == 2L) {
    b <- ch$median_R_pct
    cat(sprintf(paste("\n  BASELINE CHECK: the two cohorts' responder baselines are %.2f%% and",
                      "%.2f%%,\n  a %.1f-fold difference in the denominator. The folds of medians",
                      "(%.3f and\n  %.3f) are therefore NOT one quantity measured twice; the odds",
                      "ratios\n  (%.3f and %.3f) are. Plot the odds ratios; quote the folds as",
                      "description.\n"),
                b[1], b[2], max(b)/min(b), ch$fold_of_medians[1], ch$fold_of_medians[2],
                ch$or_NR_over_R[1], ch$or_NR_over_R[2]))
    i2 <- which(ch$cohort == "before treatment")
    if (length(i2) == 1L && isFALSE(ch$covers_on_treatment[i2]))
      cat("  NOTE: the second cohort EXCLUDES the discovery effect. That is a\n",
          "  different and stronger statement than a null; rewrite the text.\n", sep = "")
  }
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B45_share_panel"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  utils::write.csv(S1, file.path(od, "share_panel_rows.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(S1, file.path(od, "share_panel_rows.rds"))
  b45_share <<- S1
  cat("  written to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
 }

 ## =========================================================================
 ## SECTION 2 — the per-set scored table, both cohorts (the reviewer's ask)
 ## =========================================================================
 ## THE ARCHIVES ARE LOADED FROM DISK IF THE SESSION DOES NOT HAVE THEM.
 ## The first version required pitt_obs/sheba_obs to be in the session, which
 ## they are only inside the figures_v2.Rmd knit, so this section skipped when
 ## run from the analysis session -- for no reason, since the archives are on
 ## disk under paths$out_dir either way. The arm identification is NOT
 ## re-invented: it is the same test figures_v2.Rmd applies, a directory holding
 ## many .rds draw files plus one observed table, with the primary being the one
 ## whose observed COG O matches the pre-specified value. Choosing by directory
 ## name is what put the superseded arm (NES -1.76) in a panel once already.
 .is_arch <- function(x) {
   f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$")
   any(grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE)) &&
     sum(!grepl("^observed", f, ignore.case = TRUE)) >= 100
 }
 .obs_f  <- function(x) { f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
                          f[grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)][1] }
 .draw_f <- function(x) { f <- list.files(x, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
                          f[!grepl("^observed", basename(f), ignore.case = TRUE)] }
 .O_of   <- function(df) { if (!all(c("pathway","NES") %in% names(df))) return(NA_real_)
                           v <- df$NES[sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(df$pathway)) == "O"]
                           if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_ }
 .find <- function(key, target, tol = 0.05) {
   if (!exists("paths")) return(NA_character_)
   r <- list.dirs(paths$out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
   r <- Filter(.is_arch, r[grepl(key, r, ignore.case = TRUE)])
   if (!length(r)) return(NA_character_)
   sc <- vapply(r, function(d) {
     ob <- try(as.data.frame(readRDS(.obs_f(d))), silent = TRUE)
     if (inherits(ob, "try-error")) NA_real_ else .O_of(ob) }, 0)
   ok <- which(is.finite(sc) & abs(sc - target) <= tol)
   if (!length(ok)) { cat(sprintf("  no %s archive matched observed COG O = %.2f; found %s\n",
                                  key, target,
                                  paste(sprintf("%s (%.2f)", basename(r), sc), collapse = ", ")))
                      return(NA_character_) }
   r[ok][which.max(vapply(r[ok], function(d) length(.draw_f(d)), 0L))]
 }
 .load <- function(key, target) {
   d <- tryCatch(.find(key, target), error = function(e) NA_character_)
   if (is.na(d)) return(NULL)
   cat(sprintf("  %s archive: %s (%d draw files)\n", key, basename(d), length(.draw_f(d))))
   list(obs = as.data.frame(readRDS(.obs_f(d))),
        draws = do.call(rbind, lapply(.draw_f(d), function(f) as.data.frame(readRDS(f)))))
 }
 cat("\nB45 SECTION 2 - locating the draw archives\n")
 .P <- if (exists("pitt_obs")  && !is.null(get("pitt_obs")))
         list(obs = as.data.frame(pitt_obs),  draws = as.data.frame(pitt_draws)) else
         .load("pitt",  PITT_PRIMARY_NES)
 .S <- if (exists("sheba_obs") && !is.null(get("sheba_obs")))
         list(obs = as.data.frame(sheba_obs), draws = as.data.frame(sheba_draws)) else
         .load("sheba", SHEBA_PRIMARY_NES)
 if (is.null(.P) || is.null(.S) || is.null(.P$draws) || is.null(.S$draws)) {
   cat("  SKIPPED: could not assemble both cohorts' archives.\n")
 } else {
  pitt_obs <- .P$obs; pitt_draws <- .P$draws
  sheba_obs <- .S$obs; sheba_draws <- .S$draws
  bare <- function(x) sub("^[^:]+:", "", as.character(x))
  score <- function(obs, draws, tag) {
    o <- as.data.frame(obs); d <- as.data.frame(draws)
    o$set <- bare(o$pathway); d$set <- bare(d$pathway)
    ## STRIPPING THE PREFIX CAN COLLIDE. The full-space run names its sets
    ## "reported:O" and "COG:O", so two different rows can both bare() to "O"
    ## and the lookup below would silently take whichever came first -- the same
    ## failure mode that put the superseded Sheba arm in a panel. Refuse instead.
    o <- o[!is.na(o$set) & nzchar(o$set), , drop = FALSE]
    dup <- unique(o$set[duplicated(o$set)])
    if (length(dup))
      stop(sprintf("B45: %s observed table has %d set names that collide after stripping the prefix (%s). Resolve before scoring.",
                   tag, length(dup), paste(utils::head(dup, 6), collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
    nd <- length(unique(d$pathway))
    sp <- split(d$NES, d$set)
    res <- lapply(unique(o$set), function(s) {
      ob <- o$NES[o$set == s][1]; nu <- sp[[s]]
      if (is.null(nu) || !length(nu) || !is.finite(ob)) return(NULL)
      nu <- nu[is.finite(nu)]
      tibble::tibble(set = s, NES = ob, n_draws = length(nu),
                     null_mean = mean(nu), null_sd = sd(nu),
                     p_perm = (1 + sum(abs(nu) >= abs(ob))) / (1 + length(nu)),
                     size = if ("size" %in% names(o)) o$size[o$set == s][1] else NA_real_)
    })
    out <- dplyr::bind_rows(res)
    names(out)[-1] <- paste0(names(out)[-1], "_", tag)
    out
  }
  P <- score(pitt_obs,  pitt_draws,  "pitt")
  S <- score(sheba_obs, sheba_draws, "sheba")
  J <- dplyr::inner_join(P, S, by = "set")
  J$sign_agree <- sign(J$NES_pitt) == sign(J$NES_sheba)
  cat(sprintf("\nB45 SECTION 2 — %d sets scored in cohort 1, %d in cohort 2, %d in BOTH\n",
              nrow(P), nrow(S), nrow(J)))
  cat(sprintf("  of the %d shared, %d agree in sign (%.0f%%); Spearman of NES %+.3f\n",
              nrow(J), sum(J$sign_agree), 100 * mean(J$sign_agree),
              suppressWarnings(cor(J$NES_pitt, J$NES_sheba, method = "spearman"))))
  print(as.data.frame(J[order(J$NES_pitt),
          c("set","NES_pitt","p_perm_pitt","null_sd_pitt",
            "NES_sheba","p_perm_sheba","null_sd_sheba","sign_agree")]),
        digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B45_share_panel"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  utils::write.csv(J, file.path(od, "per_set_scored_both_cohorts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  b45_per_set <<- J
  cat("  written to ", file.path(od, "per_set_scored_both_cohorts.csv"), "\n", sep = "")

  ## =======================================================================
  ## SECTION 3 — the ED9 joint statistic, MEASURED BEFORE ANY PANEL IS DRAWN
  ## =======================================================================
  ## THE DECISION RULE IS WRITTEN HERE, BEFORE THE NUMBER IS SEEN. The last
  ## approved redesign of this panel was built, then measured, and had nothing
  ## to show. So: the ensemble supplies a SCALE, not a test -- COG O was fixed
  ## in advance and not drawn from this family, so its rank is descriptive.
  ## The panel is worth drawing only if COG O sits visibly in the joint tail.
  ## Threshold, fixed now: COG O must rank in the top 3 of the shared sets
  ## (about the 10th percentile at n = 29) under AT LEAST ONE of the two
  ## statistics. Below that the cloud is just a cloud and ED9 keeps the rank
  ## view alone.
  ##
  ## NES here is an ORDERING DEVICE, per the supplementary methods. Neither
  ## statistic below is an effect size and neither must be described as one.
  TOP_N <- 3L
  ## THE REFERENCE FAMILY IS NOT THE 29 SHARED SETS. Five of them are the
  ## paper's own constructed sets rather than COG categories -- O_chap,
  ## chaperones, O_chap_noGD, O_remainder and ribosomal -- and the first three
  ## are near-duplicates of the pre-specified target itself. Ranked against all
  ## 29, COG O comes third on the signed product and the two sets above it are
  ## O_chap and chaperones: the target outranked by copies of itself. That is
  ## not a reference distribution, and a reviewer sees it immediately.
  ##
  ## The reference is therefore the COG CATEGORIES only: the single-letter
  ## categories plus the merged codes (KOs sitting in several categories, which
  ## are additional sets rather than copies of the target). Dropping the merged
  ## codes as well changes nothing, and is reported as a sensitivity. Keeping
  ## them is the conservative choice because there is more to beat.
  .kind <- function(x) ifelse(grepl("_", x) | grepl("[a-z]", x), "constructed",
                       ifelse(nchar(x) == 1L, "single", "merged"))
  J$kind <- .kind(J$set)
  cat(sprintf("\n  family: %d single-letter categories, %d merged codes, %d constructed (%s)\n",
              sum(J$kind == "single"), sum(J$kind == "merged"), sum(J$kind == "constructed"),
              paste(J$set[J$kind == "constructed"], collapse = ", ")))
  cat("  the constructed sets are EXCLUDED from the reference; the target is not\n",
      "  ranked against variants of itself.\n", sep = "")
  J$joint_product <- J$NES_pitt * J$NES_sheba          # positive = agreeing
  J$joint_minabs  <- ifelse(J$sign_agree,
                            pmin(abs(J$NES_pitt), abs(J$NES_sheba)), 0)
  ## THE TWO STATISTICS ARE NOT THE SAME REFERENCE AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.
  ## The signed product is restricted to pairs that agree AND point to
  ## non-responders, because a signed product is maximised equally by two large
  ## responder-side scores, which would outrank the target for the wrong
  ## reason. min(|NES|) is restricted only by sign concordance, so sets that
  ## agree in the RESPONDER direction stay in its reference distribution. That
  ## makes min(|NES|) the stricter of the two -- there is more to beat -- so a
  ## top rank under it is the stronger statement and the one to quote.
  J$joint_product <- ifelse(J$sign_agree & J$NES_pitt < 0, J$joint_product, 0)
  rk <- function(v) rank(-v, ties.method = "min")
  ## Ranks are computed WITHIN the reference family; the constructed sets keep
  ## their statistics for the CSV but take no rank and crowd no one out.
  REF <- J$kind %in% c("single", "merged")
  J$rank_product <- NA_integer_; J$rank_minabs <- NA_integer_
  J$rank_product[REF] <- rk(J$joint_product[REF])
  J$rank_minabs[REF]  <- rk(J$joint_minabs[REF])
  N_REF <- sum(REF)
  iO <- which(J$set == "O")
  cat("\nB45 SECTION 3 — the joint statistic, and where the pre-specified set falls\n")
  if (!length(iO)) {
    cat("  COG O is NOT among the shared sets under the name \"O\". Shared set names:\n  ",
        paste(utils::head(sort(J$set), 40), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(paste("  signed product, agreeing pairs only: COG O ranks %d of %d",
                      "(%.0fth percentile)\n  min(|NES|) with sign concordance:  COG O ranks",
                      "%d of %d (%.0fth percentile)\n"),
                J$rank_product[iO], N_REF, 100 * J$rank_product[iO] / N_REF,
                J$rank_minabs[iO],  N_REF, 100 * J$rank_minabs[iO]  / N_REF))
    ## HOW FAR CLEAR IS IT? A rank of 1 against a runner-up 2% behind is a very
    ## different panel from a rank of 1 against one 2x behind, and only the
    ## second is worth a figure.
    .nz <- sort(J$joint_product[REF][J$joint_product[REF] > 0], decreasing = TRUE)
    if (length(.nz) > 1L && J$rank_product[iO] == 1L)
      cat(sprintf("  COG O leads the runner-up by %.1fx on the signed product\n",
                  .nz[1] / .nz[2]))
    ## The sensitivity: single letters only.
    S <- J$kind == "single"
    cat(sprintf("  sensitivity, single-letter categories only (n = %d): ranks %d and %d\n",
                sum(S), rk(J$joint_product[S])[which(J$set[S] == "O")],
                rk(J$joint_minabs[S])[which(J$set[S] == "O")]))
    pass <- min(J$rank_product[iO], J$rank_minabs[iO]) <= TOP_N
    ## THE THRESHOLD WAS FIXED AT TOP-3 AGAINST 29 SETS AND IS NOT RETUNED NOW
    ## THAT THE FAMILY IS SMALLER. Top-3 of a smaller family is a slightly more
    ## lenient percentile; it is left alone because moving a threshold after
    ## seeing the answer is the error this rule exists to prevent.
    cat(sprintf(paste("\n  VERDICT against the rule fixed above (top %d of %d):",
                      "%s.\n  %s\n"), TOP_N, N_REF,
                if (pass) "PASS" else "FAIL",
                if (pass)
                  paste("Draw the ED9 joint panel. Legend must say the ensemble",
                        "supplies a scale and not a test, because COG O was fixed",
                        "in advance rather than selected from this family.")
                else
                  paste("Do NOT draw it. The pre-specified set is not in the joint",
                        "tail, so the panel would show a cloud with a marked point",
                        "in the middle of it -- which argues against the paper.",
                        "Keep ED9 as the rank view and leave the ensemble result",
                        "in the text, where v66 already states it.")))
    JR <- J[REF, ]
    print(as.data.frame(JR[order(-JR$joint_minabs),
            c("set","kind","NES_pitt","NES_sheba","sign_agree","joint_minabs","joint_product")])[1:min(8, nrow(JR)), ],
          digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  utils::write.csv(J, file.path(od, "per_set_scored_both_cohorts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  b45_per_set <<- J
 }
})
```

## B46 — ptr feasibility

does PREREG_ptr.md §4f fire? A coverage-dropout check, no mapping

Source: `B46_ptr_feasibility.R`

```{r B46_ptr_feasibility, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B46 — does PREREG_ptr.md §4f fire? A coverage-dropout check, no mapping
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. Reviewer 5 proposes the replication-rate test as the one
## open item that could add evidence rather than close a hole. The test is
## already pre-registered -- PREREG_ptr.md, filed 18 Sep 2026 -- and was CLOSED
## on 22 Sep WITHOUT BEING RUN, because its motivating result (the
## Bacillota-internal ribosomal elevation) had dissolved. His version points it
## at the chaperone share instead, which is a different motivation and not
## obviously refuted. So the question is live again, and it costs weeks to
## answer by mapping.
##
## It may not need weeks. The pre-registration already names the thing most
## likely to kill it, in §4f:
##
##   "Bacteroidota is 25.8% in non-responders against 38.2% in responders, so
##    Bacteroidota species will have systematically lower coverage in
##    non-responders, and whether a species yields a PTR estimate is itself
##    response-associated for exactly the taxa the compositional question
##    concerns."
##
## with the reading fixed in advance:
##
##   "coverage dropout strongly response-associated -> the comparison is
##    confounded at source; report the dropout and treat any PTR difference as
##    uninterpretable."
##
## That is answerable from the MetaPhlAn profiles that already exist. No
## Bowtie2 index, no CoPTR, no mapping.
##
## THIS CHECK IS OPTIMISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS WORTH
## RUNNING. Relative abundance >= 0.305% is the pre-registration's own proxy
## for 5x coverage (§3: 19.1 M paired reads x 2 x 150 bp / 3.5 Mb). CoPTR's
## real criteria -- bin counts, coverage evenness -- are STRICTER, so every
## species counted here is an upper bound on what would survive mapping. A
## FAILURE here is therefore decisive; a PASS is only permission to file a new
## pre-registration, never permission to claim anything.
##
## IT LOOKS AT RESPONSE, AND THAT IS DECLARED. The original §3 feasibility was
## computed without response information. This one cannot be: dropout BY ARM is
## the quantity §4f asks for. It does not touch PTR, which does not exist yet,
## so it reveals nothing about the outcome -- but any new pre-registration must
## record that this was run and known before filing, not present itself as
## outcome-blind.
##
## THE RULE IS FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS.
##
##   NO-GO if EITHER
##     (a) the per-sample count of qualifying species differs by arm at
##         two-sided p < 0.05 (Wilcoxon rank-sum), or
##     (b) fewer than 7 of the 10 pre-specified species have >= 8 samples
##         clearing threshold in BOTH arms (§4f's own "not testable" floor).
##   GO otherwise, meaning only that §4f's trigger does not fire and the
##   primary endpoint is estimable.
##
##   source("B46_ptr_feasibility.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

 ## ---- 1. inputs, located rather than assumed -----------------------------
 ## Paths come from the project's own files. MG is defined in analysis_v17 §12;
 ## if that chunk has run, use it, otherwise search the usual places and say
 ## which was taken.
 PCT <- 0.305                     # §3: relative abundance giving 5x at 19.1 M reads
 find_one <- function(cands, what) {
   hit <- cands[file.exists(cands)]
   if (!length(hit)) stop("B46: no ", what, " found. Tried:\n  ",
                          paste(cands, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
   cat(sprintf("  %-22s %s\n", what, hit[1])); hit[1]
 }
 root <- if (exists("paths") && !is.null(paths$root)) paths$root else getwd()
 cat("B46: inputs\n")
 f_mpa <- find_one(c(
   if (exists("MG_FILES")) MG_FILES$mpa,
   file.path(root, "Data_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt_metagenomics", "Pitt",
             "merged_metaphlan_profile.txt")), "MetaPhlAn profile")
 f_samp <- find_one(file.path(root, "Results_v8", "ptr_samples_5M.txt"),
                    "76-sample list")
 f_sp   <- find_one(file.path(root, "Results_v8", "ptr_primary_species.txt"),
                    "10 primary species")
 f_cln  <- find_one(file.path(root, "pitt_clinical_metadata.tsv"), "clinical table")

 samp10 <- readLines(f_samp); samp10 <- samp10[nzchar(samp10)]
 sp10   <- readLines(f_sp);   sp10   <- sp10[nzchar(sp10)]
 stopifnot(length(sp10) == 10L)
 cat(sprintf("  %d samples, %d pre-specified species, threshold %.3f%%\n",
             length(samp10), length(sp10), PCT))

 ## ---- 2. the abundance matrix, species rows only -------------------------
 mpa <- as.data.frame(readr::read_tsv(f_mpa, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE))
 names(mpa)[1] <- "clade"
 mpa <- mpa[grepl("\\|s__", mpa$clade) & !grepl("\\|t__", mpa$clade), , drop = FALSE]
 mpa$species <- sub("^.*\\|s__", "", mpa$clade)
 ## THE PRE-SPECIFIED TEN MUST ALL BE PRESENT. A silently missing name would
 ## read as a species that never clears threshold, which is a different claim.
 absent <- setdiff(sp10, mpa$species)
 if (length(absent))
   stop("B46: ", length(absent), " of the 10 pre-specified species are not in ",
        "the profile at all: ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "),
        ". Resolve the naming before reading anything below.", call. = FALSE)

 ## COLUMN NAMES CARRY A PIPELINE PREFIX. The profile's columns are
 ## "trimmed_MF0015pGTSH10d20221212" while the pre-registered sample list holds
 ## "MF0015pGTSH10d20221212". Matching on the raw names found 0 of 76, and the
 ## first version of this script carried on regardless and printed a table of
 ## zeros -- which reads exactly like total coverage failure. Normalise, then
 ## require the match.
 .norm <- function(x) sub("^trimmed_", "", x)
 cn    <- .norm(names(mpa))
 idx   <- match(samp10, cn)
 if (anyNA(idx)) {            # fall back to substring matching before giving up
   miss <- which(is.na(idx))
   for (i in miss) {
     hit <- which(grepl(samp10[i], cn, fixed = TRUE))
     if (length(hit) == 1L) idx[i] <- hit
   }
 }
 if (all(is.na(idx)))
   stop("B46: none of the ", length(samp10), " PTR samples match a column in\n  ",
        f_mpa, "\n  profile columns look like: ",
        paste(utils::head(cn[-1], 3), collapse = ", "),
        "\n  Resolve the naming before reading anything below.", call. = FALSE)
 if (anyNA(idx))
   cat(sprintf("  NOTE: %d of %d PTR samples have no column here: %s\n",
               sum(is.na(idx)), length(samp10),
               paste(utils::head(samp10[is.na(idx)], 5), collapse = ", ")))
 cols   <- names(mpa)[idx[!is.na(idx)]]
 samp_k <- samp10[!is.na(idx)]
 cat(sprintf("  matched %d of %d PTR samples to profile columns\n",
             length(cols), length(samp10)))
 M <- as.matrix(mpa[match(sp10, mpa$species), cols, drop = FALSE])
 storage.mode(M) <- "double"; M[!is.finite(M)] <- 0
 rownames(M) <- sp10

 ## ---- 3. response labels --------------------------------------------------
 ## The profile's columns are run-level ids (MF0017pGTSH10d20221212); the
 ## clinical table keys on BioReplicate (MF0017). Strip the run suffix.
 ## PREFER THE SESSION'S CURATED MAP. pitt_clinical_metadata.tsv keys on
 ## BioReplicate, but the run ids carry suffixes ("MF1172_S16") and one entry is
 ## still under the corrupted name MF001A3A817 that §0a resolves to MF0017. A
 ## naive sub() join loses a third of the cohort, which would put this verdict
 ## on 40 samples while the pre-registration counts 68. If v17's curated table
 ## is in the session, use it.
 .sess <- NULL
 for (nm in c("pitt_meta", "pitt_clin", "pitt_clinical")) {
   if (exists(nm) && is.data.frame(get(nm))) { .sess <- get(nm); break }
 }
 ## PREFER THE SESSION TABLE, BUT DO NOT INSIST ON IT. The first version took
 ## whichever curated object it found and then stopped dead if that object did
 ## not happen to use the column names it knew -- which is what §0a's pitt_meta
 ## does, having resolved the duplicate response columns into its own naming.
 ## A preference that becomes a hard failure is worse than no preference, so an
 ## unusable session table now falls through to the file and says it did.
 .RC <- c("Response_mg", "Response_PFS_12", "resp", "Response", "response",
          "best_response", "Condition_bin", "Condition")
 .KC <- c("BioReplicate", "MF_ID", "norm_id", "sample", "Sample", "BioReplicate_norm")
 .usable <- function(d) !is.na(intersect(.RC, names(d))[1]) &&
                        !is.na(intersect(.KC, names(d))[1])
 if (!is.null(.sess) && !.usable(.sess)) {
   cat(sprintf(paste("  session table found but unusable (no response/key pair);",
                     "its columns are:\n    %s\n  falling back to %s\n"),
               paste(utils::head(names(.sess), 14), collapse = ", "), basename(f_cln)))
   .sess <- NULL
 }
 cln <- if (!is.null(.sess)) .sess else
        as.data.frame(readr::read_tsv(f_cln, show_col_types = FALSE))
 cat(sprintf("  response table: %s\n",
             if (!is.null(.sess)) "session object (curated)" else basename(f_cln)))
 rc  <- intersect(.RC, names(cln))[1]
 kc  <- intersect(.KC, names(cln))[1]
 if (is.na(rc) || is.na(kc))
   stop("B46: no response/key column pair in ", basename(f_cln),
        ". Columns are: ", paste(utils::head(names(cln), 14), collapse = ", "),
        call. = FALSE)
 cat(sprintf("  keyed on '%s', response from '%s'\n", kc, rc))
 ## Strip the run suffix, then the _S## lane suffix, then try the raw id too.
 bio  <- sub("p[A-Z].*$", "", samp_k)
 bio2 <- sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", bio)
 j    <- match(bio, cln[[kc]]); j2 <- match(bio2, cln[[kc]])
 j[is.na(j)] <- j2[is.na(j)]
 resp <- cln[[rc]][j]
 cat(sprintf("  response column '%s', levels: %s\n", rc,
             paste(sort(unique(na.omit(resp))), collapse = ", ")))
 keep <- !is.na(resp)
 if (any(!keep))
   cat(sprintf("  %d sample(s) without a response label, excluded by §4a: %s\n",
               sum(!keep), paste(utils::head(bio[!keep], 6), collapse = ", ")))
 M <- M[, keep, drop = FALSE]; resp <- resp[keep]
 ## normalise to NR / R without guessing: anything matching "non" is NR.
 g <- ifelse(grepl("non|^NR$|progress", resp, ignore.case = TRUE), "NR", "R")
 cat(sprintf("  %d labelled samples: %d NR, %d R\n", length(g), sum(g=="NR"), sum(g=="R")))
 ## THE PRE-REGISTRATION COUNTS 68 LABELLED OF 76 (§4a). Materially fewer means
 ## the join is broken, not that the cohort shrank -- and a verdict computed on
 ## a third of the samples, selected by whichever ids happened to match, is
 ## worse than no verdict. Report the dropout, then refuse.
 .JOIN_FLOOR <- 60L
 if (length(g) < .JOIN_FLOOR) {
   cat(sprintf(paste("\n  JOIN INCOMPLETE: %d labelled, against the %d the",
                     "pre-registration counts.\n  Unmatched ids look like: %s\n",
                     "  Run this inside the session that holds v17's curated",
                     "sample table,\n  or fix the join first. NO VERDICT is",
                     "issued below.\n"), length(g), 68L,
               paste(utils::head(bio[is.na(resp)], 6), collapse = ", ")))
   .WITHHOLD <<- TRUE
 } else .WITHHOLD <<- FALSE
 ## AN EMPTY TABLE IS NOT A PASSING TEST. min(table(g)) on zero rows returns
 ## Inf with a warning, so the first version sailed past this guard with no
 ## labelled samples at all and failed later inside wilcox.test, where the
 ## error named the wrong cause.
 if (!length(g) || length(unique(g)) < 2L || min(table(g)) < 8L)
   stop("B46: need >= 8 labelled samples in each arm; have ",
        if (!length(g)) "none" else paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(table(g)), table(g)),
                                          collapse = ", "),
        ". Check the response join before reading anything below.", call. = FALSE)

 ## ---- 4. §4f: per-species dropout by arm ---------------------------------
 Q <- M >= PCT                                  # qualifies at the 5x proxy
 per_sp <- data.frame(
   species = sp10,
   n_NR = rowSums(Q[, g == "NR", drop = FALSE]),
   n_R  = rowSums(Q[, g == "R",  drop = FALSE]),
   row.names = NULL)
 per_sp$pct_NR <- 100 * per_sp$n_NR / sum(g == "NR")
 per_sp$pct_R  <- 100 * per_sp$n_R  / sum(g == "R")
 ## §4f: "any species with fewer than 8 valid estimates in either arm is
 ## reported as NOT TESTABLE, not as null."
 per_sp$testable <- per_sp$n_NR >= 8 & per_sp$n_R >= 8
 ## Per-species dropout association, reported for completeness. Not the rule.
 per_sp$p_fisher <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(per_sp)), function(i)
   stats::fisher.test(matrix(c(per_sp$n_NR[i], sum(g=="NR") - per_sp$n_NR[i],
                               per_sp$n_R[i],  sum(g=="R")  - per_sp$n_R[i]),
                             2, 2))$p.value, 0)
 cat("\nB46 §4f — how many samples clear the 5x proxy, per species, per arm\n")
 print(per_sp, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
 n_testable <- sum(per_sp$testable)
 cat(sprintf("  %d of 10 species are testable (>= 8 in BOTH arms)\n", n_testable))

 ## ---- 5. the aggregate endpoint's support, per sample --------------------
 cnt <- colSums(Q)
 w   <- suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(cnt ~ factor(g)))
 cat("\nB46 — species clearing threshold per sample, the aggregate endpoint's base\n")
 cat(sprintf("  NR: median %.1f (range %d-%d)   R: median %.1f (range %d-%d)\n",
             median(cnt[g=="NR"]), min(cnt[g=="NR"]), max(cnt[g=="NR"]),
             median(cnt[g=="R"]),  min(cnt[g=="R"]),  max(cnt[g=="R"])))
 cat(sprintf("  two-sided Wilcoxon on the per-sample count: P = %.4f\n", w$p.value))
 cat(sprintf("  samples contributing fewer than 3 of the 10: %d NR, %d R\n",
             sum(cnt[g=="NR"] < 3), sum(cnt[g=="R"] < 3)))

 ## ---- 6. the verdict, against the rule fixed in the header ---------------
 fail_a <- is.finite(w$p.value) && w$p.value < 0.05
 fail_b <- n_testable < 7
 if (isTRUE(.WITHHOLD)) {
   cat("\nB46 VERDICT WITHHELD — the response join is incomplete; see above.\n",
       "  The dropout table printed above is still informative about which\n",
       "  species clear threshold at all, but its arm counts are not the\n",
       "  cohort's and must not be read as §4f's answer.\n", sep = "")
   return(invisible(NULL))
 }
 cat("\nB46 VERDICT against the rule fixed above the numbers\n")
 cat(sprintf("  (a) per-sample count differs by arm at P < 0.05 : %s (P = %.4f)\n",
             if (fail_a) "YES -> NO-GO" else "no", w$p.value))
 cat(sprintf("  (b) fewer than 7 of 10 species testable          : %s (%d testable)\n",
             if (fail_b) "YES -> NO-GO" else "no", n_testable))
 if (fail_a || fail_b) {
   cat("\n  NO-GO. PREREG_ptr.md §4f's condition is met, and its reading was\n",
       "  fixed before any data were seen: the comparison is confounded at\n",
       "  source and a PTR difference would be uninterpretable. This is the\n",
       "  answer to the reviewer, in his own currency -- the test cannot add\n",
       "  evidence here, and the pre-registration said so in advance.\n", sep = "")
 } else {
   cat("\n  GO, in the narrow sense only: §4f's trigger does not fire and the\n",
       "  primary endpoint is estimable. This is permission to FILE A NEW\n",
       "  PRE-REGISTRATION naming the chaperone-share prediction, before any\n",
       "  mapping -- not permission to reopen the closed one, and not a result.\n",
       "  Remember this check is optimistic: CoPTR's criteria are stricter than\n",
       "  a relative-abundance threshold, so these counts are upper bounds.\n", sep = "")
 }
 od <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(), "B46_ptr_feasibility")
 dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
 utils::write.csv(per_sp, file.path(od, "dropout_by_species.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 saveRDS(list(per_species = per_sp, per_sample_count = cnt, arm = g,
              wilcox_p = w$p.value, n_testable = n_testable,
              threshold_pct = PCT, verdict = if (fail_a || fail_b) "NO-GO" else "GO"),
         file.path(od, "ptr_feasibility.rds"))
 cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
 b46_ptr_feasibility <<- per_sp
})
```

## B47 — sheba species

Sheba metagenome at species level: is the omnibus separation carried

Source: `B47_sheba_species.R`

```{r B47_sheba_species, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B47 — Sheba metagenome at species level: is the omnibus separation carried
## by an identifiable taxon, and is a species-level answer even ESTIMABLE at
## the sequencing depth this cohort was built on?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. B16's header states the limit plainly: "the manuscript
## tests the metagenome at phylum level only." B15 then reports that the Sheba
## pre-treatment profiles separate by response (pseudo-F 1.377, R2 0.041,
## P = 0.0320 within ME/S) while no published taxon replicates, and that the
## separation survives removing the published taxa (P = 0.0295). A reader --
## and a reviewer -- will ask which species carries it. Nothing in the
## manuscript answers that.
##
## THIS IS POST HOC AND IS DECLARED AS SUCH. It sits in the same family as
## B15's own section [3], written after seeing the separation. It is not
## pre-registered, cannot be, and is reported as a descriptive follow-up to a
## single omnibus P of 0.032. No sentence below is licensed to read as
## discovery.
##
## TWO FAILURE MODES ARE ALREADY KNOWN, AND BOTH HAVE BEEN HIT ONCE EACH IN
## THIS PROJECT. They are why this script exists in this form rather than as a
## call to MaAsLin3 on the merged table.
##
##   [1] THE SET. B15's Sheba design is not §10e's `sh_set`. It is built by
##       matching SAMP_PRIMARY's BioReplicate to the library PREFIX, then
##       deduplicated to one library per prefix preferring the S series --
##       34 libraries, NR 8 / R 26, series ME 3/7 and S 5/19. §10e's sh_set is
##       33 patients (NR 7, R 26) and sh_set5 is 32 (NR 6, R 26); neither is
##       the set the omnibus P refers to. A set rebuilt by hand on 15 Oct 2026
##       kept both libraries of one probe, produced an NR group that was not
##       B15's, and returned a richness difference at P = 0.062 where B15's own
##       alpha diversity gives P = 0.3956. The reconstruction is therefore NOT
##       attempted here: the design block below is copied verbatim from B15 and
##       then ASSERTED against B15's printed set. If the assertion fails,
##       nothing below is comparable to the omnibus and the script stops.
##
##   [2] THE TRANSFORM. log(x + pseudo-count) on a MetaPhlAn matrix turns
##       presence/absence into effect sizes of 5 to 8 log units, and a scan run
##       that way on 15 Oct 2026 returned 13 BH survivors, every one of which
##       decomposed to prevalence with abundance-if-present at P = 0.15 to 1.00.
##       MaAsLin3 exists partly to avoid this -- it fits prevalence separately
##       for this reason -- so the two questions are asked separately here and
##       no pseudo-count is taken anywhere.
##
## AND ONE THAT IS NOT YET IN THE MANUSCRIPT. The two sequencing series differ
## in depth by a factor of four (ME median 34.1 M reads, S median 135.0 M,
## MWU P = 3.6e-05), and within the ME series richness still tracks depth
## (Spearman rho = +0.841, P = 3.4e-06 across all 20 ME libraries; +0.814
## dropping the 3.8 M library, +0.827 restricted to >= 20 M) while within the S
## series it is flat (rho = -0.008, P = 0.97). Seventeen of the twenty ME
## libraries sit below the S series' 25th percentile. Richness has NOT
## saturated in the ME half. B15's within-series permutation restriction
## already handles this for the omnibus; a species-level PREVALENCE scan that
## pools the series does not, and would read sequencing depth across the ten ME
## libraries in the set. So depth is measured first and the gate below is
## applied before any species is named.
##
## THE RULES ARE FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS.
##
##   G0  TESTED SET, declared before testing: species present in >= 4 and
##       <= 30 of the 34 libraries (10% to 90% prevalence). A species present
##       everywhere or almost nowhere carries no information at this n and
##       inflating the BH denominator with it is not conservative, it is noise.
##
##   G1  DEPTH GATE. If richness tracks depth within a series at P < 0.05 with
##       |rho| >= 0.5, that series is depth-limited for presence/absence. A
##       prevalence survivor is then reported ONLY if it also survives in the
##       saturated series alone. This gate is evaluated and printed whether or
##       not anything survives.
##
##   G2  PRIMARY SCAN, PREVALENCE. Presence/absence by response, STRATIFIED BY
##       SERIES: exact conditional test on the 2 x 2 x 2 table
##       (mantelhaen.test, exact = TRUE). BH across the tested set.
##
##   G3  SECONDARY SCAN, ABUNDANCE GIVEN PRESENCE. Among libraries where the
##       species is present, within-series rank-standardised abundance,
##       Wilcoxon by response, requiring >= 3 present per arm. BH across the
##       species that qualify. This is the question MaAsLin3's abundance model
##       asks, and it is asked on the samples where the quantity exists.
##
##   G4  READING, fixed before the numbers. If nothing survives BH in G2 or G3,
##       the reported sentence is that the separation is not carried by an
##       identifiable species at this n -- NOT that there is no species effect,
##       which 8 non-responders cannot address. If something survives G2, it is
##       reported only after G1. A G3 survivor with no G2 signal is the only
##       shape that would justify naming a taxon as differentially abundant.
##       A null here does not retract the omnibus and the omnibus does not
##       license a taxon.
##
##   source("B47_sheba_species.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

 need <- function(p) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE))
   stop("B47 needs ", p, call. = FALSE)
 need("readr")

 ## ---- 1. the species matrix and the design: COPIED VERBATIM FROM B15 ------
 ## Every line in this block is B15_omnibus.R's, unchanged. It is duplicated
 ## rather than refactored so that B47 cannot drift from the set the omnibus P
 ## was computed on, and so that a reader can diff the two.
 if (!exists("sh_mpa_raw"))
   stop("B47: sh_mpa_raw is not in the session. Knit analysis_v17.Rmd ",
        "through the Sheba metagenome chunks first.", call. = FALSE)

 sp_matrix <- function(f, cleaner) {
   h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
   t <- read.delim(f, skip = if (is.na(h)) 1 else h - 1, check.names = FALSE,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"
   sel <- grepl("\\|s__", t$clade_name) & !grepl("\\|t__", t$clade_name)
   if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
   X <- as.matrix(t[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
   rownames(X) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", t$clade_name[sel])
   M <- t(X); rownames(M) <- cleaner(rownames(M))
   M[, colSums(M, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, drop = FALSE]
 }
 sp_from_df <- function(df, cleaner) {
   tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
   write.table(df, tf, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
   on.exit(unlink(tf), add = TRUE)
   sp_matrix(tf, cleaner)
 }
 Ms <- sp_from_df(sh_mpa_raw,
         function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x))
 if (is.null(Ms)) stop("B47: no species rows in sh_mpa_raw.", call. = FALSE)
 mg_keys <- rownames(Ms)

 SP <- if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY"))
         tryCatch(as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
 if (!is.null(SP) && "cohort" %in% names(SP))
   SP <- SP[SP$cohort %in% c("sheba", "Sheba"), , drop = FALSE]
 cand <- list()
 if (!is.null(SP) && "resp" %in% names(SP) && length(mg_keys)) {
   pref <- sub("_.*$", "", mg_keys)
   for (cl in names(SP)) {
     v <- as.character(SP[[cl]]); if (all(is.na(v))) next
     hit_full <- sum(v %in% mg_keys); hit_pref <- sum(v %in% pref)
     if (hit_full >= 12) {
       d <- data.frame(mg = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% mg_keys, ]
       cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl)]] <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), ]
     } else if (hit_pref >= 12) {
       m <- data.frame(pref = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% pref, ]
       m <- m[!duplicated(m$pref), ]
       d <- data.frame(mg = mg_keys, pref = pref)
       d <- merge(d, m, by = "pref")[, c("mg", "resp")]
       cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl, " (prefix)")]] <- d
     }
   }
 }
 f12 <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(),
                  "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
 if (file.exists(f12)) {
   pr <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)
   if (all(c("sample", "mg") %in% names(pr))) {
     if (!is.null(SP) && all(c("sample", "resp") %in% names(SP))) {
       d <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
                  data.frame(sample = SP$sample, resp = as.character(SP$resp)),
                  by = "sample")
       cand[["B12 pairs + SAMP_PRIMARY"]] <- d[, c("mg", "resp")]
     }
     if (exists("OS")) {
       d <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
                  data.frame(sample = OS$d$sample, resp = as.character(OS$d$resp)),
                  by = "sample")
       cand[["B12 pairs + OS$d"]] <- d[, c("mg", "resp")]
     }
   }
 }
 score <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$resp) & d$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
   d <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), , drop = FALSE]
   tb <- table(droplevels(factor(d$resp)))
   if (!nrow(d) || length(tb) < 2) return(c(0, 0))
   c(nrow(d), min(tb)) }
 if (!length(cand))
   stop("B47: no Sheba design candidate. SAMP_PRIMARY absent and B12's pairs ",
        "not on disk -- the same inputs B15 needs.", call. = FALSE)
 sc <- t(vapply(cand, score, c(0, 0))); colnames(sc) <- c("libraries", "smaller_group")
 cat("B47: Sheba design candidates (must match B15's table)\n"); print(sc)
 best <- order(-sc[, 2], -sc[, 1])[1]
 cat("  using: ", rownames(sc)[best], "\n", sep = "")
 sd <- cand[[best]]
 sd <- sd[!is.na(sd$resp) & sd$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
 sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$mg), , drop = FALSE]
 sd$patient <- sub("_.*$", "", sd$mg)
 sd$series  <- ifelse(grepl("_ME", sd$mg), "ME", "S")
 nlib <- nrow(sd)
 sd <- sd[order(sd$patient, sd$series != "S"), , drop = FALSE]
 sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$patient), , drop = FALSE]
 cat(sprintf("  %d of %d libraries dropped as repeat tubes from the same patient\n",
             nlib - nrow(sd), nlib))

 ## ---- 2. ASSERT THE SET IS B15'S -----------------------------------------
 ## B15's printed set, 15 Oct 2026 (final_run/reanalysis_run_55c.log, l. 44-55):
 ##   34 of 46 libraries matched, 1 of 35 dropped as a repeat tube,
 ##   NR 8 / R 26, series x response  ME 3/7 and S 5/19.
 i   <- intersect(rownames(Ms), sd$mg)
 g   <- sd$resp[match(i, sd$mg)]
 ser <- sd$series[match(i, sd$mg)]
 tb  <- table(series = ser, resp = g)
 cat(sprintf("\nB47: %d libraries matched; NR %d / R %d\n",
             length(i), sum(g == "NR"), sum(g == "R")))
 print(tb)
 EXP <- matrix(c(3L, 5L, 7L, 19L), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("ME", "S"), c("NR", "R")))
 same <- identical(dim(tb), dim(EXP)) &&
         identical(dimnames(tb)$series, rownames(EXP)) &&
         identical(dimnames(tb)$resp,   colnames(EXP)) &&
         all(as.vector(tb) == as.vector(EXP))
 if (!same) {
   cat("\nB47 STOPPED. The set is NOT B15's.\n",
       "  expected  ME 3 NR / 7 R  and  S 5 NR / 19 R  (34 libraries)\n",
       "  got the table above. Every number below would be computed on a\n",
       "  different cohort from the omnibus P = 0.0320 it is meant to explain,\n",
       "  which is exactly the error this assertion exists to catch.\n", sep = "")
   return(invisible(NULL))
 }
 cat("  set matches B15. Proceeding.\n")

 ## ---- 3. depth, and the G1 gate ------------------------------------------
 dep <- NULL
 if (exists("sh_mg_meta") && all(c("raw", "reads") %in% names(sh_mg_meta))) {
   dep <- data.frame(mg = sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1",
                              as.character(sh_mg_meta$raw)),
                     reads = as.numeric(sh_mg_meta$reads))
   cat("\nB47: depth from sh_mg_meta (session)\n")
 } else if (exists("SH_FILES") && !is.null(SH_FILES$prof) && dir.exists(SH_FILES$prof)) {
   pf <- list.files(SH_FILES$prof, "\\.metaphlan\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
   dep <- data.frame(
     mg = sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1",
              sub("\\.metaphlan\\.txt$", "", basename(pf))),
     reads = vapply(pf, function(f) {
       l <- grep("reads processed", readLines(f, n = 12, warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)
       if (!length(l)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", l[1])) }, 0,
       USE.NAMES = FALSE))
   cat("\nB47: depth read from", length(pf), "MetaPhlAn profile headers\n")
 } else {
   f <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$root else getwd(),
                  "sheba_mg_reads_processed.tsv")
   if (file.exists(f)) {
     d0 <- read.delim(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
     dep <- data.frame(mg = sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1",
                                d0$library),
                       reads = as.numeric(d0$reads_processed))
     cat("\nB47: depth from", f, "\n")
   }
 }
 Mi  <- Ms[i, , drop = FALSE]
 ric <- rowSums(Mi > 0)
 Pm  <- Mi / rowSums(Mi)
 shn <- apply(Pm, 1, function(x) { x <- x[x > 0]; -sum(x * log(x)) })
 gate_me <- gate_s <- NA
 if (!is.null(dep)) {
   dep <- dep[!duplicated(dep$mg) & !is.na(dep$reads), , drop = FALSE]
   rd  <- dep$reads[match(i, dep$mg)]
   if (anyNA(rd))
     cat("  NOTE: no read count for", sum(is.na(rd)), "of", length(i), "libraries\n")
   lo <- rd < 5e6
   if (any(lo, na.rm = TRUE))
     cat(sprintf(paste0("  NOTE: %d library(s) in B15's set are below the 5M ",
                        "read floor that section 10e's sh_set5 applies: %s\n"),
                 sum(lo, na.rm = TRUE),
                 paste(sprintf("%s (%s reads)", i[which(lo)],
                               formatC(rd[which(lo)], big.mark = ",", format = "d")),
                       collapse = ", ")))
   cat("\n  depth and richness within series (the G1 gate)\n")
   gg <- data.frame(mg = i, series = ser, resp = g, reads = rd,
                    richness = as.numeric(ric), shannon = as.numeric(shn))
   for (s in c("ME", "S")) {
     k <- gg$series == s & is.finite(gg$reads)
     if (sum(k) < 5) next
     ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(gg$richness[k], gg$reads[k], method = "spearman"))
     cat(sprintf("    %-2s  n=%2d  median %s reads  richness~depth rho=%+.3f P=%.4g%s\n",
                 s, sum(k), formatC(median(gg$reads[k]), big.mark = ",", format = "d"),
                 unname(ct$estimate), ct$p.value,
                 if (is.finite(ct$p.value) && ct$p.value < 0.05 &&
                     abs(ct$estimate) >= 0.5) "   <- DEPTH-LIMITED" else ""))
     flag <- is.finite(ct$p.value) && ct$p.value < 0.05 && abs(ct$estimate) >= 0.5
     if (s == "ME") gate_me <- flag else gate_s <- flag
   }
   ## IS DEPTH ITSELF RESPONSE-ASSOCIATED? If it is, a prevalence difference
   ## is a depth difference and G1's per-series gate is not enough on its own.
   cat("\n  depth by response -- the direct confounding test\n")
   for (s in c("ME", "S", "both")) {
     k <- (if (s == "both") rep(TRUE, nrow(gg)) else gg$series == s) & is.finite(gg$reads)
     if (sum(k) < 4 || length(unique(gg$resp[k])) < 2) next
     w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(gg$reads[k] ~ factor(gg$resp[k])))
     cat(sprintf("    %-4s NR n=%2d median %13s | R n=%2d median %13s | MWU P=%.3f%s\n",
                 s, sum(k & gg$resp == "NR"),
                 formatC(median(gg$reads[k & gg$resp == "NR"]), big.mark = ",", format = "d"),
                 sum(k & gg$resp == "R"),
                 formatC(median(gg$reads[k & gg$resp == "R"]), big.mark = ",", format = "d"),
                 w$p.value,
                 if (is.finite(w$p.value) && w$p.value < 0.10) "   <- CHECK" else ""))
   }
 } else cat("\n  NOTE: no read counts found; the G1 gate cannot be evaluated.\n")

 ## ---- 4. G0, the tested set ----------------------------------------------
 PRESENT <- Mi > 0
 nprev   <- colSums(PRESENT)
 keep    <- nprev >= 4 & nprev <= 30
 cat(sprintf("\nB47: G0 tested set -- %d of %d species present in 4..30 of %d libraries\n",
             sum(keep), ncol(Mi), nrow(Mi)))
 if (!sum(keep)) { cat("  nothing to test.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
 SPN <- colnames(Mi)[keep]

 ## ---- 5. G2, prevalence stratified by series -----------------------------
 gf <- factor(g, levels = c("NR", "R")); sf <- factor(ser, levels = c("ME", "S"))
 p2 <- vapply(SPN, function(sp) {
   pz <- factor(ifelse(PRESENT[, sp], "present", "absent"),
                levels = c("present", "absent"))
   ta <- table(pz, gf, sf)
   ok <- apply(ta, 3, function(m) all(rowSums(m) > 0) && all(colSums(m) > 0))
   if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
   ta <- ta[, , ok, drop = FALSE]
   out <- tryCatch({
     if (dim(ta)[3] == 1L) stats::fisher.test(ta[, , 1])$p.value
     else stats::mantelhaen.test(ta, exact = TRUE)$p.value
   }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
   out
 }, 0)
 q2 <- p.adjust(p2, "BH")
 prev <- t(vapply(SPN, function(sp) c(
   NR_n = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "NR"), NR_tot = sum(gf == "NR"),
   R_n  = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "R"),  R_tot  = sum(gf == "R"),
   ME_NR = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "NR" & sf == "ME"),
   ME_R  = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "R"  & sf == "ME"),
   S_NR  = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "NR" & sf == "S"),
   S_R   = sum(PRESENT[, sp] & gf == "R"  & sf == "S")), numeric(8)))

 ## ---- 6. G3, abundance given presence ------------------------------------
 ## Within-series rank standardisation, then one Wilcoxon on the pooled
 ## quantiles. No pseudo-count anywhere: absent libraries are dropped, not
 ## imputed as a very small number.
 p3 <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(SPN)), SPN)
 n3 <- matrix(0L, length(SPN), 2, dimnames = list(SPN, c("NR_present", "R_present")))
 for (sp in SPN) {
   k <- PRESENT[, sp]
   n3[sp, ] <- c(sum(k & gf == "NR"), sum(k & gf == "R"))
   if (min(n3[sp, ]) < 3L) next
   u <- rep(NA_real_, length(i))
   for (s in levels(sf)) {
     j <- which(k & sf == s); if (!length(j)) next
     u[j] <- (rank(Mi[j, sp]) - 0.5) / length(j)
   }
   v <- u[k]; h <- droplevels(gf[k])
   if (nlevels(h) < 2L) next
   p3[sp] <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(v ~ h)$p.value),
                      error = function(e) NA_real_)
 }
 tst3 <- !is.na(p3)
 q3 <- rep(NA_real_, length(p3)); names(q3) <- SPN
 q3[tst3] <- p.adjust(p3[tst3], "BH")

 ## ---- 7. the table, and the verdict against the rules fixed above --------
 res <- data.frame(species = SPN, prev, n3,
                   p_prevalence = as.numeric(p2), q_prevalence = as.numeric(q2),
                   p_abundance  = as.numeric(p3), q_abundance  = as.numeric(q3),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
 res <- res[order(res$p_prevalence, res$p_abundance), ]
 n2t <- sum(!is.na(p2)); n3t <- sum(tst3)
 s2  <- which(res$q_prevalence < 0.05); s3 <- which(res$q_abundance < 0.05)
 cat(sprintf("\nB47: G2 prevalence  -- %d species tested, %d nominal at P<0.05, %d at BH<0.05 (min q %.3f)\n",
             n2t, sum(res$p_prevalence < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), length(s2),
             suppressWarnings(min(res$q_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE))))
 cat(sprintf("B47: G3 abundance   -- %d species tested, %d nominal at P<0.05, %d at BH<0.05 (min q %.3f)\n",
             n3t, sum(res$p_abundance < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), length(s3),
             suppressWarnings(min(res$q_abundance, na.rm = TRUE))))
 cat("\n  the ten smallest prevalence P, for the record (not results)\n")
 pr <- utils::head(res, 10)
 for (r in seq_len(nrow(pr))) cat(sprintf(
   "    %-46s NR %2d/%2d  R %2d/%2d   P=%.4g q=%.3f\n",
   substr(pr$species[r], 1, 46), pr$NR_n[r], pr$NR_tot[r], pr$R_n[r], pr$R_tot[r],
   pr$p_prevalence[r], pr$q_prevalence[r]))

 cat("\nB47 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
 if (!length(s2) && !length(s3)) {
   cat("  G4 applies: nothing survives BH in either scan.\n",
       "  REPORTABLE SENTENCE. The pre-treatment separation is not carried by\n",
       "  an identifiable species at this sample size: across ", n2t,
       " species present\n  in 10-90% of the 34 libraries, no prevalence or ",
       "abundance difference survives\n  Benjamini-Hochberg correction ",
       "(smallest q = ", sprintf("%.2f", suppressWarnings(min(c(res$q_prevalence, res$q_abundance), na.rm = TRUE))),
       "). This is a statement about\n  resolution, not about biology -- eight ",
       "non-responders cannot exclude a\n  species effect -- and it does not ",
       "retract the omnibus result.\n", sep = "")
 } else {
   if (length(s2)) {
     cat("  G2 survivors, to be read only through G1:\n")
     for (r in s2) cat(sprintf("    %-46s NR %d/%d (ME %d, S %d)  R %d/%d (ME %d, S %d)  q=%.4f\n",
       substr(res$species[r], 1, 46), res$NR_n[r], res$NR_tot[r], res$ME_NR[r], res$S_NR[r],
       res$R_n[r], res$R_tot[r], res$ME_R[r], res$S_R[r], res$q_prevalence[r]))
     if (isTRUE(gate_me) || isTRUE(gate_s))
       cat("    G1 FIRED (series flagged above). A prevalence survivor is\n",
           "    reportable ONLY if it holds in the saturated series alone --\n",
           "    check the S_NR / S_R columns before writing any sentence.\n", sep = "")
   }
   if (length(s3)) {
     cat("  G3 survivors (abundance given presence; the only shape that names a taxon):\n")
     for (r in s3) cat(sprintf("    %-46s present NR %d / R %d   q=%.4f\n",
       substr(res$species[r], 1, 46), res$NR_present[r], res$R_present[r], res$q_abundance[r]))
   }
 }

 od <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(), "B47_sheba_species")
 dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
 utils::write.csv(res, file.path(od, "sheba_species_scan.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 saveRDS(list(result = res, design = data.frame(mg = i, resp = g, series = ser),
              n_tested_prevalence = n2t, n_tested_abundance = n3t,
              gate_ME_depth_limited = gate_me, gate_S_depth_limited = gate_s,
              set_matches_B15 = TRUE),
         file.path(od, "sheba_species.rds"))
 cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
 b47_sheba_species <<- res
})
```

## B47b — drop82

the Sheba metagenome omnibus arm against the study's own 5 M read

Source: `B47b_drop82.R`

```{r B47b_drop82, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B47b — the Sheba metagenome omnibus arm against the study's own 5 M read
## floor, and against the loss of any single library.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. B47 printed, as a by-product, that B15's Sheba set contains
## 82_ME at 3,847,028 reads. The study's primary rule excludes it:
##
##   analysis_v17.Rmd l. 4265  "The >=5M floor is primary; the floor is set on
##                              depth, not on outcome."
##   analysis_v17.Rmd l. 4280  "The >=5M version is PRIMARY"
##   section 10e      l. 4509  sh_set5 <- dplyr::filter(sh_set, reads >= 5e6)
##   B42 inventory             "below the 5M read floor (3,847,028 reads)"
##
## Every downstream Sheba analysis -- the phylum tests, the HUMAnN arms, the
## species direction work -- runs on sh_set5. The omnibus arm does not, because
## B15 builds its design by matching the proteome roster to the library prefix
## rather than from sh_set, and that route inherits neither the timing exclusion
## nor the read floor. The timing exclusion happens not to bite: 11_ME is not in
## the set. The read floor does.
##
## AND THE ARM SITS EXACTLY ON ITS OWN POWER THRESHOLD. B15's run() carries
##
##   underpowered <- min(table(g)) < 8
##
## with the reading fixed in B15's own comment: "An underpowered arm is not a
## null result ... its p-value says nothing either way." The set has NR 8.
## 82_ME is one of those eight. So applying the study's primary floor to this
## arm takes it from 8 non-responders to 7 and trips B15's own rule.
##
## That is a tension between two pre-specified rules, not a bug, and it has to
## be resolved in the text rather than left for a reviewer to find.
##
## WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not re-specify the arm, change the reported
## P, or pick between the two rules. It measures the size of the problem.
##
## THE RULES ARE FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS.
##
##   F   FIDELITY. The full-34 run must reproduce B15's printed statistics
##       exactly -- pseudo-F 1.377, R2 0.0413, P = 0.0320 (reanalysis_run_55c.log
##       l. 56). If it does not, the helpers have drifted from B15's and nothing
##       below is comparable; the script says so and stops.
##
##   S1  THE FLOOR. Re-run with libraries below 5e6 reads removed.
##         P < 0.05 -> the arm does not depend on a sub-floor library. Report
##           the sensitivity in one line and make the Methods sentence precise.
##         P >= 0.05 -> the arm's significance depends on a library the primary
##           floor excludes. It is then reported WITH that dependence stated, or
##           re-specified on sh_set5 and reported as underpowered. Either way the
##           manuscript cannot carry P = 0.0320 unqualified.
##       B15's underpowered rule is applied to the reduced arm and printed
##       whatever S1 shows, because at NR 7 it fires regardless of the P.
##
##   S2  IS IT THAT LIBRARY, OR ANY LIBRARY? Leave-one-out over all 34. If
##       dropping 82_ME moves P no further than dropping other non-responders
##       does, the arm is fragile to losing any one of eight -- a power
##       statement -- and 82_ME is not driving the signal. If 82_ME is an
##       outlier in that distribution, it is. BOTH READINGS ARE REPORTED; the
##       first does not excuse the second.
##
##   S3  A fragile arm is still the arm that was pre-specified. Nothing here
##       licenses dropping the result, and nothing here licenses quoting it
##       without the sensitivity.
##
##   source("B47b_drop82.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

 ## ---- 0. B15's machinery, COPIED VERBATIM --------------------------------
 ## Duplicated rather than refactored so this script cannot drift from the run
 ## that produced P = 0.0320, and so a reader can diff the two. Rule F checks it.
 B_PERM <- 10000L; SEED <- 1501L

 clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-9); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
 gower <- function(D) {
   A <- -0.5 * D^2
   n <- nrow(A); J <- diag(n) - matrix(1/n, n, n)
   J %*% A %*% J
 }
 pseudoF <- function(G, g) {
   if (!all(is.finite(G))) return(NA_real_)
   n <- length(g); lv <- levels(factor(g))
   H <- matrix(0, n, n)
   for (l in lv) { i <- which(g == l); H[i, i] <- 1 / length(i) }
   ss_b <- sum(diag(H %*% G)); ss_t <- sum(diag(G)); ss_w <- ss_t - ss_b
   if (!is.finite(ss_w) || ss_w <= 0) return(NA_real_)
   (ss_b / (length(lv) - 1)) / (ss_w / (n - length(lv)))
 }
 disper <- function(G, g) {
   lv <- levels(factor(g))
   m <- vapply(lv, function(l) { i <- which(g == l)
     Gi <- G[i, i, drop = FALSE]
     mean(pmax(diag(Gi) - 2 * rowMeans(Gi) + mean(Gi), 0)) }, 0)
   unname(abs(diff(m)))
 }
 shuffle <- function(g, strata = NULL) {
   if (is.null(strata)) return(sample(g))
   out <- g
   for (s in unique(strata)) { i <- which(strata == s); out[i] <- sample(g[i]) }
   out
 }
 sp_matrix <- function(f, cleaner) {
   h <- grep("^#?clade_name", readLines(f, n = 20, warn = FALSE))[1]
   t <- read.delim(f, skip = if (is.na(h)) 1 else h - 1, check.names = FALSE,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   names(t)[1] <- "clade_name"
   sel <- grepl("\\|s__", t$clade_name) & !grepl("\\|t__", t$clade_name)
   if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
   X <- as.matrix(t[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
   rownames(X) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", t$clade_name[sel])
   M <- t(X); rownames(M) <- cleaner(rownames(M))
   M[, colSums(M, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, drop = FALSE]
 }
 sp_from_df <- function(df, cleaner) {
   tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv"); write.table(df, tf, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
   on.exit(unlink(tf), add = TRUE); sp_matrix(tf, cleaner)
 }

 ## the core of B15's run(), with the printing stripped so it can be called in
 ## a loop. Rule F validates it against run()'s own numbers on the full set.
 core <- function(M, g, strata) {
   ## run()'s two pre-filters, reproduced so rule F cannot fail on a technicality
   ok <- !is.na(g)
   M <- M[ok, , drop = FALSE]; g <- g[ok]
   strata <- if (is.null(strata)) NULL else strata[ok]
   ok <- is.finite(rowSums(M))
   M <- M[ok, , drop = FALSE]; g <- g[ok]
   strata <- if (is.null(strata)) NULL else strata[ok]
   g <- droplevels(factor(g))
   G  <- gower(as.matrix(dist(clr(M))))
   F0 <- pseudoF(G, g); d0 <- disper(G, g)
   set.seed(SEED)
   nullF <- numeric(B_PERM); nullD <- numeric(B_PERM)
   for (b in seq_len(B_PERM)) {
     gp <- shuffle(g, strata)
     nullF[b] <- pseudoF(G, gp); nullD[b] <- disper(G, gp)
   }
   pF <- (1 + sum(nullF >= F0, na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(is.finite(nullF)))
   pD <- (1 + sum(nullD >= d0, na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + sum(is.finite(nullD)))
   n <- length(g); lv <- levels(g); H <- matrix(0, n, n)
   for (l in lv) { i <- which(g == l); H[i, i] <- 1 / length(i) }
   list(F = F0, r2 = sum(diag(H %*% G)) / sum(diag(G)), p = pF,
        disp = d0, p_disp = pD, n = n, n_min = min(table(g)),
        underpowered = min(table(g)) < 8)
 }

 ## ---- 1. the matrix and the design, as in B47 ----------------------------
 if (!exists("sh_mpa_raw"))
   stop("B47b: sh_mpa_raw is not in the session.", call. = FALSE)
 Ms <- sp_from_df(sh_mpa_raw,
         function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x))
 mg_keys <- rownames(Ms)
 SP <- if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY"))
         tryCatch(as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
 if (!is.null(SP) && "cohort" %in% names(SP))
   SP <- SP[SP$cohort %in% c("sheba", "Sheba"), , drop = FALSE]
 cand <- list()
 if (!is.null(SP) && "resp" %in% names(SP) && length(mg_keys)) {
   pref <- sub("_.*$", "", mg_keys)
   for (cl in names(SP)) {
     v <- as.character(SP[[cl]]); if (all(is.na(v))) next
     if (sum(v %in% mg_keys) >= 12) {
       d <- data.frame(mg = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% mg_keys, ]
       cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl)]] <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), ]
     } else if (sum(v %in% pref) >= 12) {
       m <- data.frame(pref = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% pref, ]
       m <- m[!duplicated(m$pref), ]
       d <- data.frame(mg = mg_keys, pref = pref)
       cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cl, " (prefix)")]] <-
         merge(d, m, by = "pref")[, c("mg", "resp")]
     }
   }
 }
 f12 <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(),
                  "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
 if (file.exists(f12)) {
   pr <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)
   if (all(c("sample", "mg") %in% names(pr))) {
     if (!is.null(SP) && all(c("sample", "resp") %in% names(SP)))
       cand[["B12 pairs + SAMP_PRIMARY"]] <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
         data.frame(sample = SP$sample, resp = as.character(SP$resp)), by = "sample")[, c("mg", "resp")]
     if (exists("OS"))
       cand[["B12 pairs + OS$d"]] <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
         data.frame(sample = OS$d$sample, resp = as.character(OS$d$resp)), by = "sample")[, c("mg", "resp")]
   }
 }
 score <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$resp) & d$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
   d <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), , drop = FALSE]
   tb <- table(droplevels(factor(d$resp)))
   if (!nrow(d) || length(tb) < 2) return(c(0, 0)); c(nrow(d), min(tb)) }
 if (!length(cand)) stop("B47b: no Sheba design candidate.", call. = FALSE)
 sc <- t(vapply(cand, score, c(0, 0)))
 sd <- cand[[order(-sc[, 2], -sc[, 1])[1]]]
 sd <- sd[!is.na(sd$resp) & sd$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
 sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$mg), , drop = FALSE]
 sd$patient <- sub("_.*$", "", sd$mg)
 sd$series  <- ifelse(grepl("_ME", sd$mg), "ME", "S")
 sd <- sd[order(sd$patient, sd$series != "S"), , drop = FALSE]
 sd <- sd[!duplicated(sd$patient), , drop = FALSE]

 i   <- intersect(rownames(Ms), sd$mg)
 g   <- sd$resp[match(i, sd$mg)]
 ser <- sd$series[match(i, sd$mg)]
 tb  <- table(series = ser, resp = g)
 EXP <- matrix(c(3L, 5L, 7L, 19L), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("ME", "S"), c("NR", "R")))
 if (!(identical(dim(tb), dim(EXP)) && all(as.vector(tb) == as.vector(EXP)))) {
   cat("B47b STOPPED: the set is not B15's (expected ME 3/7, S 5/19).\n"); print(tb)
   return(invisible(NULL))
 }
 M <- Ms[i, , drop = FALSE]
 cat(sprintf("B47b: B15's set confirmed -- %d libraries, NR %d / R %d, %d features\n",
             length(i), sum(g == "NR"), sum(g == "R"), ncol(M)))

 ## ---- 2. depth ------------------------------------------------------------
 rd <- NULL
 if (exists("sh_mg_meta") && all(c("raw", "reads") %in% names(sh_mg_meta))) {
   dd <- data.frame(mg = sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1",
                             as.character(sh_mg_meta$raw)),
                    reads = as.numeric(sh_mg_meta$reads))
   dd <- dd[!duplicated(dd$mg), ]; rd <- dd$reads[match(i, dd$mg)]
 }
 if (is.null(rd) || anyNA(rd))
   stop("B47b: read counts missing for ", if (is.null(rd)) "all" else sum(is.na(rd)),
        " libraries. sh_mg_meta$reads is the source; knit section 10e first.", call. = FALSE)
 below <- rd < 5e6
 cat(sprintf("  below the 5e6 floor: %s\n",
     if (!any(below)) "none" else paste(sprintf("%s (%s reads, %s)", i[below],
       formatC(rd[below], big.mark = ",", format = "d"), g[below]), collapse = ", ")))

 ## ---- 3. rule F, fidelity -------------------------------------------------
 A <- core(M, g, ser)
 cat(sprintf("\n[F] full set: pseudo-F %.3f, R2 %.4f, P = %.4f  (B15: 1.377, 0.0413, 0.0320)\n",
             A$F, A$r2, A$p))
 okF <- abs(A$F - 1.377) < 5e-4 && abs(A$r2 - 0.0413) < 5e-5 && abs(A$p - 0.0320) < 5e-5
 if (!okF) {
   cat("\nB47b STOPPED. Rule F fails: the copied machinery does not reproduce\n",
       "  B15's printed statistics, so nothing below is comparable to the\n",
       "  reported P. Diff this script's helpers against B15_omnibus.R.\n", sep = "")
   return(invisible(NULL))
 }
 cat("  rule F passes: the machinery is B15's.\n")

 ## ---- 4. rule S1, the floor ----------------------------------------------
 cat("\n[S1] applying the study's primary >=5M floor\n")
 if (!any(below)) {
   cat("  no library is below the floor; S1 is vacuous.\n"); B <- NULL
 } else {
   k <- !below
   B <- core(M[k, , drop = FALSE], g[k], ser[k])
   cat(sprintf("  %d libraries (NR %d / R %d): pseudo-F %.3f, R2 %.4f, P = %.4f\n",
               B$n, sum(g[k] == "NR"), sum(g[k] == "R"), B$F, B$r2, B$p))
   cat(sprintf("  dispersion %.4f, P = %.4f\n", B$disp, B$p_disp))
   cat(sprintf("  B15's power rule (min group < 8): %s (smaller group = %d)\n",
               if (B$underpowered) "FIRES -- 'its p-value says nothing either way'" else "does not fire",
               B$n_min))
 }

 ## ---- 5. rule S2, leave-one-out ------------------------------------------
 cat("\n[S2] leave-one-out over all", length(i), "libraries\n")
 loo <- data.frame(mg = i, resp = g, series = ser, reads = rd,
                   p = NA_real_, F = NA_real_, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
 for (j in seq_along(i)) {
   k <- seq_along(i) != j
   if (min(table(droplevels(factor(g[k])))) < 2) next
   r <- core(M[k, , drop = FALSE], g[k], ser[k])
   loo$p[j] <- r$p; loo$F[j] <- r$F
 }
 lnr <- loo[loo$resp == "NR" & is.finite(loo$p), ]
 lr  <- loo[loo$resp == "R"  & is.finite(loo$p), ]
 cat(sprintf("  dropping one NR (n=%d): P from %.4f to %.4f, median %.4f\n",
             nrow(lnr), min(lnr$p), max(lnr$p), median(lnr$p)))
 cat(sprintf("  dropping one R  (n=%d): P from %.4f to %.4f, median %.4f\n",
             nrow(lr), min(lr$p), max(lr$p), median(lr$p)))
 cat(sprintf("  exclusions that lift P above 0.05: %d of %d\n",
             sum(loo$p >= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.finite(loo$p))))
 ## CALIBRATE THAT COUNT BEFORE ANYONE READS IT AS A DEFECT. For an observed P
 ## near 0.03 at n = 34, a jackknife that crosses 0.05 on a sizeable minority of
 ## drops is the expected behaviour of a P that size, not evidence of a broken
 ## arm. S2 exists to LOCATE an influential library, not to re-test
 ## significance, and the count above is not a second p-value.
 cat("  (a P near 0.03 at n = 34 is expected to cross 0.05 under some single\n",
     "   exclusions; this count locates influence, it does not re-test the arm)\n", sep = "")
 sub_dir <- NA_character_
 if (any(below)) {
   jb <- which(below)[1]; pb <- loo$p[jb]
   oth <- lnr$p[lnr$mg != loo$mg[jb]]
   sub_dir <- if (pb >= max(oth)) "most influential" else
              if (pb <= min(oth)) "least influential" else "mid-range"
   cat(sprintf("  sub-floor library %s: P = %.4f; other NR drops span %.4f to %.4f\n",
               loo$mg[jb], pb, min(oth), max(oth)))
   cat(sprintf("  -> it is the %s of the %d non-responders, and dropping it moves P %s\n",
               sub_dir, nrow(lnr), if (pb < A$p) "DOWN (it was suppressing the signal)" else "up"))
 }
 cat("\n  every leave-one-out result, by P\n")
 lo <- loo[order(-loo$p), ]
 for (r in seq_len(nrow(lo))) cat(sprintf("    drop %-10s %-2s %-2s %13s reads  P = %.4f%s\n",
   lo$mg[r], lo$resp[r], lo$series[r], formatC(lo$reads[r], big.mark = ",", format = "d"),
   lo$p[r], if (is.finite(lo$p[r]) && lo$p[r] >= 0.05) "   <- no longer significant" else ""))

 ## ---- 6. the verdict ------------------------------------------------------
 cat("\nB47b VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
 if (is.null(B)) {
   cat("  S1 vacuous: no sub-floor library in the set. Nothing to resolve.\n")
 } else if (B$p < 0.05) {
   cat(sprintf("  S1: P = %.4f with the floor applied -- the arm does NOT depend on\n", B$p),
       "  the sub-floor library. Report the sensitivity in one line and make the\n",
       "  Methods sentence precise about which set the omnibus uses.\n", sep = "")
   if (B$underpowered)
     cat("  NOTE: B15's own power rule still fires at the reduced n. The\n",
         "  sensitivity is reassuring about the floor, not about power.\n", sep = "")
 } else {
   cat(sprintf("  S1: P = %.4f with the floor applied -- the arm's significance\n", B$p),
       "  DEPENDS on a library the study's primary floor excludes. P = 0.0320\n",
       "  cannot be quoted unqualified. Two honest options, and they are the\n",
       "  only two: report it with the dependence stated, or re-specify the arm\n",
       "  on sh_set5 and report it as underpowered by B15's own rule.\n", sep = "")
 }
 if (nrow(lnr) && any(below)) {
   jb <- which(below)[1]
   cat("  S2: ", switch(sub_dir,
     "most influential"  = "the sub-floor library is the single most influential non-responder --\n      it is DRIVING the result and the arm must not be reported without that stated.",
     "least influential" = "the sub-floor library is the LEAST influential non-responder: dropping it\n      strengthens the separation, so it was adding noise, not signal. The floor\n      question is answered -- the result does not rest on it -- but the power\n      question is not, because removing it takes the arm to seven.",
     "dropping it moves P no further than dropping other non-responders does; the\n      arm is fragile to losing any one of eight, which is a POWER statement.\n      That does not excuse carrying a sub-floor library in a pre-specified arm."),
     "\n", sep = "")
 }
 cat("  S3: a fragile arm is still the arm that was pre-specified. Nothing here\n",
     "      licenses dropping the result, and nothing licenses quoting it without\n",
     "      the sensitivity.\n", sep = "")

 od <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(), "B47b_drop82")
 dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
 utils::write.csv(loo, file.path(od, "leave_one_out.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 saveRDS(list(full = A, floor = B, loo = loo, below_floor = i[below]),
         file.path(od, "drop82.rds"))
 cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
 b47b_drop82 <<- loo
})
```

## B48 — taxon scan

phylum, genus and species against response, in BOTH cohorts.

Source: `B48_taxon_scan.R`

```{r B48_taxon_scan, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B48 — phylum, genus and species against response, in BOTH cohorts.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. B16's header states the gap: "The manuscript tests the
## metagenome at phylum level only." That is accurate and it is incomplete in
## two directions.
##
##   PHYLUM is tested, but section 10b's test_phylum reports RAW p for four
```
