```{r B48_taxon_scan, eval=FALSE}
##   named phyla at three depth floors and applies no correction. Bacteroidota
##   25.748 vs 38.202, p = 0.0496 at the primary >=5M floor, is the number a
##   reviewer will ask about, and the question is what it becomes once the
##   phyla actually tested are corrected over.
##
##   GENUS is not tested against response anywhere, in either cohort. Genus-
##   level MetaPhlAn appears only in the coupling work (section 14), extracted
##   to pair with the proteome.
##
##   SPECIES is tested as an omnibus only -- Pittsburgh P = 0.1165, Sheba
##   P = 0.0320 -- and B47 has now scanned Sheba species (601 tested, nothing
##   survives BH, min q = 0.417). Pittsburgh species has never been scanned,
##   and it is the better-powered cohort by a wide margin: 39 NR / 35 R against
##   Sheba's 8 / 26.
##
## POST HOC, DECLARED. Same family as B15 section [3] and B47. Not
## pre-registered, cannot be. Nothing below reads as discovery.
##
## THREE THINGS DIFFER FROM B47 AND EACH IS A RULE, NOT A CHOICE MADE LATER.
##
##   [1] B15 DEDUPLICATES SHEBA TO ONE LIBRARY PER PATIENT AND DOES NOT DO SO
##       FOR PITTSBURGH. Its own comment gives the reason -- simulated with no
##       response effect at all, keeping repeats gave P < 0.05 in six of eight
##       replicates against one of eight when deduplicated, "not a small
##       correction ... the difference between a test and an artefact". A
##       per-feature scan must not inherit an unchecked assumption either way,
##       so rule D applies the same rule to both cohorts and REPORTS what it
##       finds rather than assuming repeats exist.
##
##   [2] PITTSBURGH IS SHALLOWER THAN SHEBA, NOT DEEPER. Section 10a: 82
##       libraries, median 19,118,723 read PAIRS, min 21,829, max 47,478,455 --
##       about 38 M reads in the units Sheba's MetaPhlAn headers report, against
##       135 M for Sheba's S series and 34 M for its ME series, which B47 found
##       still depth-limited for richness. Depth therefore has to be measured
##       here too, not assumed from the median. Rule G1.
##
##   [3] PITTSBURGH IS ON-TREATMENT. A species difference there is as likely to
##       be a consequence of response as a predictor of it. Sheba is where a
##       predictive claim could live and Sheba is the underpowered cohort. This
##       asymmetry is stated in the verdict whatever the scan returns.
##
## MEASURED 15 Oct 2026, ON THE REAL INPUTS, BEFORE THE RULES BELOW WERE FIXED.
## Both of the first two concerns were checked and neither holds the way it was
## first stated, which is why they are rules that report rather than rules that
## assume:
##   - Pittsburgh's labelled set at the >=5M floor is 68 libraries from 68
##     patients. There are NO repeat libraries, so rule D is vacuous there and
##     B15 was right not to apply it. It is still run, and still printed.
##   - Pittsburgh richness does NOT track depth: rho = +0.038, P = 0.758 over
##     those 68. The reason is range, not median -- after the floor Pittsburgh
##     spans 5 to 47 M pairs while Sheba's ME series spans 1.9 to 65 M. So
##     Pittsburgh's PREVALENCE scan is interpretable where Sheba's ME half is
##     not. That is the opposite of what the median alone suggested.
##
## THE RULES ARE FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS.
##
##   D   DEDUPLICATION. One library per patient, chosen by GREATEST SEQUENCING
##       DEPTH -- a quality criterion, fixed in advance, never outcome. Ties
##       broken by library name so the choice is reproducible. Sheba arrives
##       already deduplicated by B15 and is left alone.
##
##   G0  TESTED SET, per cohort x rank: prevalence is tested for features
##       present in 10-90% of libraries; abundance is tested for features with
##       at least 3 present in each arm. A feature present everywhere carries
##       no prevalence information and a feature present nowhere carries no
##       abundance information; inflating a BH denominator with either is not
##       conservative.
##
##   G1  DEPTH GATE, per cohort (and per series where there is one). Richness
##       against depth at P < 0.05 with |rho| >= 0.5 means that stratum is
##       depth-limited for presence/absence, and a prevalence survivor there is
##       reported only if it also holds where depth has saturated.
##
##   G2  PREVALENCE. Presence/absence by response. Sheba STRATIFIED BY SERIES
##       (exact conditional test on the 2x2x2); Pittsburgh unstratified, as
##       B15's Pittsburgh arm is. Fisher where a stratum is degenerate.
##
##   G3  ABUNDANCE GIVEN PRESENCE. Among libraries where the feature is
##       present, within-stratum rank-standardised abundance, Wilcoxon by
##       response. NO PSEUDO-COUNT ANYWHERE: absent libraries are dropped, not
##       imputed as a very small number. A scan run with log(x + pseudo-count)
##       on 15 Oct 2026 returned 13 BH survivors, every one of which decomposed
##       to prevalence with abundance-if-present at P = 0.15 to 1.00.
##
##   G4  CORRECTION. BH WITHIN each cohort x rank x scan -- TWELVE families
##       (2 cohorts x 3 ranks x {prevalence, abundance}), not one. These are
##       different questions at different resolutions, and pooling them after
##       seeing B47's null would be a choice made on the numbers. The count is
##       declared here so it cannot drift, and the script checks it.
##       THE COST IS DECLARED TOO: twelve families means a lone survivor at
##       q just under 0.05 in one of them is weak evidence, and the verdict
##       says so rather than leaving the reader to work it out.
##
##   G5  CROSS-COHORT AGREEMENT, the only shape that would matter. Neither
##       cohort alone can carry a taxon claim -- Pittsburgh is on-treatment,
##       Sheba has eight non-responders. A feature nominal in BOTH cohorts with
##       the SAME direction is reported separately, with the number expected by
##       chance alongside it. Agreement is not significance.
##
##   G6  READING. Nothing surviving means the response contrast is not carried
##       by an identifiable taxon at these sample sizes -- a statement about
##       resolution, not biology. A phylum that loses significance under
##       correction has not been retracted; it has been placed.
##
##   source("B48_taxon_scan.R")
## ============================================================================

local({

 BH_FAMILIES <- 12L          # G4: 2 cohorts x 3 ranks x {prevalence, abundance}; checked below
 RANKS <- c(phylum = "p", genus = "g", species = "s")

 ## ---- helpers --------------------------------------------------------------
 ## rank extraction from a MetaPhlAn clade_name column. The depth of the
 ## lineage is what identifies the rank: k|p|c|o|f|g|s|t.
 rank_matrix <- function(df, rk, cleaner) {
   cn <- names(df)[1]; names(df)[1] <- "clade_name"
   tag <- paste0("\\|", rk, "__")
   dep <- c(p = 1L, g = 5L, s = 6L)[[rk]]
   sel <- grepl(tag, df$clade_name) &
          vapply(gregexpr("\\|", df$clade_name), function(m) sum(m > 0), 0L) == dep
   if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
   X <- as.matrix(df[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
   X[!is.finite(X)] <- 0
   rownames(X) <- sub(paste0(".*\\|", rk, "__"), "", df$clade_name[sel])
   M <- t(X); rownames(M) <- cleaner(rownames(M))
   names(df)[1] <- cn
   M[, colSums(M, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, drop = FALSE]
 }

 ## G2 + G3 on one matrix. Returns one row per feature.
 scan_one <- function(M, g, strata, label) {
   g  <- factor(as.character(g), levels = c("NR", "R"))
   st <- if (is.null(strata)) factor(rep("all", length(g))) else factor(as.character(strata))
   PRESENT <- M > 0
   np <- colSums(PRESENT); n <- nrow(M)
   keep2 <- np >= max(2L, ceiling(0.10 * n)) & np <= floor(0.90 * n)
   FEA <- colnames(M)

   ## G2 prevalence
   p2 <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(FEA)), FEA)
   for (f in FEA[keep2]) {
     pz <- factor(ifelse(PRESENT[, f], "present", "absent"), levels = c("present", "absent"))
     ta <- table(pz, g, st)
     ok <- apply(ta, 3, function(m) all(rowSums(m) > 0) && all(colSums(m) > 0))
     if (!any(ok)) next
     ta <- ta[, , ok, drop = FALSE]
     p2[f] <- tryCatch({
       if (dim(ta)[3] == 1L) stats::fisher.test(ta[, , 1])$p.value
       else stats::mantelhaen.test(ta, exact = TRUE)$p.value
     }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
   }
   ## G3 abundance given presence
   p3 <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(FEA)), FEA)
   d3 <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(FEA)), FEA)
   for (f in FEA) {
     k <- PRESENT[, f]
     if (sum(k & g == "NR") < 3L || sum(k & g == "R") < 3L) next
     u <- rep(NA_real_, n)
     for (s in levels(st)) {
       j <- which(k & st == s); if (!length(j)) next
       u[j] <- (rank(M[j, f]) - 0.5) / length(j)
     }
     v <- u[k]; h <- droplevels(g[k])
     if (nlevels(h) < 2L) next
     p3[f] <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(v ~ h)$p.value),
                       error = function(e) NA_real_)
     d3[f] <- median(v[h == "NR"]) - median(v[h == "R"])      # >0 = higher in NR
   }
   q2 <- rep(NA_real_, length(FEA)); i2 <- !is.na(p2); q2[i2] <- p.adjust(p2[i2], "BH")
   q3 <- rep(NA_real_, length(FEA)); i3 <- !is.na(p3); q3[i3] <- p.adjust(p3[i3], "BH")
   ## MEDIAN RELATIVE ABUNDANCE BY ARM, carried for the figure. The volcano's
   ## effect axis is the rank-quantile difference (dir_NR_minus_R), which is the
   ## quantity G3 tests; percent is what a reader expects to see at phylum, so
   ## both are kept and neither is derived from the other.
   data.frame(cohort = label, feature = FEA,
              n_NR = colSums(PRESENT[g == "NR", , drop = FALSE]),
              tot_NR = sum(g == "NR"),
              n_R  = colSums(PRESENT[g == "R", , drop = FALSE]),
              tot_R = sum(g == "R"),
              med_NR_pct = apply(M[g == "NR", , drop = FALSE], 2, median),
              med_R_pct  = apply(M[g == "R",  , drop = FALSE], 2, median),
              mean_NR_pct = colMeans(M[g == "NR", , drop = FALSE]),
              mean_R_pct  = colMeans(M[g == "R",  , drop = FALSE]),
              p_prev = as.numeric(p2), q_prev = q2,
              p_abun = as.numeric(p3), q_abun = q3,
              dir_NR_minus_R = as.numeric(d3),
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
 }

 GATEDATA <- list()
 gate <- function(M, reads, st, label) {
   ric <- rowSums(M > 0)
   GATEDATA[[label]] <<- data.frame(library = rownames(M), cohort = label,
                                    stratum = as.character(st), reads = reads,
                                    richness = as.numeric(ric),
                                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   for (s in levels(factor(st))) {
     k <- st == s & is.finite(reads)
     if (sum(k) < 5) next
     ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(ric[k], reads[k], method = "spearman"))
     fl <- is.finite(ct$p.value) && ct$p.value < 0.05 && abs(ct$estimate) >= 0.5
     cat(sprintf("    %-10s %-4s n=%2d  median %13s  richness~depth rho=%+.3f P=%.4g%s\n",
                 label, s, sum(k), formatC(median(reads[k]), big.mark = ",", format = "d"),
                 unname(ct$estimate), ct$p.value, if (fl) "   <- DEPTH-LIMITED" else ""))
   }
 }

 ## ---- 1. PITTSBURGH --------------------------------------------------------
 need_p <- c("mpa_raw", "mg_meta", "mg_clean", "KEEP_5M", "depth")
 have_p <- all(vapply(need_p, exists, logical(1)))
 pitt <- NULL
 if (!have_p) {
   cat("B48: Pittsburgh SKIPPED, missing: ",
       paste(need_p[!vapply(need_p, exists, logical(1))], collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
 } else {
   mm <- as.data.frame(mg_meta)
   if (!"bio" %in% names(mm)) stop("B48: mg_meta has no bio column.", call. = FALSE)
   dp <- as.data.frame(depth)
   mm <- mm[!is.na(mm$resp) & mm$sample %in% KEEP_5M, , drop = FALSE]
   mm$reads <- dp$reads[match(mm$sample, dp$sample)]
   if (anyNA(mm$reads)) stop("B48: no read count for ", sum(is.na(mm$reads)),
                             " Pittsburgh samples.", call. = FALSE)
   cat(sprintf("B48 Pittsburgh: %d labelled libraries at the >=5M floor, from %d patients\n",
               nrow(mm), length(unique(mm$bio))))
   ## RULE D
   nlib <- nrow(mm)
   mm <- mm[order(mm$bio, -mm$reads, mm$sample), , drop = FALSE]
   mm <- mm[!duplicated(mm$bio), , drop = FALSE]
   cat(sprintf("  rule D: %d repeat librar%s dropped, deepest kept per patient -> %d libraries (NR %d / R %d)\n",
               nlib - nrow(mm), if (nlib - nrow(mm) == 1) "y" else "ies", nrow(mm),
               sum(mm$resp == "NR"), sum(mm$resp == "R")))
   if (min(table(droplevels(factor(mm$resp)))) < 8)
     cat("  WARNING: smaller arm below 8 after rule D; B15's power rule would fire.\n")
   pitt <- list(meta = mm)
 }

 ## ---- 2. SHEBA, B15's set (the design block as in B47) ---------------------
 shb <- NULL
 if (!exists("sh_mpa_raw")) {
   cat("B48: Sheba SKIPPED, sh_mpa_raw not in the session\n")
 } else {
   cl_s <- function(x) sub("^([0-9]+[A-Za-z]?_(ME|S[0-9]+))_.*$", "\\1", x)
   Msp <- rank_matrix(as.data.frame(sh_mpa_raw), "s", cl_s)
   mg_keys <- rownames(Msp)
   SP <- if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY")) tryCatch(as.data.frame(SAMP_PRIMARY), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
   if (!is.null(SP) && "cohort" %in% names(SP)) SP <- SP[SP$cohort %in% c("sheba", "Sheba"), , drop = FALSE]
   cand <- list()
   if (!is.null(SP) && "resp" %in% names(SP)) {
     pref <- sub("_.*$", "", mg_keys)
     for (cc in names(SP)) {
       v <- as.character(SP[[cc]]); if (all(is.na(v))) next
       if (sum(v %in% mg_keys) >= 12) {
         d <- data.frame(mg = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% mg_keys, ]
         cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cc)]] <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), ]
       } else if (sum(v %in% pref) >= 12) {
         m <- data.frame(pref = v, resp = as.character(SP$resp))[v %in% pref, ]
         m <- m[!duplicated(m$pref), ]
         cand[[paste0("SAMP_PRIMARY$", cc, " (prefix)")]] <-
           merge(data.frame(mg = mg_keys, pref = pref), m, by = "pref")[, c("mg", "resp")]
       }
     }
   }
   f12 <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(),
                    "B12_sheba_coupling", "sheba_coupling.rds")
   if (file.exists(f12)) {
     pr <- as.data.frame(readRDS(f12)$pairs)
     if (all(c("sample", "mg") %in% names(pr))) {
       if (!is.null(SP) && all(c("sample", "resp") %in% names(SP)))
         cand[["B12 pairs + SAMP_PRIMARY"]] <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
           data.frame(sample = SP$sample, resp = as.character(SP$resp)), by = "sample")[, c("mg", "resp")]
       if (exists("OS"))
         cand[["B12 pairs + OS$d"]] <- merge(pr[, c("sample", "mg")],
           data.frame(sample = OS$d$sample, resp = as.character(OS$d$resp)), by = "sample")[, c("mg", "resp")]
     }
   }
   if (!length(cand)) {
     cat("B48: Sheba SKIPPED, no design candidate\n")
   } else {
     score <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$resp) & d$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
       d <- d[!duplicated(d$mg), , drop = FALSE]
       tb <- table(droplevels(factor(d$resp)))
       if (!nrow(d) || length(tb) < 2) return(c(0, 0)); c(nrow(d), min(tb)) }
     sc <- t(vapply(cand, score, c(0, 0)))
     sdd <- cand[[order(-sc[, 2], -sc[, 1])[1]]]
     sdd <- sdd[!is.na(sdd$resp) & sdd$mg %in% mg_keys, , drop = FALSE]
     sdd <- sdd[!duplicated(sdd$mg), , drop = FALSE]
     sdd$patient <- sub("_.*$", "", sdd$mg)
     sdd$series  <- ifelse(grepl("_ME", sdd$mg), "ME", "S")
     sdd <- sdd[order(sdd$patient, sdd$series != "S"), , drop = FALSE]
     sdd <- sdd[!duplicated(sdd$patient), , drop = FALSE]
     ii  <- intersect(mg_keys, sdd$mg)
     tb  <- table(series = sdd$series[match(ii, sdd$mg)], resp = sdd$resp[match(ii, sdd$mg)])
     EXP <- matrix(c(3L, 5L, 7L, 19L), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("ME", "S"), c("NR", "R")))
     if (!(identical(dim(tb), dim(EXP)) && all(as.vector(tb) == as.vector(EXP)))) {
       cat("B48: Sheba SKIPPED -- the set is not B15's (expected ME 3/7, S 5/19):\n"); print(tb)
     } else {
       rr <- NULL
       if (exists("sh_mg_meta") && all(c("raw", "reads") %in% names(sh_mg_meta))) {
         dd <- data.frame(mg = cl_s(as.character(sh_mg_meta$raw)), reads = as.numeric(sh_mg_meta$reads))
         dd <- dd[!duplicated(dd$mg), ]; rr <- dd$reads[match(ii, dd$mg)]
       }
       shb <- list(ids = ii, resp = sdd$resp[match(ii, sdd$mg)],
                   series = sdd$series[match(ii, sdd$mg)], reads = rr, cleaner = cl_s)
       cat(sprintf("B48 Sheba: B15's set confirmed -- %d libraries, NR %d / R %d\n",
                   length(ii), sum(shb$resp == "NR"), sum(shb$resp == "R")))
     }
   }
 }
 if (is.null(pitt) && is.null(shb)) { cat("B48: nothing to do.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

 ## ---- 3. the depth gate, per cohort ---------------------------------------
 cat("\nB48: G1 depth gate (richness against depth, species level)\n")
 if (!is.null(pitt)) {
   Msp_p <- rank_matrix(as.data.frame(mpa_raw), "s", mg_clean)
   kp <- intersect(rownames(Msp_p), pitt$meta$sample)
   pitt$ids <- kp
   pitt$resp <- pitt$meta$resp[match(kp, pitt$meta$sample)]
   pitt$reads <- pitt$meta$reads[match(kp, pitt$meta$sample)]
   gate(Msp_p[kp, , drop = FALSE], pitt$reads, rep("all", length(kp)), "Pittsburgh")
 }
 if (!is.null(shb) && !is.null(shb$reads)) {
   Msp_s <- rank_matrix(as.data.frame(sh_mpa_raw), "s", shb$cleaner)
   gate(Msp_s[shb$ids, , drop = FALSE], shb$reads, shb$series, "Sheba")
 }

 ## ---- 4. the scans ---------------------------------------------------------
 out <- list(); fam <- 0L
 for (rk in names(RANKS)) {
   tag <- RANKS[[rk]]
   if (!is.null(pitt)) {
     M <- rank_matrix(as.data.frame(mpa_raw), tag, mg_clean)
     if (!is.null(M)) {
       M <- M[pitt$ids, , drop = FALSE]
       out[[paste("Pittsburgh", rk)]] <- scan_one(M, pitt$resp, NULL, "Pittsburgh")
     }
   }
   if (!is.null(shb)) {
     M <- rank_matrix(as.data.frame(sh_mpa_raw), tag, shb$cleaner)
     if (!is.null(M)) {
       M <- M[shb$ids, , drop = FALSE]
       out[[paste("Sheba", rk)]] <- scan_one(M, shb$resp, shb$series, "Sheba")
     }
   }
 }

 ## ---- 5. the summary -------------------------------------------------------
 cat("\nB48: scans (BH within each cohort x rank x test -- rule G4)\n")
 cat(sprintf("  %-20s %7s %7s %7s %7s %7s %7s %7s\n", "cohort x rank",
             "n_prev", "nom", "BH<.05", "minq", "n_abun", "nom", "minq"))
 for (nm in names(out)) {
   d <- out[[nm]]; fam <- fam + (sum(!is.na(d$p_prev)) > 0) + (sum(!is.na(d$p_abun)) > 0)
   cat(sprintf("  %-20s %7d %7d %7d %7s %7d %7d %7s\n", nm,
       sum(!is.na(d$p_prev)), sum(d$p_prev < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
       sum(d$q_prev < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
       if (all(is.na(d$q_prev))) "-" else sprintf("%.3f", min(d$q_prev, na.rm = TRUE)),
       sum(!is.na(d$p_abun)), sum(d$p_abun < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
       if (all(is.na(d$q_abun))) "-" else sprintf("%.3f", min(d$q_abun, na.rm = TRUE))))
 }
 cat(sprintf("  BH families actually formed: %d (declared %d)\n", fam, BH_FAMILIES))

 ## the four phyla section 10b names, with correction applied
 for (coh in c("Pittsburgh", "Sheba")) {
   nm <- paste(coh, "phylum"); if (is.null(out[[nm]])) next
   d <- out[[nm]]
   k <- d$feature %in% c("Bacteroidota", "Firmicutes", "Actinomycetota", "Pseudomonadota")
   if (!any(k)) next
   cat(sprintf("\n  %s -- the four phyla section 10b names, abundance scan\n", coh))
   for (r in which(k)) cat(sprintf("    %-16s present %2d/%2d NR, %2d/%2d R   P=%.4g  q=%.3f  %s\n",
     d$feature[r], d$n_NR[r], d$tot_NR[r], d$n_R[r], d$tot_R[r], d$p_abun[r], d$q_abun[r],
     if (is.finite(d$dir_NR_minus_R[r])) (if (d$dir_NR_minus_R[r] > 0) "higher in NR" else "higher in R") else ""))
 }

 ## ---- 6. rule G5, cross-cohort agreement -----------------------------------
 cat("\nB48: G5 cross-cohort agreement (nominal in both, same direction)\n")
 agree <- list()
 for (rk in names(RANKS)) {
   a <- out[[paste("Pittsburgh", rk)]]; b <- out[[paste("Sheba", rk)]]
   if (is.null(a) || is.null(b)) next
   m <- merge(a[, c("feature", "p_abun", "dir_NR_minus_R")],
              b[, c("feature", "p_abun", "dir_NR_minus_R")], by = "feature",
              suffixes = c("_pitt", "_sheba"))
   m <- m[is.finite(m$p_abun_pitt) & is.finite(m$p_abun_sheba), , drop = FALSE]
   hit <- m[m$p_abun_pitt < 0.05 & m$p_abun_sheba < 0.05 &
            sign(m$dir_NR_minus_R_pitt) == sign(m$dir_NR_minus_R_sheba), , drop = FALSE]
   exp_chance <- nrow(m) * 0.05 * 0.05 / 2
   cat(sprintf("  %-8s %d features in both; %d nominal in both with the same sign (%.2f expected by chance)\n",
               rk, nrow(m), nrow(hit), exp_chance))
   if (nrow(hit)) {
     for (r in seq_len(nrow(hit))) cat(sprintf("    %-44s Pitt P=%.4g  Sheba P=%.4g  %s\n",
       substr(hit$feature[r], 1, 44), hit$p_abun_pitt[r], hit$p_abun_sheba[r],
       if (hit$dir_NR_minus_R_pitt[r] > 0) "higher in NR" else "higher in R"))
     hit$rank <- rk; agree[[rk]] <- hit
   }
 }

 ## ---- 7. verdict -----------------------------------------------------------
 surv <- sum(vapply(out, function(d) sum(d$q_prev < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) +
                                     sum(d$q_abun < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), 0L))
 cat("\nB48 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
 if (!surv) {
   cat("  G6 applies: nothing survives BH at any rank in either cohort.\n",
       "  REPORTABLE. The response contrast is not carried by an identifiable\n",
       "  taxon at phylum, genus or species in either cohort once the features\n",
       "  actually tested are corrected over. This is a statement about\n",
       "  resolution, not biology, and it PLACES section 10b's phylum result\n",
       "  rather than retracting it.\n", sep = "")
 } else {
   cat(sprintf("  %d feature(s) survive BH. Read each through G1 (depth) and G5\n", surv),
       "  (cross-cohort) before any sentence is written. A Pittsburgh-only\n",
       "  survivor is on-treatment and cannot be called predictive.\n", sep = "")
   for (nm in names(out)) {
     d <- out[[nm]]
     for (r in which(d$q_prev < 0.05)) cat(sprintf("    %-18s %-40s prevalence NR %d/%d vs R %d/%d  q=%.4f\n",
       nm, substr(d$feature[r], 1, 40), d$n_NR[r], d$tot_NR[r], d$n_R[r], d$tot_R[r], d$q_prev[r]))
     for (r in which(d$q_abun < 0.05)) cat(sprintf("    %-18s %-40s abundance  present NR %d / R %d  q=%.4f  %s\n",
       nm, substr(d$feature[r], 1, 40), d$n_NR[r], d$n_R[r], d$q_abun[r],
       if (d$dir_NR_minus_R[r] > 0) "higher in NR" else "higher in R"))
   }
   if (surv == 1L)
     cat("  G4's cost, stated in advance: ONE survivor just under 0.05 in one of\n",
         "  twelve declared families is weak. It is a lead to be tested on other\n",
         "  data, not a result to report as a finding.\n", sep = "")
 }
 if (!length(agree))
   cat("  G5: no feature is nominal in both cohorts with the same direction at any rank.\n")
 cat("  G6: Pittsburgh is on-treatment and Sheba has eight non-responders.\n",
     "      Neither cohort alone can carry a taxon claim.\n", sep = "")

 od <- file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else getwd(), "B48_taxon_scan")
 dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
 for (nm in names(out))
   utils::write.csv(out[[nm]], file.path(od, paste0(gsub(" ", "_", nm), ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
 gd <- if (length(GATEDATA)) do.call(rbind, GATEDATA) else NULL
 if (!is.null(gd)) {
   rownames(gd) <- NULL
   rsp <- c(if (!is.null(pitt)) setNames(as.character(pitt$resp), pitt$ids),
            if (!is.null(shb))  setNames(as.character(shb$resp),  shb$ids))
   gd$resp <- unname(rsp[gd$library])
   utils::write.csv(gd, file.path(od, "depth_gate.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 }
 saveRDS(list(scans = out, agreement = agree, gate = gd,
              bh_families = fam,
              pitt_design = if (is.null(pitt)) NULL else pitt$meta[, c("sample", "bio", "resp", "reads")],
              sheba_design = if (is.null(shb)) NULL else
                data.frame(mg = shb$ids, resp = shb$resp, series = shb$series, reads = shb$reads)),
         file.path(od, "taxon_scan.rds"))
 cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
 b48_taxon_scan <<- out
})
```

## B49 — abundance class control

is the ribosomal elevation a property of these proteins, or of their

Source: `B49_abundance_class_control.R`

```{r B49_abundance_class_control, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B49 — is the ribosomal elevation a property of these proteins, or of their
## ABUNDANCE? The control that can take the result away.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. The within-Blautia ribosomal share is the only BH survivor
## across 25 genera (-0.364, P = 0.00045, q = 0.011; R - NR, so negative means
## higher in non-responders), and the chaperone share co-varies with it at
## +0.46 within plex. Growth is excluded, oxidative stress is excluded, and the
## mechanism slot is now empty. Before anything is built on that slot, one
## alternative has to be closed that needs no physiology at all.
##
## THE ALTERNATIVE. The stool metaproteome is a STANDING POOL in a terminal
## compartment, not a snapshot of living cells. Ribosomal protein and
## chaperones are the two most abundant cytosolic protein classes in a
## bacterium. If non-responder communities lyse more in the colon, or release
## cytosol more readily under the same extraction, then the most abundant
## cytosolic proteins are over-represented in non-responders FOR REASONS THAT
## HAVE NOTHING TO DO WITH RIBOSOMES. The observed pattern -- two abundant
## cytosolic classes up together, with translational activity and replication
## flat -- is exactly what that produces.
##
## THIS IS A DESTRUCTIVE TEST AND IT IS MEANT TO BE. It is run first because a
## positive result invalidates every mechanistic reading downstream of it,
## including the ones in B50 and in the hypotheses document. A control that can
## only confirm is not a control.
##
## TWO ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE DECISIVE ONE.
##
##   [1] GLYCOLYSIS. Abundant, cytosolic, housekeeping, and functionally
##       unrelated to ribosome content. Defined by KO so a wrong entry shows as
##       a zero in the per-KO count printed before any fit, as in export_v4.
##
##   [2] AN ABUNDANCE-MATCHED SET WITH NO FUNCTION AT ALL. For each ribosomal
##       protein detected in the genus, the nearest-abundance protein that is
##       not ribosomal, chaperone, translation-factor or RNA-polymerase is
##       taken, without replacement. The result is a set with the ribosomal
##       set's abundance profile and no functional coherence whatsoever. It
##       cannot respond to anything biological as a set. If it moves with
##       response, the measurement is reading abundance class.
##
## THE READING IS FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS. `est` is R - NR throughout,
## and the ribosomal reference is RECOMPUTED here on the same rows so the
## comparison is like for like.
##
##   SAME SIGN as ribosomal, comparable magnitude, in either arm
##       -> ABUNDANCE-CLASS ARTEFACT. The within-genus share is reading how
##          much cytosol reached the sample, not what the cells were doing.
##          The mechanistic reading collapses and the chaperone/ribosomal
##          result must be re-stated as a lysis-or-release difference.
##
##   OPPOSITE SIGN in glycolysis (positive est, higher in responders)
##       -> PROTEOME REALLOCATION. Ribosome sector up means metabolic sector
##          down; this is the growth-law trade-off without the growth. The
##          result survives and gains a positive reading.
##
##   FLAT, with a 95% interval EXCLUDING the ribosomal estimate, in both arms
##       -> the ribosomal elevation is SPECIFIC. Neither artefact nor
##          reallocation. The result survives as an unexplained specific shift.
##
##   FLAT with an interval that COVERS the ribosomal estimate
##       -> NO INFORMATION. Not a null. Report the interval and say so; this
##          is the mistake the hibernation set already illustrates
##          (-0.130, CI -0.443 to +0.183, which settles nothing).
##
##   source("B49_abundance_class_control.R")
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new", "annot_new", "ribo_new", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, TRUE)]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("B49 needs: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
         ". ribo_new is required -- it is the reference arm, not optional.",
         call. = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("row", "Protein", "tax") %in% names(pep_g)),
            all(c("sample", "Mixture", "resp") %in% names(OP$d)),
            all(c("protein", "cohort", "ko_primary") %in% names(annot_new)))

  GENUS <- "Blautia"            # where the whole result localises; 53% of Bacillota protein mass
  REF   <- -0.364               # the published within-Blautia ribosomal estimate, for the reading

  ## ---- the v4 machinery, unchanged so the fits are comparable --------------
  gf <- function(prots, g) {
    x   <- pep_g[pep_g$tax == g, , drop = FALSE]
    den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE],
                   na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- OP$d; d$num <- num; d$den <- den; d$f <- num / den
    d[is.finite(d$den) & d$den > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  .ko <- function(v) unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                              annot_new$ko_primary %in% v])
  .each <- function(v, label) {
    t <- vapply(v, function(k) sum(annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                   annot_new$ko_primary == k), 0L)
    cat("\n", label, " -- proteins per KO:\n", sep = ""); print(t[order(-t)])
    cat("  peptide rows in pep_g: ", sum(pep_g$Protein %in% .ko(v)),
        " | of those in ", GENUS, ": ",
        sum(pep_g$Protein %in% .ko(v) & pep_g$tax == GENUS), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  fit <- function(d, label) {
    d <- d[is.finite(d$f) & d$f > 0 & d$f < 1, , drop = FALSE]
    d$Mixture <- factor(as.character(d$Mixture))
    d$resp    <- factor(as.character(d$resp))
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || nlevels(d$Mixture) < 2 || nlevels(d$resp) < 2) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-22s NOT TESTABLE (n = %d, plexes = %d, arms = %d)\n",
                  label, nrow(d), nlevels(d$Mixture), nlevels(d$resp)))
      return(NULL)
    }
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d)))
    if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) { cat("  ", label, ": no respR term\n"); return(NULL) }
    e <- cf["respR", 1]; s <- cf["respR", 2]
    ci <- e + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df.residual(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d))) * s
    cat(sprintf("  %-22s n=%2d  medNR %.4f  medR %.4f  est %+.3f  SE %.3f  CI %+.3f..%+.3f  P %.4g\n",
                label, nrow(d), median(d$f[d$resp == "NR"]), median(d$f[d$resp == "R"]),
                e, s, ci[1], ci[2], cf["respR", 4]))
    list(label = label, n = nrow(d), est = e, se = s, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2],
         p = cf["respR", 4])
  }

  ## ---- arm 1: glycolysis ---------------------------------------------------
  ## Core EMP enzymes only. Each is among the most abundant cytosolic proteins
  ## in a fermentative Firmicute, which is the property being tested; the
  ## pathway identity is incidental.
  GLYC <- c("K00134",  # gapA, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (NAD+)
            "K01689",  # eno, enolase
            "K00927",  # pgk, phosphoglycerate kinase
            "K00873",  # pyk, pyruvate kinase
            "K01623",  # fbaA, fructose-bisphosphate aldolase class I
            "K01624",  # fba,  fructose-bisphosphate aldolase class II
            "K01803",  # tpiA, triose-phosphate isomerase
            "K01834",  # gpmA, 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate-dependent PGAM
            "K15633",  # gpmI, cofactor-independent PGAM (the Firmicute form)
            "K01810",  # pgi,  glucose-6-phosphate isomerase
            "K00850")  # pfkA, 6-phosphofructokinase
  TRAN <- c("K02358","K02355","K02357","K02356","K02518","K02519","K02520",
            "K02835","K02836","K02837")
  RNAP <- c("K03040","K03043","K03046","K03060")
  .each(GLYC, "GLYCOLYSIS")

  ## ---- arm 2: the abundance-matched set ------------------------------------
  ## Per-protein total intensity inside the genus, then nearest-abundance
  ## matching to the ribosomal set without replacement, excluding anything with
  ## a function that could plausibly co-move.
  x    <- pep_g[pep_g$tax == GENUS, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(x)) stop("B49: no peptide rows for ", GENUS, call. = FALSE)
  pint <- tapply(rowSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
                 x$Protein, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
  pint <- pint[is.finite(pint) & pint > 0]
  EXCL <- unique(c(ribo_new, chap_new, .ko(TRAN), .ko(RNAP), .ko(GLYC)))
  ribo_here <- intersect(names(pint), ribo_new)
  pool      <- setdiff(names(pint), EXCL)
  cat(sprintf("\nABUNDANCE MATCHING in %s: %d proteins with signal, %d ribosomal, %d eligible as controls\n",
              GENUS, length(pint), length(ribo_here), length(pool)))
  if (length(ribo_here) < 5 || length(pool) < length(ribo_here)) {
    cat("  too few proteins to match; arm 2 is not run\n"); matched <- character(0)
  } else {
    lr <- log(pint[ribo_here]); lp <- log(pint[pool]); matched <- character(0)
    for (v in sort(lr, decreasing = TRUE)) {          # deepest first, so the
      if (!length(lp)) break                          # scarce high end matches
      j <- which.min(abs(lp - v))
      matched <- c(matched, names(lp)[j]); lp <- lp[-j]
    }
    cat(sprintf("  matched %d control proteins; median log-intensity ribosomal %.2f vs control %.2f\n",
                length(matched), median(lr), median(log(pint[matched]))))
  }

  ## ---- the fits ------------------------------------------------------------
  cat("\nB49 within ", GENUS, " (est is R - NR; negative = higher in non-responders)\n", sep = "")
  res <- list()
  res$ribosomal <- fit(gf(ribo_new,  GENUS), "ribosomal (reference)")
  res$chaperone <- fit(gf(chap_new,  GENUS), "chaperone")
  res$glycolysis <- fit(gf(.ko(GLYC), GENUS), "glycolysis")
  if (length(matched)) res$matched <- fit(gf(matched, GENUS), "abundance-matched")

  ## ---- the verdict, against the rules fixed above --------------------------
  cat("\nB49 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
  r <- res$ribosomal
  if (is.null(r)) { cat("  reference arm did not fit; nothing can be read.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  cat(sprintf("  reference: ribosomal est %+.3f (published %+.3f)\n", r$est, REF))
  for (k in c("glycolysis", "matched")) {
    a <- res[[k]]; if (is.null(a)) next
    same <- sign(a$est) == sign(r$est) && abs(a$est) >= 0.5 * abs(r$est) && a$p < 0.05
    opp  <- sign(a$est) != sign(r$est) && a$p < 0.05
    excl <- (r$est < a$lo) || (r$est > a$hi)
    cat(sprintf("  %-18s ", k))
    if (same)      cat("SAME SIGN and comparable -> ABUNDANCE-CLASS ARTEFACT; the\n",
                       "                     mechanistic reading collapses and the result must be\n",
                       "                     re-stated as a lysis-or-release difference.\n", sep = "")
    else if (opp)  cat("OPPOSITE SIGN -> proteome reallocation; the ribosome sector\n",
                       "                     rises as the metabolic sector falls. Result survives.\n", sep = "")
    else if (excl) cat("flat, and its interval EXCLUDES the ribosomal estimate ->\n",
                       "                     the ribosomal elevation is specific. Result survives.\n", sep = "")
    else           cat("flat, but its interval COVERS the ribosomal estimate ->\n",
                       "                     NO INFORMATION. Not a null. Do not report it as one.\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n  Arm 2 is the decisive one: an abundance-matched set has no function,\n",
      "  so it cannot respond to anything biological. Read it before arm 1.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B49_abundance_class"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(list(genus = GENUS, fits = res, matched = matched,
               glycolysis_kos = GLYC), file.path(od, "abundance_class.rds"))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(Filter(Negate(is.null), res), as.data.frame))
  utils::write.csv(out, file.path(od, "fits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b49_abundance_class <<- out
})
```

## B50 — prophage induction

does prophage induction explain the ribosome-and-chaperone state?

Source: `B50_prophage_induction.R`

```{r B50_prophage_induction, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B50 — does prophage induction explain the ribosome-and-chaperone state?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. The state to explain is specific: within Blautia, ribosomal
## protein is elevated in non-responders (-0.364, P = 0.00045), chaperones
## co-vary with it (+0.46 within plex), while translation factors are flat with
## an interval that EXCLUDES the ribosomal effect, and replication rate is null.
## More ribosome mass, no more elongation, no more division.
##
## Prophage induction produces that combination for a reason that has nothing to
## do with growth. An induced cell mounts a heat-shock response -- DnaK and
## GroEL are the canonical induction markers -- stops dividing, keeps the
## ribosomes it already has, and eventually lyses. Lachnospiraceae are
## prophage-rich, and the search database for this cohort was assembled from the
## cohort's own metagenomes and called with Prokka, so phage structural ORFs are
## in the searched space already. This costs no new measurement.
##
## IT ALSO BRIDGES TO B49. Induction ends in lysis, so a positive result here is
## not independent of the abundance-class artefact B49 tests -- it is a
## mechanism FOR it. RUN B49 FIRST. If B49 says the signal is abundance class,
## this script tells you what drove the lysis; if B49 says the signal is
## specific, this script tests a cause of the specific state. The two readings
## are different and the order decides which one applies.
##
## THE FEASIBILITY GATE IS DECLARED BEFORE THE NUMBERS, AND IT IS NOT A
## FORMALITY. A set proposed on 15 Oct 2026 for an adjacent question returned
## three peptide rows in one genus, and was only caught because detectability
## was checked before the fit rather than after. Phage structural proteins in a
## stool metaproteome are expected to be scarce.
##
##   GATE: a set is testable only with >= 10 distinct proteins carrying peptide
##   rows AND >= 20 samples with a non-zero numerator. Below either, the script
##   prints the counts and reports NOT TESTABLE. A thin set that happens to
##   produce a small p is not a result, and no p is printed for a set that
##   fails the gate.
##
## THE READING IS FIXED HERE. `est` is R - NR, so NEGATIVE means higher in
## non-responders, the same direction as the ribosomal and chaperone shares.
##
##   phage structural share NEGATIVE and its within-plex residual correlation
##   with the chaperone share POSITIVE
##       -> consistent with induction. NOT established by this alone: the next
##          step is prophage-region coverage and induction ratios in the
##          metagenome assemblies, which this script does not touch.
##
##   phage structural share flat, OR uncorrelated with the chaperone share
##       -> induction does not explain the state. Record and close.
##
##   gate fails
##       -> NOT TESTABLE in this assay. Say so. Do not report the fit.
##
## A POSITIVE CORRELATION IS THE WEAKER HALF OF THE EVIDENCE, not the stronger.
## Chaperones are induced by many things and phage proteins are abundant in
## lysed material, so the two can co-vary through lysis alone. The arm-level
## difference is what carries weight; the correlation only says the two live in
## the same samples.
##
##   source("B50_prophage_induction.R")
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new", "annot_new", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, TRUE)]
  if (length(miss)) stop("B50 needs: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  GENUS <- "Blautia"
  MIN_PROT <- 10L; MIN_SAMP <- 20L          # the gate, fixed above

  gf <- function(prots, g = NULL) {
    x   <- if (is.null(g)) pep_g else pep_g[pep_g$tax == g, , drop = FALSE]
    den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE],
                   na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- OP$d; d$num <- num; d$den <- den; d$f <- num / den
    d[is.finite(d$den) & d$den > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  ## ---- 1. find the free-text annotation, rather than assuming it -----------
  ## annot_new carries ko_primary, which does not describe phage structure:
  ## KEGG orthology is sparse for virion proteins. The product description is
  ## what Prokka and eggNOG supply, and its column name is not fixed, so the
  ## column is DISCOVERED and named in the output.
  cand <- names(annot_new)[vapply(annot_new, is.character, TRUE)]
  cand <- setdiff(cand, c("protein", "cohort", "ko_primary"))
  score <- vapply(cand, function(k) {
    v <- annot_new[[k]][annot_new$cohort == "pitt"]
    mean(nchar(v) > 12, na.rm = TRUE) }, 0)
  if (!length(cand) || max(score, na.rm = TRUE) < 0.2) {
    cat("B50 STOPPED: annot_new carries no free-text description column.\n",
        "  columns present: ", paste(names(annot_new), collapse = ", "), "\n",
        "  Phage structural proteins cannot be identified from ko_primary alone.\n",
        "  Resolve by joining the Prokka product field for the Pittsburgh\n",
        "  assembly before running this.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  DESC <- cand[which.max(score)]
  cat("B50: using '", DESC, "' as the description column (", nrow(annot_new),
      " annotation rows)\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- 2. the term lists, with per-term counts printed before any fit ------
  ## Terms are deliberately conservative. "integrase" is kept OUT of the
  ## structural set: it marks a prophage's PRESENCE, not its induction, and it
  ## is promiscuous across mobile elements. Amidase is kept out of the lytic
  ## set for the same reason -- host autolysins carry the same description.
  STRUCT_T <- c("major capsid", "capsid protein", "portal protein", "terminase",
                "tail fiber", "tail fibre", "tape measure", "baseplate",
                "head-tail", "major tail", "prohead", "phage tail", "phage head")
  LYTIC_T  <- c("holin", "endolysin", "phage lysin", "antiholin")
  MARK_T   <- c("phage integrase", "prophage")        # presence, not induction
  hits <- function(terms) {
    v <- tolower(annot_new[[DESC]]); k <- annot_new$cohort == "pitt"
    unique(annot_new$protein[k & Reduce(`|`, lapply(terms, function(t)
      grepl(t, v, fixed = TRUE)))])
  }
  report <- function(terms, label) {
    v <- tolower(annot_new[[DESC]]); k <- annot_new$cohort == "pitt"
    t <- vapply(terms, function(t) sum(k & grepl(t, v, fixed = TRUE)), 0L)
    cat("\n", label, " -- proteins per term:\n", sep = ""); print(t[order(-t)])
    p <- hits(terms)
    inpep <- unique(pep_g$Protein[pep_g$Protein %in% p])
    ing   <- unique(pep_g$Protein[pep_g$Protein %in% p & pep_g$tax == GENUS])
    cat(sprintf("  %d proteins | %d with peptide rows | %d of those in %s\n",
                length(p), length(inpep), length(ing), GENUS))
    p
  }
  STRUCT <- report(STRUCT_T, "PHAGE STRUCTURAL")
  LYTIC  <- report(LYTIC_T,  "PHAGE LYTIC")
  MARK   <- report(MARK_T,   "PROPHAGE MARKER (presence, not induction)")

  ## ---- 3. the gate ---------------------------------------------------------
  gated <- function(prots, g, label) {
    d <- gf(prots, g)
    np <- length(unique(pep_g$Protein[pep_g$Protein %in% prots &
                                      (is.null(g) | pep_g$tax %in% g)]))
    ns <- sum(d$num > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (np < MIN_PROT || ns < MIN_SAMP) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-34s NOT TESTABLE: %d proteins (need %d), %d samples with signal (need %d)\n",
                  label, np, MIN_PROT, ns, MIN_SAMP))
      return(NULL)
    }
    d <- d[is.finite(d$f) & d$f > 0 & d$f < 1, , drop = FALSE]
    d$Mixture <- factor(as.character(d$Mixture)); d$resp <- factor(as.character(d$resp))
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || nlevels(d$Mixture) < 2 || nlevels(d$resp) < 2) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-34s NOT TESTABLE after the share filter (n = %d)\n", label, nrow(d)))
      return(NULL)
    }
    m  <- lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d); cf <- coef(summary(m))
    if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) return(NULL)
    e <- cf["respR", 1]; s <- cf["respR", 2]
    ci <- e + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df.residual(m)) * s
    cat(sprintf("  %-34s n=%2d  medNR %.5f  medR %.5f  est %+.3f  CI %+.3f..%+.3f  P %.4g\n",
                label, nrow(d), median(d$f[d$resp == "NR"]), median(d$f[d$resp == "R"]),
                e, ci[1], ci[2], cf["respR", 4]))
    list(label = label, n = nrow(d), est = e, se = s, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2],
         p = cf["respR", 4], d = d[, c("sample", "Mixture", "resp", "f")])
  }
  cat("\nB50 arm-level tests (est is R - NR; negative = higher in non-responders)\n")
  res <- list(
    struct_blautia = gated(STRUCT, GENUS, paste("phage structural, ", GENUS)),
    struct_all     = gated(STRUCT, NULL,  "phage structural, all taxa"),
    lytic_all      = gated(LYTIC,  NULL,  "phage lytic, all taxa"),
    marker_all     = gated(MARK,   NULL,  "prophage marker, all taxa"))

  ## ---- 4. the link, within plex -------------------------------------------
  ## Residualise each share on Mixture, then correlate across samples. This is
  ## the same within-plex footing every other correlation in this project uses.
  link <- NULL
  A <- res$struct_all
  if (!is.null(A)) {
    ch <- gf(chap_new, GENUS); rb <- if (exists("ribo_new")) gf(ribo_new, GENUS) else NULL
    mk <- function(d) { d <- d[is.finite(d$f) & d$f > 0 & d$f < 1, , drop = FALSE]
      stats::setNames(residuals(lm(qlogis(f) ~ factor(Mixture), d)), d$sample) }
    rp <- mk(A$d); rc <- mk(ch); rr <- if (is.null(rb)) NULL else mk(rb)
    cat("\nB50 within-plex residual correlation of the phage structural share with\n")
    for (nm in c("chaperone", "ribosomal")) {
      y <- if (nm == "chaperone") rc else rr
      if (is.null(y)) { cat(sprintf("  %-10s not available\n", nm)); next }
      i <- intersect(names(rp), names(y))
      if (length(i) < 15) { cat(sprintf("  %-10s too few shared samples (%d)\n", nm, length(i))); next }
      ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(rp[i], y[i], method = "spearman"))
      cat(sprintf("  %-10s rho = %+.3f  P = %.4g  (n = %d)\n", nm,
                  unname(ct$estimate), ct$p.value, length(i)))
      link <- rbind(link, data.frame(with = nm, rho = unname(ct$estimate),
                                     p = ct$p.value, n = length(i)))
    }
  }

  ## ---- 5. the verdict ------------------------------------------------------
  cat("\nB50 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
  if (is.null(res$struct_all) && is.null(res$struct_blautia)) {
    cat("  GATE FAILS. Phage structural protein is not detectable at the depth\n",
        "  this assay reaches, so prophage induction is NOT TESTABLE here and no\n",
        "  p-value from this script should be quoted. The question is not closed;\n",
        "  it is unasked. The metagenome route -- prophage-region coverage and\n",
        "  induction ratios in the cohort assemblies -- remains open and needs no\n",
        "  proteome detection at all.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    a <- if (!is.null(res$struct_all)) res$struct_all else res$struct_blautia
    pos <- !is.null(link) && any(link$with == "chaperone" & link$rho > 0 & link$p < 0.05)
    if (a$est < 0 && a$p < 0.05 && pos)
      cat("  CONSISTENT WITH INDUCTION: phage structural protein is higher in\n",
          "  non-responders and co-varies with the chaperone share within plex.\n",
          "  This is not established. Next: prophage-region coverage and induction\n",
          "  ratios in the metagenome assemblies. And read it against B49 -- if the\n",
          "  signal there is abundance class, this is the mechanism for the lysis,\n",
          "  not for a physiological state.\n", sep = "")
    else if (a$p >= 0.05)
      cat(sprintf("  NOT SUPPORTED: the arm-level difference is flat (est %+.3f, CI %+.3f..%+.3f).\n",
                  a$est, a$lo, a$hi),
          "  Induction does not explain the state. Record and close.\n", sep = "")
    else
      cat("  PARTIAL: an arm-level difference without the within-plex correlation,\n",
          "  or the reverse. Neither half alone supports induction; report both.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B50_prophage"); dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  fits <- Filter(Negate(is.null), res)
  if (length(fits)) {
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, function(z) as.data.frame(z[setdiff(names(z), "d")])))
    utils::write.csv(out, file.path(od, "fits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }
  saveRDS(list(desc_column = DESC, struct = STRUCT, lytic = LYTIC, marker = MARK,
               fits = lapply(fits, function(z) z[setdiff(names(z), "d")]), link = link),
          file.path(od, "prophage.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

## B51 — subgenus composition

is the within-Blautia ribosomal elevation a SUB-GENUS COMPOSITION

Source: `B51_subgenus_composition.R`

```{r B51_subgenus_composition, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B51 — is the within-Blautia ribosomal elevation a SUB-GENUS COMPOSITION
## effect? The second destructive test.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS. After B49, the state is: ribosome sector up in
## non-responders (-0.364), glycolytic sector down (+0.206), the paired
## contrast ribosomal - glycolysis -0.558 (P = 0.0034), translation factors
## flat with an interval excluding the effect, replication null, no
## abundance-class artefact (matched set +0.028, SE 0.068), and hibernation
## disfavoured and in the wrong direction (+0.122 on HPF per ribosome).
##
## That reads as proteome reallocation. It is also EXACTLY what a shift in
## which Blautia species a patient carries would produce, for no physiological
## reason at all: Blautia species differ in rRNA operon copy number and
## baseline ribosome content, and in fermentative strategy -- sugar users
## against amino-acid and mucin users -- which moves the glycolytic sector the
## other way. Every observation to date is consistent with both.
##
## THE SPECIES SCREEN DID NOT SETTLE IT AND WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT. Fourteen
## Wilcoxon tests on Blautia species composition (68 libraries, NR 36 / R 32)
## returned nothing at BH, min q = 0.257 -- but the two nominal hits sit at
## median 0.0000 in both arms, which cannot move a protein share, while the
## species that could move one are UNTESTED rather than null: B. massiliensis
## 12.1% vs 3.4% at P = 0.26, B. faecis 6.3% vs 11.3%, B. obeum 6.7% vs 9.4%,
## B. wexlerae 45.2% vs 41.8%. Those are large compositional differences the
## test could not resolve. An interval that covers everything is not absence.
##
## SO ASK THE QUESTION THAT NEEDS NO SPECIES TO BE SIGNIFICANT. Does the
## species mix, taken as a whole, predict the ribosomal protein share? And
## does conditioning on it remove the response coefficient?
##
## THE PRIOR QUESTION IS CLEANER THAN THE RETENTION NUMBER. If the species mix
## does not predict the ribosomal share at all, it cannot be the confounder,
## and B is closed without any adjustment being interpreted. That test is run
## first and reported whatever it shows.
##
## AND A FALL IN THE COEFFICIENT WOULD NOT PROVE CONFOUNDING. Section 10's
## existing note applies here one rank down: if response acts partly THROUGH
## which species a patient carries, then adjusting for the species mix removes
## mediated effect rather than bias, and the adjusted value bounds the
## non-compositional part rather than establishing an artefact. The script says
## this in its own verdict so the number is not over-read.
##
## COMPOSITION IS SUMMARISED WITHOUT A PSEUDO-COUNT. Hellinger (square-root)
## transform, then PCA. CLR would need zeros filled, and filling zeros on
## compositional data is the move that produced thirteen spurious survivors in
## this project on 15 Oct.
##
## THE READING IS FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS.
##
##   [1] composition does NOT predict the ribosomal share (joint P >= 0.05 and
##       small partial R2)
##         -> sub-genus composition is not the explanation. B closed. The
##            reallocation reading survives this test.
##
##   [2] composition predicts it AND conditioning retains < 50% of the response
##       coefficient
##         -> the effect is substantially sub-genus composition. The
##            reallocation reading must be re-stated, and the bound in the note
##            above applies: this is the non-compositional part, not proof of
##            artefact.
##
##   [3] composition predicts it and retention stays >= 80%
##         -> composition is a correlate, not the explanation. B closed.
##
##   [4] fewer than 30 paired samples
##         -> NOT TESTABLE here. Say so; do not report a coefficient.
##
##   source("B51_subgenus_composition.R")
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("mpa_raw", "mg_clean", "mg_meta", "KEEP_5M", "OP", "pep_g",
            "ribo_new", "annot_new", "norm_id", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, TRUE)]
  if (length(miss)) stop("B51 needs: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  G <- "Blautia"; MIN_PAIR <- 30L
  GLYC <- c("K00134","K01689","K00927","K00873","K01623","K01624",
            "K01803","K01834","K15633","K01810","K00850")

  ## ---- 1. Blautia species composition, per metagenome library -------------
  cn  <- names(mpa_raw)[1]
  sel <- grepl(paste0("\\|g__", G, "\\|s__"), mpa_raw[[cn]]) &
         !grepl("\\|t__", mpa_raw[[cn]])
  if (!any(sel)) stop("B51: no ", G, " species rows in mpa_raw", call. = FALSE)
  X <- as.matrix(mpa_raw[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); storage.mode(X) <- "double"
  X[!is.finite(X)] <- 0
  rownames(X) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", mpa_raw[[cn]][sel])
  colnames(X) <- mg_clean(colnames(X))
  mg_ok <- intersect(colnames(X), intersect(mg_meta$sample[!is.na(mg_meta$resp)], KEEP_5M))
  X <- X[, mg_ok, drop = FALSE]
  X <- X[, colSums(X) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  FR <- sweep(X, 2, colSums(X), "/")                 # within-genus composition
  FR <- FR[rowSums(FR > 0) >= 10, , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("B51: %d %s species over %d metagenome libraries\n",
              nrow(FR), G, ncol(FR)))

  ## ---- 2. proteome shares, per proteome sample ----------------------------
  gf <- function(prots) {
    x   <- pep_g[pep_g$tax == G, , drop = FALSE]
    den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE],
                   na.rm = TRUE)
    stats::setNames(num / den, OP$d$sample)
  }
  .ko <- function(v) unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                              annot_new$ko_primary %in% v])
  f_ribo <- gf(ribo_new); f_glyc <- gf(.ko(GLYC))

  ## ---- 3. the join, reported at every step --------------------------------
  .f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B41_supp_tables", "supp_data_sample_metadata.csv")
  if (!file.exists(.f)) stop("B51: roster not found: ", .f, call. = FALSE)
  ros <- utils::read.csv(.f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  ros <- ros[grepl("^Pittsburgh", ros$cohort), c("sample", "patient")]
  ros$key <- norm_id(ros$patient)
  mgk <- mg_meta$bio[match(mg_ok, mg_meta$sample)]
  cat(sprintf("  roster rows %d | metagenome libraries with a patient key %d\n",
              nrow(ros), sum(!is.na(mgk))))
  prot_s <- OP$d$sample
  key_p  <- ros$key[match(prot_s, ros$sample)]
  mg_for <- mg_ok[match(key_p, mgk)]
  ok <- !is.na(key_p) & !is.na(mg_for) & mg_for %in% colnames(FR) &
        is.finite(f_ribo[prot_s]) & f_ribo[prot_s] > 0 & f_ribo[prot_s] < 1
  cat(sprintf("  proteome samples %d | with a patient key %d | paired to a metagenome %d\n",
              length(prot_s), sum(!is.na(key_p)), sum(ok)))
  if (sum(ok) < MIN_PAIR) {
    cat(sprintf("\nB51 STOPPED: only %d paired samples, below the %d declared above.\n",
                sum(ok), MIN_PAIR),
        "  This is rule [4]: NOT TESTABLE. No coefficient is reported.\n",
        "  Check the roster patient field against mg_meta$bio before rerunning.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  d <- data.frame(sample = prot_s[ok], mg = mg_for[ok],
                  Mixture = factor(as.character(OP$d$Mixture[ok])),
                  resp = factor(as.character(OP$d$resp[ok]), levels = c("NR", "R")),
                  ribo = f_ribo[prot_s[ok]], glyc = f_glyc[prot_s[ok]],
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  d$y <- qlogis(d$ribo)
  d$contrast <- ifelse(is.finite(d$glyc) & d$glyc > 0 & d$glyc < 1,
                       qlogis(d$ribo) - qlogis(d$glyc), NA_real_)

  ## ---- 4. composition axes, Hellinger then PCA, no pseudo-count -----------
  H  <- t(sqrt(FR[, d$mg, drop = FALSE]))
  H  <- H[, apply(H, 2, stats::sd) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  pc <- stats::prcomp(H, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  ev <- pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2)
  d$PC1 <- pc$x[, 1]; d$PC2 <- pc$x[, 2]
  if ("Blautia_wexlerae" %in% rownames(FR)) d$wex <- as.numeric(FR["Blautia_wexlerae", d$mg])
  cat(sprintf("  composition axes: PC1 %.1f%% of variance, PC2 %.1f%% (%d species, %d samples)\n",
              100 * ev[1], 100 * ev[2], ncol(H), nrow(H)))

  ## ---- 5. the prior question, then the conditioning -----------------------
  say <- function(m, lab) {
    cf <- coef(summary(m))
    if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) { cat("  ", lab, ": no respR term\n"); return(NA_real_) }
    cat(sprintf("  %-34s est %+.3f  SE %.3f  P %.4g\n", lab,
                cf["respR", 1], cf["respR", 2], cf["respR", 4]))
    cf["respR", 1]
  }
  cat("\nB51 [prior question] does the species mix predict the ribosomal share?\n")
  m0 <- lm(y ~ Mixture, d); m1 <- lm(y ~ Mixture + PC1 + PC2, d)
  an <- stats::anova(m0, m1)
  r2 <- summary(m1)$r.squared - summary(m0)$r.squared
  cat(sprintf("  joint F = %.3f on %d and %d df, P = %.4g | partial R2 = %.3f\n",
              an$F[2], an$Df[2], an$Res.Df[2], an$`Pr(>F)`[2], r2))
  predicts <- is.finite(an$`Pr(>F)`[2]) && an$`Pr(>F)`[2] < 0.05

  cat("\nB51 [conditioning] ribosomal share by response\n")
  e_raw <- say(lm(y ~ Mixture + resp, d),                   "unadjusted (paired subset)")
  e_pc  <- say(lm(y ~ Mixture + PC1 + PC2 + resp, d),       "+ species-mix axes")
  if (!is.null(d$wex))
    say(lm(y ~ Mixture + wex + resp, d),                    "+ B. wexlerae fraction")
  dc <- d[is.finite(d$contrast), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(dc) >= MIN_PAIR) {
    cat("\nB51 [conditioning] ribosomal - glycolysis contrast\n")
    say(lm(contrast ~ Mixture + resp, dc),                  "unadjusted")
    say(lm(contrast ~ Mixture + PC1 + PC2 + resp, dc),      "+ species-mix axes")
  } else cat("\n  contrast not run: only ", nrow(dc), " samples carry both shares\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- 6. the verdict -----------------------------------------------------
  ret <- if (is.finite(e_raw) && e_raw != 0) e_pc / e_raw else NA_real_
  cat("\nB51 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
  if (!predicts) {
    cat("  [1] The species mix does NOT predict the ribosomal share. Sub-genus\n",
        "      composition cannot be the explanation, and B is closed without any\n",
        "      adjustment needing interpretation. The reallocation reading survives\n",
        "      this test.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (is.finite(ret) && ret < 0.5) {
    cat(sprintf("  [2] The species mix predicts the share and conditioning retains %.0f%%\n", 100 * ret),
        "      of the response coefficient. The effect is substantially sub-genus\n",
        "      composition and the reallocation reading must be re-stated.\n",
        "      BUT: if response acts partly through which species a patient carries,\n",
        "      this adjustment removes MEDIATED effect, not bias. The adjusted value\n",
        "      bounds the non-compositional part; it does not establish an artefact.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (is.finite(ret) && ret >= 0.8) {
    cat(sprintf("  [3] The species mix predicts the share, but conditioning retains %.0f%%\n", 100 * ret),
        "      of the response coefficient. Composition is a correlate, not the\n",
        "      explanation. B closed.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  BETWEEN THE RULES: retention %.0f%%. Neither [2] nor [3] applies as\n", 100 * ret),
        "      written. Report both coefficients and the partial R2 and let the\n",
        "      reader see the partial attenuation; do not pick a branch after the fact.\n", sep = "")
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B51_subgenus_composition")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  utils::write.csv(d[, setdiff(names(d), "y")], file.path(od, "paired.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(fractions = FR, paired = d, pca_var = ev,
               predicts = predicts, est_raw = e_raw, est_adj = e_pc, retention = ret),
          file.path(od, "subgenus.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
  b51_subgenus <<- d
})
```

## B52 — sporulation

is the non-responder state a SPORULATION / DORMANCY state?

Source: `B52_sporulation.R`

```{r B52_sporulation, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B52 — is the non-responder state a SPORULATION / DORMANCY state?
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS HYPOTHESIS. After B49 and B51 the state to explain is: ribosome
## sector up in non-responders (-0.364), glycolytic sector down (+0.206,
## paired contrast -0.558, P = 0.0034), translation factors flat with an
## interval EXCLUDING the effect, replication null, no abundance-class
## artefact (matched set +0.028, SE 0.068), hibernation disfavoured and in the
## wrong direction (+0.122), and only a fifth of the effect attributable to
## which Blautia species the patient carries. Allocation without activity.
##
## A dormant endospore is that state by construction. Zhou et al. (PNAS 2019,
## doi:10.1073/pnas.1817742116) show that dormant Bacillus spores RETAIN their
## ribosomes and translational machinery while holding them inactive through
## arginine phosphorylation, and that germination proceeds by dephosphorylating
## them -- the YwlE phosphatase acting on the ribosome-associated chaperone
## TRIGGER FACTOR to let it re-associate with the ribosome and restart
## translation, and on SigA to restart transcription. Ribosomes present,
## translation suppressed, metabolism off, no division, no lysis: every
## constraint at once, including the chaperone co-elevation.
##
## Spore-formers are a major component of the gut microbiota, not a curiosity
## (doi:10.3390/ijms23063405), and bile salts induce sporulation by promoting
## Spo0A phosphorylation (doi:10.1128/AEM.00252-16) -- which puts this on the
## same bile-acid axis the ICB literature already occupies.
##
## THE KOs WERE LOOKED UP, NOT RECALLED. Every identifier below was resolved
## against the KEGG REST API on 15 Oct 2026 (rest.kegg.jp/find/ko/...), because
## a mis-remembered KO enters a set silently and a scan built on one is worse
## than no scan. Per-KO counts are printed before any fit regardless, as in
## export_v4, so a zero is visible.
##
## DETECTABILITY IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THESE SETS, AND THAT ASYMMETRY GOVERNS
## THE READING. Small acid-soluble spore proteins are tiny, highly basic and
## lysine/arginine-rich, so tryptic digestion leaves peptides too short to
## identify; spore coat proteins are cross-linked and poorly solubilised. Both
## are expected to be under-detected for STRUCTURAL reasons that have nothing
## to do with whether sporulation is happening. The germination apparatus and
## the sporulation machinery are ordinary soluble proteins and are the ones
## this assay can actually test.
##
##   THEREFORE: a null on SASP or COAT is NOT evidence against sporulation.
##   Only MACH and GERM carry evidential weight in either direction, and the
##   gate below is what separates "absent" from "undetectable".
##
## GATE, fixed above the numbers: a set is testable with >= 5 distinct proteins
## carrying peptide rows AND >= 20 samples with a non-zero numerator. Below
## either, the counts are printed and NO p-value is reported for that set.
##
## THE READING IS FIXED HERE. `est` is R - NR, so NEGATIVE means higher in
## non-responders, the direction of the ribosomal and chaperone shares.
##
##   [1] MACH or GERM negative and surviving its gate
##         -> consistent with a sporulation/dormancy state, and the ribosome
##            elevation has a named cause. Not established: the next step is
##            the spore-marker genes in the metagenome, and the bile-acid link.
##
##   [2] MACH and GERM both flat with intervals EXCLUDING -0.364
##         -> sporulation excluded as the explanation. Record and close.
##
##   [3] gates fail on MACH and GERM
##         -> NOT TESTABLE in this assay. The question is unasked, not closed.
##
## PART 2 IS A SHARPER TEST THAN PART 1. Zhou et al.'s mechanism runs through
## TRIGGER FACTOR (tig, K03545), the ribosome-associated chaperone. If the
## chaperone co-elevation is carried by tig rather than by DnaK and GroEL, that
## is this mechanism's fingerprint rather than a heat-shock signature. If tig
## is flat and the classical chaperones carry it, that argues against.
##
##   source("B52_sporulation.R")
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "annot_new", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, TRUE)]
  if (length(miss)) stop("B52 needs: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  G <- "Blautia"; MIN_PROT <- 5L; MIN_SAMP <- 20L

  gf <- function(prots, g = NULL) {
    x   <- if (is.null(g)) pep_g else pep_g[pep_g$tax == g, , drop = FALSE]
    den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE],
                   na.rm = TRUE)
    d <- OP$d; d$num <- num; d$den <- den; d$f <- num / den
    d[is.finite(d$den) & d$den > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  .ko <- function(v) unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                              annot_new$ko_primary %in% v])

  ## ---- the sets, every KO resolved against KEGG 15 Oct 2026 ---------------
  ## small acid-soluble spore proteins -- the most spore-specific marker there
  ## is, and the least likely to be detectable. K06418 covers sspA/B/C/D.
  SASP <- c("K06418","K06422","K06423","K06424","K06425","K06426","K06427",
            "K06428","K06429","K06430","K06431","K06432","K06433","K06434")
  ## spore coat, cortex and maturation -- cross-linked, poorly solubilised
  COAT <- c("K06324","K06325","K06326","K06327","K06328","K06329","K06330",
            "K06331","K06332","K06333","K06334","K06335","K06336","K06337",
            "K06338","K06339","K06340","K06341","K06342","K06343","K06345",
            "K06436","K01994","K06319","K06320","K06321","K06322","K06323",
            "K06373","K06374")
  ## germination apparatus -- ordinary soluble proteins, testable
  GERM <- c("K06288","K06289","K06290","K06291","K06292","K06293","K06294",
            "K06295","K06296","K06297","K06299","K06300","K06301","K06302",
            "K06303","K06304","K06305","K06307","K06308","K06309","K06310",
            "K06311","K06312","K06313","K06012","K03716")
  ## sporulation initiation and machinery -- the stage-specific proteins, plus
  ## dipicolinate synthase, which makes the spore's defining small molecule
  MACH <- c("K07699","K02490","K06375","K02491","K07697","K07698","K13532",
            "K13533","K06376","K06377","K06371","K06378","K06379","K06380",
            "K06381","K06382","K06383","K06384","K06385","K06386","K06387",
            "K06390","K06391","K06392","K06393","K06394","K06395","K06396",
            "K06397","K06398","K06399","K06401","K06402","K06403","K06404",
            "K06405","K06406","K06407","K06408","K06409","K06412","K06413",
            "K06414","K06415","K06416","K06417","K04769","K06283","K06410",
            "K06411","K08384","K06437","K06438","K06314","K06318")
  TIG  <- "K03545"                                   # trigger factor

  .each <- function(v, label) {
    t <- vapply(v, function(k) sum(annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                   annot_new$ko_primary == k), 0L)
    nz <- t[t > 0]
    cat("\n", label, " -- ", sum(t), " proteins over ", length(v), " KOs; ",
        length(nz), " KOs non-empty\n", sep = "")
    if (length(nz)) print(sort(nz, decreasing = TRUE))
    p <- .ko(v)
    cat(sprintf("  peptide rows %d | in %s %d\n",
                sum(pep_g$Protein %in% p), G, sum(pep_g$Protein %in% p & pep_g$tax == G)))
    p
  }
  P <- list(SASP = .each(SASP, "SASP (expect under-detection)"),
            COAT = .each(COAT, "SPORE COAT (expect under-detection)"),
            GERM = .each(GERM, "GERMINATION apparatus"),
            MACH = .each(MACH, "SPORULATION machinery"),
            TIG  = .each(TIG,  "TRIGGER FACTOR"))

  ## ---- the gated fit ------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- function(prots, g, label) {
    d  <- gf(prots, g)
    np <- length(unique(pep_g$Protein[pep_g$Protein %in% prots &
                 (if (is.null(g)) TRUE else pep_g$tax == g)]))
    ns <- sum(d$num > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (np < MIN_PROT || ns < MIN_SAMP) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-28s NOT TESTABLE: %d proteins (need %d), %d samples with signal (need %d)\n",
                  label, np, MIN_PROT, ns, MIN_SAMP))
      return(NULL)
    }
    d <- d[is.finite(d$f) & d$f > 0 & d$f < 1, , drop = FALSE]
    d$Mixture <- factor(as.character(d$Mixture)); d$resp <- factor(as.character(d$resp))
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || nlevels(d$Mixture) < 2 || nlevels(d$resp) < 2) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-28s NOT TESTABLE after the share filter (n = %d)\n", label, nrow(d)))
      return(NULL)
    }
    m <- lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d); cf <- coef(summary(m))
    if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) return(NULL)
    e <- cf["respR", 1]; s <- cf["respR", 2]
    ci <- e + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df.residual(m)) * s
    cat(sprintf("  %-28s n=%2d  medNR %.5f  medR %.5f  est %+.3f  CI %+.3f..%+.3f  P %.4g\n",
                label, nrow(d), median(d$f[d$resp == "NR"]), median(d$f[d$resp == "R"]),
                e, ci[1], ci[2], cf["respR", 4]))
    list(label = label, n = nrow(d), est = e, se = s, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2], p = cf["respR", 4])
  }

  cat("\nB52 PART 1 -- sporulation markers within ", G,
      " (est is R - NR; negative = higher in non-responders)\n", sep = "")
  r1 <- lapply(c("SASP","COAT","GERM","MACH"),
               function(k) fit(P[[k]], G, paste(k, "in", G)))
  names(r1) <- c("SASP","COAT","GERM","MACH")
  cat("\nB52 PART 1 -- the same sets community-wide (better powered, loses the genus control)\n")
  r2 <- lapply(c("SASP","COAT","GERM","MACH"),
               function(k) fit(P[[k]], NULL, paste(k, "all taxa")))
  names(r2) <- c("SASP","COAT","GERM","MACH")

  ## ---- part 2: does trigger factor carry the chaperone signal? ------------
  cat("\nB52 PART 2 -- is the chaperone co-elevation carried by trigger factor?\n")
  tig_in <- intersect(P$TIG, chap_new)
  cat(sprintf("  trigger factor proteins: %d | already inside chap_new: %d\n",
              length(P$TIG), length(tig_in)))
  r3 <- list(
    chaperone = fit(chap_new,                 G, "chaperone (reference)"),
    tig       = fit(P$TIG,                    G, "trigger factor alone"),
    minus_tig = fit(setdiff(chap_new, P$TIG), G, "chaperone minus trigger factor"))

  ## ---- the verdict --------------------------------------------------------
  cat("\nB52 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
  test <- Filter(Negate(is.null), c(r1[c("GERM","MACH")], r2[c("GERM","MACH")]))
  if (!length(test)) {
    cat("  [3] GATES FAIL on the germination apparatus and the sporulation\n",
        "      machinery. Sporulation is NOT TESTABLE in this assay and no\n",
        "      p-value from this script should be quoted. The question is\n",
        "      unasked, not closed -- and the metagenome route (spore-marker\n",
        "      gene coverage, Spo0A regulon) needs no proteome detection.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    neg <- Filter(function(z) z$est < 0 && z$p < 0.05, test)
    exc <- all(vapply(test, function(z) z$lo > -0.364 || z$hi < -0.364, TRUE))
    if (length(neg)) {
      cat("  [1] CONSISTENT WITH A SPORULATION STATE:\n")
      for (z in neg) cat(sprintf("      %-28s est %+.3f  P %.4g\n", z$label, z$est, z$p))
      cat("      Not established. Next: spore-marker genes and the Spo0A regulon\n",
          "      in the metagenome, where detectability is not the limit.\n", sep = "")
    } else if (exc) {
      cat("  [2] Every testable set is flat with an interval excluding -0.364.\n",
          "      Sporulation is excluded as the explanation. Record and close.\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("  Flat, but at least one interval COVERS -0.364: no information from\n",
          "  that set, not a null. Report the intervals and say so.\n", sep = "")
    }
    cat("  Reminder: a null on SASP or COAT carries no weight either way --\n",
        "  both are expected to be under-detected for structural reasons.\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.null(r3$tig) && !is.null(r3$minus_tig)) {
    carried <- r3$tig$est < 0 && r3$tig$p < 0.05 && r3$minus_tig$p >= 0.05
    cat(sprintf("  PART 2: %s\n", if (carried)
      "trigger factor carries the chaperone signal -- the fingerprint of the\n          ribosome-storage mechanism rather than a heat-shock response." else
      "trigger factor does NOT carry the chaperone signal on its own; the\n          classical chaperones do, which argues against this mechanism."))
  }

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B52_sporulation")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  all <- Filter(Negate(is.null), c(r1, r2, r3))
  if (length(all))
    utils::write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(all, as.data.frame)),
                     file.path(od, "fits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(sets = P, blautia = r1, all_taxa = r2, trigger = r3),
          file.path(od, "sporulation.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

## B53 — stability class

is the ribosomal elevation DIFFERENTIAL PROTEOLYTIC SURVIVAL?

Source: `B53_stability_class.R`

```{r B53_stability_class, eval=FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## B53 — is the ribosomal elevation DIFFERENTIAL PROTEOLYTIC SURVIVAL?
## The last alternative that can take the result away.
## ============================================================================
##
## WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS A GAP IN B49. B49 excluded the
## abundance-class artefact with a well-powered null: 67 control proteins
## matched to the ribosomal set at identical median log-intensity moved +0.028
## (SE 0.068) against the ribosomal set's -0.364. But B49 matched on ABUNDANCE,
## not on PROTEASE ACCESSIBILITY. Ribosomal proteins are assembled into a large
## ribonucleoprotein particle and are substantially buried; glycolytic enzymes
## are soluble, accessible oligomers. A difference in proteolytic exposure
## during gut transit would raise the ribosomal share and lower the glycolytic
## share with no physiology whatsoever -- and a control set matched only on
## abundance, mixed in stability by construction, averages that away.
##
## So the state after five mechanisms (abundance class excluded, sub-genus
## composition a one-fifth correlate, hibernation disfavoured, prophage
## untestable, sporulation not supported) still has one way to be an artefact.
##
## THE DISCRIMINATOR IS UNIFORMITY ACROSS THE SET, AND IT NEEDS NO SEQUENCES.
## Ribosomal proteins are STOICHIOMETRIC: one copy each per particle. If
## non-responders carry more ribosomes, every ribosomal protein must rise by
## the same factor, and the per-protein response coefficients should be
## HOMOGENEOUS around the set estimate.
##
## Protease accessibility is NOT uniform across the set. The surface stalk and
## peripheral proteins are far more exposed than the buried core. If
## differential proteolysis drives the signal, the per-protein coefficients
## must be HETEROGENEOUS, concentrated in the protected members.
##
##   uniform  -> stoichiometric ribosome content; proteolysis is not driving it
##   scattered -> a protein-specific effect; stability is live
##
## That test uses only the data already in the session. It is reported for the
## glycolytic set too, where the same logic runs the other way: glycolytic
## enzymes are NOT stoichiometric with each other, so heterogeneity there is
## expected and is the internal control on the method.
##
## PART 0 IS A DISCOVERY STEP, NOT A TEST. A direct readout of in-vivo
## proteolysis exists if the peptide table carries sequences or termini: the
## fraction of semi-tryptic peptides per protein measures degradation directly.
## B50 stopped because it assumed an annotation column that was not there, so
## this script LOOKS and REPORTS rather than assuming, and says what a stronger
## follow-up would need.
##
## THE READING IS FIXED HERE, ABOVE THE NUMBERS. `est` is R - NR.
##
##   [1] ribosomal coefficients homogeneous (Cochran Q P >= 0.05, I2 < 50%)
##         -> the shift is uniform across the particle, as stoichiometry
##            requires. Differential proteolysis does not explain it, and the
##            last artefactual route is closed.
##
##   [2] ribosomal coefficients heterogeneous (Q P < 0.05 and I2 >= 50%)
##         -> the shift is carried by a SUBSET of ribosomal proteins. Stability
##            is live, and the next question is what distinguishes the movers.
##            The result must not be described as a ribosome-content difference
##            until that is answered.
##
##   [3] fewer than 10 ribosomal proteins fit individually
##         -> NOT TESTABLE at this depth. Report the count, not a verdict.
##
## A CAUTION THAT APPLIES TO EITHER OUTCOME. Homogeneity is consistent with
## stoichiometry but does not prove it: a proteolytic process that happened to
## act evenly would look the same. This test can falsify the stability account
## cleanly and can only support the physiological one weakly. That asymmetry is
## stated so the result is not over-read in the direction we would prefer.
##
##   source("B53_stability_class.R")
## ============================================================================

local({
  need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "ribo_new", "annot_new", "paths")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, TRUE)]
  if (length(miss)) stop("B53 needs: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  G <- "Blautia"; MIN_FIT <- 10L; MIN_SAMP <- 20L
  GLYC <- c("K00134","K01689","K00927","K00873","K01623","K01624",
            "K01803","K01834","K15633","K01810","K00850")
  .ko <- function(v) unique(annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                                              annot_new$ko_primary %in% v])

  ## ---- part 0: what does the session actually carry? ----------------------
  cat("B53 PART 0 -- what is available (discovery, not a test)\n")
  cat("  pep_g columns: ", paste(names(pep_g), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  OP elements:   ", paste(names(OP), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  seqcol <- NULL
```
