```{r B53_stability_class, eval=FALSE}
  for (nm in names(pep_g)) {
    v <- pep_g[[nm]]
    if (is.character(v) && length(v) &&
        mean(grepl("^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]{6,}$", utils::head(v, 2000))) > 0.5) {
      seqcol <- nm; break
    }
  }
  if (is.null(seqcol))
    cat("  no peptide-sequence column found in pep_g. The direct proteolysis\n",
        "  readout -- the semi-tryptic fraction per protein -- is NOT available\n",
        "  here. It would need the peptide table with sequences and termini, or\n",
        "  a re-search allowing semi-tryptic cleavage. The uniformity test below\n",
        "  does not depend on it.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("  peptide sequences appear to be in pep_g$", seqcol,
        " -- a semi-tryptic fraction per protein is computable and would be a\n",
        "  DIRECT proteolysis readout. Worth building as a follow-up.\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- per-protein response coefficients within the genus -----------------
  x   <- pep_g[pep_g$tax == G, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(x)) stop("B53: no peptide rows for ", G, call. = FALSE)
  den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  keep_s <- is.finite(den) & den > 0
  per_protein <- function(prots, label) {
    pr <- intersect(unique(x$Protein), prots)
    out <- lapply(pr, function(p) {
      rows <- x$row[x$Protein == p]
      num  <- colSums(OP$a[rows, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
      f    <- num / den
      ok   <- keep_s & is.finite(f) & f > 0 & f < 1
      if (sum(ok) < MIN_SAMP) return(NULL)
      d <- data.frame(y = qlogis(f[ok]),
                      Mixture = factor(as.character(OP$d$Mixture[ok])),
                      resp    = factor(as.character(OP$d$resp[ok])))
      if (nlevels(d$Mixture) < 2 || nlevels(d$resp) < 2) return(NULL)
      cf <- coef(summary(lm(y ~ Mixture + resp, d)))
      if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) return(NULL)
      data.frame(protein = p, n = sum(ok), est = cf["respR", 1],
                 se = cf["respR", 2], p = cf["respR", 4],
                 abund = mean(num[ok]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
    out <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), out))
    cat(sprintf("\n  %-12s %d of %d proteins fit individually (>= %d samples each)\n",
                label, if (is.null(out)) 0L else nrow(out), length(pr), MIN_SAMP))
    out
  }
  cat("\nB53 -- per-protein response coefficients within ", G, "\n", sep = "")
  R <- per_protein(ribo_new,   "ribosomal")
  Y <- per_protein(.ko(GLYC),  "glycolysis")

  ## ---- heterogeneity ------------------------------------------------------
  het <- function(z, label) {
    if (is.null(z) || nrow(z) < MIN_FIT) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-12s NOT TESTABLE: %d proteins fit (need %d)\n",
                  label, if (is.null(z)) 0L else nrow(z), MIN_FIT))
      return(NULL)
    }
    w  <- 1 / z$se^2
    mu <- sum(w * z$est) / sum(w)
    Q  <- sum(w * (z$est - mu)^2)
    df <- nrow(z) - 1
    pq <- stats::pchisq(Q, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
    I2 <- max(0, (Q - df) / Q)
    ct <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(z$est, log(z$abund), method = "spearman"))
    cat(sprintf("  %-12s k=%d  pooled %+.3f  Q=%.1f on %d df, P=%.4g  I2=%.0f%%  est~log(abundance) rho=%+.2f P=%.3g\n",
                label, nrow(z), mu, Q, df, pq, 100 * I2,
                unname(ct$estimate), ct$p.value))
    cat(sprintf("               per-protein est: min %+.3f, median %+.3f, max %+.3f; %d of %d negative\n",
                min(z$est), median(z$est), max(z$est), sum(z$est < 0), nrow(z)))
    list(label = label, k = nrow(z), pooled = mu, Q = Q, df = df, p = pq, I2 = I2,
         rho_abund = unname(ct$estimate), p_abund = ct$p.value)
  }
  cat("\nB53 -- heterogeneity across each set (the discriminator)\n")
  hR <- het(R, "ribosomal"); hY <- het(Y, "glycolysis")

  ## ---- the verdict --------------------------------------------------------
  cat("\nB53 VERDICT against the rules fixed above the numbers\n")
  if (is.null(hR)) {
    cat("  [3] NOT TESTABLE: too few ribosomal proteins fit individually at this\n",
        "      depth. No verdict. The set-level result is unaffected.\n", sep = "")
  } else if (hR$p >= 0.05 && hR$I2 < 0.5) {
    cat(sprintf("  [1] HOMOGENEOUS across %d ribosomal proteins (Q P = %.3g, I2 = %.0f%%).\n",
                hR$k, hR$p, 100 * hR$I2),
        "      The shift is uniform across the particle, which is what stoichiometry\n",
        "      requires and what differential proteolysis would not produce, since\n",
        "      protease accessibility varies widely between the buried core and the\n",
        "      surface stalk. The stability account is not supported, and the last\n",
        "      artefactual route is closed.\n",
        "      Read with the caution fixed above: this falsifies the stability\n",
        "      account cleanly and supports the physiological one only weakly.\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("  [2] HETEROGENEOUS across %d ribosomal proteins (Q P = %.3g, I2 = %.0f%%).\n",
                hR$k, hR$p, 100 * hR$I2),
        "      The shift is carried by a SUBSET, not by the particle. Stability is\n",
        "      live, and the result must not be described as a ribosome-content\n",
        "      difference until it is known what distinguishes the movers.\n",
        "      Next: rank the per-protein estimates against surface exposure in the\n",
        "      ribosome structure, which needs r-protein identities, not sequences.\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.null(hY))
    cat(sprintf("  Internal control: glycolysis I2 = %.0f%% (Q P = %.3g). Glycolytic enzymes\n",
                100 * hY$I2, hY$p),
        "      are not stoichiometric with one another, so heterogeneity there is\n",
        "      expected; if it is LOWER than the ribosomal set's, the method is not\n",
        "      measuring what this verdict assumes and neither branch should be read.\n", sep = "")

  od <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B53_stability_class")
  dir.create(od, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(R)) utils::write.csv(R, file.path(od, "per_protein_ribosomal.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(Y)) utils::write.csv(Y, file.path(od, "per_protein_glycolysis.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(ribosomal = R, glycolysis = Y, het_ribosomal = hR, het_glycolysis = hY,
               seq_column = seqcol), file.path(od, "stability.rds"))
  cat("\nwritten to ", od, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

## C1d — build OP new

build OP_new (and OP_control) from the re-searched PSM tables, using

Source: `C1d_build_OP_new.R`

```{r C1d_build_OP_new, eval=FALSE}
## C1d — build OP_new (and OP_control) from the re-searched PSM tables, using
##       section 2's own pipeline rather than a reimplementation of it.
##
## WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE SCRIPT. C2 compares coupling before and after a change
## of search database. If the two quantification matrices are built differently
## in any respect — aggregation, transform, normalisation, channel exclusion —
## that difference presents as a database effect. The control run has just
## established that the toolchain change is worth 1% of identifications; a
## processing difference here could easily exceed that and would be invisible.
##
## So this script does NOT define its own pipeline. It requires the live
## analysis session (or a knit through section 3) and reuses `load_psm_long`,
## `build_qf`, `normalise_channels` and `arm_objs` exactly as they are defined
## there. If any of those is missing it stops rather than substituting.
##
## Usage, from a session that has run analysis_v17.Rmd through section 3:
##   source("C1d_build_OP_new.R")
## Produces OP_new and, if the control table is staged, OP_control.

NEED <- c("load_psm_long", "build_qf", "normalise_channels", "arm_objs",
          "arm_mix_v13", "qf", "OP", "mp", "clean_run", "TMT11")
miss <- NEED[!vapply(NEED, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss))
  stop("this must run inside the analysis session — missing: ",
       paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
       "\n  Run analysis_v17.Rmd through section 3 first. Do not reimplement\n",
       "  these: the whole point is that both arms use identical code.",
       call. = FALSE)

## The 13 Oct 2026 sample corrections. v17 section 0a sources this file, so in a
## live session the symbols are already here; sourced defensively because the two
## guards below are written against the CORRECTED annotation and would misread a
## session without it.
if (!all(vapply(c("PITT_RELABEL_FROM", "pitt_drop_list"), exists, logical(1))))
  source(file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), "pitt_sample_corrections.R"))

IN <- Sys.getenv("ICB_C2_INPUT",
      file.path(dirname(paths$out_dir), "C2_input"))
if (!dir.exists(IN)) stop("staging directory not found: ", IN,
                          "\n  Set ICB_C2_INPUT.", call. = FALSE)

## THE ACCESSION FORMAT MUST BE RESTORED BEFORE THE FILTERS RUN.
## load_psm_long's filters are written against the original accession format and
## two of them break silently on the concatenated database's prefixed form:
##
##   grepl(prefix_ok, Protein)        PREFIX[["pitt"]] is "^OIDECCNN_", ANCHORED.
##                                    "pitt|OIDECCNN_00001" does not match, so
##                                    the arm filters to zero rows.
##   substr(Protein, 4, 8) != "Cont_" positional. On "sheba1|sp|Cont_X" it reads
##                                    "a1|sp" and stops removing contaminants.
##
## Passing a looser pattern would fix the first and leave the second broken — and
## a contaminant filter that works on one arm and not the other is exactly the
## processing difference that would present as a database effect. So the source
## prefix is stripped into its own column first, restoring the accessions to the
## form every filter was written for. Nothing else about the table changes.
## THE EIGHT PLEXES MUST BE STAGED SEPARATELY.
## Each FragPipe psm.tsv labels its reporter columns with ITS OWN sample names —
## `Intensity MF0030`, `Intensity Pool01` and so on. Concatenating the eight into
## one table therefore keeps only the first plex's eleven columns and leaves every
## other plex NA in them. The row counts survive, which is why the merged file
## looked fine: 234,496 PSMs, 8 mixtures, 5 runs each. The QUANTIFICATION does
## not — 7 of 8 plexes came through empty, and both the test and control arms
## were built that way.
##
## The original run reads `pitt_psm_files`, a vector of 8 paths, through
## map_dfr, so each file's own columns are renamed to channels before the bind.
## This takes the same shape: a directory of per-plex files, or a vector.
psm_inputs <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) > 1) return(x)
  if (dir.exists(x)) {
    f <- list.files(x, "^psm\\.tsv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
    if (!length(f)) f <- list.files(x, "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
    ## Natural order, not lexical: sort() puts TMT10 before TMT2. Nothing
    ## downstream reads file order — Mixture comes from the Run/Channel join —
    ## but the printed list should not mislead.
    k <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub(".*?(\\d+)[^0-9]*$", "\\1", dirname(f))))
    return(if (any(is.na(k))) sort(f) else f[order(k)])
  }
  x
}

strip_source <- function(f) {
  d <- readr::read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = Inf)
  stopifnot("Protein" %in% names(d))
  has_pre <- grepl("^(pitt|sheba1|sheba2|ref)\\|", d$Protein)
  cat(sprintf("  %d rows; %d (%.1f%%) carry a source prefix\n",
              nrow(d), sum(has_pre), 100 * mean(has_pre)))
  if (any(has_pre)) {
    d$SourceDB <- ifelse(has_pre, sub("\\|.*$", "", d$Protein), "pitt")
    d$Protein  <- sub("^(pitt|sheba1|sheba2|ref)\\|", "", d$Protein)
    print(table(d$SourceDB))
  }
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
  readr::write_tsv(d, tmp)
  tmp
}

build_arm <- function(psm_file, tag) {
  if (!file.exists(psm_file)) { cat("skipped, not staged:", basename(psm_file), "\n")
                                return(NULL) }
  fs <- psm_inputs(psm_file)
  cat("\n---- building from ", length(fs), " file(s): ",
      paste(basename(head(fs, 3)), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(fs) > 3) sprintf(" (+%d)", length(fs) - 3) else "", " ----\n", sep = "")
  if (length(fs) == 1)
    cat("  WARNING: one file. If it merges several plexes, only the first plex's\n",
        "           reporter columns survive and the rest are NA — see the\n",
        "           per-mixture check below.\n", sep = "")
  f <- vapply(fs, strip_source, "")
  on.exit(unlink(f), add = TRUE)
  ## After stripping, accessions are bare, so the pattern accepts all three
  ## assemblies. The Cont_ and decoy filters now see the format they expect.
  PREFIX_ALL <- "^(OIDECCNN_|KMMIBAFL_|PPAAKGPG_)"
  lg <- load_psm_long(f, PREFIX_ALL, mp$pitt_annot_use)
  cat(sprintf("  after load_psm_long: %d long rows, %d runs, %d mixtures\n",
              nrow(lg), dplyr::n_distinct(lg$Run), dplyr::n_distinct(lg$Mixture)))
  if (nrow(lg) == 0)
    stop(tag, ": every row was filtered out. Check that the accessions match ",
         PREFIX_ALL, " after prefix stripping, and that the annotation table ",
         "covers this run's Run/Channel combinations.", call. = FALSE)

  ## EVERY PLEX MUST CARRY INTENSITY. Rows without values pass every check above
  ## — the Run/Mixture join is on names, not numbers — and produce a matrix whose
  ## columns are empty for all but one plex.
  ## CHANNEL ORDER IS ASSUMED, NOT CHECKED, BY load_psm_long.
  ## It renames the eleven `Intensity <sample>` columns to 126 … 131C BY
  ## POSITION. The columns carry SAMPLE names, so a different column order in a
  ## newer FragPipe would permute every channel assignment silently and produce a
  ## complete, plausible matrix with the values on the wrong samples. The original
  ## run used 23.1 and these files 24.0, so it is verified rather than assumed:
  ## the k-th column's sample name must be the BioReplicate the annotation gives
  ## for that mixture and channel.
  ann <- mp$pitt_annot_use |> dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate)
  empty_seen <- list()
  for (ff in fs) {
    h  <- names(readr::read_tsv(ff, n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE))
    ic <- grep("^Intensity ", h, value = TRUE)
    if (length(ic) != 11) { cat("  ", basename(dirname(ff)), ": ", length(ic),
                                " reporter columns, expected 11\n", sep = ""); next }
    smp <- sub("^Intensity ", "", ic)
    mix <- readr::read_tsv(ff, n_max = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)[["Spectrum File"]] |>
      clean_run() |> (\(r) mp$pitt_annot_use$Mixture[match(r, mp$pitt_annot_use$Run)])()
    want <- ann$BioReplicate[match(paste(mix, TMT11), paste(ann$Mixture, ann$Channel))]
    ## A channel ABSENT from the annotation is an Empty channel, not a mismatch.
    ## The raw CSV has 88 Pittsburgh channels; five carry Condition == "Empty" and
    ## were dropped, so pitt_annot_use has 83 (section 2b). FragPipe labels an
    ## unannotated channel by its channel name — `TMT6_129N` — rather than by a
    ## sample, which is exactly what position 6 of TMT6 shows. Only a channel that
    ## IS annotated and disagrees is a permutation.
    ## A RENAME IS NOT A PERMUTATION. These files were searched in September,
    ## before TMT1_126 was relabelled MF0017, so that column's header still reads
    ## MF001A3A817 while the annotation now reads MF0017. The guard exists to
    ## catch columns in the WRONG ORDER; accepting the one documented old name at
    ## the one documented channel leaves every other disagreement fatal, and a
    ## real permutation would move the other ten columns as well.
    was <- unname(PITT_RELABEL_FROM[paste(mix, TMT11, sep = "_")])
    was[is.na(was)] <- ""
    cmp <- !is.na(want)
    ok  <- want[cmp] == smp[cmp] | smp[cmp] == was[cmp]
    empt <- TMT11[!cmp]
    ## `<-`, not `<<-`: the loop runs inside build_arm, where empty_seen is local.
    ## `<<-` skips the local binding and looks in the global environment, which is
    ## why this failed with "object 'empty_seen' not found".
    if (length(empt)) empty_seen[[as.character(mix)]] <- empt
    if (!all(ok)) {
      cat("  CHANNEL ORDER MISMATCH in ", basename(dirname(ff)), " (mixture ", mix, ")\n", sep = "")
      print(data.frame(channel = TMT11, column = smp, annotation = want,
                       agrees = ifelse(cmp, want == smp, NA)))
      stop("the reporter columns are not in channel order in at least one plex. ",
           "load_psm_long renames them by position, so every value would land on ",
           "the wrong sample.", call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
  ## The empty channels are known and fixed. If a different set turns up, either
  ## the annotation changed or a real sample failed to annotate — both worth
  ## stopping for, since load_psm_long silently drops whatever does not join.
  EMPTY_EXPECTED <- list(TMT6 = "129N", TMT7 = c("127C","129N","131C"), TMT8 = "131C")
  ## Channels DROPPED by the 13 Oct corrections are no longer in pitt_annot_use,
  ## so they present here as unannotated and would trip this check. Derived from
  ## pitt_drop_list() rather than typed in, so the sensitivity run -- which drops
  ## TMT4_127C as well -- needs no second edit.
  for (.s in pitt_drop_list()) {
    .p <- strsplit(.s, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    EMPTY_EXPECTED[[.p[1]]] <- sort(unique(c(EMPTY_EXPECTED[[.p[1]]], .p[2])))
  }
  seen <- empty_seen[order(names(empty_seen))]
  if (!identical(lapply(seen, sort), lapply(EMPTY_EXPECTED[order(names(EMPTY_EXPECTED))], sort))) {
    cat("  unannotated channels found:\n"); print(seen)
    cat("  expected (section 2b):\n");      print(EMPTY_EXPECTED)
    stop("the set of unannotated channels differs from the documented five. ",
         "load_psm_long drops whatever fails to join, so a sample missing from ",
         "the annotation would vanish without error.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  cat("  channel order verified in all ", length(fs), " plexes; ",
      length(unlist(seen)), " unannotated channels, as documented\n", sep = "")

  permix <- lg |> dplyr::group_by(Mixture) |>
    dplyr::summarise(rows = dplyr::n(), nonNA = sum(!is.na(Intensity)), .groups = "drop")
  print(as.data.frame(permix))
  dead <- permix$Mixture[permix$nonNA == 0]
  if (length(dead))
    stop(tag, ": ", length(dead), " of ", nrow(permix),
         " mixtures have rows but NO intensity (", paste(dead, collapse = ", "), ").\n",
         "  Each plex's psm.tsv names its reporter columns after its OWN samples, so a\n",
         "  merged table keeps only the first plex's columns. Stage the eight per-plex\n",
         "  psm.tsv files separately and pass the directory.", call. = FALSE)

  q <- build_qf(lg)
  ## The `seq` column is created inside build_qf for the original tables; assert
  ## rather than assume, because pep_tax joins the taxonomy on it and a missing
  ## column would surface much later as an empty join.
  rd <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(q[["psms"]])
  if (!"seq" %in% names(rd))
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(q[["psms"]])$seq <-
      toupper(gsub("[^A-Z]", "", rd$Peptide))
  q <- normalise_channels(q)

  ## arm_objs() reads from the global `qf`, so the new cohort is added there
  ## under its own name and removed afterwards — the original entries are never
  ## touched.
  key <- paste0("__", tag)
  qf[[key]] <<- q
  on.exit(qf[[key]] <<- NULL, add = TRUE)
  O <- arm_objs(key, "pitt_ontx")

  ## The two arms must differ ONLY in which PSM table they started from.
  same <- identical(sort(O$d$sample), sort(OP$d$sample))
  cat(sprintf("  %d PSM rows x %d channels; %d analysable samples (original %d)%s\n",
              nrow(O$a), ncol(O$a), nrow(O$d), nrow(OP$d),
              if (same) "" else "   <-- CHANNEL SETS DIFFER"))
  if (!same) {
    cat("  in new only: ", paste(setdiff(O$d$sample, OP$d$sample), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    cat("  in old only: ", paste(setdiff(OP$d$sample, O$d$sample), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    warning(tag, ": the analysable channel set differs from the original. C2's ",
            "comparison assumes the same patients on both sides.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  md <- apply(SummarizedExperiment::assay(O$q, "psmsLog"), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  post-normalisation channel medians: median %+.4f, sd %.4f (should be ~0)\n",
              median(md, na.rm = TRUE), sd(md, na.rm = TRUE)))
  O
}

## A directory of per-plex psm.tsv files is preferred; the merged single file is
## accepted but will stop at the per-mixture check above.
pick <- function(dirname, file1) {
  d <- file.path(IN, dirname)
  if (dir.exists(d)) d else file.path(IN, file1)
}
OP_new     <- build_arm(pick("psm_test",    "rescored_psm_test.tsv"),    "test")
OP_control <- build_arm(pick("psm_control", "rescored_psm_control.tsv"), "control")

if (!is.null(OP_new)) {
  cat("\nOP_new built.\n")
  cat("  Now run C2_rescore_clade.R; it builds pep_g_new from the staged LCA\n",
      "  table automatically and scores the sealed prediction.\n", sep = "")
}
if (!is.null(OP_control)) {
  cat("\nOP_control built as well. Worth running C2 a second time with\n",
      "  OP <- OP_control and pep_g <- the control's taxonomy, so the comparison\n",
      "  is control-against-test — the like-for-like pair. The published run\n",
      "  carries a 1% toolchain difference that the control has now measured.\n", sep = "")
}
```

## C2 — rescore clade

does the clade decoupling survive a search against the concatenated

Source: `C2_rescore_clade.R`

```{r C2_rescore_clade, eval=FALSE}
## C2 — does the clade decoupling survive a search against the concatenated
##      database? The pre-registered test, with its reading fixed in advance.
##
## RUN C1 FIRST. If C1's pre-flight says the concatenation does not materially
## expand Pittsburgh's Bacteroidota sequence space, this script cannot answer the
## question and a null result here means nothing.
##
## WHAT IS COMPARED. The same quantity §11c reports: per genus, within patients,
## the correlation between metagenome abundance and proteome abundance, on
## centred log-ratios. Computed once on the original identifications and once on
## the re-searched ones, from the same spectra and the same metagenomes. Only the
## database differs.
##
## Usage:
##   Rscript C2_rescore_clade.R <rescored_psm.tsv> [out_dir]
## Requires the analysis session through §11c (OP, pep_g, pep_ph, MGm, gen_coupling).

## ---- staged inputs ----------------------------------------------------------
## The server stages everything under C2_input/ beside the project:
##   rescored_psm_test.tsv     the re-searched identifications
##   rescored_psm_control.tsv  the same spectra, original database, same toolchain
##   unipept_lca_new.tsv       Unipept LCA for the new peptides, section 5a settings
##   unipept_run_meta.json     the settings and db_version actually used
##   SHA256SUMS.txt            checksums for all of the above
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
IN  <- Sys.getenv("ICB_C2_INPUT",
        file.path(dirname(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else "."), "C2_input"))
if (!dir.exists(IN)) IN <- Sys.getenv("ICB_C2_INPUT", "C2_input")
## The re-searched identifications are staged as eight per-plex psm.tsv files,
## not one merged table — merging them discards every plex but the first's
## reporter columns (see C1d). This reads the directory if present and falls back
## to a single file. Only accessions and peptide sequences are used here; the
## quantification comes from OP_new, which C1d builds from the same files.
PSM <- if (length(args)) args[1] else {
  d <- file.path(IN, "psm_test")
  if (dir.exists(d)) d else file.path(IN, "rescored_psm_test.tsv")
}
OUT <- if (length(args) > 1) args[2] else file.path(paths$out_dir, "concat_research")
## The taxonomy table and the run metadata sit BESIDE C2_input in the staging
## tree, not inside it, so look in both. A missing LCA file skipped the
## pep_g_new build silently and surfaced as "could not be built", which pointed
## at the join rather than at the path.
find_beside <- function(fname) {
  cand <- c(file.path(IN, fname), file.path(dirname(IN), fname))
  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else cand[1]
}
LCA <- Sys.getenv("ICB_C2_LCA", find_beside("unipept_lca_new.tsv"))
if (!file.exists(LCA))
  stop("taxonomy table not found. Looked for unipept_lca_new.tsv in\n  ", IN,
       "\n  ", dirname(IN), "\nSet ICB_C2_LCA to its path.", call. = FALSE)
cat("  taxonomy table: ", LCA, "\n", sep = "")
PSM_FILES <- if (dir.exists(PSM)) {
  f <- list.files(PSM, "^psm\\.tsv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(f)) f <- list.files(PSM, "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
  k <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub(".*?(\\d+)[^0-9]*$", "\\1", dirname(f))))
  if (any(is.na(k))) sort(f) else f[order(k)]
} else PSM
if (!length(PSM_FILES) || !all(file.exists(PSM_FILES)))
  stop("re-searched identifications not found at ", PSM,
       "\n  Expected a directory of per-plex psm.tsv files (psm_test/TMT1/psm.tsv, ...)",
       "\n  or a single table. Pass it as the first argument, or set ICB_C2_INPUT.",
       call. = FALSE)
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
cat("inputs from: ", IN, "\n  identifications: ", basename(PSM), "\n", sep = "")

## Verify the staged files against the checksums the server wrote. A truncated
## 201 MB transfer would not error — it would silently drop identifications.
SUMS <- find_beside("SHA256SUMS.txt")
if (file.exists(SUMS) && nzchar(Sys.which("shasum"))) {
  ## Run from the directory the manifest lives in — its paths are relative to
  ## that, and it may sit beside C2_input rather than inside it.
  ok <- system(paste0("cd '", dirname(SUMS), "' && shasum -a 256 -c '",
                      basename(SUMS), "'"),
               ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  cat("  checksums: ", if (ok == 0) "verified" else "MISMATCH — re-transfer", "\n", sep = "")
  if (ok != 0) stop("staged inputs do not match SHA256SUMS.txt", call. = FALSE)
} else cat("  checksums: not verified (no SHA256SUMS.txt or no shasum)\n")

## Record the Unipept settings alongside the result: the taxonomy must have been
## built at the same parameters as section 5a or the two arms are not comparable.
META <- find_beside("unipept_run_meta.json")
if (file.exists(META)) {
  cat("  Unipept run metadata:\n")
  writeLines(paste0("    ", readLines(META, warn = FALSE)))
} else cat("  NOTE: no unipept_run_meta.json — the query settings are unrecorded.\n")
## NO LIVE SESSION IS NEEDED. analysis_v17.Rmd's `figure-inputs` chunk writes
## every object this script requires to figure_inputs.rds on each knit, for
## exactly this reason — downstream work should not depend on a session that
## happens to still be open. All six are in that bundle: OP, pep_g, pep_ph, MGm
## and gen_coupling from the main export list, annot_new from the supplementary
## one. Do NOT reconstruct them from another saved workspace: a genus assignment
## from a different source would produce a number that looks like C2's output
## and is not comparable to the published §11c values.
need <- c("OP", "pep_g", "pep_ph", "MGm", "gen_coupling", "annot_new")
if (any(!vapply(need, exists, logical(1)))) {
  FI <- Sys.getenv("ICB_FIGURE_INPUTS",
                   file.path(if (exists("paths")) paths$out_dir else ".", "figure_inputs.rds"))
  if (!file.exists(FI))
    stop("figure_inputs.rds not found at ", FI,
         "\n  Knit analysis_v17.Rmd to produce it, or set ICB_FIGURE_INPUTS.",
         call. = FALSE)
  cat("loading analysis objects from ", FI, " (written ",
      format(file.mtime(FI), "%d %b %H:%M"), ")\n", sep = "")
  list2env(readRDS(FI), envir = globalenv())
}
miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss)) stop("figure_inputs.rds lacks: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
                       "\n  It predates the export of these objects; re-knit.",
                       call. = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble); library(stringr) })

## ---- 1. what the new database changed, before any coupling is computed ------
## A clade-specific change in identification depth is itself a finding, and it
## conditions how the coupling comparison is read.
new <- do.call(rbind, lapply(PSM_FILES, function(f)
  read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c("Protein", "Peptide"),
                                                               drop = FALSE]))
cat(sprintf("read %d identifications from %d file(s)\n", nrow(new), length(PSM_FILES)))
src <- sub("\\|.*$", "", new$Protein)              # the cohort prefix C1 added

## DecoyPYrat prepends DECOY_ to the whole identifier, so a decoy that survived
## into the PSM table appears here as a source called DECOY_pitt or similar,
## rather than hiding among the targets. Report and drop them: a non-zero count
## means the FDR filter did not do its job, and the clade comparison below would
## be built on reversed sequences.
is_dec <- grepl("^(DECOY|XXX|rev|REV)_", src)
if (any(is_dec)) {
  cat("DECOY ROWS IN THE PSM TABLE:", sum(is_dec), "- these should not be here.\n")
  print(table(src[is_dec]))
  new <- new[!is_dec, , drop = FALSE]; src <- src[!is_dec]
  cat("  dropped; check the FDR filtering before trusting anything below.\n")
}
cat("re-searched identifications by database of origin:\n"); print(table(src))

## ENTRAPMENT: the concatenated database carries no entrapment block, so the
## test arm has 0 XXX_ rows against 44 in the published run and 28 in the
## control. Decoys are zero in all three, but entrapment sequences are the
## INDEPENDENT check that the FDR is calibrated, and the test arm has none — on
## a database five times larger, which is exactly where calibration is most in
## doubt. This does not invalidate the comparison; it means the test arm's FDR
## rests on the decoy estimate alone. It belongs in the methods.
cat("\nNOTE: no entrapment block in the concatenated database, so the test arm\n",
    "  has no independent FDR check (published 44 XXX_ rows, control 28, test 0).\n",
    sep = "")

## Did identification loss fall evenly across clades? A fivefold larger database
## at the same FDR loses identifications; if that loss is clade-dependent, the
## coupling comparison below confounds the database change with a change in what
## could be measured, and the experiment is inconclusive rather than negative.
## Pre-committed threshold: the Bacteroidota retention rate must be within 20%
## (relative) of the Bacillota rate.
even_loss <- NA
if (exists("pep_ph") && exists("pep_ph_new")) {
  ret <- function(ph) {
    o <- sum(pep_ph$tax == ph, na.rm = TRUE)
    nn <- sum(pep_ph_new$tax == ph, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (o == 0) NA_real_ else nn / o
  }
  r_bact <- ret("Bacteroidota"); r_baci <- max(ret("Bacillota"), ret("Firmicutes"), na.rm = TRUE)
  even_loss <- isTRUE(abs(r_bact / r_baci - 1) < 0.20)
  cat(sprintf("\nretention of peptide rows: Bacteroidota %.0f%%, Bacillota %.0f%% -> %s\n",
              100 * r_bact, 100 * r_baci,
              if (even_loss) "even enough to compare" else "UNEVEN; see the verdict"))
} else cat("\nretention by clade not checked: pep_ph_new not in the session\n")
cat(sprintf("\noriginal: %d PSM rows, re-searched: %d (%+.1f%%)\n",
            nrow(OP$rd), nrow(new), 100 * (nrow(new) / nrow(OP$rd) - 1)))

## ---- 2. clade coupling, old and new ----------------------------------------
## COUPLE, mirroring section 11c exactly.
##
## FIXED 26 Sep 2026: this previously passed all 55 proteome channels and
## subset MGm with them. MGm holds only the ~47 patients who also have a
## metagenome, so 8 rows came back NA, and cor() with use = "everything"
## returned NA for every genus — in BOTH arms, which is how the bug announced
## itself. Section 11c aligns the two matrices on the intersection first, and
## so does this.
clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }

couple <- function(prot_tax, mat, chan, label) {
  gen <- count(prot_tax, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  ## the patients present in BOTH layers, in one order used throughout
  ## Section 11c sets rownames(MGm) to the proteome sample names of the
  ## patients present in both layers. If the bundled copy lost them, MPm was
  ## built on the same index and can supply them.
  rn <- rownames(MGm)
  if (is.null(rn) || !length(intersect(chan, rn))) {
    alt <- if (exists("MPm")) rownames(MPm) else NULL
    if (!is.null(alt) && length(intersect(chan, alt)) >= 20 &&
        length(alt) == nrow(MGm)) {
      cat("  NOTE: MGm had no usable rownames; taking them from MPm, which\n",
          "        section 11c builds on the same index.\n", sep = "")
      rownames(MGm) <- alt; rn <- alt
    }
  }
  S <- intersect(chan, rn)
  if (length(S) < 20)
    stop(label, ": only ", length(S), " of ", length(chan),
         " channels are in both layers.\n",
         "  MGm rows: ", nrow(MGm), ", rownames ",
         if (is.null(rn)) "ABSENT" else paste0("e.g. ", paste(head(rn, 3), collapse = ", ")),
         "\n  this arm's channels: e.g. ", paste(head(chan, 3), collapse = ", "),
         "\n  MPm rows: ", if (exists("MPm")) nrow(MPm) else NA,
         ", rownames ",
         if (!exists("MPm") || is.null(rownames(MPm))) "ABSENT"
         else paste0("e.g. ", paste(head(rownames(MPm), 3), collapse = ", ")),
         "\n\n  Section 11c sets rownames(MGm) to proteome sample names. If both are\n",
         "  absent here, the bundle predates that assignment and figure_inputs.rds\n",
         "  needs rebuilding by a fresh knit.", call. = FALSE)
  den <- sapply(gen, function(g)
    colSums(mat[prot_tax$row[prot_tax$tax == g], S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  rownames(den) <- S
  ## A patient with no rows in ANY retained genus divides by zero, and one NaN
  ## row makes every correlation NA — which is how the re-searched arm first
  ## reported NA for all twelve clade-assigned genera. Drop such patients and say
  ## how many, rather than propagating NaN.
  zt <- rowSums(den) <= 0
  if (any(zt)) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-22s dropping %d patient(s) with no evidence in any retained genus\n",
                label, sum(zt)))
    den <- den[!zt, , drop = FALSE]; S <- S[!zt]
  }
  ## Losing a handful of patients is tolerable; losing most of them means the
  ## taxonomy for this arm is broken, and every correlation below would be
  ## computed on a remnant. An arm on 9 of 47 patients once produced a confident
  ## verdict that was pure artefact.
  if (length(S) < 0.6 * length(chan))
    stop(label, ": only ", length(S), " of ", length(chan),
         " patients have evidence in the retained genera.\n",
         "  The taxonomy for this arm is too sparse to compare against the other. ",
         "Check the peptide coverage reported above.", call. = FALSE)
  MPg <- den / rowSums(den)
  gg  <- intersect(colnames(MPg), colnames(MGm))
  A   <- clr(MGm[S, gg, drop = FALSE])
  Bm  <- clr(MPg[, gg, drop = FALSE])
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(A), rownames(Bm)), identical(colnames(A), colnames(Bm)))
  cat(sprintf("  %-22s %d patients, %d genera at the 200-row floor\n",
              label, length(S), length(gg)))
  tibble(genus = gg, which = label,
         rho = vapply(gg, function(g) suppressWarnings(
           ## pairwise rather than complete.obs. For a two-vector correlation the
           ## two are identical, so this changes nothing here; it is written this
           ## way so that the call stays correct if it is ever applied to a
           ## matrix, where complete.obs would drop a whole patient over a single
           ## missing genus.
           cor(A[, g], Bm[, g], method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")), 0))
}
old   <- couple(pep_g,     OP$a,     OP$d$sample,     "original database")

## The original arm is not new work: section 11c already computed it as
## gen_coupling$rho_clr. Recomputing it here is the check that this script's
## couple() reproduces the published pipeline. If the two disagree, nothing
## below is comparable to the published numbers and the run should stop.
if (exists("gen_coupling")) {
  chk <- old |> inner_join(gen_coupling |> select(genus, published = rho_clr), by = "genus")
  d_max <- max(abs(chk$rho - chk$published), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  reproduces section 11c on %d shared genera: max |difference| %.4f\n",
              nrow(chk), d_max))
  if (!is.finite(d_max) || d_max > 0.01) {
    print(chk |> mutate(diff = rho - published) |> arrange(desc(abs(diff))) |> head(8))
    stop("this script's couple() does not reproduce section 11c's rho_clr. ",
         "Fix that before reading anything below — the comparison is against ",
         "the published values.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}
## The re-searched rows need the same taxonomic assignment pipeline applied to
## them; this expects a pep_g-equivalent for the new identifications.
## TWO OBJECTS ARE NEEDED FOR THE RE-SEARCHED ARM, not one.
##
## pep_g_new  — Unipept genus assignment of the re-searched peptides, at the
##              §5a settings (equate_il, extra, names, genus from genus_name).
## OP_new     — the re-searched run's OWN quantification: $a, $rd, $d, built by
##              running section 2's pipeline on the re-searched PSM table.
##
## BUG FIXED 26 Sep 2026: this line previously passed OP$a, the ORIGINAL
## quantification matrix, with the new taxonomy. That is not a taxonomy-only
## comparison, it is incoherent — pep_g_new$row indexes the NEW run's rows, so
## indexing OP$a with them selects arbitrary rows of the old matrix. The
## prediction this script scores is about CLR profiles computed from the new
## quantification, so the new matrix is required.
##
## OP_new MUST COME FROM THE SAME PIPELINE. Build it by running section 2's
## qfeatures and normalise chunks on the re-searched PSM table, not by
## assembling a matrix of the right shape. A different aggregation or
## normalisation would reintroduce exactly the confound the control run was run
## to eliminate: a processing difference presenting as a database effect. If the
## two matrices are not processed identically, this comparison is not
## interpretable and no verdict below should be believed.
## pep_g_new can be built here from the staged LCA table; OP_new cannot, because
## it must come from section 2's own pipeline (see below).
## REBUILD ON INADEQUACY, NOT ON ABSENCE.
## This was `if (!exists("pep_g_new") ...)`, so a stale object from an earlier
## attempt in the same session silently suppressed the build — and the run that
## produced it had no access to the frozen cache. The result was a test arm on 9
## patients and 14 genera, which then produced a confident and entirely spurious
## verdict. Test the object's coverage of THIS run's peptides; rebuild if thin.
.pgn_ok <- exists("pep_g_new") && is.data.frame(pep_g_new) &&
  all(c("row","tax") %in% names(pep_g_new)) && exists("OP_new") &&
  max(pep_g_new$row, na.rm = TRUE) <= nrow(OP_new$a) &&
  nrow(pep_g_new) >= 0.15 * nrow(OP_new$a)
if (exists("pep_g_new") && !.pgn_ok)
  cat("  discarding the pep_g_new in this session: ",
      if (!exists("OP_new")) "OP_new absent"
      else sprintf("%d rows against %d PSM rows (%.1f%%) — too thin, or built for a different run",
                   nrow(pep_g_new), nrow(OP_new$a), 100*nrow(pep_g_new)/nrow(OP_new$a)),
      "\n", sep = "")
if (!.pgn_ok && file.exists(LCA) && exists("OP_new")) {
  lca <- read.delim(LCA, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  gcol <- intersect(c("genus_name","genus"), names(lca))[1]
  pcol <- intersect(c("peptide","seq","sequence"), names(lca))[1]
  if (is.na(gcol) || is.na(pcol))
    stop(LCA, ": needs a peptide column and genus_name", call. = FALSE)
  tax_new <- tibble(seq = lca[[pcol]], tax = lca[[gcol]])

  ## THE STAGED TABLE HOLDS ONLY THE NEWLY QUERIED PEPTIDES.
  ## The re-searched run contains both: peptides the original database also found,
  ## whose taxonomy is in the frozen cache, and peptides only the concatenated
  ## database finds, which is what was queried. Building from the new table alone
  ## covered 25,378 of 56,877 sequences (45%) against the original arm's 89%, and
  ## the missing half is precisely the peptides the original run already knew —
  ## the ones carrying the existing signal. That would not thin the comparison
  ## evenly; it would gut one side of it. The frozen cache is unioned in, and the
  ## cache wins any collision, since it is the taxonomy the published run used.
  if (exists("lca_all2") && all(c("peptide","genus_name") %in% names(lca_all2))) {
    cached <- lca_all2 |> filter(cohort == "pitt") |>
      transmute(seq = peptide, tax = genus_name)
    tax_new <- bind_rows(cached, tax_new)
    cat(sprintf("  taxonomy: %d cached + %d newly queried\n", nrow(cached), nrow(lca)))
  } else {
    cat("  NOTE: lca_all2 not in the session, so only the newly queried peptides\n",
        "        are available. Coverage is reported below — if it is far under\n",
        "        the original arm's, the comparison is not usable.\n", sep = "")
  }
  tax_new <- tax_new |> filter(!is.na(tax), nzchar(tax)) |> distinct(seq, .keep_all = TRUE)

  ## LIKE FOR LIKE. An earlier version compared the re-searched arm's
  ## GENUS-RESOLVED fraction against the original arm's PRESENCE-IN-CACHE
  ## fraction — 31.7% against 88.9% — and stopped the run on a gap that was an
  ## artefact of measuring two different things. Both sides are the fraction of
  ## that arm's distinct peptides carrying a genus, and the absolute counts are
  ## reported too, since the two runs have different peptide totals.
  sq  <- unique(OP_new$rd$seq)
  sqo <- unique(OP$rd$seq)
  ## NOT g_new / g_old: those are the clade-gap variables further down, and this
  ## block assigns at top level. Four objects have been silently overwritten this
  ## way in this project already.
  ngen_new <- sum(sq %in% tax_new$seq); ngen_old <- sum(sqo %in% pep_g$seq)
  cat(sprintf("  genus-resolved peptides: re-searched %d of %d (%.1f%%), original %d of %d (%.1f%%)\n",
              ngen_new, length(sq), 100*ngen_new/length(sq),
              ngen_old, length(sqo), 100*ngen_old/length(sqo)))
  if (ngen_new < 0.6 * ngen_old)
    stop("the re-searched arm has ", ngen_new, " genus-resolved peptides against the ",
         "original's ", ngen_old, ".\n  Too few to compare: its taxonomy is missing ",
         "peptides the original had.\n  Check that the staged table covers this ",
         "run's peptide set, not only the newly queried ones.", call. = FALSE)

  pep_g_new <- tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(OP_new$a)), seq = OP_new$rd$seq) |>
    inner_join(tax_new, by = "seq")
  cat(sprintf("  pep_g_new: %d rows with a genus (%.1f%% of %d PSM rows)\n",
              nrow(pep_g_new), 100 * nrow(pep_g_new) / nrow(OP_new$a), nrow(OP_new$a)))
}
## OP_new IS CHECKED FIRST, because pep_g_new is built from it. Checking
## pep_g_new first reported it missing when the real blocker was OP_new, which
## sent the reader to the Unipept step that had already been done.
if (!exists("OP_new"))
  stop("OP_new not found — this is the only thing still missing.\n\n",
       "  It is the re-searched run's own quantification: $a (rows x channels),\n",
       "  $rd (with Protein and seq), $d (with sample). Build it by running\n",
       "  section 2's qfeatures and normalise chunks against\n",
       "    ", PSM, "\n",
       "  in place of the original PSM table, then arm_objs() for the same arm.\n\n",
       "  C1d_build_OP_new.R does this: it reuses load_psm_long, build_qf,\n",
       "  normalise_channels and arm_objs from the live session rather than\n",
       "  reimplementing them, so both arms are processed by identical code.\n",
       "  Run it from a session that has reached section 3:\n",
       "    source(\"C1d_build_OP_new.R\")\n\n",
       "  Do NOT assemble a matrix of the right shape by hand: a different\n",
       "  aggregation or normalisation would present as a database effect and\n",
       "  would reintroduce exactly the confound the control run was run to\n",
       "  eliminate.\n\n",
       "  The Unipept step is already done — ", basename(LCA), " is staged and\n",
       "  pep_g_new is built from it automatically once OP_new exists.",
       call. = FALSE)
if (!exists("pep_g_new"))
  stop("pep_g_new could not be built from ", LCA, ".\n",
       "  OP_new exists, so check that its $rd carries a `seq` column and that\n",
       "  the LCA table's peptide column matches those sequences.", call. = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(sort(OP_new$d$sample), sort(OP$d$sample)),
          max(pep_g_new$row) <= nrow(OP_new$a))
new_c <- couple(pep_g_new, OP_new$a, OP_new$d$sample, "concatenated database")

## THE TWO ARMS MUST BE COMPARED ON THE SAME GENERA.
## pep_g_new is sparser than pep_g — 17,428 genus-assigned rows over 175,867 PSMs
## against 36,228 over 151,712 — so the 200-row floor admits far fewer genera in
## the re-searched arm. A median over 29 genera against a median over 14 is not
## the same quantity, and the sealed prediction is per genus. Restrict both arms
## to the genera that clear the floor in BOTH, report the restricted comparison
## as primary, and show the unrestricted one beside it so the loss is visible.
shared_gen <- intersect(old$genus, new_c$genus)
cat(sprintf("\ngenera clearing the floor: %d original, %d re-searched, %d in both\n",
            nrow(old), nrow(new_c), length(shared_gen)))
if (length(shared_gen) < 8)
  cat("  WARNING: too few shared genera for a per-clade median. The re-searched\n",
      "  taxonomy is much thinner than the original, which is itself the finding:\n",
      "  the comparison cannot be made at this floor.\n", sep = "")
lost <- setdiff(old$genus, new_c$genus)
if (length(lost))
  cat("  present originally, below the floor after re-search: ",
      paste(head(lost, 12), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(lost) > 12) sprintf(" (+%d more)", length(lost) - 12) else "", "\n", sep = "")
d_all <- bind_rows(old, new_c)
old <- filter(old, genus %in% shared_gen)
new_c <- filter(new_c, genus %in% shared_gen)

phy <- pep_ph |> select(row, phylum = tax) |>
  inner_join(pep_g |> select(row, genus = tax), by = "row") |>
  count(genus, phylum) |> group_by(genus) |> slice_max(n, n = 1) |> ungroup()
d <- bind_rows(old, new_c) |>
  mutate(phylum = phy$phylum[match(genus, phy$genus)],
         clade = case_when(phylum %in% c("Bacillota", "Firmicutes") ~ "Bacillota",
                           phylum == "Bacteroidota" ~ "Bacteroidota", TRUE ~ "other"))
tab <- d |> filter(clade != "other") |> group_by(which, clade) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_rho = median(rho, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
cat("\nclade coupling, centred log-ratios, within patients:\n"); print(as.data.frame(tab))

gap <- function(w) {
  x <- tab$median_rho[tab$which == w]
  tab$median_rho[tab$which == w & tab$clade == "Bacillota"] -
  tab$median_rho[tab$which == w & tab$clade == "Bacteroidota"]
}
g_old <- gap("original database"); g_new <- gap("concatenated database")
cat(sprintf("\nBacillota minus Bacteroidota: %+.3f originally, %+.3f re-searched (%.0f%% retained)\n",
            g_old, g_new, 100 * g_new / g_old))
if (!is.finite(g_old) || !is.finite(g_new))
  stop("the clade gap is not finite on one or both arms. Check the genus counts ",
       "and the dropped-patient lines above — nothing below is interpretable.",
       call. = FALSE)

## ---- 3. THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION -------------------------------------
## Recorded on 25 September, BEFORE this script was run, from the test run's own
## peptide evidence: per-genus CLR profile correlations between the published and
## re-searched proteomes, and the alignment of each genus's residual with its
## metagenome vector. Those give a signed expected shift per genus. The point of
## writing them here is that they cannot be adjusted after seeing the output.
PRED <- data.frame(
  genus   = c("Phocaeicola","Bacteroides","Segatella","Alistipes","Parabacteroides",
              "Lachnospira","Lachnoclostridium","Blautia"),
  clade   = c(rep("Bacteroidota",5), rep("Bacillota",3)),
  rho     = c(0.9944,0.9950,0.9968,0.9949,0.9607,0.9697,0.9066,0.9919),
  expect  = c(-0.016,-0.003,-0.017,-0.030,-0.040,+0.093,+0.066,+0.036),
  bound   = c(0.106,0.099,0.080,0.101,0.277,NA,NA,NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
PRED_GAP <- 0.021          # predicted WIDENING of Bacillota minus Bacteroidota
WELL_COVERED <- c("Phocaeicola","Bacteroides","Segatella","Alistipes")

score_prediction <- function(d) {
  obs <- d |> filter(which == "concatenated database") |> select(genus, rho_new = rho) |>
    inner_join(d |> filter(which == "original database") |> select(genus, rho_old = rho),
               by = "genus") |>
    mutate(delta = rho_new - rho_old)
  tab <- PRED |> inner_join(obs, by = "genus") |>
    mutate(err = delta - expect,
           within_bound = is.na(bound) | abs(delta) <= bound)
  cat("\n---- the pre-registered prediction, scored ----\n")
  print(tab |> select(genus, clade, expect, delta, err, within_bound), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

  ## the stated falsification conditions, each evaluated separately
  bact <- tab |> filter(clade == "Bacteroidota")
  f1 <- any(bact$delta > 0.02, na.rm = TRUE)
  f2 <- any(tab$genus %in% WELL_COVERED & abs(tab$delta) > 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  f3 <- (g_new - g_old) < 0
  cat(sprintf("\n  F1  a Bacteroidota genus moved positively by > 0.02 : %s\n", f1))
  cat(sprintf("  F2  a well-covered genus moved by > 0.05           : %s\n", f2))
  cat(sprintf("  F3  the Bacillota-minus-Bacteroidota gap narrowed  : %s  (%+.3f, predicted %+.3f)\n",
              f3, g_new - g_old, PRED_GAP))
  if (any(c(f1, f2, f3)))
    cat("\n  PREDICTION FALSIFIED. The re-search moved the coupling more, or in a\n",
        "  different direction, than the inputs implied. That makes it informative\n",
        "  rather than weak survival, and the mechanism needs explaining before any\n",
        "  conclusion is drawn about R3.\n", sep = "")
  else
    cat("\n  PREDICTION HOLDS. The shifts are what the profile correlations implied,\n",
        "  so the re-search did not perturb the Bacteroidota measurements enough to\n",
        "  test the database explanation. Report as weak survival, not exclusion.\n", sep = "")
  invisible(tab)
}

## ---- 4. the reading, fixed before the result -------------------------------
cat("\n---- verdict ----\n")
verdict <- if (g_new >= 0.6 * g_old) {
  paste0("THE CLADE RESULT SURVIVES. The decoupling is not an artefact of searching\n",
      "each cohort against its own assembly: it persists when the same spectra are\n",
      "identified against a database containing both. R3's last technical\n",
      "explanation is excluded, and the clade structure can be reported as a\n",
      "property of the measurement rather than of the search space.\n")
} else if (g_new <= 0.3 * g_old) {
  paste0("THE CLADE RESULT DOES NOT SURVIVE. Most of the gap closes when the search\n",
      "space changes, so the decoupling is substantially a database artefact. R3\n",
      "must be withdrawn or restated as a property of assembly-derived databases,\n",
      "and the composition-weighted prediction failure in §R3 has to be re-examined\n",
      "on the same basis. This is the outcome the two-pillar structure does NOT\n",
      "absorb - reassess the venue before submitting.\n")
} else if (exists("even_loss") && !isTRUE(even_loss)) {
  paste0("INCONCLUSIVE. Identification loss did not fall evenly across clades, so
the before/after comparison confounds the database change with a change in what
could be measured. This is neither a positive nor a negative result: report the
per-clade recovery and say the experiment did not settle the question.")
} else {
  paste0("PARTIAL. The gap narrows but does not close. Report both values and the\n",
      "proportion retained; do not claim the database is excluded, and do not\n",
      "withdraw the result. State that the search space accounts for part of the\n",
      "clade difference and that the remainder is unexplained.\n")
}
cat(verdict)

pred_scored <- tryCatch(score_prediction(d), error = function(e) {
  cat("prediction not scored:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

saveRDS(list(per_genus = d, summary = tab, gap_old = g_old, gap_new = g_new,
             prediction = PRED, prediction_scored = pred_scored,
             n_rows_old = nrow(OP$rd), n_rows_new = nrow(new), by_source = table(src)),
        file.path(OUT, "concat_research_clade.rds"))
## ---- 5. follow-up: is the Bacteroidota anti-alignment a property of the
##         clade, or of the sequence the Sheba databases added? ---------------
## All nine Bacteroidota genera's residuals align negatively with the metagenome
## (p = 0.003). If that is confined to peptides assigned to a sheba| accession it
## is a property of the added database — those sequences come from a differently
## preserved community whose Bacteroidota may be a different subset of strains —
## and must not be read as clade biology. If pitt|-assigned peptides show it too,
## it is the more interesting finding. Run this AFTER the verdict above, never
## before: it characterises the inputs and would tune the prediction if seen
## first.
if (exists("pep_g_new") && "Protein" %in% names(new)) {
  srcs <- sub("\\|.*$", "", new$Protein)
  cat("\n---- residual anti-alignment by source database ----\n")
  for (grp in c("pitt", "sheba1", "sheba2")) {
    k <- srcs == grp
    cat(sprintf("  %-7s %7d PSMs, %6d peptides\n", grp, sum(k),
                length(unique(new$Peptide[k]))))
  }
  cat("  (split the per-genus residuals by these groups and recompute cor(x, e);\n",
      "   confined to sheba -> database property, present in pitt -> clade property)\n",
      sep = "")
}

cat("\nwritten to ", OUT, "\n", sep = "")
```

## S8 — sheba power

Supplementary Figure — Sheba cohort power analysis.

Source: `S8_sheba_power.R`

```{r S8_sheba_power, eval=FALSE}
# S8_sheba_power.R
# Supplementary Figure — Sheba cohort power analysis.
#
# Quantifies what the pre-treatment cohort can and cannot resolve:
#   A — Detectable effect size (Cohen's d) as a function of alpha and
#       desired power, at each cohort's analysed sample size.
#   B — Power vs effect size at fixed alpha.
#   C — Pitt-anchored simulation: of Pitt-significant features at q < 0.10,
#       what fraction would be expected to replicate in Sheba at p < 0.05?
#
# Inputs:
#   metaproteomics_post14.rds
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXED 11 Oct 2026 — the sample sizes were wrong, and the figure was
# therefore optimistic.
#
# `supp_get_meta()` returns the per-CHANNEL x RUN annotation: 280 rows for
# Sheba, 415 for Pitt. The previous version summed Response over those rows,
# giving Sheba R=175 NR=75 and Pitt R=180 NR=195 — run counts, not patients.
# Reducing to one row per patient is not enough on its own either:
#   * reference ("Norm") channels must be dropped;
#   * plexes that carry no within-plex response contrast are not analysed
#     (Pitt TMT2 and TMT5; Sheba mixture 2) and TMT9 was never searched;
#   * two Sheba samples come from one patient (135 in mixture 4 and 682 in
#     mixture 5), and the primary takes one sample per patient — the earliest
#     pre-treatment episode — so 682 is dropped in favour of 135. The
#     annotation carries no patient column, so a BioReplicate-level dedup
#     cannot see this and returns 9 non-responders instead of 8.
#
# The analysed sets are therefore declared explicitly below and asserted
# against the counts the manuscript reports. The authoritative per-sample
# record is `comment[analysed in primary analysis]` in the deposited SDRF.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

source("00_supp_common.R")

set.seed(42L)
N_BOOT <- 500L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. The analysed sets, declared
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PLEXES_ANALYSED <- list(
  pitt  = c("TMT1", "TMT3", "TMT4", "TMT6", "TMT7", "TMT8"),
  sheba = c("1", "3", "4", "5")
)
# Patient-level exclusions the plex filter cannot express.
PATIENTS_EXCLUDED <- list(
  pitt  = character(0),
  sheba = c("682")              # same patient as 135; 135 is the earlier tube
)
# What the manuscript reports. The script stops if the data stop matching.
EXPECTED <- list(pitt = c(R = 25, NR = 30), sheba = c(R = 27, NR = 8))

#' One row per analysed patient, from the per-channel annotation.
cohort_patients <- function(state, cohort = c("pitt", "sheba")) {
  cohort <- match.arg(cohort)
  ann <- supp_get_meta(state, cohort)
  need <- c("BioReplicate", "Condition", "Mixture")
  if (!all(need %in% names(ann)))
    stop(cohort, ": annotation lacks ", paste(setdiff(need, names(ann)),
                                               collapse = ", "))
  d <- unique(ann[, need])
  d$Response <- ifelse(grepl("^non", d$Condition, ignore.case = TRUE), "NR",
                ifelse(grepl("^resp", d$Condition, ignore.case = TRUE), "R", NA))
  d <- d[!is.na(d$Response), ]                                   # drops Norm
  d <- d[as.character(d$Mixture) %in% PLEXES_ANALYSED[[cohort]], ]
  d <- d[!d$BioReplicate %in% PATIENTS_EXCLUDED[[cohort]], ]
  d <- d[!duplicated(d$BioReplicate), ]
  got <- c(R = sum(d$Response == "R"), NR = sum(d$Response == "NR"))
  exp <- EXPECTED[[cohort]]
  cat(sprintf("  %-5s %d R / %d NR (n = %d) from %d annotation rows\n",
              cohort, got["R"], got["NR"], nrow(d), nrow(ann)))
  if (!identical(as.integer(got), as.integer(exp)))
    stop(sprintf(paste0("%s: analysed set is %d R / %d NR but the manuscript ",
                        "reports %d R / %d NR. Reconcile before plotting -- ",
                        "see comment[analysed in primary analysis] in the SDRF."),
                 cohort, got["R"], got["NR"], exp["R"], exp["NR"]))
  d
}

state <- supp_load_state()
cat("Analysed sample sizes (one row per patient):\n")
pitt_pat  <- cohort_patients(state, "pitt")
sheba_pat <- cohort_patients(state, "sheba")

n_R_pitt   <- sum(pitt_pat$Response  == "R");  n_NR_pitt  <- sum(pitt_pat$Response  == "NR")
n_R_sheba  <- sum(sheba_pat$Response == "R");  n_NR_sheba <- sum(sheba_pat$Response == "NR")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Power calculator (two-sample t, two-sided)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (requireNamespace("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  POWER_FN <- "pwr"
  power_at <- function(d, alpha, n1, n2)
    pwr::pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n1, n2 = n2, d = d, sig.level = alpha,
                      alternative = "two.sided")$power
  d_at <- function(alpha, power, n1, n2)
    pwr::pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n1, n2 = n2, sig.level = alpha, power = power,
                      alternative = "two.sided")$d
} else {
  POWER_FN <- "manual"
  cat("Note: pwr not installed; using the non-central t directly.\n")
  power_at <- function(d, alpha, n1, n2) {
    df <- n1 + n2 - 2; ncp <- d / sqrt(1 / n1 + 1 / n2)
    crit <- stats::qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
    1 - stats::pt(crit, df, ncp) + stats::pt(-crit, df, ncp)
  }
  d_at <- function(alpha, power, n1, n2)
    stats::uniroot(function(d) power_at(d, alpha, n1, n2) - power,
                   interval = c(0.001, 6))$root
}
cat("Power backend: ", POWER_FN, "\n", sep = "")

# The two effects the manuscript reports at protein level, for annotation.
D_CHAPERONE <- 0.59
D_RIBOSOMAL <- 0.72
cat(sprintf("Power at the reported protein-level effects: chaperone d=%.2f -> %.3f; ribosomal d=%.2f -> %.3f\n",
            D_CHAPERONE, power_at(D_CHAPERONE, 0.05, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba),
            D_RIBOSOMAL, power_at(D_RIBOSOMAL, 0.05, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Panel A — detectable effect size
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
alpha_grid <- c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10)
power_grid <- seq(0.50, 0.95, by = 0.05)

detect_curve <- expand.grid(alpha = alpha_grid, power = power_grid,
                            KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    d_sheba = mapply(d_at, alpha, power,
                     MoreArgs = list(n1 = n_R_sheba, n2 = n_NR_sheba)),
    d_pitt  = mapply(d_at, alpha, power,
                     MoreArgs = list(n1 = n_R_pitt,  n2 = n_NR_pitt)),
    alpha_lab = paste0("α = ", alpha)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(alpha, power)

d80_sheba <- d_at(0.05, 0.80, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba)

p_A <- ggplot(detect_curve, aes(x = power)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = d_sheba, color = "Sheba"), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = d_pitt,  color = "Pitt"),  linewidth = 0.6,
            linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 0.8), linetype = "dotted",
             color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = data.frame(y = c(0.5, 0.8),
                              lbl = c("medium d=0.5", "large d=0.8")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, aes(x = 0.5, y = y, label = lbl),
            hjust = 0, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.4, color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ alpha_lab, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Pitt = SUPP_COLORS$Pitt,
                                Sheba = SUPP_COLORS$Sheba), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "A. Detectable effect size (Cohen's d) at each cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("Two-sample t-test, two-sided, at the analysed ",
                                 "sample sizes. Pitt R=%d NR=%d; Sheba R=%d NR=%d."),
                          n_R_pitt, n_NR_pitt, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba),
       x = "Desired power", y = "Detectable Cohen's d") +
  SUPP_THEME +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")

write_csv(detect_curve, file.path(SUPP_TABS_DIR, "S8_detectable_d.csv"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Panel B — power vs effect size
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
power_curve <- expand.grid(d = seq(0.1, 2.5, by = 0.05),
                           alpha = c(0.05, 0.10, 0.001),
                           KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pow_sheba = mapply(power_at, d, alpha,
                       MoreArgs = list(n1 = n_R_sheba, n2 = n_NR_sheba)),
    pow_pitt  = mapply(power_at, d, alpha,
                       MoreArgs = list(n1 = n_R_pitt,  n2 = n_NR_pitt)),
    alpha_lab = paste0("α = ", alpha))

power_long <- power_curve %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(pow_sheba, pow_pitt), names_to = "cohort",
                      values_to = "power") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cohort = ifelse(cohort == "pow_sheba", "Sheba", "Pitt"),
                cohort = factor(cohort, levels = c("Pitt", "Sheba")))

p_B <- ggplot(power_long, aes(x = d, y = power, color = cohort,
                              linetype = cohort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 0.8), linetype = "dotted",
             color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = D_CHAPERONE, linetype = "dotted",
             color = SUPP_COLORS$Sheba, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ alpha_lab, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Pitt = SUPP_COLORS$Pitt,
                                Sheba = SUPP_COLORS$Sheba), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Pitt = "dashed", Sheba = "solid"),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
  labs(title = "B. Power vs Cohen's d, at fixed α",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("Dotted horizontals: 0.5 and 0.8 power. ",
                                 "Vertical: the reported chaperone effect, ",
                                 "d = %.2f, at which Sheba has power %.2f."),
                          D_CHAPERONE,
                          power_at(D_CHAPERONE, 0.05, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba)),
       x = "Cohen's d (effect size)", y = "Power") +
  SUPP_THEME +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Panel C — Pitt-anchored replication
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The previous version looked only under state$mp$..., where these slots do
# not exist when the state is loaded at top level, so panel C could not run.
pick <- function(nm) if (!is.null(state[[nm]])) state[[nm]] else state$mp[[nm]]
pitt_pw_da <- pick("pitt_path_consensus")
if (is.null(pitt_pw_da)) pitt_pw_da <- pick("pitt_consensus")
if (is.null(pitt_pw_da))
  stop("No Pitt DA table at pitt_path_consensus or pitt_consensus.")

lfc_col <- supp_first_colname(pitt_pw_da, c("logFC", "logFC_lim", "log2FC"))
p_col   <- supp_first_colname(pitt_pw_da, c("p_lim", "p_limma", "P.Value"))
q_col   <- supp_first_colname(pitt_pw_da, c("q_lim", "q_limma", "adj.P.Val"))
if (any(is.na(c(lfc_col, p_col, q_col))))
  stop("Pitt DA columns missing. Available: ",
       paste(names(pitt_pw_da), collapse = ", "))

# NOTE ON THE ESTIMATOR. p_lim / q_lim come from the fit WITHOUT the plex
# term. Methods states that an unconditioned contrast is partly a between-plex
# comparison and supports no claim. The conditioned fit (q_lim_cond) has no
# feature at q < 0.10, so this panel cannot be built on it. The anchor is
# therefore named in the subtitle rather than left implicit.
if (identical(q_col, "q_lim"))
  warning("Panel C is anchored on the unconditioned fit (q_lim); ",
          "the conditioned fit yields no feature at q < 0.10.")

pitt_sig <- pitt_pw_da %>%
  dplyr::transmute(logFC = .data[[lfc_col]], p = .data[[p_col]],
                   q = .data[[q_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(q), q < 0.10, !is.na(logFC), !is.na(p), p > 0, p < 1)

cat("\nPitt features in simulation pool: ", nrow(pitt_sig), "\n", sep = "")

# Each feature's observed standardised effect, inverted from its own two-sided
# p at Pitt's n. The previous version computed this, then discarded it in
# favour of a single median d/|logFC| scale applied to every feature, which
# threw away the per-feature information it had just recovered.
df_pitt <- n_R_pitt + n_NR_pitt - 2
pitt_sig$d_obs <- abs(stats::qt(1 - pitt_sig$p / 2, df_pitt)) *
  sqrt(1 / n_R_pitt + 1 / n_NR_pitt)
cat("Median observed |d| among Pitt q<0.10 features: ",
    round(stats::median(pitt_sig$d_obs), 3), "\n", sep = "")

pitt_sig$power_sheba_05 <- power_at(pitt_sig$d_obs, 0.05, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba)
pitt_sig$power_sheba_10 <- power_at(pitt_sig$d_obs, 0.10, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba)

sim_replicate <- function(d, n1, n2, B, alpha) {
  if (!is.finite(d)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(replicate(B, stats::t.test(stats::rnorm(n1, 0, 1),
                                  stats::rnorm(n2, d, 1))$p.value) < alpha)
}
cat("Running ", N_BOOT, "-iteration MC for ", nrow(pitt_sig), " features...\n",
    sep = "")
pitt_sig$power_sheba_mc <- vapply(pitt_sig$d_obs, sim_replicate,
                                  n1 = n_R_sheba, n2 = n_NR_sheba,
                                  B = N_BOOT, alpha = 0.05, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1))

write_csv(pitt_sig, file.path(SUPP_TABS_DIR, "S8_pitt_sim.csv"))

expected_repl_rate <- mean(pitt_sig$power_sheba_05, na.rm = TRUE)
expected_repl_mc   <- mean(pitt_sig$power_sheba_mc, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("\nExpected fraction of Pitt q<0.10 features replicating in Sheba\n",
    "  analytic, α=0.05: ", round(expected_repl_rate, 3), "\n",
    "  MC, α=0.05, B=", N_BOOT, ": ", round(expected_repl_mc, 3), "\n", sep = "")

p_C <- ggplot(pitt_sig, aes(x = power_sheba_mc)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = SUPP_COLORS$Sheba, alpha = 0.85,
                 color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = expected_repl_mc, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey15", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = expected_repl_mc, y = Inf,
           label = paste0("mean = ", round(expected_repl_mc, 2)),
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.6, color = "grey15") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.02, 1.02),
                     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "C. Pitt-anchored Sheba replication probability",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("%d Pitt features at %s < 0.10, each at its own ",
                                 "observed effect; %d MC draws at Sheba n, α = 0.05. ",
                                 "Anchored on the unconditioned fit."),
                          nrow(pitt_sig), q_col, N_BOOT),
       x = "Per-feature replication probability in Sheba",
       y = "Count of Pitt features") +
  SUPP_THEME

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Assemble
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fig <- (p_A / p_B / p_C) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Supplementary Figure — what the pre-treatment cohort can resolve",
    subtitle = sprintf(paste0("Analysed sizes: Pitt R=%d NR=%d; Sheba R=%d NR=%d. ",
                              "At α = 0.05 Sheba resolves d ≥ %.2f at 80%% power, ",
                              "and %.0f%% of Pitt q<0.10 features are expected to ",
                              "replicate at p < 0.05."),
                       n_R_pitt, n_NR_pitt, n_R_sheba, n_NR_sheba,
                       d80_sheba, expected_repl_mc * 100),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey25")))

cat("\nSaving the figure...\n")
supp_save(fig, "S8_sheba_power", width_mm = 200, height_mm = 280)

cat("\nDone. Source data:\n",
    "  ", file.path(SUPP_TABS_DIR, "S8_detectable_d.csv"), "\n",
    "  ", file.path(SUPP_TABS_DIR, "S8_pitt_sim.csv"), "\n", sep = "")
```
